outlook.text: Gibbs has finished in the top 10 among running backs in yards per carry, routes, targets, receptions, touchdowns and fantasy points in each of his first three campaigns. In fact, his 38 touchdowns over the past two seasons are four more than any other player. Though Gibbs has finished as a top-three fantasy back in each of the past two years, he has yet to finish a season higher than seventh in touches. That very well could change this season with David Montgomery no longer in the mix. The 24-year-old Gibbs is one of the NFL's top playmakers in one of its best offenses. He's a strong option with the first pick of fantasy drafts.

profile_notes.subject: Jahmyr Gibbs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Top-of-draft foundation in non-superflex formats.
profile_notes.summary: Both view Gibbs as among the safest premium players despite the unknown of a season without David Montgomery.
profile_notes.evidence: Josh cites consecutive top-four RB finishes, Gibbs's prime-age profile, and Detroit's likely strong offense; Harris identifies no dominant risk beyond the team not being an absolute certainty.
profile_notes.counterweight: The transcript notes they have not yet seen Gibbs without Montgomery, and Detroit was not great the prior year.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Gibbs as a low-risk early anchor rather than fading him for theoretical workload uncertainty.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Jahmyr Gibbs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Elite non-superflex pick; retained A-plus speed grade.
profile_notes.summary: Gibbs remains one of Harris's two fastest running backs and no longer has a contract-related camp concern.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris names Gibbs and De'Von Achane as unchanged A-plus speed players, then says the resolved signing situations permit drafting elite backs in comfort.
profile_notes.counterweight: The segment adds no new role or injury issue for Gibbs.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Gibbs in the premium RB tier rather than discounting speed, preparation, or contract risk.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Move out of RB1/RB2 consideration if either continues holding in through late August; panic date is around August 29.
profile_notes.summary: Richard's top story is whether Gibbs and Robinson keep holding in, because a late resolution can erase early-season effectiveness from otherwise worthy 1.01/1.02 selections.
profile_notes.evidence: He cites repeated examples of players missing camp, signing late, then struggling or getting hurt in the first four weeks; both would elevate Jonathan Taylor, and perhaps McCaffrey in PPR, if the risk persists.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris initially assumed the teams would pay them and does not want a hyperreactive cut; a deal before the late-August threshold would largely resolve the concern.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not spend the 1.01/1.02 on an unsigned hold-in near the deadline without pricing in ramp-up and injury risk.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Jahmyr Gibbs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris's RB1; Erickson agrees he belongs in the top two.
profile_notes.summary: Harris selects Gibbs above every RB because no other elite runner matches his game-breaking weekly ceiling.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris calls Gibbs's stop-foot/go-foot and cutback ability historically elite, cites six 40-plus-yard runs, and says massive plays differentiate fantasy production. David Montgomery is gone and Pacheco's past goal-line usage suggests Gibbs may get first try near the end zone.
profile_notes.counterweight: Gibbs hunts big plays, had six low-yardage games and a quiet fantasy playoff stretch in a less consistent Lions offense; bigger backs retain a stronger theoretical goal-line claim.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Gibbs as a premium anchor and accept occasional volatility in exchange for unmatched week-winning plays.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Robinson enters his fourth season having finished in the top five among running backs in carries, rushing yards, touches, yards and fantasy points in each of the past two seasons. Also a big factor as a receiver, he has ranked no lower than fifth at the position in routes, targets, receptions and receiving yards in his three pro seasons. In 2025, PFF tracked him with 86 forced missed tackles, which was easily the most among backs. The 24-year-old is in his prime and, though he has a new coach in Kevin Stefanski, his path to a massive offensive role remains clear. He's on the short list of players who should be considered with the first pick of your fantasy draft.

profile_notes.subject: Bijan Robinson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Premium RB option, with a small quarterback-related risk adjustment.
profile_notes.summary: Robinson is a high-end RB1 with only slightly more risk than Gibbs.
profile_notes.evidence: Josh notes an RB3 finish despite poor quarterback play, peak-career status, and no stated injury concern; Harris's extra point is specifically tied to the uglier quarterback setting.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both expect the quarterback situation to remain a drag, which can narrow ceiling and makes him marginally less secure than Gibbs.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Robinson confidently at an elite price, but recognize the offense is the small differentiator versus Gibbs.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Bijan Robinson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Top non-superflex draft pick with holdout concern removed.
profile_notes.summary: Robinson's signing lets drafters remove the concern that a protracted hold-in could affect his preparation.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Robinson signed, is practicing, and joins Gibbs and Jonathan Taylor as top backs no longer carrying an August contract concern.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris did not believe a deep-August Robinson holdout was likely in the first place.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Robinson in the elite tier without discounting him for a camp-contract scenario.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Move out of RB1/RB2 consideration if either continues holding in through late August; panic date is around August 29.
profile_notes.summary: Richard's top story is whether Gibbs and Robinson keep holding in, because a late resolution can erase early-season effectiveness from otherwise worthy 1.01/1.02 selections.
profile_notes.evidence: He cites repeated examples of players missing camp, signing late, then struggling or getting hurt in the first four weeks; both would elevate Jonathan Taylor, and perhaps McCaffrey in PPR, if the risk persists.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris initially assumed the teams would pay them and does not want a hyperreactive cut; a deal before the late-August threshold would largely resolve the concern.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not spend the 1.01/1.02 on an unsigned hold-in near the deadline without pricing in ramp-up and injury risk.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

outlook.text: Nacua has defied the odds, emerging from fifth-round flier in 2023 to one of the most relied upon and productive offensive players in the league. Nacua has finished each of his three pro seasons sixth or better among receivers in fantasy PPG and peaked with a first-place finish last season. Matthew Stafford's top target led the league with 129 receptions and finished no lower than third among receivers in targets, yardage and touchdowns, while also adding 105 yards and one score as a rusher. More goal-line work would be nice (he has 11 end zone targets over the past two seasons), but Nacua's heavy usage in an elite offense locks in the 25-year-old as arguably the top receiver in fantasy.

profile_notes.subject: Puka Nacua
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Recheck groin status and Week 1 availability immediately before drafting.
profile_notes.summary: Harris treats Nacua's prolonged groin-related absence as a real Week 1 concern for a first-round player.
profile_notes.evidence: The concern comes from missing roughly 10 days with camp nearly complete rather than a reported long-term diagnosis.
profile_notes.counterweight: The source does not establish that Nacua will miss Week 1, and a prompt return would reduce the concern.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Check current reporting before the draft and avoid assuming full Week 1 availability.
profile_notes.episode_title: More Flag Players & Cousin Josh's Frag Players

profile_notes.subject: Puka Nacua
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Consider near the back of Round 1, not at ADP 4.
profile_notes.summary: Nacua is an elite receiver but carries meaningful injury and possible off-field uncertainty at an early-first price.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites Adam Schefter's suggestion that something may be brewing and Nacua's pattern of getting injured, including a significant absence two years earlier; Josh agrees on a 5.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris believes a Josh Jacobs suspension is more likely than a Nacua suspension, and Nacua often returns after taking hits.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Nacua as a discounted late-first option rather than a no-doubt top-four selection.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Rams offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a strong environment, but do not let that alone erase individual age, role, and price concerns.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see Los Angeles as the NFC West offense most widely expected to be elite, while Harris warns that assumed certainty creates contradictory player valuations.
profile_notes.evidence: They discuss a possible 30-point-per-game offense, the resolution of Matthew Stafford's prior back concern, and the Rams' recent history of meaningful August role signals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris opens the episode by showing that consensus team projections frequently fail, and individual Rams can still decline or lose role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Rams environment as a supporting factor, then make player decisions on role, talent, health, and market cost.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Chase is fresh off yet another elite fantasy season and he's now finished four of his five NFL campaigns no lower than fifth in fantasy PPG (the exception was 11th in 2023). Chase actually saw a big dip in yardage (1,740 to 1,426), TDs (17 to 8) and fantasy PPG (23.7 to 19.6) from 2024 to 2025 (which was no surprise with Joe Burrow missing nine games), but still put up big numbers thanks to pacing the league in pass routes and targets for the second season in a row. In fact, Chase's 125 receptions make him the third receiver in NFL history with 125-plus catches in multiple seasons. The 26-year-old remains the top target in a high-scoring Bengals offense, and is one of the top players in all of fantasy.

profile_notes.subject: Ja'Marr Chase
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Prefer closer to the middle of Round 1 than at the absolute top.
profile_notes.summary: Chase remains low risk as a player; the elevated concern is Joe Burrow's availability rather than Chase's ability.
profile_notes.evidence: Both assign a 2, and Josh cites Chase reaching 1,400 yards and eight touchdowns even with Burrow missing time.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris says the Burrow issue is the reason Chase moves from last year's risk factor of 1 to 2.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not fade Chase over a small quarterback-risk adjustment, but use RB alternatives if choosing at the very top.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Cincinnati Bengals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not change elite-player ranks on camp drills; monitor credible evidence of more under-center and modern-concept usage.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers regard Cincinnati's core as settled and already elite, with offensive evolution as a possible path from top-five to No. 1 production.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon wants to see Joe Burrow under center more and the offense move beyond an almost exclusively shotgun approach; he notes incremental increases in Chase motion and varied alignment.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harmon repeatedly says camp talk will not force rank changes for Burrow, Chase, Higgins, or Brown, and the preference may remain Burrow's existing style.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat schematic reports as upside context, not a reason to chase already-expensive Bengals players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year, Smith-Njigba is fresh off a breakout season in which he paced all receivers in target share (36%), receiving yards (1,793), air yards (1,858) and yards per route run (3.8), while finishing no lower than fourth in targets, catches, touchdowns and fantasy points. JSN delivered top-10 fantasy weeks 10 times throughout 2025 and scored at least 13 points in 16 of 17 games. The 24-year-old is just now entering his prime and remains well positioned to handle one-third of the targets in Seattle's Sam Darnold-led offense. Smith-Njigba is an elite fantasy option who should be off the board in the early-to-middle part of Round 1.

profile_notes.subject: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Comfortable anywhere in Round 1 under the cited ADP.
profile_notes.summary: Smith-Njigba is viewed as a minimal-risk first-round receiver.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris assigns a 2; Josh calls the risk minimal and describes his prior target share and efficiency results as absurd, while saying he is fine with him anywhere in the first.
profile_notes.counterweight: Josh identifies quarterback Darnold as the residual risk and notes the efficiency is unlikely to be repeated exactly.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Smith-Njigba as a safe WR anchor if you choose receiver early.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris would take him in Round 1 but acknowledges a mid-first cost requires a second elite season.
profile_notes.summary: Harris endorses JSN's elite film and Round-1 talent but frames him as a swing because drafters are paying for a second superstar season after one enormous year.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says he was a major booster and cites 18 catches on 20-plus-air-yard throws; Funston says the film is elite. Both identify defenses' ability to focus on JSN and Seattle's limited punishment options as the core test.
profile_notes.counterweight: The season could prove a one-year peak, and the middle of Round 1 contains receivers with a longer repeat-production record.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft JSN for elite upside if comfortable with the repeat-performance question, rather than treating his outcome as guaranteed.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris's WR2 and a first-round pick when selecting in the later first half.
profile_notes.summary: Harris elevates Smith-Njigba to his No. 2 receiver after an elite hands season and believes the player has earned first-round trust.
profile_notes.evidence: He cites innumerable strong catches throughout the field and only one official drop, which came on a shallow cross against Indianapolis that might have become an 80-yard score.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris says it remains only one huge season and defenses will key on him, so he is not yet a fully proven repeat performer.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Smith-Njigba as a premium receiver while acknowledging the repeat-performance and defensive-attention risks.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

outlook.text: McCaffrey is back for his fifth season with the 49ers after a bounce-back 2025 campaign in which he led all running backs in snaps, routes, touches, targets, receptions, receiving yards, receiving touchdowns and fantasy points. McCaffrey's rushing efficiency wasn't great (3.86 yards per carry), and he's entering his age-30 season after handling 450 touches (including the playoffs) in 2025. The history of overworked backs suggests we should expect a step back in 2026, but CMC is a unicorn, and the combination of his skill set and hefty usage in Kyle Shanahan's offense suggests he can overcome history. There's obvious risk here, but McCaffrey will be an elite option whenever he's on the field.

profile_notes.subject: Christian McCaffrey
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Accept only with deliberate risk management in Round 1.
profile_notes.summary: McCaffrey has elite reward but one of the board's most dangerous lower-body-injury outcome ranges.
profile_notes.evidence: Josh says his lower-extremity injuries tend to cost six to eight games rather than one week, yet would rank him around second or third if assured 14 games; Harris still ranks him fifth overall and would take him at three in PPR.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both explicitly acknowledge the possible league-winning reward and agree that risk does not make a player undraftable.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft only if you consciously avoid piling further high-risk profiles onto the same roster.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Christian McCaffrey
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Check whether the muscle-tightness absence repeats during camp.
profile_notes.summary: McCaffrey's missed Monday practice is likely minor, but his injury history makes it worth tracking.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says McCaffrey sat with muscle tightness and calls it a literal nothing burger for most players; his strong guess is that it is also nothing for McCaffrey.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris expressly notes McCaffrey is oft-injured, so a repeated absence would carry more significance than the initial report.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not react to one missed practice, but recheck practice participation over the next several days.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: 49ers running-back handcuff
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not spend material draft capital attempting to identify Christian McCaffrey's backup from opaque August reports.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers have extremely low confidence that camp will identify a usable McCaffrey handcuff.
profile_notes.evidence: Jordan James logged only three regular-season offensive snaps; Kaelon Black was viewed as a reach, neither prospect has a McCaffrey-like receiving profile, and San Francisco does not disclose roles clearly.
profile_notes.counterweight: If a reserve is repeatedly reported to run the receiving playbook, that would matter, and managers with deep benches can cheaply stash both options.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Accept McCaffrey's unique injury risk rather than overpaying for a false certainty; use waivers or very late stashes if needed.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Taylor enters the 2026 season having improved in fantasy points per game in each of the past three years. Last season, he delivered his best production since his huge 2021 campaign, as he paced the NFL in carries and TDs while finishing second in carries inside the 5-yard line (19) and fourth in fantasy points. A piece of the step forward was increased usage in the passing game, as he ranked in the top 10 among backs in routes, targets, catches and receiving yards, setting career highs in each. Taylor's season likely would've been even better had QB Daniel Jones not been injured, as the running back averaged 24.8 points with Jones but 12.9 without him. Jones is expected to be ready to play in Week 1, so the 27-year-old Taylor is safe to value as a mid- to high-end RB1.

profile_notes.subject: Jonathan Taylor
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Account for recurring injury/workload risk at his premium ADP.
profile_notes.summary: Taylor's risk is mostly health and a high workload rather than an immediate threat to his role.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris calls him injury-risky but not risky for anything around him; Josh cites prior 11-, 10-, and 14-game seasons, workload, and negative Colts vibes after Jones left.
profile_notes.counterweight: Taylor was very good last year and received a new contract, preserving the lead-back case.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not treat Taylor as a risk-free RB1; pair him with more dependable profiles if selected early.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Jonathan Taylor
profile_notes.action_qualifier: If Jones has a meaningful setback, move from early-round pricing toward the middle of Round 2, not a total fade.
profile_notes.summary: Taylor remains a strong player, but the speakers agree a Jones absence would materially reduce his ceiling and force an ADP downgrade.
profile_notes.evidence: Kluge says Taylor was the top-scoring runner with Jones but only an RB3 without him; Harris agrees a delayed Jones return changes the entire Colts offense.
profile_notes.counterweight: Kluge would not drop Taylor near RB30 because workload remains valuable even in a poor environment.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not treat Taylor as unchanged if Jones cannot practice; lower him meaningfully while retaining him as a volume-based starter.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing AFC South & Almanac Stuff

outlook.text: The only player in NFL history with 90-plus catches in each of his first five NFL seasons, St. Brown continues to assert himself as one of the league's best players. The 2021 fourth-round pick has finished exactly third among receivers in fantasy points three seasons in a row, ranking no lower than fourth in catches, yards and touchdowns each year. St. Brown actually enjoyed a career-high target share in 2025 (31.6%), which helped him to 13 top-20 fantasy outings. The 26-year-old has no added target competition and remains Jared Goff's clear No. 1 target. He should be off the board in the first round of your draft.

profile_notes.subject: Amon-Ra St. Brown
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Safe premium WR selection.
profile_notes.summary: St. Brown is the safest fallback when an early drafter needs a receiver.
profile_notes.evidence: Josh calls him WR3 for three straight years and the safest pick available if stuck; Harris gives a 2.
profile_notes.counterweight: No specific risk case is offered in the episode.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use St. Brown as a stabilizing elite WR rather than searching for more speculative upside.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Amon-Ra St. Brown
profile_notes.action_qualifier: First-round receiver; no material camp adjustment is discussed.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers treat St. Brown as a first-round Lions anchor and the standard that prevents lazy Chicago-player comparisons.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Amon-Ra is better than the Bears receivers being cast into his role and, in the Lions discussion, both treat him as a first-round pick.
profile_notes.counterweight: No new health, role, or price concern is offered in the episode.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Maintain an elite-receiver valuation; do not use unrelated Ben Johnson camp narratives to change it.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Lamb is eyeing a bounceback season following a 2025 campaign in which he finished 12th among receivers in fantasy PPG � his worst finish since 2021. Lamb did go over 1,000 yards for the fifth season in a row, but he missed three games, led all receivers with eight drops and was unlucky in the TD department, having scored three touchdowns (6.6 expected) despite seeing 11 end zone targets. Lamb, 27, remains in his prime and he was fantasy's top-scoring receiver the last time he played a full season (2023). As long Dak Prescott is on the field with him, Lamb will be a solid fantasy WR1 with elite upside.

profile_notes.subject: CeeDee Lamb
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Prefer later in Round 1 or early Round 2 rather than ADP 10.
profile_notes.summary: Lamb's elite ceiling is real, but the speakers see too much injury, volatility, and price risk at this exact slot.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says 'it's always something' with injury or distraction and notes only one incredible season; Josh says later players make the price unattractive and doubts a huge touchdown total.
profile_notes.counterweight: Josh still expects a WR1 season, and Harris says Lamb belongs around the late first/early second in full PPR.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Let a small fall come to you rather than force Lamb at the top of his range.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Dallas Cowboys skill players
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ignore Cowboys camp hype absent injury or a genuine George Pickens hold-in.
profile_notes.summary: Dallas offers little camp information likely to change established fantasy evaluations.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris describes annual hype around Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, while Ciely says the relevant fantasy roles have little genuine competition. Pickens signed his tag and attended work despite a possible future contract dispute.
profile_notes.counterweight: A Pickens hold-in could hurt early games, and injuries or unavoidably negative reports would be meaningful.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Filter positive Cowboys clips out of draft decisions; only move players for material availability news.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Achane has quickly staked his claim as one of the best running backs in the league. The 2023 third-round pick has scored either 11 or 12 touchdowns in each of his three seasons and put up a career-high 1,838 scrimmage yards in 2025. Achane's elite receiving production is nothing new (he has finished in the top five among backs in targets and receiving yards in each of the past two years), but he made another leap forward as a rusher last season, finishing fifth at the position in rushing yards. His 5.62 yards per carry is best among qualified backs since he entered the league. The 24-year-old is eyeing his third straight top-five fantasy campaign, and while that might be tricky in an overhauled Miami offense led by quarterback Malik Willis, Achane has minimal competition for touches and should easily be the offensive centerpiece. He's a solid RB1 option.

profile_notes.subject: De'Von Achane
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Value near RB13 in standard and RB16 in PPR; monitor through Week 1.
profile_notes.summary: Harris lowers Achane because Miami's offensive competence and protection looked poor in consecutive joint-practice reports.
profile_notes.evidence: The derived account ties the move to repeated offensive struggles rather than a new judgment that Achane lacks talent.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris explicitly says this is not a bust call and acknowledges that a functional Miami offense would invalidate the downgrade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not force Achane as an RB1 target above the low-teens range, and reassess when real-game evidence clarifies Miami's offense.
profile_notes.episode_title: More Flag Players & Cousin Josh's Frag Players

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade associated players only if the offense proves at least competent.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers identify the possibility that Miami is merely mediocre rather than historically bad as a major assumption that could overturn rankings.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon points to under-the-radar line additions, Malik Willis's small-sample improvement, and the fact that Achane could lose roughly four points per game and still approach the cited price.
profile_notes.counterweight: Practice performance remains poor and neither speaker declares the offense fixed.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor quarterback and line competence; buy individual Dolphins only when their price assumes an unrealistically disastrous offense.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: De'Von Achane
profile_notes.action_qualifier: High-ceiling selection, but pair with safer players and reassess after negative camp signals.
profile_notes.summary: Achane's ceiling supports an early selection, but his health, projected workload, quarterback/receiving concerns, and bad-team risk are substantial.
profile_notes.evidence: Both score him 7; Harris says he could be awesome if everything works, while Josh worries about coach talk of extreme workload, the Dolphins' quality, a reduction from 80-90 to 50 catches, and a late-season shutdown if the team collapses.
profile_notes.counterweight: They have already seen Achane score and Harris still ranks him 10th overall; Josh ranks him 13th.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Take the upside only with intentional downside protection elsewhere and be ready to revise after camp/offense evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line and overall-environment reports before making broad Dolphins downgrades.
profile_notes.summary: Harris treats Washington's dominant joint-practice performance against Miami as a meaningful warning about the Dolphins' environment, but not a final verdict.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Washington reporters described Miami's offensive line as overrun throughout the drills and its defense as repeatedly beaten by Jayden Daniels.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris explicitly wants to see the issue again and look for improvement through the month; De'Von Achane also reportedly broke a third-down touchdown play.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the offensive-line concern in Dolphins player evaluations and seek confirming reports rather than automatically abandoning every Miami asset.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: De'Von Achane
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Soft fade near the Round 1/2 turn when Miami's quarterback, receiver room, coaching change, and scheme volatility are not discounted.
profile_notes.summary: Zachariason agrees Achane is clearly excellent on film but is more worried than Harris that Miami's environment has become too fragile to justify an aggressive fantasy price.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Achane's speed fits Mike McDaniel's system, but points to McDaniel's departure, a very poor receiver room, Malik Willis uncertainty, and prior stretches when Tua's concussion situation made the offense ineffective and diminished Achane's value.
profile_notes.counterweight: Zachariason explicitly rejects a no-draft stance: Achane has shown he is good beyond any one scheme, a mobile quarterback could help create running lanes, and he understands Harris's talent-over-situation argument.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Achane as a soft fade rather than an avoid; choose him only when his explosive talent appropriately offsets a wider range of offensive outcomes.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

profile_notes.subject: De'Von Achane
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris is comfortable around pick 10 overall, provided managers accept the small-back health tail risk and Miami's unknown floor.
profile_notes.summary: Harris reverses his earlier durability-based bust call and now calls Achane a Film Room Hero whose elite speed and quickness can overcome a bleak roster forecast.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris calls both traits A-plus, says Achane needs only a sliver of space to become a problem, and notes he has remained healthy so far despite previous fear that his size would lead to constant injuries.
profile_notes.counterweight: Achane can produce negative runs, the health sample remains small, and Miami has lost Tua Tagovailoa and Jaylen Waddle; Harris recognizes the team may be unable to support fantasy weapons.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Achane as a first-round talent bet instead of automatically fading the team context, while acknowledging that durability and offense failure remain material risks.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

profile_notes.subject: De'Von Achane
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Elite speed/elusiveness talent; no player-specific price stated.
profile_notes.summary: Achane remains an exceptional two-trait outlier in Harris's film grades.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris gives him an unchanged A-plus for speed and an unchanged A-plus for elusiveness, the latter shared only with McCaffrey in this discussion.
profile_notes.counterweight: No workload, health, or price discussion accompanies the grade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: The segment reinforces an elite talent assessment but does not itself create a new price-specific drafting directive.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: De'Von Achane
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Daugherty targets him at RB9-10 and argues RB5-6 talent; Harris remains wary of size/workload but accepts potential market value.
profile_notes.summary: Daugherty believes Achane is mispriced by fear of Miami's environment because the offense must run and his talent should still make him central; Harris sees a real downside but not certainty of collapse.
profile_notes.evidence: Daugherty argues no one else has meaningful ADP and Miami must lean on the run. Harris agrees that even a mediocre offense must score through someone and that the market can over-predict team failure.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris fears a small back taking more punishment in a bad offense, defensive attention to the edge, and an alternative runner such as Ollie Gordon stealing touchdowns.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Target Achane at the depressed RB9-10 range, but do not ignore his workload and environment tail risk.

outlook.text: After finishing in the top 10 among receivers in fantasy PPG during each of his first five seasons, Jefferson plummeted to 30th in 2025. The fall was, of course, unrelated to Jefferson's ability, as the team's quarterback woes limited the star receiver to career-low showings in yardage (1,048), touchdowns (two), catch rate (60%) and yards per target (7.4). Jefferson's fall came despite him seeing a career-high 30.1% target share and ranking in the top six at the position in targets (141) and end zone targets (15). The 27-year-old remains an elite player, but the quarterback concerns remain, with dual-threat Kyler Murray (one receiver managed a top-25 fantasy campaign during his time as a starter in Arizona) set to battle incumbent J.J. McCarthy for the team's starting job. Perhaps Murray can ignite Jefferson similar to how he did DeAndre Hopkins at times, but there's certainly some risk. Jefferson is best considered as a mid-range WR1.

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Justin Jefferson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Price in quarterback uncertainty despite elite talent.
profile_notes.summary: Jefferson's talent and production temper, but do not eliminate, the quarterback-driven risk.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris calls him risky because of what happened last year; Josh questions whether Kyler Murray is a savior but notes Jefferson has exceeded 1,400 yards in every full season except one.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both call him an extreme talent, and Josh reduces his original 6 to 5 after reconsidering the record.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Jefferson in the premium tier but do not ignore the quarterback outcome range when breaking close WR ties.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Justin Jefferson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris has him WR7 standard / WR6 PPR and will not take him in Round 1.
profile_notes.summary: Harris believes Jefferson remains one of football's two most talented receivers but cannot pay first-round cost given the quarterback setting.
profile_notes.evidence: He says the new quarterback is at least NFL quality compared with McCarthy, yet agrees the fit is stylistically poor and attributes some of last year's failure to an awful quarterback. He also cites 15 end-zone targets but only two touchdowns.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris wants elite historical players to rebound and ranks Jefferson only slightly below market rather than calling him a talent fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft only if he slips to a second-round price; do not let talent alone erase the quarterback and scoring-conversion uncertainty.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Justin Jefferson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Funston ranks him just outside his top 10, below the WR7 market.
profile_notes.summary: Funston downgrades Jefferson because he does not trust Kyler Murray to restore elite receiver production despite Jefferson's unquestioned talent.
profile_notes.evidence: Funston notes Jefferson was in the mid-20s at WR last season with poor J.J. McCarthy play and argues Murray's historical Arizona record has not elevated receivers, especially on Jefferson's timing-based routes.
profile_notes.counterweight: He still calls Jefferson great in a vacuum and expects him to be better than last season.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Let Jefferson fall below his market price instead of assuming the quarterback change fully solves the prior season.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not raise Jefferson from near his current ceiling on 'dialed in' Kyler Murray camp reports; downgrade only if doubts become sustained evidence.
profile_notes.summary: Richard sees Minnesota quarterback competence as an offense-wide variable for Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and the run game, but Harris sees mostly downside because Jefferson is already near ceiling.
profile_notes.evidence: Richard wants confirmation the quarterback competition is not real and that Murray outplays Minnesota's prior passers, which could force defenses deeper and improve the ecosystem.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both have heard optimistic Kyler camp narratives before and retain concerns about anticipation and inconsistency; Harris says the plausible adjustment is Jefferson falling toward WR12, not rising substantially.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid acting on generic camp praise; retain elite Jefferson pricing but watch for repeated evidence that Minnesota's passing environment is failing.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Justin Jefferson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris WR7/second round; Erickson has him 17th standard and 13th PPR, with further fall if Darrisaw is limited.
profile_notes.summary: Jefferson's talent still supports an early selection, but neither speaker will price him as if the 2025 quarterback/offense failure never happened.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris calls him perhaps the NFL's best overall player but says the season got worse as it went. Erickson says he would drop Jefferson to the middle of Round 2 if Darrisaw is not fully practicing.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Vikings spent the offseason seeking a solution and may force-feed their best player; Murray should be better than McCarthy.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Take Jefferson only at a tempered second-round valuation and monitor Darrisaw plus Murray rather than projecting an automatic elite rebound.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat all Vikings except Jefferson as non-starter-level drafts until Kyler Murray and line health prove functional.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers believe Minnesota's broken 2025 offense makes a Kyler Murray rescue uncertain, especially for secondary receivers.
profile_notes.evidence: They say J.J. McCarthy was not fine and the offense deteriorated; Murray is better but not automatically a panacea for Jefferson or Addison. Erickson identifies an injured/inconsistent Christian Darrisaw and center instability after Ryan Kelly's concussion-related retirement as major 2025 line failures.
profile_notes.counterweight: Minnesota changed quarterbacks and added linemen, and a coaching offseason could prioritize Jefferson successfully.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid treating secondary Vikings as automatic starters; demand a discount and monitor quarterback/line health rather than believing generic positive camp stories.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Cook signed a contract extension last offseason and was immediately vaulted into the biggest role of his career. The 2022 second-round NFL draft pick finished in the top five among backs in carries, rushing yards (league-high 1,621), touchdowns and yards per carry (5.25). The one limiting factor in Cook's fantasy output was a minimal receiving role (his 40 targets ranked 26th among RBs), but he still came through with a sixth-place finish in fantasy points. The 26-year-old is set to play the same role in Joe Brady's scheme and will be a candidate for his third straight double-digit touchdown campaign as long as Josh Allen is under center. Consider Cook a midrange RB1.

profile_notes.subject: James Cook
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Low-risk early RB at his stated ADP.
profile_notes.summary: Cook has less realized risk than his small build and running style might suggest.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says he should perhaps be riskier because of how small he is and how he runs, but that nothing scary has actually manifested; Josh also assigns 3.
profile_notes.counterweight: The size/style concern remains an acknowledged theoretical risk.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Cook as a comparatively safe early RB instead of preemptively fading him for body-type concerns.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: James Cook and Ray Davis
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draft Cook at first-round cost for talent, but do not assume Davis becomes a clean handcuff.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers like Cook but see no credible path to a clean Ray Davis inheritance because Allen and multiple complementary backs would likely create a committee.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris calls Cook durable and a transformed runner worthy of a first-round price, but notes his small build and Allen's ability to take goal-line scores. Daugherty expects Davis, Ty Johnson, and Allen usage to frustrate any handcuff.
profile_notes.counterweight: Davis's rookie film appealed to Harris, and a strong team declaration could change the view, but neither expects it.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Cook for his own production, not as a stack with presumed Davis insurance.
profile_notes.episode_title: Drake Maye & Josh Allen & Previewing AFC East

outlook.text: Love was selected by the Cardinals with the No. 3 overall pick of April's draft. Love has good size and terrific speed (4.36 40-yard dash) to go along with a three-down skill set. He led this year's rookie class in both yards per carry (6.66) and yards after contact (4.16) while ranking second in forced missed tackle rate (3.5) during his collegiate career. He's a capable receiver at all levels, a competent pass blocker and protects the ball well (one fumble on 496 career touches). Love will immediately slot in as Arizona's feature back and, especially considering each of the past nine running backs drafted in the top 12 went on to finish top 12 in fantasy points as a rookie, he should be valued as a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

profile_notes.subject: Jeremiyah Love
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Fade at the top of Round 3.
profile_notes.summary: Josh fades Love's price rather than his talent, arguing the market is assuming an immediate rookie breakout.
profile_notes.evidence: The cited risks are an already-dinged ankle, a difficult early schedule, and competition from Tyler Allgeier; Harris agrees the ADP reflects rookie-running-back enthusiasm.
profile_notes.counterweight: The talent case could still win if Love secures the role quickly and the offense exceeds expectations.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Let another manager pay for the best-case rookie outcome and reconsider only after a discount.
profile_notes.episode_title: More Flag Players & Cousin Josh's Frag Players

profile_notes.subject: Jeremiyah Love
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Value below the late-third-round market while recovering from the reported high-ankle sprain.
profile_notes.summary: Harris argues Love's market has not adjusted enough to the reported high-ankle sprain.
profile_notes.evidence: The ranking move reflects injury timing and the danger of paying an unaffected rookie premium.
profile_notes.counterweight: Love's talent and eventual role can still produce upside if recovery is faster than expected.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid reaching at the existing ADP and reconsider only after a discount or clearer recovery evidence.

profile_notes.subject: Jeremiyah Love
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Downgrade for redraft after the high-ankle sprain; reassess when his Week 1 availability and price are known.
profile_notes.summary: Harris lowers Love after the reported high-ankle sprain; Waldman still places his prospect talent around the Gibbs/Bijan tier, but sees a post-recovery committee path.
profile_notes.evidence: Love is expected to miss the rest of August and perhaps September; Tyler Allgeier has a credible screen, protection, and inside-running profile.
profile_notes.counterweight: Waldman thinks Love can eventually add volume at Allgeier's expense once healthy.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft him as if a healthy immediate bell cow; take the discount only after accounting for injury and early committee risk.

profile_notes.subject: Jeremiyah Love
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris will not draft a rookie RB in the first three rounds; he ranks Love 33rd overall.
profile_notes.summary: Love's Round-3 price is more palatable than prior rookie-RB extremes, but Harris still rejects it.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says he will recommend not indulging in Love, cites dislike of the team, and says he does not draft rookie RBs in the first three rounds; Josh says the ADP is a round above Harris's rank.
profile_notes.counterweight: Josh says the current price is far more palatable than the previous year's early Jeanty price, and Harris is not falling out of his chair over it.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Let Love slide past the first three rounds or choose established RB/WR alternatives.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Arizona Cardinals backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat Jeremiah Love as RB16 upside only if roster and usage clarity arrives; do not assume top-five draft capital mandates a massive workload.
profile_notes.summary: Harris makes Arizona's unresolved four-back camp hierarchy a key story because Love's ADP can be distorted both by rookie draft capital and pessimistic team projections; Richard sees a constrained environment.
profile_notes.evidence: The camp may end with only Love and Tyler Allgeier clearly relevant, or retain four bodies. Richard cites a hard schedule, weak line, first-year offense, and low team outlook; Harris cites historical splits involving Bijan Robinson/Allgeier and Gibbs/Montgomery.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris argues fantasy analysts routinely overstate certainty about bad teams, and a Conner or Benson trade could create immediate upside; Love is talented enough for hot-hand games.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor cuts, trades, joint practices, and ADP; draft Love only where a committee outcome is already discounted.

profile_notes.subject: Jeremiyah Love
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris has him RB17; monitor roster moves and role evidence, but resist a camp-driven jump into Round 2.
profile_notes.summary: Harris is willing to be relatively aggressive on Love because the market may over-discount Arizona, while Gretch agrees his draft investment makes him central to the future plan.
profile_notes.evidence: The discussion cites top-five draft capital and a roster with potential movement among James Conner, Tyler Allgeier, and Trey Benson; Harris identifies a possible camp path that makes Love's role obvious.
profile_notes.counterweight: Four competing backs, a tough schedule, and a broadly pessimistic offensive expectation limit certainty; Harris says Round-2 hype is possible but should not be assumed.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Love as a high-upside RB at the stated tier and reevaluate only if depth-chart changes create a clearer workload.

profile_notes.counterweight: The schedule and quarterback uncertainty can make running-back and passing-game efficiency difficult.

outlook.text: London enters his fifth NFL season with eyes on finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game for the third season in a row. The 2022 first-round pick broke out with a 100-1,271-9 receiving line and a fifth-place finish in fantasy points (14th PPG) in 2024. Last season, he missed five games and fell to 19th in fantasy points, but he was actually better on a per-game basis (seventh) and was the top scorer among receivers three times between Weeks 6 and 10. London remains heavily targeted (career 28% share) and sees plenty of work near the goal line (25 end zone targets over the past two seasons). As long as one of Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. can play somewhat competent ball, the 25-year-old London shouldn't have trouble providing fringe-WR1 fantasy production.

profile_notes.counterweight: Both say the volume is present when he plays and agree he is a WR1-quality player.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft London only if you can live with volatile weekly scoring and quarterback uncertainty.

profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor Michael Penix recovery versus Tua Tagovailoa starting; it affects Drake London/Kyle Pitts predictability more than Bijan Robinson's elite draft status.
profile_notes.summary: The Falcons' actionable camp fork is whether Penix can take first-team work and be ready Week 1 or whether Tua begins the season, with the quarterback mostly changing receiver/tight-end certainty.
profile_notes.evidence: McCormick prefers Tua's timing and predictability for London/Pitts, while Harris worries Tua should not be playing and might feel better if Penix wins. Both say Bijan's elite selection would not become a no-draft solely from Penix.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither option is a clean projection: Tua may be degraded, Penix's NFL competence is unproven, and the new coaching environment adds uncertainty.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track actual first-team recovery evidence; adjust passing-game players more readily than Bijan.

outlook.text: Jeanty is eyeing a leap forward in his second NFL season after an uneven rookie campaign in which the first-round pick enjoyed a ton of volume (seventh among backs in carries, targets and receptions) and played fairly well (eighth among RBs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF) but struggled to overcome the shaky Las Vegas offense. The good news is that the Raiders' offense should improve in 2026 with a better/healthier offensive line, a new coach in Super Bowl champion Klint Kubiak and a new quarterback in projected No. 1 NFL draft pick Fernando Mendoza. Jeanty has a clean path to a massive offensive role and is a strong bet for a leap forward. The 22-year-old is a midrange RB1 with elite upside.

profile_notes.subject: Ashton Jeanty
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Acceptable at market, but account for offense quality.
profile_notes.summary: Jeanty has a secure lead role, with risk concentrated in the quality of the offense.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says there is no threat to his primacy and Josh calls the workload phenomenal; Josh also references Tyler Linderbaum as encouraging offensive-line news.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both identify the offense, rather than player talent or role, as the unresolved downside.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Jeanty for role certainty while avoiding a projection that assumes an automatically strong offense.

profile_notes.subject: Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Jeanty is RB7-8 and Bowers is premium-priced despite Raiders environment; do not use positional talent to erase price risk.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers acknowledge Jeanty and Bowers as the Raiders' two clearly excellent players, but note that neither comes cheap in an offense most analysts dislike.
profile_notes.evidence: Behrens has Jeanty RB7 and Harris RB8, while both say Bowers is not a fit for their usual price-sensitive draft approach.
profile_notes.counterweight: Jeanty may be talented enough to overcome a weak environment, and evidence of a functional passing game could improve the outlook; Harris asks why the market treats the unproven Jeanty more favorably than established Achane.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not let known player quality override team and draft-cost risk; take them only if the actual market softens.

outlook.text: Rice enters Year 4 of his career still seeking his first full season as a starter. The 2023 second-round pick was sidelined for most of 2024 due to injury and missed nine games last season due to suspension (Weeks 1-6) and injury (Weeks 16-18). The good news is that Rice remained highly productive when active. He handled 9.8 targets per game and was a top-12 fantasy receiver in five of his eight outings in 2025. Rice is Patrick Mahomes' top target, and his 8.0 RAC is tops among qualified receivers over the past three seasons. Assuming Mahomes (ACL recovery) is ready to play early this season as expected, Rice will find himself in the WR1 mix.

profile_notes.subject: Rashee Rice
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Fade at WR12 or approximately pick 30.
profile_notes.summary: Josh calls Rice the strongest fade because the market price is driven by name recognition and proximity to Patrick Mahomes more than demonstrated ceiling.
profile_notes.evidence: He cites a very low average depth of target, no 1,000-yard season, legal/off-field uncertainty, and broader concern about Kansas City's passing offense; Harris agrees.
profile_notes.counterweight: A high-volume PPR role and a rebound by Mahomes remain the path to beating the fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Pass near pick 30 and select another receiver unless Rice falls far enough to absorb the role and legal risks.
profile_notes.episode_title: More Flag Players & Cousin Josh's Frag Players

profile_notes.subject: Rashee Rice
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Josh has him off his board at Round-3 ADP; Harris may lower his current WR14 PPR rank.
profile_notes.summary: Rice is too risky at a third-round price because the desired full-season role is still mostly projection amid legal and team-offense uncertainty.
profile_notes.evidence: Josh notes Rice has not exceeded 600 yards in either of the past two years, has legal uncertainty, and overlaps with Ken Walker's screen work; Harris adds that the Chiefs may no longer be the Chiefs offensively.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris still ranks Rice materially higher than Josh, though he says Josh's case may move his PPR rank down a few spots.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft Rice as if a 17-game breakout is established; wait for an appreciable fall or avoid the profile.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Rashee Rice
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris WR18 and Behrens WR12 depend more on health and off-field availability than ordinary camp football reports.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers agree that Rice's meaningful downgrade triggers are likely health or non-football/availability events, rather than a routine camp usage report.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says a beat report about goal-line practice would not be decisive and frames the risks as health and 'HOA' rather than ordinary football deployment.
profile_notes.counterweight: Wide receiver ranks are extremely flat, so WR12 versus WR18 is not necessarily a massive practical disagreement; actual missed time would be decisive.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor availability and legal/health developments, not superficial camp headlines, before moving Rice.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: McBride has emerged as one of the league's top pass catchers -- not just tight ends -- as he trails only Ja'Marr Chase in targets (317) and receptions (252) over the past two seasons and is sixth in receiving yards (2,385). McBride led the tight end position in every fantasy-relevant counting stat in 2025, and his league-high 15 top-12 fantasy weeks were six more than any other player at the position. He finished third in the NFL with 17 end zone targets. McBride really thrived when Jacoby Brissett (21.1 PPG) replaced Kyler Murray (12.5) under center, which only adds to his 2026 appeal. The 26-year-old should be on your radar at the first-/second-round turn.

profile_notes.subject: Trey McBride
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid the premium early tight-end build despite elite talent.
profile_notes.summary: McBride receives the same premium-tight-end risk treatment as Bowers.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says he does not like the quarterback; both explain that they love the players but dislike a strategy that forces catch-up at RB and WR.
profile_notes.counterweight: The issue is not McBride's talent, and Josh says a prior early McBride selection did work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Favor RB/WR at the price and wait for a later TE unless intentionally choosing the structural tradeoff.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Cardinals quarterback situation
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Prefer Jacoby Brissett stability for Cardinals pass-catcher volume; lower expectations if Carson Beck earns substantial early work.
profile_notes.summary: Gretch treats the Brissett-versus-Beck outcome as central to Arizona receiver/tight-end volume, while Harris agrees the rookie quarterback would be less exciting.
profile_notes.evidence: Gretch says Brissett's quick release and willingness to throw generated huge target volume, including Wilson's 18-target game and two 15-target games, whereas young quarterbacks can hold the ball and take sacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: A new offense could change deployment regardless of starter, and the transcript does not declare either quarterback the confirmed season-long choice.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use camp/preseason quarterback evidence to refine Cardinals pass-catcher projections rather than treating last year's targets as automatic.

outlook.text: Hampton is primed for a breakout second season following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie campaign. The first-round pick was busy during nine appearances, averaging 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets. He scored five touchdowns, averaged 15.1 fantasy points per game (13th best) and ranked third among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF. With Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell as his primary competition, Hampton has a clear path to lead rusher duties in 2026, and his targets only figure to increase with Greg Roman out and Mike McDaniel in as the team's playcaller. Add in a much-improved offensive line with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back healthy, and Hampton has nothing short of elite upside. Value him as a fringe RB1 with room for much more.

profile_notes.subject: Omarion Hampton
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid at an early-second-round cost.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers consider Hampton too expensive because the market assumes a bell-cow role that the player evaluation and backfield design do not support.
profile_notes.evidence: Kluge cites poor college-to-pro film traits, while the expected Keaton Mitchell speed and passing-down role creates meaningful competition.
profile_notes.counterweight: Hampton can still produce if he wins more work than expected or the offense creates abundant scoring opportunities.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Pass at the premium and reconsider only after the price reflects a genuine timeshare.
profile_notes.episode_title: Five ADP Surprises Plus More Injuries

profile_notes.subject: Omarion Hampton
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid at ADP 17; Harris ranks him roughly 34th overall.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers can see Hampton's upside but view the current price as too aggressive for an unproven and injured player in an uncertain committee/offense setup.
profile_notes.evidence: Josh cites a small sample, a prior injury, Keaton Mitchell and other backfield competition, and uncertain usage; Harris says a strong Chargers offense and a better Hampton could validate the bet but sees no sure thing.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both acknowledge the favorable scenario could make the ranking defensible, and Josh labels the risk 6 rather than an extreme score.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Pass at the cited ADP and seek him only after a major discount or stronger role evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Omarion Hampton
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris is out at top-10 RB ADP, though he recognizes the upside.
profile_notes.summary: Harris understands Hampton's size-speed upside but does not view his film or role as deserving top-10 RB certainty.
profile_notes.evidence: He calls Hampton a big, fast player but questions his wiggle, compares the style to a faster Tyler Allgeier/Tevin Coleman type, and says virtually every NFL backfield is a platoon. He notes Hampton had limited usable tape after both tackles were lost and he was injured.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris says a scheme upgrade and more healthy tape could reveal new traits, and he admits Hampton could become RB3 and prove him wrong.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Choose a more proven elite back at this price; revisit Hampton only when the market builds in his shared-workload and evaluation risk.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Omarion Hampton
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Funston fades a top-10 RB price because a three-back role can limit volume.
profile_notes.summary: Funston sees Hampton as the episode's archetypal swing player because drafters assume featured-back usage that the new environment may not deliver.
profile_notes.evidence: He questions whether prior passing-game utility will persist, notes a healthier line could change Herbert's checkdown behavior, and cites Keith Mitchell, Kimani Vidal, and Mike McDaniel's indication of frequent three-headed usage.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense may improve under McDaniel, the line may be better, and Hampton's big-game path is clear.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Fade Hampton at bell-cow pricing and do not assume the passing work or dominant snap share follows him into the new setup.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not assume a healthy or cohesive unit until tackle and interior questions are answered.
profile_notes.summary: The Chargers could benefit from an offensive-line-friendly McDaniel system, but Tucker sees legitimate uncertainty at every starting position.
profile_notes.evidence: Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt are returning from major injuries; Tucker questions center Tyler Biadasz's recovery, Jake Slaughter's shift from Florida center to left guard, and Cole Strange's fit after New England. Harris notes Alt was not fully participating when camp opened.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Shanahan-McVay tree can aid blockers, and all questions can resolve favorably.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor training-camp participation and interior cohesion before assigning a strong line-driven boost to Chargers skill players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Omarion Hampton
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Fade at second-round cost because the market leaves little downside, while retaining him as the Chargers' most valuable back.
profile_notes.summary: Both rank Hampton as the Chargers' most valuable runner but believe his second-round market assumes too much of a healthy, efficient offense and near-ceiling role.
profile_notes.evidence: They describe an upside story where protected Herbert and healthy tackles create easy rushing lanes and a dozen touchdowns; that path validates the cost only if several team conditions occur.
profile_notes.counterweight: Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal can take work, and the Chargers' health profile makes the bullish environment uncertain.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Hampton only after price builds in committee and environment risk; do not treat a lower rank as a claim Mitchell is the better asset.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target discounted Chargers pieces only on the conditional thesis of healthy line, protected Herbert, and a real offensive jump.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers can imagine a Chargers offense becoming a fantasy answer if health and protection finally cooperate, but view it as a conditional upside case rather than baseline.
profile_notes.evidence: Behrens says a healthy line and protected Justin Herbert could unlock a 28-30-point offense; Harris gives Herbert a mulligan and ties McConkey's rebound to the same factors.
profile_notes.counterweight: It requires unusually good Chargers injury luck, and the team has frequently failed to meet that sort of optimistic offensive projection.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the upside scenario as a tiebreaker for discounted Chargers, not as permission to erase downside.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Barkley is looking to rebound in his ninth NFL season (third with the Eagles) following a big step back in 2025. After producing 2,283 yards and 15 touchdowns on 378 touches in his first season with Philly, Barkley dipped to 1,413 yards and nine scores on 317 touches in 2025. Barkley fell from first among backs in fantasy points per game (22.5) to 15th (14.5). Now 29 years old, it's possible Barkley's best days are behind him, but he's still positioned as a clear feature back in a good offense that will have a healthier line and a new playcaller in Sean Mannion. Barkley is riskier than ever, but he's still worthy of mid- to back-end RB1 consideration.

profile_notes.subject: Saquon Barkley
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Accept at the end of Round 1 while acknowledging a rebuilt offense and age risk.
profile_notes.summary: Barkley remains usable at an end-of-first cost, but is no longer the near-riskless profile they saw a year earlier.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris points to age approaching 30, a rebuilt offense, and a difficult prior season behind unblocked bodies; Josh adds lost explosive-run production, no Lane Johnson, no A.J. Brown, and a new offensive coordinator.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both say they are comfortable at the end of Round 1, and Josh emphasizes he is not merely grading the ADP.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Barkley only as a slightly fragile early foundation, not as an automatic safe RB selection.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade offense and Saquon Barkley context if interior health holds in the new scheme.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker believes Philadelphia has a high ceiling and high floor because last year's underperformance was substantially injury-driven and the new system should help blockers.
profile_notes.evidence: Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson fought through multiple injuries, surgeries, and rehabilitation; Lane Johnson missed the second half with plantar fasciitis. Tucker says the new coordinator's increased play action avoids isolating tackles in straight dropbacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: The line did not play as a top-five unit last year, and the recovery of injured interior starters must persist.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat a healthy Eagles line as a positive contextual upgrade for Barkley and the offense rather than anchoring on last year's unit ranking.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Keep outside the small trusted-offense tier until the new Mannion system succeeds in games.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers refuse to restore Philadelphia to an automatic top-offense projection after last year's collapse and coordinator replacement.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites A.J. Brown's trade, questions around the line, and the team's decision to replace the coordinator despite prior Super Bowl success. Ciely believes Mannion's changes can help but says practice and preseason cannot prove a top-five result.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense has Jalen Hurts, a strong history, and a scheme that could improve play action/middle-field work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid building draft projections on an assumed Eagles bounce-back; wait for regular-season evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Henry continues to defy the odds, playing at a high level despite now entering his age-32 season. In 2025, he finished exactly second in the NFL in rushing yards for the fourth season in a row, and his 24 carries inside the 5-yard line were easily the most in the league. Henry leads the NFL in carries inside the 5-yard line (42) and is second in touchdowns (34) since joining Baltimore prior to the 2024 season, and he hasn't finished lower than eighth among RBs in touchdowns since 2017. Henry continues to run at a high level (his 5.20 yards per carry last season ranked fifth among qualified backs), but he's still a nonfactor as a receiver (outside the top 45 backs in targets, catches and yards last season). He remains a featured rusher in a terrific offense and is well positioned for his fifth consecutive top-eight fantasy campaign.

profile_notes.subject: Derrick Henry
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Preferred over Omarion Hampton even in PPR.
profile_notes.summary: Despite age, Henry is a low-risk early RB relative to surrounding alternatives because the speakers have not seen a meaningful decline.
profile_notes.evidence: Josh calls him a rare running back whose decline has not appeared and doubts it will come suddenly; Harris agrees and would select Henry over Hampton even in PPR.
profile_notes.counterweight: Age remains the obvious risk and Henry does not offer Hampton's reception upside.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Favor Henry when choosing between the two; do not overreact to age without evidence of decline.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Baltimore Ravens offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor the three new interior pieces and tackle performance before assuming a strong rushing environment.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker sees Baltimore's changed interior and new under-center offense as a significant continuity risk despite potential upside.
profile_notes.evidence: He names injured-center returnee Ethan Pocic, returning Simpson, and first-round Penn State guard Vega Ioane as a substantially remade interior, while noting the rookie may switch sides. He also says neither Ronnie Stanley nor Roger Rosengarten met expectations last year.
profile_notes.counterweight: If the interior questions resolve positively, Tucker says the line could be good; Derrick Henry remains a rare durability/production outlier.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the interior transition in the downside range for Ravens runners and passing-game projections rather than presuming past line quality.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

outlook.text: Brown is entering his fourth NFL season and third as Cincinnati's lead back. His 2025 season got off to a rocky start (10.1 fantasy points per game and one touchdown during his first seven games), but it turned around drastically down the stretch (21.2 points per game and 10 TDs during his final 10 games). The improvement coincided with Cincinnati's improved QB play, which should continue into 2026 with a healthy Joe Burrow. Brown has yet to finish a season higher than 16th in carries or rushing yards, but he has scored exactly 11 TDs and has finished fifth in receptions in each of the past two years, both of which have resulted in top-10 fantasy campaigns. The 26-year-old once again has minimal competition for touches in a very good Bengals offense. He's best valued as a fringe RB1.

profile_notes.subject: Chase Brown
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris is priced out at ADP 14; Josh considers that price appropriate.
profile_notes.summary: Brown is safe enough as a player, but Harris finds the current cost too high while Josh does not.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris calls Brown very good but says ADP 14 is above any price he would pay; Josh calls him one of the safer picks and says that is where he belongs.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris still ranks him in his top 20 and does not call the ADP absurd.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Brown only if you share Josh's price view; otherwise select the receivers Harris prefers ahead of him.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Chase Brown
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Second-round consideration, though Harris does not call him a first-round/transcendent RB and conditions the bet on Bengals offense health.
profile_notes.summary: Zachariason and Harris both see Brown as a legitimately good, decisive runner and unusually natural receiver rather than a Day 3 illusion.
profile_notes.evidence: Zachariason says Brown takes blocked yards plus more, finishes runs, has enough explosiveness, and catches smoothly; both attribute his slow start to Joe Burrow's absence and improve the picture once the offense did.
profile_notes.counterweight: Zachariason says he can be too decisive and is not an elite tackle-breaker; Harris says a truly transcendent back would have carried a collapsing offense better.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Target Brown as a strong RB1/2 when the cost reflects offense dependence, not as a player immune to quarterback deterioration.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

profile_notes.subject: Chase Brown
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target more aggressively if another capable back lowers his ADP without erasing Brown's lead role.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers like Brown but believe a competent complementary back could make his price safer rather than destroy his fantasy case.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris frames the choice as extreme workload upside versus durability risk for a smaller runner; Harmon says Brown would benefit from a better second back and expects the Bengals offense to improve.
profile_notes.counterweight: A trade for a player such as James Conner would narrow Brown's path to an RB4-type overall ceiling, and current backups remain unsettled.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not overreact to a complementary-back addition; reassess Brown as a potentially better-priced lead-back investment.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: Cincinnati Bengals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not change elite-player ranks on camp drills; monitor credible evidence of more under-center and modern-concept usage.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers regard Cincinnati's core as settled and already elite, with offensive evolution as a possible path from top-five to No. 1 production.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon wants to see Joe Burrow under center more and the offense move beyond an almost exclusively shotgun approach; he notes incremental increases in Chase motion and varied alignment.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harmon repeatedly says camp talk will not force rank changes for Burrow, Chase, Higgins, or Brown, and the preference may remain Burrow's existing style.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat schematic reports as upside context, not a reason to chase already-expensive Bengals players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Walker signed with the Chiefs after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Seahawks. The reigning Super Bowl MVP and PFF's highest-graded running back from 2025, Walker is poised for feature-back duties in a good, Andy Reid-led offense.
