Having worked in a committee most of last season, Walker was limited to only five touchdowns and 11.3 fantasy points per game (both career lows), but he still generated 252 touches and a career-high 1,309 yards. He has yet to finish a season better than 18th in fantasy points (12th on a per-game basis) and has missed at least two games in three of four seasons in the league, but the 25-year-old's ability to contribute at a high level as a rusher and receiver is enough to position him as, at least, a solid fantasy RB2 in 2026.

profile_notes.subject: Kenneth Walker
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not assume a team change resolves his injury and offense risk.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Walker as a legitimate but clearly riskier early pick because the optimistic projection assumes several unproven things go right.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites repeated lower-body absences and questions whether the Chiefs offense will be good; Josh agrees Walker has been hurt in every season, though he is more optimistic about the talent.
profile_notes.counterweight: Josh says Walker is a very good player and believes a productive season could happen.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not use a team-change narrative as the primary justification for an aggressive price; draft only with meaningful health/offense downside budgeted.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Kenneth Walker III
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris will not pay a top-15/end-of-Round-1-to-early-Round-2 type price.
profile_notes.summary: Harris likes Walker's talent but rejects the premium market that assumes a great Chiefs offense, full Patrick Mahomes mobility, and a large receiving role.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Kansas City is not a top-five and perhaps not a top-10 offense, while Mahomes is returning from an ACL tear. Josh notes Walker's lower-body history and says the projected 60-catch season is a familiar offseason story rather than established usage.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both call Walker explosive and capable; Josh thinks he can catch more than he did in Seattle, especially in standard formats.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Pass at an elite-RB price and require a discount that reflects offense, health, and receiving-volume uncertainty.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

outlook.text: Jacobs' 2025 season can be split in two parts: pre-injury and post-injury. While healthy during his first nine games, Jacobs picked up where he left off from a terrific 2024 debut season with Green Bay, averaging 21.1 touches and 19.6 fantasy points while scoring 11 TDs. After missing all but 11 snaps during Weeks 11 and 12, Jacobs returned and wasn't quite the same, averaging 14.6 touches and 11.3 points while totaling three touchdowns in his final five games. But Jacobs, 28, was still effective overall (PFF's fourth-highest-graded back) and has a clear grasp on lead-back duties in a good Green Bay offense that has afforded him 30 touchdowns (fifth most in the NFL) in 32 games. He's a fine back-end RB1, but a potential suspension makes him less valuable on draft day.

profile_notes.subject: Josh Jacobs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris is comfortable being out while the groin injury and possible suspension remain unresolved.
profile_notes.summary: Jacobs's availability outlook is too uncertain to support Harris's usual above-market enthusiasm.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites possible suspension, last year's injury after heavy usage, a groin injury expected to cost a significant portion of training camp, and the chance the team reduces workload.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris's ranks are not far below market, and Josh's 7 recognizes a risky but not unusable player.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Let other drafters assume a clean return; revisit only after health and availability information improve.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Josh Jacobs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draftable around RB13/Rounds 3-4 only while accepting unresolved suspension risk.
profile_notes.summary: Jacobs is an RB1 whenever he plays, but the unresolved legal case makes the season-long investment psychologically and strategically difficult.
profile_notes.evidence: Josh says Green Bay has not changed the role that produced an RB1 season and would pair Jacobs with Gibbs or Bijan. Harris says the issue is the constant possibility of a suspension rather than a decline in his game.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris and Josh infer that absent a new high-visibility development, NFL discipline may arrive after this season; this is their actuarial speculation, not a prediction of case outcome.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Take Jacobs only if the active-week RB1 value offsets your tolerance for legal/availability uncertainty; monitor news throughout the season.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

profile_notes.subject: Josh Jacobs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor charges or suspension developments; active-week role remains RB1-caliber.
profile_notes.summary: Jacobs's on-field role is valuable, but an unresolved legal/suspension possibility must remain in the draft downside.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says charges filed before Labor Day would increase suspension probability, although a suspension could arrive in 2027 instead. Erickson says the looming issue should direct attention to Green Bay's other backs, while both call Jacobs a really good player if active.
profile_notes.counterweight: They do not claim to know legal outcomes or timing, and the prior county decision reportedly did not file assault charges after the alleged incident.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft only after consciously pricing availability risk and follow official legal/league news rather than speculative camp signals.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Bowers entered 2025 with high expectations and appeared well on his way to another productive season with 103 yards in Week 1, but a late-game injury limited him for three weeks and led to five full missed games. Bowers remained productive when healthy, finishing second among tight ends in fantasy PPG. Incredibly, he tied for fifth in the NFL with 13 end zone targets despite all the missed action. Bowers, who posted a 112-1,194-5 receiving line as a rookie in 2024, will be the top target for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. The 23-year-old is well positioned for a highly productive season and should be on your radar in the second or third round.

profile_notes.subject: Brock Bowers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid the mid-to-late Round-2 tight-end price.
profile_notes.summary: Bowers is talented, but both speakers reject his price because player and build risk compound.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris remains uneasy about Chip Kelly and Geno Smith and notes Bowers was injured/hobbled for half the prior year; both say they will not roster him at this ADP.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris reduced Bowers from an 8 risk score the previous year to 6, and Josh gives only a 5.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the pick on RB/WR and take a later tight end rather than paying Bowers's premium.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Jeanty is RB7-8 and Bowers is premium-priced despite Raiders environment; do not use positional talent to erase price risk.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers acknowledge Jeanty and Bowers as the Raiders' two clearly excellent players, but note that neither comes cheap in an offense most analysts dislike.
profile_notes.evidence: Behrens has Jeanty RB7 and Harris RB8, while both say Bowers is not a fit for their usual price-sensitive draft approach.
profile_notes.counterweight: Jeanty may be talented enough to overcome a weak environment, and evidence of a functional passing game could improve the outlook; Harris asks why the market treats the unproven Jeanty more favorably than established Achane.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not let known player quality override team and draft-cost risk; take them only if the actual market softens.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

profile_notes.subject: Las Vegas Raiders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round receiver watch only if a receiver hierarchy emerges and Fernando Mendoza threatens Kirk Cousins for the starting job.
profile_notes.summary: Both see Las Vegas as a useful camp watch because an inexpensive receiver could become relevant if the passing game is better than assumed and a quarterback competition changes the outlook.
profile_notes.evidence: The Raiders publicly prefer Cousins to start the season, but a strong camp/preseason from first-overall-pick Mendoza could force a conversation. Harris says nobody is entitled to a role and wants to identify a clear winner such as Trey Tucker or Jalen Naylor.
profile_notes.counterweight: Brock Bowers is the primary target, the offense is widely expected to be poor, and Harris doubts Naylor's speed/film despite repeated organizational praise.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Follow the receiver and QB hierarchy for a cheap final-round target, but do not rely on a Raiders passer in standard one-QB leagues.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Collins heads into his sixth NFL campaign yet to play a full 17-game season, but having been very productive when on the field. The 2021 third-round pick has cleared 1,000 yards and scored either seven or eight touchdowns each of the past three seasons, finishing in the top 10 in fantasy PPG and top 12 in yards per route run in all three. A force near the goal line, Collins ranked fourth among receivers with 13 end zone targets in 2025. The 27-year-old's target share doesn't stack up with other top receivers (he has never cleared 24.4%), but his high-end efficiency is just enough to keep him in the back-end WR1 mix.

profile_notes.subject: Nico Collins
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Price in injury, quarterback, and boom-bust weekly risk.
profile_notes.summary: Collins is an exceptional physical receiver whose health and offensive setting cause a volatile projection.
profile_notes.evidence: Josh calls him a six-foot-four freak and cites concussions/lower-hamstring problems plus skepticism about Stroud and Houston; Harris says he is often hurt and can alternate 130-yard games with eight-yard duds.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both clearly love the talent, and Josh's 4 is lower than Harris's 5.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Collins for ceiling but plan around wide weekly swings and injury downside.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Nico Collins
profile_notes.action_qualifier: High-end WR1 consideration around Harris WR5 and Zachariason WR9, while accepting Houston's target competition and quarterback uncertainty.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers regard Collins as a complete elite-caliber receiver rather than merely a contested-catch X, with clear growth through his NFL career.
profile_notes.evidence: Zachariason highlights immediate release separation, sustained speed, physical YAC, and improvement from a raw player; Harris adds better hands, routes, elusiveness, and a role that is central rather than sacrificial.
profile_notes.counterweight: Houston's quarterback, Jaden Higgins, Jaylin Noel, and a possible healthy Tank Dell constrain certainty, so the projection is not a guaranteed 1,600-yard season.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Pay a high-end receiver cost when comfortable with Houston's volume risk, because the film supports a true WR1 outcome.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

profile_notes.subject: Houston Texans offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Downgrade Texans skill players only if repeated padded-practice and controlled-scrimmage failures show the line cannot gel.
profile_notes.summary: Richard calls persistent Houston line instability a medium red flag for the offense, while Harris asks what concrete camp evidence would justify changing player ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: Reports had Houston changing lineups daily and struggling to gel; Richard says his current skill-position ranks are optimistic relative to that risk.
profile_notes.counterweight: Preseason games are less useful than controlled scrimmages, and teams can solve line combinations as Chicago did the prior year.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track repeated protection failures in meaningful practice settings before discounting Houston's fantasy assets.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

outlook.text: Wilson is eyeing a bounce-back following an injury-shortened 2025 that limited him to seven games. It was the first time Wilson had missed time, having appeared in all 51 games during his first three seasons. The 2022 first-round pick ranked no lower than sixth among receivers in targets in each of those years, but he failed to produce a fantasy campaign better than 20th (PPG) due to New York's quarterback woes. Wilson was off to a hot start last season (four TDs, 14.2 fantasy PPG) thanks to a massive 33% target share (second highest). New York's signal-caller problems still aren't completely solved, but veteran Geno Smith should provide an upgrade over last year's Justin Fields/Tyrod Taylor duo. Wilson, 26, is one of the best raw talents at the position and should be valued as a good WR2.

profile_notes.subject: Garrett Wilson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid top-20 WR/third-round price despite route talent until Geno Smith and Frank Reich prove a viable Jets passing environment.
profile_notes.summary: Both refuse to pay Garrett Wilson's premium price because the upside argument asks them to trust Geno Smith and Frank Reich after repeated Jets failures.
profile_notes.evidence: They acknowledge Wilson as a precise route runner who has suffered a tragic Jets context, but Daugherty calls Smith's prior-season quarterback play horrific and sees no elite staff mechanism to rescue it.
profile_notes.counterweight: Wilson is talented and Geno has had good moments; the Jets have upgraded line/quarterback stability relative to Miami in market perception.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Let others buy the rescue narrative and use later Jets receivers for cheap exposure instead.
profile_notes.episode_title: Drake Maye & Josh Allen & Previewing AFC East

outlook.text: Brown was traded to the Patriots in June. The veteran receiver enters 2026 looking to continue his streak of finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game during each of the four seasons he was with the Eagles. That includes an 11th-place finish in 2025 in which Brown reached the 1,000-yard mark for the sixth time in his seven NFL seasons while finding the end zone exactly seven times for the third year in a row. Brown continues to benefit from elite usage (he has finished no lower than seventh among WRs in target share each of the past seven seasons) and elite efficiency (he has finished 80th percentile or better in yards per route run all seven years). He could use more end zone targets in New England (he had a career-low four last season), but Brown, 29, is set to work as Drake Maye's top target in a good Patriots' offense. He is a fringe fantasy WR1.

profile_notes.subject: A.J. Brown
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Josh would select him at this fair-ish early price; Harris assigns a lower risk score but flags the knee.
profile_notes.summary: Josh sees elite-season upside after a change of scenery, while Harris's more modest risk score still centers on knee concerns.
profile_notes.evidence: Josh believes Brown gets the best quarterback of his career and notes a 24-to-1 touchdown wager; Harris identifies the knee as the main risk while agreeing the new situation should be better.
profile_notes.counterweight: Josh also recognizes lower separation/yard-per-route-run indicators and that Brown may no longer turn short slants into long gains.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Brown is a playable premium WR if you accept knee risk, with Josh materially more optimistic about the ceiling.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

outlook.text: Olave is fresh off a career year in which he reached new highs in targets (156), receptions (100), yardage (1,163) and touchdowns (nine). He finished eighth among receivers in fantasy PPG, which beat out his previous career best of 19th in 2023. Olave finished no lower than seventh among receivers in nearly every counting stat, including end zone targets (12) and air yards (1,816). The big season was a sigh of relief after a 2024 campaign riddled with concussions, and it positions the 26-year-old right back in the fringe-WR1 discussion. Especially with No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson expected to miss a month or two with a hamstring injury, Olave will remain Tyler Shough's top target, and that sets him up for another highly productive campaign.

profile_notes.subject: Chris Olave
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Hold at WR24 rather than chasing him upward after Jordyn Tyson's injury.
profile_notes.summary: Harris does not automatically upgrade Olave after Tyson's injury because target consolidation can be offset by defenses respecting the remaining passing game less.
profile_notes.evidence: The analysis balances increased target availability against a potentially weaker overall offensive environment.
profile_notes.counterweight: Olave could still benefit if the offense maintains efficiency despite losing Tyson.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Maintain the existing ranking and avoid paying an injury-driven premium.
profile_notes.episode_title: Five ADP Surprises Plus More Injuries

profile_notes.subject: Chris Olave
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draftable in Round 3 only with concussion risk explicitly accepted.
profile_notes.summary: Olave is a high-end talent with a manageable but real concussion-risk profile.
profile_notes.evidence: Both score him 4 and identify concussions as the issue; Harris calls him exceptional when active, while Josh notes a doubled touchdown total could restore early-third-round value.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither speaker identifies a major role or talent concern beyond the concussion history.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Select Olave for skill and upside only if your roster can absorb medical volatility.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

outlook.text: Pickens drew the franchise tag from Dallas after a career year in which he ranked near the top of the wide receiver position in most categories, including catches, yards, TDs, end zone targets (second with 18) and air yards (fourth with 1,576). Fantasy's No. 5-scoring receiver in 2025 certainly benefited from CeeDee Lamb missing time (24% target share, or 8.8 per game, and 24.2 fantasy PPG in four games Lamb was injured), but his "with Lamb" splits were also strong. Consider: In 12 full games with Lamb, Pickens handled a 23% target share (8.3 per game) and averaged 16.1 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth at the position over the full season. The 25-year-old will play the same role in Dallas' high-scoring offense in 2026 and has the look of a strong fantasy WR2.

profile_notes.subject: George Pickens
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris accepts ADP 24 only with an upside-oriented build; Josh is more willing at the price.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Pickens as a volatile bet whose cost is close to fair but whose behavior and two-receiver offense assumptions create major failure paths; Josh has more personal optimism.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris flags the possibility that Pickens 'goes off the reservation' and questions whether two receivers on the same offense can both justify top-12 WR pricing; Josh recalls a game in which Pickens did not try but thinks contract motivation helps.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris ranks Pickens only two spots below the live ADP and says he is not anti-ADP; Josh is willing to ride the player.
profile_notes.practical_implication: If drafting Pickens near market, ensure the rest of the build can absorb major volatility rather than treating him as a safe WR2.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: George Pickens
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris ranks him WR13 and prefers a clearer team alpha at top-10 WR cost.
profile_notes.summary: Pickens has a concentrated-target offense and top-end fantasy path, but both speakers question whether he can be drafted as a top-10 receiver while competing with CeeDee Lamb.
profile_notes.evidence: Funston says on-field opportunity favored Lamb and that it is hard to select a team's No. 2 receiver that high, though both should have targets. Harris says some post-injury games featured Pickens and that he cannot know September's target leader.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris is not certain Lamb stays clearly ahead and has Pickens WR13 because the broader WR tier thins out; Funston expects a large enough passing pie for both.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Prefer a clearer alpha at the premium price; if drafting Pickens, accept competition, team-plan, and behavioral volatility.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Dallas Cowboys skill players
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ignore Cowboys camp hype absent injury or a genuine George Pickens hold-in.
profile_notes.summary: Dallas offers little camp information likely to change established fantasy evaluations.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris describes annual hype around Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, while Ciely says the relevant fantasy roles have little genuine competition. Pickens signed his tag and attended work despite a possible future contract dispute.
profile_notes.counterweight: A Pickens hold-in could hurt early games, and injuries or unavoidably negative reports would be meaningful.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Filter positive Cowboys clips out of draft decisions; only move players for material availability news.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Hall received the franchise tag during the offseason and will return for his fifth season with the Jets. Having worked in the Jets' underwhelming offenses the past two years, Hall has struggled to finishes of 17th and 21st in fantasy points per game among RBs, which is a far cry from top-eight finishes during his first two seasons. Hall has remained busy, however, producing 266-plus touches each of the past three seasons. The 2022 second-round pick saw a dip in receiving work in 2025 (career-low 10% target share) but finished fourth in that category in both 2023 and 2024, so a rebound is possible with pocket QB Geno Smith now under center. Though the Jets' offense might continue to limit Hall's upside, the 25-year-old's combination of workload and talent positions him as a solid RB2.

profile_notes.subject: Breece Hall
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Move from a late-second-round RB13 valuation to RB16 in the middle/late third.
profile_notes.summary: Harris lowers Hall because a groin issue that expands into a multi-week absence creates meaningful recurrence risk.
profile_notes.evidence: The downgrade is driven by duration and reinjury probability rather than a changed talent evaluation.
profile_notes.counterweight: Hall can recover fully, and the derived source does not establish his regular-season availability.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not pay the pre-injury price; recheck health before the draft and buy only after the market reflects the risk.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Breece Hall
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Favorite ADP value at 34, but only with extreme offense/role risk accepted.
profile_notes.summary: Hall is a major third-round bargain for both speakers, but the bargain exists because the Jets offense and late-season workload outcome could be ugly.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris calls it his favorite ADP and says he would select Hall far earlier; Josh sees a 20-pick discount from Achane and cites past 60-70-catch ability.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both score the risk high because the team could be poor, Geno Smith has not looked good, and a 2-10 season could reduce Hall's usefulness even without a major injury.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Take Hall if he lasts to this value, but build as though team context can cause volatile weekly and late-season outcomes.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Breece Hall
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris ranks RB13 and Josh RB14, but both require faith in a better Jets offense.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers love Hall's ability and can draft him around RB13-14, but feel queasy because the payoff requires the Jets to function better with Geno Smith.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris calls Hall fast, elusive, strong, a capable goal-line back, and a very good receiver; he notes 1,400 scrimmage yards despite an RB18 finish caused largely by too few touchdowns. Josh says a rebound toward 80 targets and 55-60 catches could easily restore value.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Jets were poor last season, Geno Smith is not an automatic solution, and Hall did not create the hoped-for outcome one year younger in the same environment.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Select Hall for talent and receiving rebound only if you accept team-context uncertainty; do not project a 10-TD season as certain.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

profile_notes.subject: Breece Hall and Adonai Mitchell
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target Hall if nearby RB2 turmoil discounts him; Mitchell is a free deep-league final-bench flyer only.
profile_notes.summary: Harris and Daugherty see Hall as unusually settled as the Jets' lead back despite poor team expectations, while preferring Mitchell only as a no-cost way to test for early-season opportunity.
profile_notes.evidence: Hall is not holding out, being traded, or facing the prior uncertainty; Harris says camp Braylon Allen headlines are least important, while Daugherty agrees the two-back concern failed to manifest. Both call Mitchell a free flyer.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Jets offense may still be poor, Hall's RB2 neighborhood can shift as other camp news arrives, and Mitchell's likely hype would not distinguish him from many free receivers.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid camp overreaction, buy Hall at a discount, and churn Mitchell after one or two weeks if usage does not appear.
profile_notes.episode_title: Drake Maye & Josh Allen & Previewing AFC East

outlook.text: Williams re-signed with the Cowboys following a successful first year with the team. After failing to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign during his final three seasons in Denver, Williams finished 12th in 2025, setting career-best marks in carries, rushing yards, touches (287), scrimmage yards (1,338) and yards per carry (4.77). He also scored a career-high 13 touchdowns after totaling 16 during his first four campaigns, and his 16 carries inside the 5-yard line were fifth most among backs. That helped offset his receiving struggles, as his 2.7 yards per target was last among qualified RBs. With minimal competition for touches in a high-scoring Dallas offense, the 26-year-old is a solid RB2 target.

profile_notes.subject: Javonte Williams
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Fine at ADP 35, but not a bet on elite talent.
profile_notes.summary: Williams is an acceptable but unexciting late-third-round selection.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris assigns 4, says Williams is not an amazing player, and notes an injury path in his career.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris concludes 'but, like, fine,' which keeps this from a full fade; Josh's numerical score is not captured in the transcript.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Williams only as a price-appropriate RB, not as a high-ceiling cornerstone.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Javonte Williams
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris would be thrilled in Round 4 and would consider Round 3.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Williams as a newly validated power back and attractive touchdown-area investment in Dallas.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Williams ran mean, moved piles, broke tackles, and on one Jets run escaped a defensive tackle wrapped around both legs for a gain over 60 yards. Harris thinks Dallas quickly recognized more than it expected after signing him alongside Miles Sanders and drafting Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah.
profile_notes.counterweight: Williams is not particularly fast or elusive, and Harris expects Malik Davis to take some irritating touches because no back owns a full backfield.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Target Williams as a physical, goal-line-capable RB at the stated middle-round price, without projecting an uncontested role.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Dallas Cowboys skill players
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ignore Cowboys camp hype absent injury or a genuine George Pickens hold-in.
profile_notes.summary: Dallas offers little camp information likely to change established fantasy evaluations.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris describes annual hype around Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, while Ciely says the relevant fantasy roles have little genuine competition. Pickens signed his tag and attended work despite a possible future contract dispute.
profile_notes.counterweight: A Pickens hold-in could hurt early games, and injuries or unavoidably negative reports would be meaningful.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Filter positive Cowboys clips out of draft decisions; only move players for material availability news.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Nabers is on the comeback trail after a torn ACL limited him to only four appearances last season. In 18 full games in his career, Nabers has a massive 35% target share (11.3 per game) and he's averaging 18.2 fantasy PPG. As a rookie, the 2024 sixth overall pick finished seventh or better among receivers in targets, receptions, yards and fantasy points despite missing two games and dealing with New York's offensive struggles. Nabers' massive target share allowed him a high floor, as he was a top-30 fantasy scorer in 13 of 15 games, including 10 straight to end the 2024 season. He essentially has a new quarterback (Jaxson Dart threw only three passes his way last season), a new coach (John Harbaugh), a new offensive playcaller (Matt Nagy) and is recovering from the knee, so there are a lot of variables here, but the 23-year-old still holds elite upside. A healthy Nabers should be valued as a mid-to-back-end WR1, but the potential for a slow start (perhaps including missed games) needs…

profile_notes.subject: Malik Nabers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Wait below Harris's roughly 39th-overall rank until the knee proves stable beyond Week 1.
profile_notes.summary: Nabers is the board's clearest injury-driven fade for Harris despite both speakers acknowledging extraordinary talent.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris assigns his only 10, warning that first-team practice work does not prevent knee swelling in Week 3; he has raised Nabers but remains at 39 overall behind Tetairoa McMillan, Tee Higgins, and Terry McLaurin.
profile_notes.counterweight: Josh calls Nabers an amazing, generational-caliber talent and gives an 8 rather than dismissing him completely.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not use a Week-1 clearance as proof of season-long knee stability; require a substantial price discount.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: New York Giants offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat Giants outcomes as high-variance rather than projecting certainty into Week 1 roles.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers identify the Giants as a team full of volatile fantasy outcomes centered on Skattebo, Jaxson Dart, and Malik Nabers.
profile_notes.evidence: Funston says all three carry wild ranges of outcomes and calls the team fascinating from a fantasy perspective. Harris agrees on Skattebo and Nabers as swing possibilities.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris sharply differs on Dart, saying he disliked the tape and is out on him; the team label is an uncertainty signal, not a blanket endorsement.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not stack Giants assumptions as settled facts; assess each player separately and demand a price that accommodates role and quarterback uncertainty.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Malik Nabers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Third-round redraft consideration, but do not chase a materially more aggressive market while ACL durability remains unproven.
profile_notes.summary: Harris is more optimistic that Nabers can be ready for Week 1 and raises him into his top 20 receivers, while retaining a meaningful health discount.
profile_notes.evidence: Giants camp observers say Nabers looks good even though, as of August 10, he had not yet done 7-on-7 or 11-on-11 work; Harris calls the return a process and says the player would otherwise carry Round 1 upside.
profile_notes.counterweight: The torn ACL still creates downward mobility, and playing Week 1 does not establish that the knee will hold up over the full season.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Nabers as a discounted ceiling receiver rather than drafting as though the ACL risk has disappeared.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Malik Nabers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not upgrade until full-team practice work and several weeks of reliable health reporting arrive.
profile_notes.summary: Harris acknowledges Nabers has avoided the worst early-camp outcome but declines to raise his rank yet.
profile_notes.evidence: Nabers avoided the PUP list and was running routes after a second knee procedure, but Harris says he was still working off to the side rather than in full team practice.
profile_notes.counterweight: New York beat reporting can overstate developments, and Harris wants to evaluate the next couple of weeks rather than one optimistic update.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Preserve health risk in Nabers's price until full participation is sustained.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: Malik Nabers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Both rank WR26; can rise near WR10 on full health or fall further if camp absence continues.
profile_notes.summary: Nabers's second knee procedure creates a genuinely two-sided camp decision: a healthy return restores elite talent value, while continued absence makes the downside material.
profile_notes.evidence: Ciely says the second procedure may have been corrective but does not guarantee full recovery and notes no field work by mid/late July. Harris calls WR26 a placeholder and says full drills/preseason health could move Nabers close to WR10.
profile_notes.counterweight: If he slips to WR40, both would accept the late-draft gamble; the primary uncertainty is availability, not talent.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Follow practice and preseason workload closely; unlike generic camp hype, this medical information should move the rank.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: The reigning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, McMillan is a candidate to make the leap into the "elite" conversation at wide receiver this season. The 2025 eighth overall pick was very busy as a rookie (top 15 among WRs in snaps, routes, target share, targets, yards, end zone targets and touchdowns) and, while he finished 16th among receivers in fantasy points (22nd PPG), he lacked upside, producing only one top-10 outing (Week 9). Improving on a 56% catch rate will be key in Year 2, though that would require improvement from Bryce Young. McMillan, 23, remains positioned as Carolina's clear top target and, though Young's limitations may cap his ceiling a bit, McMillan's talent/usage combo supplies him with top-10 upside. He's safest as a midrange fantasy WR2.

profile_notes.subject: Tetairoa McMillan
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris ranks him WR15 and views the healthy floor as strong despite Josh's environment concern.
profile_notes.summary: Harris counters that McMillan's strong floor can produce high-end fantasy value even without a dramatic offensive transformation.
profile_notes.evidence: He says McMillan could reach a Drake London-like 1,209-yard outcome from only a couple more favorable plays than his 1,000-yard/seven-TD rookie line, and observes that fantasy WR standings flatten quickly after the very top tier.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris does not claim Carolina's environment is ideal; his response accepts Josh's concern but argues it is not enough to erase the player-level floor.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Harris's view supports taking McMillan at a fair WR2 cost rather than fading solely because the team may remain run-oriented.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

profile_notes.subject: Tetairoa McMillan
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Josh ranks him WR21 and worries about a late-Round-3 price; Harris ranks him WR15.
profile_notes.summary: Josh likes McMillan's player profile but fears Carolina's constrained passing environment caps the ceiling at a price near more explosive alternatives.
profile_notes.evidence: He notes the strong rookie production, size, and performance with below-average quarterback play, but says the team invested in defense, wants to run, and Bryce Young had under 200 passing yards 12 times. He also flags Jalen Coker's target competitiveness.
profile_notes.counterweight: Josh says McMillan's healthy floor feels good and Harris argues two additional broken-play outcomes could turn last year's 1,000-yard/seven-TD line into a high-end fantasy season.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use McMillan as a stable WR2-type choice only if you accept a lower implied ceiling; do not assume Carolina becomes a high-volume passing offense.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

profile_notes.subject: Carolina Panthers receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Jalen Coker is a late WR5/6 only; do not let ordinary camp praise create enthusiasm for receivers behind Tetairoa McMillan.
profile_notes.summary: Harris has a soft spot for Coker but neither speaker expects Carolina camp to create strong value beyond McMillan.
profile_notes.evidence: Coker had a standout playoff game and previously flashed as an undrafted player; Harris has him inside his top 60. Chris Brazell joins as a third-round rookie but does not obviously displace him.
profile_notes.counterweight: McCormick calls Coker a theoretical/deep option and sees no serious competition signal; McMillan's expected second-year improvement is not informative.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Coker only as a cheap late dart and do not chase positive camp blurbs.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Flowers' emergence into a star continued in 2025, as the 2023 first-round pick posted career-best marks in target share (29%), targets (118), catches (86) and yardage (1,211). Despite still lacking a role near the goal line (he has never cleared seven end zone targets or six touchdowns in a single season), Flowers finished seventh among receivers in fantasy points (13th PPG), which marks his first finish better than 25th (31st PPG). A highly targeted, short-range RAC specialist, Flowers' ceiling is lower than other top receivers, but the 25-year-old remains positioned as Lamar Jackson's top target in Baltimore's new-look offense. Flowers makes for a solid fantasy WR2.

profile_notes.subject: Zay Flowers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target at current ADP, especially when available slightly after DeVonta Smith.
profile_notes.summary: Harris considers Flowers a complete receiver whose market price understates breakout potential.
profile_notes.evidence: He cites Flowers's play-action production and argues that touchdown variance, including Derrick Henry's goal-line role, constrained the fantasy result more than receiver limitations did.
profile_notes.counterweight: Baltimore's touchdown distribution remains volatile, and the episode does not state an exact ADP.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Flowers as a priority receiver target at his prevailing price without reaching far beyond the surrounding tier.
profile_notes.episode_title: More Flag Players & Cousin Josh's Frag Players

profile_notes.subject: Zay Flowers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Low-risk third-round complement, especially after a risky Round-1 player.
profile_notes.summary: Flowers is one of the low-risk values at the bottom of the third round.
profile_notes.evidence: Both give him a 3; Harris says he likes the value and sees minimal risk, while Josh says Flowers is the type of player he would want on the same roster as McCaffrey because he feels he knows the outcome range.
profile_notes.counterweight: No material counterargument is offered beyond the normal uncertainty of any projection.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Flowers as a stabilizing WR selection after opening with a volatile elite player.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Baltimore Ravens offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor the three new interior pieces and tackle performance before assuming a strong rushing environment.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker sees Baltimore's changed interior and new under-center offense as a significant continuity risk despite potential upside.
profile_notes.evidence: He names injured-center returnee Ethan Pocic, returning Simpson, and first-round Penn State guard Vega Ioane as a substantially remade interior, while noting the rookie may switch sides. He also says neither Ronnie Stanley nor Roger Rosengarten met expectations last year.
profile_notes.counterweight: If the interior questions resolve positively, Tucker says the line could be good; Derrick Henry remains a rare durability/production outlier.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the interior transition in the downside range for Ravens runners and passing-game projections rather than presuming past line quality.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Zay Flowers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Maintain an above-market receiver stance; no camp event is needed to validate the established role.
profile_notes.summary: Harris is higher on Flowers than many drafters, and Harmon is enthusiastic about Flowers's 2026 outlook.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon says the new staff sees Flowers as a room leader and wants him heavily involved; both describe Baltimore's principal roles as settled.
profile_notes.counterweight: The transcript gives no new workload number or ADP, and other established Baltimore options can still absorb targets.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Flowers as a target at his normal market price rather than waiting for a camp headline.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: It's generally tough for a former Heisman Trophy winner and first-round draft pick to fly under the radar, but that has been the case for Smith in recent years. With all eyes on A.J. Brown, Smith has finished no lower than 30th among receivers in fantasy PPG in each of his five seasons (top 30 in PPG each of the last four). The "slim reaper" saw a big dip in touchdowns last season (four, after at least seven the prior three seasons), but remained very efficient (career 9.1 yards per target and 2.1 yards per route run). Smith has handled roughly one-quarter of the Eagles' targets throughout his career, and that may rise slightly after Brown was traded to New England. Smith, 27, is the Eagles' No. 1 receiver for the first time as a non-rookie and is well positioned for a strong WR2 campaign.

profile_notes.subject: DeVonta Smith
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target at approximately WR14 market cost.
profile_notes.summary: Harris considers Smith an underpriced difference-making receiver and ranks him four positional spots above the cited market.
profile_notes.evidence: Smith's big-play ability supports the ranking, and his return to practice reduces concern about the camp hamstring issue.
profile_notes.counterweight: The episode does not establish a scoring-format-specific volume projection, and the hamstring still merits monitoring.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Prefer Smith when he remains available around his market cost; treat the injury as a monitoring item rather than a reason to remove him.
profile_notes.episode_title: More Flag Players & Cousin Josh's Frag Players

profile_notes.subject: DeVonta Smith
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Low-risk third-round receiver, aided by the other rookie's slow start.
profile_notes.summary: Smith is a low-risk top receiver in his new Eagles role.
profile_notes.evidence: Both give him 3; Harris says the only meaningful question is whether the Eagles have already peaked, while Josh likes that Makai Lemon is injured and reminds listeners Smith won the Heisman.
profile_notes.counterweight: The ceiling depends on how much of the Eagles' prior offensive peak remains.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Smith as a stable third-round WR rather than overemphasizing the team-level peak concern.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: DeVonta Smith
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Top-10/12 WR target for both speakers, accepting high variance and durability concern in a new Eagles offense.
profile_notes.summary: Harris and Zachariason believe Smith is a complete, dangerous receiver rather than merely a situational deep threat, and both rank him at the top of the position.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says defenses rolled coverage toward Smith more than A.J. Brown and praises his use on both deep routes and screens; Zachariason calls him one of the league's best route runners, a strong ball tracker, and a creator of separation-driven YAC.
profile_notes.counterweight: Smith is notably thin, has knee/sturdiness questions, and faces a new Eagles offense without Brown, creating high variance even if the talent is clear.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Target Smith at elite-WR cost when comfortable accepting durability and system uncertainty, because the downside is not a talent or processing concern.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade offense and Saquon Barkley context if interior health holds in the new scheme.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker believes Philadelphia has a high ceiling and high floor because last year's underperformance was substantially injury-driven and the new system should help blockers.
profile_notes.evidence: Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson fought through multiple injuries, surgeries, and rehabilitation; Lane Johnson missed the second half with plantar fasciitis. Tucker says the new coordinator's increased play action avoids isolating tackles in straight dropbacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: The line did not play as a top-five unit last year, and the recovery of injured interior starters must persist.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat a healthy Eagles line as a positive contextual upgrade for Barkley and the offense rather than anchoring on last year's unit ranking.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Keep outside the small trusted-offense tier until the new Mannion system succeeds in games.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers refuse to restore Philadelphia to an automatic top-offense projection after last year's collapse and coordinator replacement.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites A.J. Brown's trade, questions around the line, and the team's decision to replace the coordinator despite prior Super Bowl success. Ciely believes Mannion's changes can help but says practice and preseason cannot prove a top-five result.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense has Jalen Hurts, a strong history, and a scheme that could improve play action/middle-field work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid building draft projections on an assumed Eagles bounce-back; wait for regular-season evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Allen enters his age-30 campaign having finished each of the past six seasons no worse than second among quarterbacks in fantasy points. Despite seeing less passing volume the past two seasons (14th or lower in pass attempts both years), the 2024 NFL MVP has finished in the top 10 in passing TDs six seasons in a row and remains a major threat with his legs (top five in carries and rushing TDs among quarterbacks all eight seasons of his career). Allen's 21.4 fantasy points per game in 2025 was actually his lowest since 2019, but it was still enough to lead the position. With Joe Brady returning as playcaller and the Bills adding a No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore, Allen remains an elite fantasy quarterback.

profile_notes.subject: Josh Allen
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Low player risk, but not preferred at ADP 21 in one-QB builds.
profile_notes.summary: Allen is a safe quarterback whose draft cost nevertheless conflicts with their preferred build.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris explicitly says Allen is not risky but assigns 3 because he does not like taking a QB at this point; Josh assigns 2 and agrees with the strategic objection.
profile_notes.counterweight: The episode notes Allen can be first overall in superflex, which is a different format.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Pass in standard one-QB construction, but do not confuse that choice with a negative projection for Allen.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Josh Allen
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Maintain elite-QB treatment, but account for his goal-line rushing reducing both Bills receiver certainty and the value of a James Cook handcuff.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers treat Allen as Buffalo's central fantasy ecosystem variable: a better receiver room could restore passing upside, but his own rushing and goal-line role limits certainty for every surrounding asset.
profile_notes.evidence: They note Buffalo has gone multiple seasons without a reliable fantasy receiver despite Allen, discuss DJ Moore as a possible target, and say Cook's handcuff case is weakened because Allen can absorb goal-line work.
profile_notes.counterweight: A healthy, freer DJ Moore or improved receiver play could make Allen's supporting cast more productive; Allen's rushing does not prevent Cook from being a first-round-caliber player.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Allen for his own elite rushing/passing profile, but avoid assuming a Bills receiver or backup RB automatically inherits all available high-value work.
profile_notes.episode_title: Drake Maye & Josh Allen & Previewing AFC East

outlook.text: Williams continues to produce at a high level as the Rams' lead back. The 2022 fifth-round pick has produced 1,350-plus scrimmage yards in three straight seasons (including a career-high 1,533 in 2025), and he's one of 11 backs in NFL history who have scored 13-plus touchdowns in three of his first four seasons. Williams' carry share actually dropped quite a bit last season, but it was mostly offset by a boost in both rushing and receiving efficiency, and he still averaged a healthy 15.5 fantasy points. Williams doesn't do much as a receiver (he has never cleared 36 catches in a season), but his overall usage and scoring potential in the Rams' elite offense is enough to make the 26-year-old a solid RB2 option.

profile_notes.subject: Kyren Williams
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target in Round 3; pass if pushed into the high/middle second.
profile_notes.summary: Harris still expects Williams to provide strong value and dismisses Blake Corum committee speculation as enthusiasm unsupported by a clear role shift.
profile_notes.evidence: The positive case rests on Williams's established workload and production rather than a new camp narrative.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris objects when market sources place Williams around 27–31 overall or higher, making this a tightly price-sensitive Flag.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Set a draft-room ceiling in advance and take Williams only when his actual price falls into the preferred range.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Kyren Williams
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris accepts Round 2; Kluge prefers as late as Round 4.
profile_notes.summary: Harris considers Williams's established production strong enough for Round 2, while Kluge prefers multiple receivers in the same range and pushes Williams much later.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris emphasizes three consecutive top-eight seasons; Kluge places more weight on touch-share and opportunity-cost concerns.
profile_notes.counterweight: The speakers' disagreement is partly roster-construction philosophy rather than a simple dispute about Williams's ability.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Set the price according to the chosen RB/WR construction and do not report a merged consensus rank.
profile_notes.episode_title: Five ADP Surprises Plus More Injuries

profile_notes.subject: Kyren Williams
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris would draft him well ahead of ADP 27.
profile_notes.summary: Williams is an ADP value with only modest weekly-workload annoyance risk from Blake Corum.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Corum's increased involvement might be mildly annoying but would take Williams much higher; Josh cites touchdown instinct and an excellent offense.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both acknowledge Corum can erode some week-to-week volume, and Josh has historically been skeptical of Williams.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Target Williams as a value RB rather than allowing committee anxiety to suppress his price.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Kyren Williams
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Maintain a relatively high baseline rank unless a sustained Blake Corum passing-down drumbeat emerges.
profile_notes.summary: Harris is higher on Williams than drafters who fear Corum, and Gretch sees Williams's passing role as the key reason he remains materially more valuable.
profile_notes.evidence: Gretch says Williams ran over three times Corum's routes, was more efficient, and is trusted in pass protection; Harris expects normal backfield sharing rather than an automatic 50/50 split.
profile_notes.counterweight: Corum can create frustrating weekly variance, and a heavy, credible report that he will take passing-down work would change the split concern.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Williams at the existing strong baseline, then downgrade only for repeated evidence that the receiving role is changing.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

profile_notes.subject: Rams offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a strong environment, but do not let that alone erase individual age, role, and price concerns.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see Los Angeles as the NFC West offense most widely expected to be elite, while Harris warns that assumed certainty creates contradictory player valuations.
profile_notes.evidence: They discuss a possible 30-point-per-game offense, the resolution of Matthew Stafford's prior back concern, and the Rams' recent history of meaningful August role signals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris opens the episode by showing that consensus team projections frequently fail, and individual Rams can still decline or lose role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Rams environment as a supporting factor, then make player decisions on role, talent, health, and market cost.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Etienne signed with the Saints after spending the first five seasons of his pro career with the Jaguars. The 2021 first-round pick has produced at least 1,399 scrimmage yards in three of the past four seasons and scored a career-high 13 touchdowns in 2025. A capable rusher and receiver, Etienne has already reached 1,000-plus rushing yards three times and has 35-plus catches in each of the past four seasons. Even if the Saints retain Alvin Kamara as a situational player, Etienne will have a clear path to feature-back duties in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough. That will be enough to position the 27-year-old for his third top-15 fantasy campaign in four years. Consider Etienne a solid RB2 target with backend RB1 upside.

profile_notes.subject: Travis Etienne
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris ranks him RB19; value depends on accepting Kamara's continuing role.
profile_notes.summary: Harris upgrades Etienne's speed after a sharp 2025 film season, but does not project an uncontested New Orleans workload.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Etienne looked sharper turning upfield and dusting defenders than expected for a fifth-year player, made the Jaguars offense go in 2025, and showed more tackle breaking than remembered.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris says Etienne remains less physical than expected at 215 pounds, tends to bounce/dance near the goal line, and Alvin Kamara's pay cut signals a preserved passing-game role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft for speed and receiving-space upside, but do not assume Kamara disappears or that Etienne becomes an elite goal-line back.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Travis Etienne
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris lowers to RB19 standard/RB20 PPR after Kamara signing; restore only if camp proves Etienne clearly owns the workload.
profile_notes.summary: Harris downgrades Etienne because Kamara is a more credible receiving-role drain than younger alternatives, even though full workloads are rare.
profile_notes.evidence: Kamara is a franchise legend and elite historical receiving back; Etienne had only roughly 70% of carries even in a good Jacksonville season.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris is skeptical coaches will disclose the split, and he allows that camp could show Kamara treated as a backup or limited third-down contributor.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Build in committee risk now, then raise Etienne only for clear, repeated evidence of feature usage.
profile_notes.episode_title: Drake Maye & Josh Allen & Previewing AFC East

profile_notes.subject: New Orleans Saints backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Etienne is RB16 pending Kamara's contract/roster outcome; no-Kamara clarity can accelerate his ADP toward RB11-12.
profile_notes.summary: Kamara's contractual status is the Saints' decisive backfield variable: Etienne has an RB16 baseline after a strong year, but Kamara's receiving trust can materially cap him.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says the Saints may not intend to pay Kamara's $11 million, while McCormick sees Etienne's payment as a path to a clean lead role. Harris names Kendre Miller and Devin Neal as less established alternatives.
profile_notes.counterweight: Kamara staying may be an institutional nuisance but gives a known role; he remains a capable receiver, and any no-Kamara outcome could be followed by another acquisition.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor actual contract/transaction news, not camp touches; draft Etienne more aggressively only once Kamara risk is truly resolved.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Skattebo is a Year 2 breakout candidate following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie season. The fourth-round pick first played a significant offensive role in Week 2 and went on to average 16.0 carries, 4.7 targets and 96.3 yards while scoring six TDs during his six full games. His 19.1 fantasy points per game during the span would've ranked sixth over the full season. The 24-year-old enters 2026 with a new coach (John Harbaugh) and playcaller (Matt Nagy), but his competition for touches are the same guys he beat out for work in 2025 (Tyrone Tracy Jr., Devin Singletary). Assuming his ankle heals up as expected, Skattebo will be on the RB2 radar with upside for more.

profile_notes.subject: New York Giants offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat Giants outcomes as high-variance rather than projecting certainty into Week 1 roles.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers identify the Giants as a team full of volatile fantasy outcomes centered on Skattebo, Jaxson Dart, and Malik Nabers.
profile_notes.evidence: Funston says all three carry wild ranges of outcomes and calls the team fascinating from a fantasy perspective. Harris agrees on Skattebo and Nabers as swing possibilities.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris sharply differs on Dart, saying he disliked the tape and is out on him; the team label is an uncertainty signal, not a blanket endorsement.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not stack Giants assumptions as settled facts; assess each player separately and demand a price that accommodates role and quarterback uncertainty.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Cam Skattebo
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draft only while accepting role, style, and durability volatility.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees a clear path to a huge Skattebo season but also a wide downside tied to role and violent playing style.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says the Giants' new featured back has obvious main-character potential and could reach RB7 through a Mike Alstott-like year. Funston includes Skattebo in an unusually volatile Giants set.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris mentions concern that he leads with his head and could not be the unquestioned Week 1 starter; Andy Behrens had named him as most likely to lose that job. Harris also notes his prior injury was a leg injury, not a head injury.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Value the league-winning path but avoid treating Skattebo as a stable workload or health projection.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Cam Skattebo
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ciely RB21 with only upside to RB19 but greater downside if leg rehab is incomplete.
profile_notes.summary: Skattebo's severe leg injury is more likely to lower a currently optimistic rank than to create large upside through good camp reports.
profile_notes.evidence: Ciely cites encouraging workouts but says a Harbaugh/Roman run-focused system historically does not give one back 70-75% of work. Harris agrees a full role is unnecessary for RB2 value but says camp likely cannot clarify the normal shared workload.
profile_notes.counterweight: Full participation could make the medical outlook more comfortable, and the scheme should run the ball.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor rehab and preseason availability; do not equate routine first-team reps with a guaranteed workhorse role.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Judkins is entering his second NFL season after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which a solid 14-game stretch of action was bookended by missed time early because of an off-field issue and late because of a season-ending leg injury in Week 16. When on the field, Judkins handled a massive 71.4% share of Cleveland's designed rush attempts (16.4 per game). Though he was held to 3.6 yards per carry, he was dealing with a league-high 7.4 box defenders per attempt. He wasn't involved much as a receiver (2.6 targets per game), however, and was limited to 12.1 fantasy points per game (26th among RBs). The Cleveland offense has a new coach (Todd Monken) and quarterback questions remain, so while Judkins has a clear path to a big carry total, the 22-year-old might cap out as a midrange RB2 in 2026.

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Conditionally upgrade pass catchers if quarterback play becomes merely passable.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers argue that Cleveland does not need excellent quarterback play for its pass catchers to beat depressed prices.
profile_notes.evidence: The derived analysis identifies KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, and Harold Fannin as players who could benefit if Shedeur Sanders or Dylan Gabriel is simply adequate.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither host expresses confidence that the quarterback outcome will actually be adequate.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Cleveland receivers and tight ends as conditional value rather than automatic targets, and update after credible quarterback evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat early-season cohesion as uncertain after a nearly complete starting-line overhaul.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker calls Cleveland's nearly wholesale replacement of the starting line an unprecedented continuity experiment with high early variance.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Teven Jenkins had been on the team but was not a starter, and cites Spencer Fano, Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins, and Titus Howard as new additions. Tucker grants that most have played meaningful NFL football.
profile_notes.counterweight: The individual additions have shown positive things and could gel by December; Harris also says he is not qualified to make every technique judgment and is not down on every member.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid assuming immediate line quality for Browns assets; prioritize early-season evidence of the new group functioning together.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Quinshon Judkins
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Accept as an RB2 at Harris's current RB16 standard/RB18 PPR range, while monitoring health and passing-down role.
profile_notes.summary: Harris is comfortable with Judkins as an RB2 because he likes the player and expects a well-designed Todd Monken run game, while Harmon flags conditions that cap ceiling.
profile_notes.evidence: The speakers cite good pre-injury tape, optimistic recovery reports, and a potentially strong run-game design; Harris has drafted him as an RB2.
profile_notes.counterweight: A poor Browns environment and Dylan Sampson's possible third-down role could restrict passing work, and neither expects Cleveland to disclose that split cleanly in camp.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Judkins as a viable RB2 at this tier, but preserve downside for quarterback quality and third-down sharing.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Irving enters his third season coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he missed seven games and struggled with efficiency. After averaging 5.42 yards per carry and producing 1,514 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, Irving fell to 3.40 YPC (fourth worst among qualified RBs), 865 yards and four touchdowns in 2025. He failed to clear 4.2 YPC in any of his 10 outings. The 24-year-old remains positioned as the lead back in Tampa Bay, but the combination of his small frame (5-foot-9, 192 pounds) and the arrival of Kenneth Gainwell suggest he might play a lesser role moving forward. Irving should be valued as a back-end RB2.

profile_notes.subject: Bucky Irving
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Pass in Round 4; reconsider near the mid-sixth-round Jaylen Warren/Tyjae Spears tier.
profile_notes.summary: Josh believes Irving is overvalued because his size already contributed to durability problems and his prior role lacked premium goal-line work.
profile_notes.evidence: The derived summary cites zero Irving carries inside the five versus 17 combined for White and Tucker, plus Kenneth Gainwell's arrival and uncertainty around the Zac Robinson offense.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris counters that Irving already demonstrated a top-10 workload and that the market discount more than compensates for those concerns.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Risk-averse managers should pass at the market price and only reconsider after a meaningful fall.
profile_notes.episode_title: More Flag Players & Cousin Josh's Frag Players

profile_notes.subject: Bucky Irving
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris would buy at a Round 4–5 cost.
profile_notes.summary: Harris interprets Irving's fall from a prior 13th-overall price into Rounds 4–5 as a large discount on a back who previously handled a top-10 workload.
profile_notes.evidence: He emphasizes that the workload remained strong even after Irving aggravated a shoulder injury and argues that analysts apply backfield-competition concerns selectively.
profile_notes.counterweight: Cousin Josh presents a substantive contrary case involving durability, goal-line work, competition, and the offense.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Managers accepting Harris's workload thesis should buy the discount, but should record this as one speaker's target rather than consensus.
profile_notes.episode_title: More Flag Players & Cousin Josh's Frag Players

profile_notes.subject: Bucky Irving
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris still wants him on rosters, while recognizing small-back durability and multi-backfield risk.
profile_notes.summary: Harris does not join McCormick's full fade: he continues to value Irving's lateral quickness, decisiveness, and vision but sees realistic fragility and workload limits.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites Irving's lightning-quick side-to-side movement and notes the poor line plus a confusing foot-to-shoulder injury sequence that eventually led to shoulder surgery.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris calls Irving a sub-200-pound runner who seeks traffic, a difficult physical profile, and says Tampa pairs him with Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker, creating touchdown-sharing risk.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Irving in the draft pool but build in a discount for durability and committee outcomes instead of assuming McCormick's concerns are disproven.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Bucky Irving
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Downgrade from a prior high expectation and factor in a likely committee with Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker; Harris still sees a draftable player.
profile_notes.summary: McCormick is newly skeptical of Irving after seeing the contact balance, home-run gear, and escape ability that defined his early career decline last season.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Irving struggled to escape early chaos behind a poor line, fell sharply in yards after contact, and comes off a series of injuries; he identifies a less forceful version of the prior bowling-ball runner.
profile_notes.counterweight: McCormick acknowledges the line was poor. Harris offers a distinct, more favorable view: Irving remains lightning quick side to side, decisive, and a good reader, and the post-Eagles foot/shoulder injury sequence may explain the decline.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Lower Irving for health and touchdown-share risk, but preserve the distinction that Harris still would draft him rather than treating McCormick's fade as consensus.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Bucky Irving
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris ranks him RB20; target for talent at an ADP-adjusted price while discounting goal-line, receiving, health, and committee risk.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers call Irving a Film Room Hero because of rare lateral agility, elusiveness, contact balance, and a willingness to run where plays are blocked despite his size.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says he did not find the frustrating 10-game season discouraging on ability and praises quickness through traffic; Zachariason says defenders seem ready to swallow him before he escapes and adds that he is a natural receiver.
profile_notes.counterweight: Health is unsettled after a foot issue that was later characterized as shoulder-related, and the Bucs used Sean Tucker at the goal line, have Rachaad White, and added Kenneth Gainwell. Zachariason is below Harris because high-leverage work may remain split.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Irving for player quality if the role questions are priced in; do not project bankable touchdowns or passing volume.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

profile_notes.subject: Bucky Irving
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris lowered him for unresolved health and committee risks; retain as a talent bet only after those risks are reflected in price.
profile_notes.summary: Harris likes Irving's runner ability but lowered him because the prior injury story was confusing and Tampa's backfield can siphon high-value work.
profile_notes.evidence: He was first reported to have a sprained foot against Philadelphia, returned immediately for a 72-yard touchdown, then later information emphasized shoulder issues. Sean Tucker and Kenneth Gainwell add goal-line and passing-down uncertainty.
profile_notes.counterweight: Irving's talent remains compelling and a healthy role could make the downgrade excessive; camp can clarify availability but may not reveal usage truthfully.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Discount Irving for health and committee outcomes; do not assume a clean lead-back projection.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Egbuka is a fascinating evaluation following a rookie season that couldn't have started much better (five TDs and 20.5 fantasy PPG during his first five games), but that fell apart from there (one TD and 7.8 PPG during his final 12 games). By season's end, Egbuka sat in the top 10 in targets and air yards, but a horrific 49% catch rate led to a 34th-place finish in fantasy PPG. The good news is that, with Mike Evans out of the picture and Chris Godwin now 30 years old, Egbuka has a shot to emerge as Baker Mayfield's No. 1 target. The 2025 first-round pick is a strong bet for a leap forward and should be viewed as a WR2 with the potential for a full-on breakout.

profile_notes.subject: Tampa Bay Buccaneers receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Prefer Egbuka at a reasonable price, but avoid letting camp helium force a WR13 price; Godwin/McMillan remain health and role-dependent.
profile_notes.summary: Harris expects Egbuka to earn the strongest camp drumbeat but warns that any receiver price can become untenable; Tampa's frequent three-WR usage limits the value of two-WR-set chatter.
profile_notes.evidence: Egbuka has helium and is Harris's preferred player; Godwin is a good player recovering from serious injury, while McMillan returned late after a frightening broken-neck injury.
profile_notes.counterweight: Egbuka had hands issues in the prior season, Godwin has burned managers through injury, and camp cannot definitively establish the target order among three regular receivers.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft upside at a rational price and ignore shallow formation/depth-chart claims in a three-WR offense.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Adams' first season in Los Angeles was a success, as the veteran led the wide receiver position in touchdowns for the third time in the past six seasons. His 27 end zone targets were nine more than any other player and he now sits second in that category (148) and in TDs from scrimmage (117) since entering the league in 2014. Adams' ninth-place finish in fantasy PPG marked his ninth top-10 in his past 10 seasons. Now 33 years old, he isn't targeted as much as in years past (24% target share in 2025 was his lowest since 2016), but he's the clear No. 2 behind Puka Nacua in the Rams' elite, Matthew Stafford-led offense. Adams' heavy usage near the goal line helps cement him as a fine fantasy WR2.

profile_notes.subject: Davante Adams
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris would consider him at WR17 depending on price, but do not pay as though last season's touchdown rate is repeatable.
profile_notes.summary: McCormick fades Adams because the remaining short-area route craft cannot replace lost downfield separation without another touchdown-heavy season; Harris shares the athletic concern but is less absolute at a discount.
profile_notes.evidence: McCormick says Adams looked slower and could not carry fantasy output without touchdowns; Harris says he still wins immediately off the line and in the red zone but no longer backs it up on deep crosses, digs, or go routes.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both acknowledge that Adams is one of the rare players for whom a 12-touchdown outcome is plausible, and his first move remains sudden.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Adams as volatile and touchdown-dependent; select him only after the draft price compensates for the shrinking route tree.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Davante Adams
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris ranks WR17; Josh ranks WR22, with age and touchdown dependence creating the stress.
profile_notes.summary: Adams is still elite in tight red-zone spaces and attached to an offense Harris trusts, but the speakers do not know how much age-related decline and touchdown reliance to price in.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris lowers his speed grade to C but raises his end-zone grade to A-plus, cites 14 touchdowns in a WR7 season, and says the offense repeatedly succeeds on fades. Josh highlights his back-shoulder/end-zone skill.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris says he is no longer asked to win downfield and is touchdown dependent; his research found only six WR1 seasons since 2000 by receivers in their 13th season or later.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft only after deciding whether the red-zone role and offense justify age and volume risk; do not project a repeat solely from last year's TD total.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

profile_notes.subject: Davante Adams
