profile_notes.action_qualifier: Consider around Round 4, especially in PPR, only if roster construction and price account for age and touchdown regression.
profile_notes.summary: Harris can still take Adams at the right cost because a great Rams offense could preserve exceptional touchdown production, while Gretch is more skeptical of repeating that outcome at age 34.
profile_notes.evidence: Adams led the league in receiving touchdowns and finished WR7 despite fewer than 800 yards; both say he remains dangerous in tight spaces and the red zone.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris calls him a lesser version of himself, and Gretch says age plus a touchdown repeat is a meaningful risk.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Adams only when the price treats touchdowns as upside rather than a guaranteed repeat.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

profile_notes.subject: Rams offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a strong environment, but do not let that alone erase individual age, role, and price concerns.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see Los Angeles as the NFC West offense most widely expected to be elite, while Harris warns that assumed certainty creates contradictory player valuations.
profile_notes.evidence: They discuss a possible 30-point-per-game offense, the resolution of Matthew Stafford's prior back concern, and the Rams' recent history of meaningful August role signals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris opens the episode by showing that consensus team projections frequently fail, and individual Rams can still decline or lose role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Rams environment as a supporting factor, then make player decisions on role, talent, health, and market cost.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: McConkey is looking to rebound after falling short of high expectations in 2025. The 2024 second-round pick was terrific as a rookie (82-1,155-7 receiving line and a 12th-place finish among WRs in fantasy points), but dipped to 66-789-6 line and a 30th-place finish last season. Though he ran considerably more routes, saw similar target numbers and was used a lot more near the goal line (seventh among WRs with 12 end zone targets), McConkey's efficiency plummeted, with his catch rate dipping from 74% to 62% and his yards per target from 10.4 to 7.4. The good news is that there's reason for optimism that he'll bounce back, as he has a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel, the Chargers' offense figures to improve with a much healthier line, and Keenan Allen is out of the picture. McConkey, 24, makes for a fine fantasy WR3.

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not assume a healthy or cohesive unit until tackle and interior questions are answered.
profile_notes.summary: The Chargers could benefit from an offensive-line-friendly McDaniel system, but Tucker sees legitimate uncertainty at every starting position.
profile_notes.evidence: Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt are returning from major injuries; Tucker questions center Tyler Biadasz's recovery, Jake Slaughter's shift from Florida center to left guard, and Cole Strange's fit after New England. Harris notes Alt was not fully participating when camp opened.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Shanahan-McVay tree can aid blockers, and all questions can resolve favorably.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor training-camp participation and interior cohesion before assigning a strong line-driven boost to Chargers skill players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target discounted Chargers pieces only on the conditional thesis of healthy line, protected Herbert, and a real offensive jump.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers can imagine a Chargers offense becoming a fantasy answer if health and protection finally cooperate, but view it as a conditional upside case rather than baseline.
profile_notes.evidence: Behrens says a healthy line and protected Justin Herbert could unlock a 28-30-point offense; Harris gives Herbert a mulligan and ties McConkey's rebound to the same factors.
profile_notes.counterweight: It requires unusually good Chargers injury luck, and the team has frequently failed to meet that sort of optimistic offensive projection.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the upside scenario as a tiebreaker for discounted Chargers, not as permission to erase downside.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

profile_notes.subject: Ladd McConkey
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target as a rebound bet only if price reflects slot-role limits and the Chargers' 2025 offensive failure.
profile_notes.summary: Harris expects McConkey to rebound more than his 2025 numbers because he attributes much of the outcome to a broken Chargers offense rather than a vanished skill set.
profile_notes.evidence: McConkey was quick out of breaks and Harris believes a healthy elite tackle pair, better coordinator, and strong Herbert can restore offense; he acknowledges minor ankle, AC-joint, calf, and foot reports did not cost meaningful games.
profile_notes.counterweight: McConkey is mainly a slot player who does not consistently beat press or win with size/speed, and he was never as undeniable a force as late-rookie-year hype suggested. Keenan Allen or target competition could further matter.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft McConkey on a Chargers bounce-back thesis, but do not price him as a guaranteed alpha receiver.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: McLaurin is eyeing a bounce-back campaign following a lost 2025 season in which both he (seven missed games) and quarterback Jayden Daniels (10 missed games) were sidelined for extended periods. The dud season came after Daniels helped McLaurin to a career year in 2024, which included 13 touchdowns (second most among WRs) and a seventh-place finish in fantasy points. McLaurin's target ceiling remains a concern (he's been in the 21-25% target share range each of his seven seasons), but with his quarterback healthy and his role as a vertical threat in new playcaller David Blough's offense, McLaurin is certainly poised for a rebound. The 30-year-old is best valued as a mid-to-back-end WR2.

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line fallout after starting LT Laremy Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps tear; Harris makes no automatic player-rank change.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps injury as a meaningful downgrade to Washington's offensive environment, though not one that can be precisely assigned to individual ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: He describes the line as thin without its starting left tackle and explicitly says losing good players hurts an offense.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris cannot draw a straight line from the injury to exactly how far Terry McLaurin or Jayden Daniels should fall, so he declines a mechanical rank adjustment.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Washington's pass-game options under review as replacement-line and protection information emerges instead of overreacting with a fixed downgrade.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Terry McLaurin
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris would take him in Round 4 and possibly about 90 spots above his early market position.
profile_notes.summary: Harris still sees McLaurin as an elite receiver and value at a fourth-round price, but his recent availability and production history make the pick stressful.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris praises his speed, routes, and alpha traits, but says last year included a holdout, conditioning issue, injury, and quarterback injury. He also notes that, outside the 13-TD season, McLaurin's production has generally been 1,000-1,100 yards.
profile_notes.counterweight: A full healthy season with Jayden Daniels and additional help from Stefon Diggs could restore the ceiling, but the film praise has exceeded his recurring production.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Target McLaurin at the discounted Round-4-type cost, but construct expectations around a volatile rather than automatic career-year outcome.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Modest environmental upgrade following Diggs's signing; no Harris downgrade for Terry McLaurin.
profile_notes.summary: Harris believes Diggs gives Washington a needed credible receiver and can improve the environment for Jayden Daniels, McLaurin, and the offense without taking McLaurin out of his prime role.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris notes that all Commanders pass catchers other than McLaurin had unstable week-to-week roles, while Diggs has a distinctly stronger portfolio. More sustained offense would create additional yards, touchdowns, and possession time.
profile_notes.counterweight: Diggs's personal ceiling is tied to the offense returning to its better two-years-ago form; Washington was not good last year, and Harris says some of that may have been Marcus Mariota-related.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not downgrade McLaurin just for a normal complementary receiver addition; modestly improve the outlook for a functional Commanders passing ecosystem.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

profile_notes.subject: Terry McLaurin
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ciely WR17 with or without a Stefon Diggs signing.
profile_notes.summary: McLaurin remains Washington's stable receiver value because a competent No. 2 would complement rather than automatically cannibalize him.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Daniels needs more than one viable target and notes the present cast behind McLaurin is makeshift. Ciely says Diggs would fit as a No. 2 and remains in the WR40s, while McLaurin stays WR17.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Commanders offense is not trusted, and no existing secondary receiver has a secure high-volume role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep McLaurin's valuation steady; do not lower him merely because Washington adds a credible complementary receiver.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Higgins may be overshadowed by teammate Ja'Marr Chase, but that hasn't stopped the veteran receiver from playing a key role near the goal line in the Bengals' pass-friendly offense. Despite missing seven games over the past two seasons, Higgins sits eighth among receivers in end zone targets (24) and fourth in touchdowns (21) during the span. The 2020 second-round pick finished both seasons in the top 20 in fantasy points (overall and per game). Durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2020) and a limited target share are concerns here, but Higgins' combination of talent and role in a Joe Burrow-led offense are enough to allow fringe-WR2 production.

profile_notes.subject: Tee Higgins
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris treats him as riskier than Josh due to annual missed games and Burrow uncertainty.
profile_notes.summary: Higgins's recurring absences make him a riskier selection for Harris than for Josh.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris assigns 6 and says Higgins gets hurt a lot and misses a couple games each year; Josh's 4 identifies the Burrow risk but is materially more forgiving.
profile_notes.counterweight: No direct criticism of Higgins's talent or role is made.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Higgins only after deciding whether Harris's durability concern outweighs the role/talent case.
profile_notes.episode_title: Risk Factors For First Three ADP Rounds

profile_notes.subject: Cincinnati Bengals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not change elite-player ranks on camp drills; monitor credible evidence of more under-center and modern-concept usage.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers regard Cincinnati's core as settled and already elite, with offensive evolution as a possible path from top-five to No. 1 production.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon wants to see Joe Burrow under center more and the offense move beyond an almost exclusively shotgun approach; he notes incremental increases in Chase motion and varied alignment.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harmon repeatedly says camp talk will not force rank changes for Burrow, Chase, Higgins, or Brown, and the preference may remain Burrow's existing style.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat schematic reports as upside context, not a reason to chase already-expensive Bengals players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Waddle was traded to Denver after spending his first five seasons in Miami. The 2021 first-round pick was solid during his Dolphins tenure, finishing in the top 30 among receivers in fantasy PPG four times, though never reaching the top 10 while often playing second fiddle to Tyreek Hill. Although he has been a reliable target and has missed only seven games in five years, Waddle hasn't finished a season higher than 20th in targets or catches since 2021. In Denver, the 27-year-old Waddle will compete with Courtland Sutton for the team lead in targets in a scheme that likes to spread the ball around. Not utilized near the goal line much at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds (he's yet to clear seven end zone targets in a season), Waddle is likely to max out as a back-end WR2 in Denver.

profile_notes.subject: Jalen Waddle
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor the expected one-week hamstring absence before changing rank.
profile_notes.summary: Harris does not move Waddle immediately, but the hamstring report is a negative input worth tracking.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Waddle pulled a hamstring and is expected to miss a week.
profile_notes.counterweight: The stated absence is short and Harris says he is not moving Waddle yet.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not overreact to the initial report; check whether he returns on schedule and avoids recurrence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

profile_notes.subject: Denver Broncos wide receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not elevate Troy Franklin or Pat Bryant on four-wide camp headlines without actual sustainable usage.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers reject a reported Broncos move toward more four-wide formations as a reason to project multiple new fantasy receivers.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Denver threw from four-wide only 15 times last year, while Behrens categorizes the report with familiar but unfulfilled preseason role claims.
profile_notes.counterweight: An injury could alter the depth chart, and Courtland Sutton/Waddle opinions differ, but they do not believe the offense and quarterback can support three or four viable fantasy receivers.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Franklin and Bryant off priority lists unless game-relevant volume emerges.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: The slow start to Williams' career is a thing of the past after the speedster delivered 1,000-plus-yard campaigns each of the past two seasons. After breaking out with a 22nd-place fantasy finish (25th PPG) in 2024, Williams set new career highs in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns en route to a 12th-place finish (19th PPG) last season. A lack of goal-line work (eight career end zone targets) and some drop woes (NFL-high eight in 2025) are drawbacks, but Williams' explosive-play ability has led him to finish sixth or better in yards per reception and yards per target each of the past two seasons. The 25-year-old remains one of Jared Goff's top targets in Detroit's high-scoring offense and is a fine fantasy WR3 target.

profile_notes.subject: Jameson Williams
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target in Rounds 5–6 for explosive upside.
profile_notes.summary: Harris believes Williams's late-season usage and explosiveness make him an attractive mid-round upside selection.
profile_notes.evidence: The supporting production is a WR4 standard and WR5 PPR pace from Week 10 onward under Dan Campbell's playcalling.
profile_notes.counterweight: Campbell is no longer calling plays, Drew Petzing's prior playcalling is a concern, and a healthy Sam LaPorta could reclaim targets.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Williams for ceiling in the middle rounds while building enough receiver depth to absorb coaching and target-share risk.
profile_notes.episode_title: More Flag Players & Cousin Josh's Frag Players

profile_notes.subject: Jameson Williams
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris WR16 standard / WR18 PPR; Erickson WR25, with upside tied to broader second-half usage.
profile_notes.summary: Harris is newly willing to draft Williams because second-half usage suggested he can do more than serve as a volatile deep-ball specialist.
profile_notes.evidence: He says the Dan Campbell play-calling period featured more interesting usage, including intermediate routes, and film on all 65 catches showed more than deep balls. Erickson agrees the second half improved, though he remembers two total zeroes and the 29-route Tampa game with no targets.
profile_notes.counterweight: The role change may instead have resulted from LaPorta's absence, a Drew Petzing offense remains unknown, and the boom-bust profile can still create unusable weeks.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Target Williams if paying for explosive upside and the broader role, but monitor LaPorta's health and do not let camp alone validate the projection.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: After averaging 4.1 targets and 8.5 fantasy PPG during his first 14 NFL games, Loveland leaped to 12.0 targets (10-plus in each) and 20.0 fantasy PPG during his final four games of 2025 (including the playoffs). For perspective, there have been only 12 instances of a tight end seeing at least 10 targets in four consecutive regular-season games in NFL history (and only one was a rookie). Loveland's overall efficiency was terrific, as he ranked eighth or better among tight ends in YPR, YPT and YPRR. With DJ Moore gone, the 2025 first-round pick enters his age-22 season all but locked into a massive workload alongside Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Loveland's ceiling is lofty, and midrange fantasy TE1 should be his floor.

profile_notes.action_qualifier: Prefer Warren when he is available roughly two rounds after Loveland.

profile_notes.evidence: Warren's prior production and the two-round discount support choosing him when the decision is between the two.
profile_notes.counterweight: Loveland's talent and strong finish can still justify optimism, so this is relative value rather than an outright Loveland fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Select Warren later instead of paying the recency-driven premium for a similarly ranked tight end.

profile_notes.counterweight: The offense could still improve and Chicago's traded DJ Moore leaves targets available, but that allocation cannot be known from camp clips.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft Chicago receivers on role-mapping narratives; wait for actual season usage and make only evidence-based adjustments.

outlook.text: Warren put together a solid rookie season, but it could've been even better. In 12 games with a healthy Daniel Jones, Warren scored five touchdowns and averaged 13.1 fantasy PPG. In five games without Jones, Warren fell to 6.3 PPG and failed to find the end zone. In fact, the 2025 first-round pick was unlucky in the scoring department, ranking fifth among tight ends in end zone targets (seven) and expected TDs (7.5). Warren finished the season third among tight ends in targets and also had three goal-line carries. The 24-year-old was already a featured target and might see even more work with Michael Pittman Jr. shipped to Pittsburgh. Warren is a quality TE1.

outlook.text: Tate was selected by the Titans with the fourth overall pick of April's draft. He didn't see a ton of volume at Ohio State, but he was efficient, averaging 13.1 yards per target (first in this rookie WR class) and 3.06 yards per route run (third) in 2025. He also paced the class in YPT for his career (11.6) and caught an impressive 75% of his targets during the 39-game span. Tate underwhelmed in the 40-yard dash at the combine (4.53 at 192 pounds), but he measured in with big hands and a large wingspan. Wide receivers selected in the top 10 handle, on average, one-quarter of their team's targets and generally deliver WR2/3 fantasy production. Cam Ward's development will be key here, but Tate's combination of talent and projected target volume is enough to make him an appealing WR3.

profile_notes.subject: Carnell Tate
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draft around the sixth round as a high-upside WR2 bet.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers endorse Tate as the episode's primary rookie-receiver target, with Waldman projecting a viable immediate WR2 outcome and higher ceiling.
profile_notes.evidence: Waldman says Tate runs the full route tree, is slated for Z/short-intermediate usage, and is a better runner after catch than assumed.
profile_notes.counterweight: He remains a rookie without an NFL record, and the highest ceiling is not guaranteed.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Tate is the exception to the episode's general rookie caution: take him at his stated market tier, then build depth later.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Tennessee Titans offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-draft Titans skill players gain volume appeal if the planned up-tempo system is confirmed.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker's key Tennessee nugget is a planned up-tempo attack, which could create more snaps for Cam Ward, Tony Pollard, Carnell Tate, and other Titans assets.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Brian Daboll brought Austin Schlottmann in at center because the coordinator trusts him to align the offense, make calls, and play fast. Tucker explicitly connects tempo and snap volume to fantasy value.
profile_notes.counterweight: Tucker says Schlottmann and right guard Volson are not considered average starters; Harris notes August tempo plans can vanish when a weak team is hit in the mouth.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the up-tempo possibility as a late-round upside input, but wait for preseason confirmation that the line can execute it.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Carnell Tate
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draft through Round 5/around Harris's 57-60 overall range; stop once camp hype pushes him into Round 4.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers like Tate's prospect profile and see a fifth-round cost as a rational rookie swing, while placing a strict cap on training-camp helium.
profile_notes.evidence: Kluge cites fourth-overall draft capital, production, and athleticism; Harris's 57-60 overall ranks align with a Round-5 choice.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Titans and their media are incentivized to publicize every contested catch, and rookie receiver hype has historically inflated ADPs beyond rational risk.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Take the upside at the baseline tier, but let a quiet camp preserve value rather than chasing promotional clips.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing AFC South & Almanac Stuff

outlook.text: Odunze opened the 2025 season with a bang, scoring five touchdowns in his first four games and producing 15-plus fantasy points in each game. Things fell apart from there, as the 2024 first-round pick went on to deliver one touchdown and two double-digit fantasy outings over his next eight games prior to missing Weeks 14 through 18 due to injury. On the plus side, Odunze remained heavily targeted throughout the season, especially near the goal line, and he is ninth in the NFL with 24 end zone targets since he was drafted. On the other hand, his connection with Caleb Williams needs work, as his 48% catch rate ranked near the basement at the position. Odunze, 24, is still ascending and has a clearer path to targets with DJ Moore out of the mix. He's a candidate for a Year 3 leap and should be valued as a WR3 with upside.

profile_notes.action_qualifier: Rank above Luther Burden while Odunze's foot remains healthy.
profile_notes.summary: Harris finds Odunze much more agile and polished on healthy tape than the offseason foot panic suggests.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Odunze played injured late last year but before that showed impressive stop-start ability for a six-foot-three receiver, double moves, quick breaks, and at times Nico Collins-like traits. Harris upgrades him to A-minus elusiveness.
profile_notes.counterweight: Odunze did look hurt late, Caleb Williams was inconsistent, and the foot remains the condition for the ranking.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Prefer Odunze to Burden if the foot continues to hold up; do not let stale foot speculation erase the healthy-film evaluation.

profile_notes.subject: Rome Odunze
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris ranks WR21; lower if foot limits practice, while Erickson could raise him from WR30 toward WR19 if fully active.
profile_notes.summary: Odunze's foot participation is the Bears camp issue most capable of changing ranks; Harris currently prefers him to Burden, unlike Erickson.
profile_notes.evidence: Odunze called his foot a new normal after last year's stress fracture. Erickson wants to see daily practice and full joint-practice work; Harris says persistent absence or sitting more series than peers would be a real concern.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both allow the quote may mean little after an offseason of recovery, and Harris expects him to be fine unless he starts missing work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor availability rather than highlights: downgrade on constrained work, but Erickson's rank offers real upside if health is unequivocal.

outlook.text: Burden enters his second NFL season as one of the most popular breakout candidates in fantasy. The 2025 second-round pick played sparingly during most of his rookie season, but flashed elite efficiency when called upon, ranking in the top five among wide receivers in catch rate (77%), yards per target (10.8), RAC (7.3) and YPRR (2.9). Burden is obviously an unproven commodity (he has two career top-20 fantasy outings, after all), but with DJ Moore no longer on the roster, he's a lock for a larger role and very well could lead Chicago in targets. He could cost a pretty penny on draft day, but Burden, 22, is a fine WR3 target with upside for more.

outlook.text: Moore was traded to Buffalo after spending his first eight NFL seasons with Carolina and Chicago. A featured target throughout most of his career, Moore was reduced to a 16% target share in 2025 -- his lowest since his rookie year in 2018. The result was a 35th-place finish in fantasy points, which ended a streak of six consecutive top 25s. Moore now heads to Buffalo with Khalil Shakir as his only roadblock to emerging as Josh Allen's No. 1 target in Buffalo's high-scoring offense. Still in his prime at age 29, Moore has the look of a fantasy WR3 with upside for more.

profile_notes.subject: D.J. Moore
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target in Round 4 at approximately WR24–25 market cost.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers view Moore as substantially underpriced for a player expected to function as Josh Allen's clear lead receiver.
profile_notes.evidence: They cite Moore's ability to get open, fit with Ben Johnson's offense, and quarterback trust as reasons the WR3 market label is too low.
profile_notes.counterweight: The main headwind is market skepticism created by his disappointing prior season in a broken quarterback environment.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Moore as a priority mid-round receiver whose role and talent support low-end WR1 upside.
profile_notes.episode_title: Five ADP Surprises Plus More Injuries

profile_notes.subject: D.J. Moore
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target at a price well below a Diggs-like Buffalo ceiling.
profile_notes.summary: Funston loves Moore's move to Buffalo and sees a realistic path to a Stefon Diggs-like connection with Josh Allen; Harris agrees with the stylistic fit.
profile_notes.evidence: Funston highlights Moore's ability to find open pockets while Allen extends plays and Buffalo's recent lack of a true receiver. Harris says Moore is exactly the type to keep a route alive when Allen buys time.
profile_notes.counterweight: Moore's depressed ADP reflects a poor prior season and apparent friction with his former coach, so the fit remains a projection rather than established production.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Moore as a discounted high-upside Buffalo receiver, while accepting that a team change creates a wide range of results.

profile_notes.subject: DJ Moore
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris is WR20 standard/WR24 PPR; Daugherty could move from mid-WR3 to low-WR2 if health and freedom reports are strong.
profile_notes.summary: Harris is already bullish on Moore as Buffalo's potential return to a real Josh Allen fantasy receiver, while Daugherty needs signs of health and less rigid usage before joining him.
profile_notes.evidence: Daugherty wants reports that Moore is healthy and allowed to freelance/get open rather than forced into Ben Johnson's structure; Harris sees the talent possibility as already baked into his ranks.
profile_notes.counterweight: Buffalo has disappointed with receivers for years, Allen has increasingly run, and good camp reports may never materialize; Harris concedes he is a Moore 'honk.'
profile_notes.practical_implication: Target Moore when price remains beneath Harris's ranking, but do not assume camp optimism guarantees a top outcome.

outlook.text: Daniels is looking to bounce back after appearing in only seven games due to injury last season. The 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year began his career with a bang, tossing 25 touchdowns and adding 891 yards and six scores with his legs in his first season. He wasn't quite as dominant when healthy last season (16.3 points per game, compared to 20.9 in 2024), but he remained a major factor with his legs (58-278-2 in seven games, three of which were partial appearances). Daniels' supporting cast is underwhelming and he'll be working with a new playcaller (David Blough), but the dual-threat ability supplies the 25-year-old with elite upside. He's a strong QB1 target.
