profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line fallout after starting LT Laremy Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps tear; Harris makes no automatic player-rank change.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps injury as a meaningful downgrade to Washington's offensive environment, though not one that can be precisely assigned to individual ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: He describes the line as thin without its starting left tackle and explicitly says losing good players hurts an offense.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris cannot draw a straight line from the injury to exactly how far Terry McLaurin or Jayden Daniels should fall, so he declines a mechanical rank adjustment.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Washington's pass-game options under review as replacement-line and protection information emerges instead of overreacting with a fixed downgrade.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Modest environmental upgrade following Diggs's signing; no Harris downgrade for Terry McLaurin.
profile_notes.summary: Harris believes Diggs gives Washington a needed credible receiver and can improve the environment for Jayden Daniels, McLaurin, and the offense without taking McLaurin out of his prime role.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris notes that all Commanders pass catchers other than McLaurin had unstable week-to-week roles, while Diggs has a distinctly stronger portfolio. More sustained offense would create additional yards, touchdowns, and possession time.
profile_notes.counterweight: Diggs's personal ceiling is tied to the offense returning to its better two-years-ago form; Washington was not good last year, and Harris says some of that may have been Marcus Mariota-related.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not downgrade McLaurin just for a normal complementary receiver addition; modestly improve the outlook for a functional Commanders passing ecosystem.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

profile_notes.subject: Jayden Daniels
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris QB7; do not raise him for glowing practice reports, only reconsider on material health news.
profile_notes.summary: Daniels retains a league-winning healthy range but carries a greatly reduced floor after a disastrous, injury-ridden second season.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris recounts knee, hamstring, and dislocated-elbow injuries, poor tape, and a failed Week 14 return; he still remembers rookie-year deep accuracy and elite running. Kingsbury is gone, the line is mostly unchanged, and the receiving group beyond McLaurin is untested.
profile_notes.counterweight: The knee injury may have removed his top gear and poisoned the environment rather than exposed permanent player decline; healthy running plus deep accuracy is still rare.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not chase inevitable positive camp headlines; draft only if willing to absorb serious health/situation volatility.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Jackson, 29, is eyeing a rebound after a disappointing, injury-plagued 2025. Jackson started the season strong (26-plus fantasy points in each of his first three games) but left Week 4 because of an injury and wasn't the same once he returned in Week 9 (13.5 fantasy points per game in his final nine outings). Jackson's overall rushing was down, but that was likely a product of him not being fully healthy, especially considering his scramble rate (8.4%) remained high. Jackson has a new coach (Jesse Minter) and playcaller (Declan Doyle), but his supporting cast is otherwise similar to a 2024 campaign in which he paced all quarterbacks in fantasy points. Assuming he's back to full health, Jackson is a strong bet for a rebound and should be valued as a high-end QB1.

profile_notes.subject: Baltimore Ravens offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor the three new interior pieces and tackle performance before assuming a strong rushing environment.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker sees Baltimore's changed interior and new under-center offense as a significant continuity risk despite potential upside.
profile_notes.evidence: He names injured-center returnee Ethan Pocic, returning Simpson, and first-round Penn State guard Vega Ioane as a substantially remade interior, while noting the rookie may switch sides. He also says neither Ronnie Stanley nor Roger Rosengarten met expectations last year.
profile_notes.counterweight: If the interior questions resolve positively, Tucker says the line could be good; Derrick Henry remains a rare durability/production outlier.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the interior transition in the downside range for Ravens runners and passing-game projections rather than presuming past line quality.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

outlook.text: Maye is entering his third NFL season and second full season as New England's starter. The 2024 No. 3 draft pick is fresh off a breakout 2025 campaign in which he finished in the top five among quarterbacks in pass completions, yards and TDs, as well as rush attempts and yards. Maye, who led the league in completion percentage (72%) and yards per attempt (8.9), trailed only Josh Allen in fantasy points (351.9), fantasy points per game (20.7) and top-10 fantasy weeks (10). The NFL MVP runner-up will need to overcome a tougher schedule, but he has a better supporting cast (including A.J. Brown) and the 24-year-old's combination of passing talent and rushing ability have him well positioned for another top-five fantasy campaign.

profile_notes.subject: Drake Maye
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris ranks him QB4 in single-QB formats, while recognizing second-year downside.
profile_notes.summary: Harris upgrades Maye's accuracy to an A and buys a premium second-year breakout.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Maye already had A arm strength, was tied for second among qualifiers in air yards at target, led the league at 72% completion, and repeatedly made on-time deep-window throws on film.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris remembers disappointing second seasons from C.J. Stroud and Jayden Daniels and notes New England's schedule was very easy.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Maye as an elite-QB option if the room lets him fall, not merely a late breakout dart.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Drake Maye
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Maintain existing rank absent injury; the profile presents exceptional promise but the camp segment does not specify a new actionable rank.
profile_notes.summary: Harris's Almanac profile frames Maye as a young quarterback with enormous promise, while the preview says camp should not materially move his established rank unless he is injured.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris introduces the profile as one of his favorites and says he will not talk much about Maye in camp because the rank is already set.
profile_notes.counterweight: The profile language deliberately recalls earlier Harris young-QB misses, so promise is not certainty; no specific camp benchmark or ranking number is supplied.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Maye at current value and do not overreact to routine Patriots camp reports.
profile_notes.episode_title: Drake Maye & Josh Allen & Previewing AFC East

outlook.text: Hurts enters his seventh NFL season and sixth as the starter in Philadelphia. The 28-year-old tossed a career-high 25 touchdowns last season, but his rushing production was way down (105-421-8 after delivering at least 139 carries, 605 yards and 10 TDs in each of the prior four seasons). Hurts' fantasy production dipped, as his 18.7 points per game was his lowest as a starter and ranked eighth at the position after three straight top-five campaigns. Hurts' supporting cast remains strong (even without A.J. Brown), and new playcaller Sean Mannion very well could add some juice back to the offense. Hurts' fantasy stock is down a bit from years past, but his dual-threat ability locks him in as a midrange QB1.

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade offense and Saquon Barkley context if interior health holds in the new scheme.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker believes Philadelphia has a high ceiling and high floor because last year's underperformance was substantially injury-driven and the new system should help blockers.
profile_notes.evidence: Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson fought through multiple injuries, surgeries, and rehabilitation; Lane Johnson missed the second half with plantar fasciitis. Tucker says the new coordinator's increased play action avoids isolating tackles in straight dropbacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: The line did not play as a top-five unit last year, and the recovery of injured interior starters must persist.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat a healthy Eagles line as a positive contextual upgrade for Barkley and the offense rather than anchoring on last year's unit ranking.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Keep outside the small trusted-offense tier until the new Mannion system succeeds in games.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers refuse to restore Philadelphia to an automatic top-offense projection after last year's collapse and coordinator replacement.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites A.J. Brown's trade, questions around the line, and the team's decision to replace the coordinator despite prior Super Bowl success. Ciely believes Mannion's changes can help but says practice and preseason cannot prove a top-five result.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense has Jalen Hurts, a strong history, and a scheme that could improve play action/middle-field work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid building draft projections on an assumed Eagles bounce-back; wait for regular-season evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Henderson enters Year 2 after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which he delivered three huge fantasy performances (28-plus points in all three) but otherwise played second fiddle to Rhamondre Stevenson (8.3 points per game in his other 14 games). Though his role was limited, Henderson was effective, averaging 5.1 yards per carry (eighth best) and catching 83% of his targets while scoring 10 touchdowns. The 2025 second-round pick is a candidate for a larger role in 2026, but it's unlikely that Stevenson will completely disappear after he also had a strong 2025. Henderson is safest as a flex option, but there's upside for a lot more if the 23-year-old is promoted to a lead role.

profile_notes.subject: TreVeyon Henderson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Downgrade for early-season redraft while pass-protection trust and third-down usage are unsettled.
profile_notes.summary: Harris is newly worried Henderson will not receive enough early third-down work to justify his prior rank.
profile_notes.evidence: He cites August/joint-practice reporting that Henderson is still not trusted in pass protection and that Patriots reporters view Rhamondre Stevenson as first among equals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris still calls Henderson a big-play threat whose winning weeks matter in an era of split workloads.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Lower Henderson from an assumed immediate lead-back outcome and require a discount for the early usage risk.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: TreVeyon Henderson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris accepts the risk around RB21-22 because explosive production can matter even on a 45% work share.
profile_notes.summary: Harris grants the role risk but believes Henderson's rare explosive-play profile makes him viable even without a full-time job.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Henderson finished RB19 despite minimal early-season play and says much of the production came from long touchdowns that still count. He compares the alternatives to backs such as Cam Skattebo, D'Andre Swift, David Montgomery, Chuba Hubbard, Tony Pollard, Jadarian Price, and Bhayshul Tuten.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris agrees that a failure to improve in pass protection, frustration from coaches, and a dry spell in big plays could make him hard to start for weeks.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Take Henderson only if you value contingent/long-play upside and can survive a frustrating weekly workload floor.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

profile_notes.subject: TreVeyon Henderson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Josh is uneasy with an end-of-Round-4/early-Round-5 RB2 cost; Harris ranks him RB21-22.
profile_notes.summary: Josh sees Henderson as an expensive contingent-upside play whose RB2 cost effectively bets on a Rhamondre Stevenson injury.
profile_notes.evidence: Josh says Stevenson had 25 carries in a late Denver game and about six TDs in the three games before playoffs, while Henderson cannot pass protect and had only nine third-down carries. He compares the role-cost tension with Blake Corum going much later.
profile_notes.counterweight: Josh agrees Henderson has league-winning potential if Stevenson misses time, and Harris argues Henderson's elite long speed can create 80-yard TDs even on limited work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft Henderson as a stable workload back; if selecting him, plan enough RB depth to cover a small or volatile early role.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

profile_notes.subject: TreVeyon Henderson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Continue lowering if Rhamondre Stevenson keeps first-team work and Henderson remains a 1B.
profile_notes.summary: Richard fears Henderson will fail to make the second-year jump and is willing to narrow or reverse the gap to Stevenson; Harris never expected Stevenson to disappear.
profile_notes.evidence: Camp reports repeatedly gave Stevenson first-team reps; last year Stevenson was the main back while Henderson was 1B, despite Henderson thriving during Stevenson's absence.
profile_notes.counterweight: Henderson had strong prior practice reports and Harris heard the team had plans for him; role can change as camp develops.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft Henderson as a secure breakout lead; demand a discount until first-team role evidence changes.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: TreVeyon Henderson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: RB21-22 baseline can rise only toward RB18-19 if credible reports show improved trust, speed, and pass protection.
profile_notes.summary: Both see Henderson as an RB2 gamble with room to improve, but only if second-year reports demonstrate a real improvement rather than empty cliché.
profile_notes.evidence: Daugherty would credit reports of more coaching trust or faster play because young backs can make genuine Year-2 gains; Harris says pass protection was the major incongruity from a profile that had called it a strength.
profile_notes.counterweight: Many beat-report observations cannot expose the vision and decision concerns Harris wants resolved, and any committee with Rhamondre Stevenson caps certainty.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Take Henderson as an RB2 upside bet; raise modestly only if protection and coaching-trust reports persist.
profile_notes.episode_title: Drake Maye & Josh Allen & Previewing AFC East

outlook.text: Tuten is positioned to take over lead-back duties in Jacksonville following the offseason departure of Travis Etienne Jr. Tuten played sparingly as a rookie, totaling 83 carries and 14 targets in 15 games. He cleared 10 touches in only one game (a 15-touch, 74-yard effort in Week 11), but he did find the end zone in all four games in which he had at least eight touches. The 2025 fourth-round pick will see some scoring regression (seven TDs on 93 touches), but he flashed in limited work, can contribute as a rusher and receiver, is working in a good offense and has only journeyman Chris Rodriguez Jr. and passing-down specialist LeQuint Allen Jr. as his competition. Tuten is still unproven, but the 23-year-old has a path to a breakout season.

profile_notes.subject: Bhayshul Tuten
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris ranks him RB28 and expects ADP to rise with positive camp noise.
profile_notes.summary: Harris can tolerate Tuten around RB28 but sees him as a fast complementary back rather than a proven lead runner.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris notes good training-camp reports and Rodriguez's relative inactivity, but says Tuten's tape showed speed with poor vision and too few big plays; he compares him to a faster Rico Dowdle or Damien Pierce.
profile_notes.counterweight: As a second-year player, Tuten can improve, and an actual main role would make him fantasy valuable.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid chasing camp hype above RB28; revisit if the role becomes clear or the market discounts committee risk.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Bhayshul Tuten
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Funston will not pay inside the top 25 RBs.
profile_notes.summary: Funston believes Tuten's market is projecting a lead role that his uneven rookie film and depth chart have not earned.
profile_notes.evidence: He cites Liam Coen-linked Chris Rodriguez as a potential early-down or goal-line threat and LaQuint Allen as a possible third-down siphon, expecting a committee rather than a guaranteed lead job.
profile_notes.counterweight: Funston grants that Tuten has upside and could succeed if pushed into a main role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Pass at a lead-RB cost and only reconsider if his price reflects a complementary role.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Bashaud Tuten
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not draft as the certain Jaguars lead unless he repeatedly stays with the ones and all camps sources identify him as the guy.
profile_notes.summary: Tuten's athletic profile makes a lead-back outcome possible, but both speakers reject ordinary practice buzz as proof in a three-skill-set committee.
profile_notes.evidence: Kluge says he would require a Puka-style unified drumbeat plus constant first-team work; Harris's film review found raw tools but questions his decision-making and tendency to run into defenders.
profile_notes.counterweight: Tuten's speed and draft-market popularity can create upside, and a true role takeover would matter.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Tuten's existing upside in mind, but do not let highlights or goal-line claims displace cheaper alternatives.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing AFC South & Almanac Stuff

outlook.text: Swift is entering his seventh NFL season and third with Chicago. The veteran back was busy as both a rusher and receiver en route to clearing 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of his first two seasons with the Bears. Though he found the end zone 10 times and finished 17th among backs in fantasy points per game last season, Swift deferred substantial work to Kyle Monangai and is likely to be in even more of a timeshare in 2026. Still in his prime at age 27, Swift continues to play at a high level (4.87 yards per carry last season), but his role in the Chicago offense figures to limit him to low-ceiling RB2/flex production.

profile_notes.subject: D'Andre Swift
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not rank above a Round-5 ceiling despite Kyle Monangai's temporary absence.
profile_notes.summary: Harris resists a major Swift upgrade because a short-term opening does not guarantee a season-long workload.
profile_notes.evidence: He cites Swift's history of losing volume when a timeshare partner returns and treats Monangai's knee injury as temporary.
profile_notes.counterweight: Swift can receive an early-season workload bump if Monangai remains unavailable.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not price a temporary depth-chart change as a full-season bell-cow role.
profile_notes.episode_title: Five ADP Surprises Plus More Injuries

profile_notes.subject: DeAndre Swift
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris still ranks him RB23, but avoid projecting an uncontested Chicago role or last year's RB13-from-Week-7 pace.
profile_notes.summary: McCormick sees Swift as a frustrating edge-seeking runner vulnerable to losing work, and Harris agrees that the annual clear-lead-back assumption has repeatedly failed.
profile_notes.evidence: McCormick says Swift bypasses what is available to chase the outside; Harris notes Kyle Monangai received more red-zone touches from Week 10 onward and that the backfield's strong late ranks came from an efficient but heavily split run game.
profile_notes.counterweight: Swift remains legitimately fast and Harris still ranks him RB23; Harris did not see Monangai as an especially good player and would draft Swift first.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Swift only at a committee-adjusted price, with expectation of volatile weeks and meaningful Monangai competition.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Chicago Bears running backs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris has Swift RB23 and Kyle Monangai RB37; do not infer a takeover from camp without injury.
profile_notes.summary: Both expect Swift and Monangai to play, but neither believes training camp can prove that the rookie has surpassed the veteran.
profile_notes.evidence: Erickson says both should get significant run. Harris calls Monangai tough and physical but not especially agile, explosive, or likely to catch extensively, leaving a substantial ranking gap behind Swift.
profile_notes.counterweight: An injury changes the entire conversation, and a shared workload can still make either player usable at the right price.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft Monangai as a presumed Swift replacement from camp reports; price both as a committee until a material event occurs.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Montgomery was traded to Houston after spending his first seven NFL seasons with Chicago and Detroit. The veteran back is coming off a down year in 2025, when he posted career lows in touches (182), yardage (908, his first season under 1,000) and fantasy points per game (9.8). Montgomery was still effective as a rusher (4.53 yards per carry, 2.28 yards after contact) but lost work to Jahmyr Gibbs and wasn't involved much as receiver. The latter doesn't figure to change much in Houston, and while Montgomery is a decent bet to pace the team in carries, second-year back Woody Marks figures to sustain a substantial offensive role. Montgomery enters his age-29 season as a touchdown-dependent flex with limited upside.

profile_notes.subject: Houston Texans offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Downgrade Texans skill players only if repeated padded-practice and controlled-scrimmage failures show the line cannot gel.
profile_notes.summary: Richard calls persistent Houston line instability a medium red flag for the offense, while Harris asks what concrete camp evidence would justify changing player ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: Reports had Houston changing lineups daily and struggling to gel; Richard says his current skill-position ranks are optimistic relative to that risk.
profile_notes.counterweight: Preseason games are less useful than controlled scrimmages, and teams can solve line combinations as Chicago did the prior year.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track repeated protection failures in meaningful practice settings before discounting Houston's fantasy assets.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: David Montgomery
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Hold the three-down-back valuation even if isolated Woody Marks pass-catching reports create late-summer ADP noise.
profile_notes.summary: Kluge views Montgomery as Houston's clear three-down leader, while Harris agrees that exhibition/camp comments cannot resolve the detailed backfield split.
profile_notes.evidence: Kluge compares the intended role to the team's prior Nick Chubb/Joe Mixon usage and says he rates Montgomery far above Marks; Harris says managers who like Montgomery's August ADP should not abandon him after one favorable Marks mention.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris believes Marks can handle some third downs, so the exact split remains unresolved until Week 1.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Montgomery at a reasonable price and ignore minor Marks helium unless tangible first-team usage changes.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing AFC South & Almanac Stuff

outlook.text: Price was selected by the Seahawks with the No. 32 overall pick of April's draft. Price managed only 280 career carries while stuck behind Jeremiyah Love at Notre Dame, but he showed well, posting a 4.13 YAC (second best in this rookie class) and 3.6 forced missed tackle rate (third best). He wasn't a factor as a receiver, however, totaling 15 receptions in 41 games. Price has a path to an immediate feature role in Seattle's run-first offense, though he may eventually defer substantial work to Zach Charbonnet (ACL recovery). Value Price as a flex, though he should land on the weekly RB2 radar while Charbonnet is sidelined.

profile_notes.subject: Jadarian Price
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Only after Round 7-8, with limited exposure.
profile_notes.summary: Waldman likes Price as a future committee lead or possible every-down back but considers his immediate redraft price too high.
profile_notes.evidence: He cites protection and reaction/footwork issues plus George Holani, Emmanuel Wilson, and likely limited Zach Charbonnet competition in a projected two- or three-back Seattle rotation.
profile_notes.counterweight: Charbonnet's ACL recovery may limit him, and Price has meaningful long-term upside.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Price as a discounted upside selection, not a presumed breakout.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Jadarian Price
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target near RB25-27 only if beat reports confirm pass protection, receiving, and feature usage; fade if ADP reaches RB19.
profile_notes.summary: Both name Price as their most important camp story because proof of protection/receiving skill and first-team trust could establish a high-value Seattle lead role before Charbonnet returns.
profile_notes.evidence: Price was first up with the first offense in a full-pads scrimmage and reportedly looked good. Richard says draft interest requires certainty he is the feature; Harris will treat credible beat reporters as his eyes on a rapidly changing depth chart.
profile_notes.counterweight: Charbonnet may return later from a January ACL tear and can take physical/goal-line work; Emmanuel Wilson or a continuing committee could also erase the clarity.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use daily role evidence and actual mid-August ADP, not rookie enthusiasm, to decide whether Price is value or a stay-away.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Jadarian Price
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Fifth- or sixth-round range is tolerable; seek repeated evidence that other Seattle RBs fade and Price can handle early work.
profile_notes.summary: Price is the Seattle back most likely to cost a meaningful pick, but the speakers do not expect ordinary camp praise to conclusively define his workload.
profile_notes.evidence: Gretch wants signals of early work and notes Price's first-round investment; he would weigh it more if George Holani and Emmanuel Wilson disappear from reports. Harris expects positive team messaging and thinks Price will likely remain a manageable fifth- or sixth-round bet.
profile_notes.counterweight: Late ACL recovery for Zach Charbonnet and several viable backs make the backfield unsettled, while Seattle is unlikely to reveal a final plan.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor role-specific evidence rather than headlines, and avoid paying for a certain workhorse outcome.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Pollard has handled a hefty 67.2% of the Titans' designed rushing attempts since his arrival two seasons ago (15.2 per game) and, even with solid efficiency, he has finished 22nd and 30th in fantasy points per game. The culprits? Tennessee's struggling offense (Pollard has exactly five TDs in both seasons) and a limited receiving role when Tyjae Spears has been healthy (Pollard's targets fell from 3.5 per game in 2024 to 2.5 per game in 2025). Barring a major leap from quarterback Cam Ward, Pollard is unlikely to deliver only the second top-20 fantasy campaign (in points per game) of his career. The 29-year-old, entering his eighth NFL season (third with Tennessee), is a low-ceiling flex.

profile_notes.subject: Tennessee Titans offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-draft Titans skill players gain volume appeal if the planned up-tempo system is confirmed.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker's key Tennessee nugget is a planned up-tempo attack, which could create more snaps for Cam Ward, Tony Pollard, Carnell Tate, and other Titans assets.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Brian Daboll brought Austin Schlottmann in at center because the coordinator trusts him to align the offense, make calls, and play fast. Tucker explicitly connects tempo and snap volume to fantasy value.
profile_notes.counterweight: Tucker says Schlottmann and right guard Volson are not considered average starters; Harris notes August tempo plans can vanish when a weak team is hit in the mouth.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the up-tempo possibility as a late-round upside input, but wait for preseason confirmation that the line can execute it.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Tony Pollard
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Reasonable at a discounted middle-round price; downgrade if Singleton is healthy/involved or Spears repeatedly takes first-team workload.
profile_notes.summary: Harris views Pollard as a serviceable veteran whose attractiveness depends on price, while Kluge sees new-regime depth-chart risk rather than a talent collapse.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says he would draft Pollard in Round 7 but not Round 3; Kluge notes that both Pollard and Spears are on expiring deals and that a healthy Singleton could create a three-headed committee.
profile_notes.counterweight: Pollard has retained the job for years, and normal youth bias can wrongly presume every younger back must replace an incumbent.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Hold Pollard at a proper discount, but reduce exposure if actual camp roles point to a newly fragmented workload.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing AFC South & Almanac Stuff

outlook.text: After producing one season with 1,000 yards and a top-20 fantasy finish during his first six NFL campaigns, Sutton has achieved both in each of the past two years. The 2018 second-round pick's target share actually dipped from 24% in 2024 to 21% in 2025, but he remained heavily involved near the goal line and has now ranked in the top 12 among receivers in TDs each of the last three seasons. In fact, Sutton has now finished in the top 10 at the position in end zone targets four years in a row, tying for third with 56 during the span. Sutton will remain one of Bo Nix's go-to targets, but now 30 years old and with added target competition in Jaylen Waddle, he's best valued as a fantasy WR3.

profile_notes.subject: Denver Broncos wide receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not elevate Troy Franklin or Pat Bryant on four-wide camp headlines without actual sustainable usage.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers reject a reported Broncos move toward more four-wide formations as a reason to project multiple new fantasy receivers.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Denver threw from four-wide only 15 times last year, while Behrens categorizes the report with familiar but unfulfilled preseason role claims.
profile_notes.counterweight: An injury could alter the depth chart, and Courtland Sutton/Waddle opinions differ, but they do not believe the offense and quarterback can support three or four viable fantasy receivers.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Franklin and Bryant off priority lists unless game-relevant volume emerges.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Pittman was traded to the Steelers after spending his first six NFL seasons with the Colts. The 2020 second-round pick handled a hefty 23.6% of Indianapolis' targets during his tenure, which helped him to four top-20 fantasy campaigns. Pittman has reached 800 receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while primarily operating as a short-to-intermediate target. The role has limited his scoring (he has 25 TDs in 95 games) and that may not change much with DK Metcalf on the other side in Pittsburgh. Of course, Pittman will be a featured target in an offense led by Aaron Rodgers. That's enough to put the 28-year-old squarely in the weekly WR3 mix.

profile_notes.subject: Michael Pittman
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Prefer in PPR or receiver-needy early-RB builds for safer production than boom-bust alternatives.
profile_notes.summary: Harris and Harmon view Pittman as a safer Steelers receiver choice whose style fits Rodgers, especially when a roster needs catches rather than volatile upside.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon says Pittman could lead the team in receptions because of the Rodgers fit; Harris ranks him ahead of Metcalf in PPR and cites his possession-oriented profile.
profile_notes.counterweight: Pittman's age/physical style and the offense's overall ceiling limit a breakout expectation.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Pittman as a roster-construction-based target for reception floor, not as an upside bet.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: Pittsburgh Steelers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a stable, projectable offense; do not manufacture large camp-based projections.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see a reasonably high/projectable Steelers floor if Aaron Rodgers remains healthy, without an exciting ceiling case.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Mike McCarthy's high-floor play calling, a settled enough offensive line, and known top receivers; Harris calls the roster full of good professionals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both retain concern that Rodgers may have declined further and will avoid contact, limiting offensive aggression.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep established Steelers values near their baseline projections instead of reacting sharply to routine camp headlines.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Pierce has spent the majority of his first four NFL seasons as a situational deep threat, but that didn't stop him from becoming one of the league's highest-paid wide receivers during the offseason. The 2022 second-round pick is fresh off a career year and he's now paced all receivers in YPR, YPT and aDOT each of the last two seasons. However, he's yet to finish a season better than 48th at WR in target share (18%), 42nd in targets (84), 45th in catches (47), 18th in yards (1,003), 18th in TDs (seven) or 25th in fantasy PPG. Of course, with Michael Pittman Jr. no longer in the mix, Pierce is a good bet for a more well-rounded role as Daniel Jones' top target. There's some risk here, but the 26-year-old's hefty contract suggests we should take him seriously as a fantasy WR3.

profile_notes.subject: Alec Pierce and Keenan Allen
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Push Pierce into double-digit rounds; consider Allen only as a very late flier.
profile_notes.summary: Harris reads Indianapolis signing Allen as negative information about confidence in Pierce's recovery timeline, but not as proof Allen becomes an immediate fantasy starter.
profile_notes.evidence: The contract size and Pierce's lingering ankle problem support a depth-chart downgrade for Pierce.
profile_notes.counterweight: Allen's age and uncertain role keep him from becoming more than a late selection.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid paying for Pierce's prior role and use Allen only as inexpensive bench speculation.
profile_notes.episode_title: Five ADP Surprises Plus More Injuries

profile_notes.subject: Alec Pierce
profile_notes.action_qualifier: WR40 standard / WR43 PPR (about Round 8); do not draft as a true starter while ankle status is unresolved.
profile_notes.summary: Harris lowers Pierce materially because the ankle rehabilitation is not progressing as the team expected.
profile_notes.evidence: Pierce had ankle surgery in March, was supposed to be practicing by this point, and reportedly received a second PRP injection. Harris says a missed camp creates risk of a delay lasting weeks or months and of poor game readiness.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris still believes Pierce's long-term career upswing is intact and allows that he could suddenly become healthy and turn into a draft bargain.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not select Pierce as a starting receiver now; monitor the ankle and be prepared to lower him further if the news worsens.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Alec Pierce
profile_notes.action_qualifier: WR33 standard / WR36 PPR with additional downside while no return timeline exists.
profile_notes.summary: Pierce's continuing absence after ankle surgery lowers Harris's redraft outlook further.
profile_notes.evidence: The Colts coach reportedly gave no timeline, despite GM Chris Ballard having said nine days earlier that Pierce was one or two weeks away; Harris warns that players unable to practice all August often are not immediately effective in Week 1.
profile_notes.counterweight: Week 1 remains more than a month away, so the injury can still resolve before the season.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid drafting Pierce as if a quick return is assured; monitor the next one to two weeks for a real practice timeline.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

profile_notes.subject: Alec Pierce
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor recovery from summer ankle surgery and practice return; target only at a discount if health clears.
profile_notes.summary: Harris calls Pierce one of the skill-position players who most changed his opinion in 2025, and Zachariason agrees that his improved routes and elite downfield/contested-catch work are real.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris saw Pierce make stop routes for the first time, with speed forcing defensive overreaction; Zachariason cites improved zone awareness, body control, and exceptional contested-catch results after a raw entry profile.
profile_notes.counterweight: The immediate obstacle is major summer ankle surgery and lack of practice; Harris also still worries about inconsistent hands. His linear, lighter build limits the assumption of a complete target-hog role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft Pierce as if healthy now; follow practice participation, then use a late discount for the expanded route-tree upside.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

outlook.text: Harrison's pro career is off to a slow start after he was selected with the No. 4 overall pick back in 2024. The Ohio State product was serviceable as a rookie (885 yards and eight TDs), but he missed five full games and was limited in others en route to a 41-608-4 receiving line in 2025. Harrison has finished 41st and 39th, respectively, in fantasy PPG despite a massive role near the goal line (he's third in the NFL in end zone targets since he was drafted and finished both seasons in the top five). Harrison is only entering his prime at age 24 and perhaps he'll make a Year 3 leap with new coach Mike LaFleur calling the plays and with Kyler Murray no longer under center. Harrison has the raw talent to make him well worth post-hype consideration in the middle rounds.

profile_notes.subject: Marvin Harrison Jr.
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris is not drafting him at his current profile; he ranks Michael Wilson two WR spots higher at WR38 versus WR40.
profile_notes.summary: Harris calls Harrison a Film Room Zero because he has not yet supplied the separation or all-around NFL tape that his pedigree and draft slot imply.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Harrison has not separated on long balls or routes; he sees contested-catch skill but little distinctly better than Quentin Johnston's tape, while preferring Wilson's ball skills, speed, and routes.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harrison has legitimate context—late-stage Kyler Murray play, appendectomy, concussion, and heel trouble—and young players can improve; McCormick says he is not ready to call him simply bad.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not buy the generational prospect narrative without a discount; choose alternatives with demonstrated separation until the film changes.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Marvin Harrison Jr.
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Josh is interested around projected Rounds 6-7, but not if late-camp hype restores a Round-4 cost.
profile_notes.summary: Josh sees Harrison as a tempting but uncomfortable post-hype bet: the cost may now be tolerable, but his role and development remain unsettled.
profile_notes.evidence: Josh cites the former generational-prospect profile, a possible new offensive system, his belief that Trey McBride is the team's best receiver, practice-drop concern, and an offense unlikely to throw as much as last year.
profile_notes.counterweight: A third-year breakout remains possible, and the lower WR3-like cost can pay off even with a modest 1,000-yard, six-to-seven-TD season.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Only take the discounted rebound shot; do not chase a preseason narrative that reprices Harrison close to his old premium.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

profile_notes.subject: Marvin Harrison Jr.
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Take a discounted shot in the broad WR40-type range, not at the premium price attached to his first two seasons.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers find Harrison difficult: his first two seasons and film were disappointing, but they do not rule out later fulfillment of his elite prospect profile at a much cheaper cost.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites appendicitis and other injuries but says Wilson outproduced him; Gretch says Harrison was highly productive in college and some per-route measures are not disqualifyingly poor.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both say he has looked worse on film than the numbers, and there is no camp development likely to settle the question.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Take Harrison only as a measured upside bet, not as a presumed return to prospect-hype production.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

profile_notes.subject: Cardinals quarterback situation
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Prefer Jacoby Brissett stability for Cardinals pass-catcher volume; lower expectations if Carson Beck earns substantial early work.
profile_notes.summary: Gretch treats the Brissett-versus-Beck outcome as central to Arizona receiver/tight-end volume, while Harris agrees the rookie quarterback would be less exciting.
profile_notes.evidence: Gretch says Brissett's quick release and willingness to throw generated huge target volume, including Wilson's 18-target game and two 15-target games, whereas young quarterbacks can hold the ball and take sacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: A new offense could change deployment regardless of starter, and the transcript does not declare either quarterback the confirmed season-long choice.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use camp/preseason quarterback evidence to refine Cardinals pass-catcher projections rather than treating last year's targets as automatic.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

profile_notes.subject: Arizona Cardinals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not write off the offense because of rebuilding expectations; balance possible skill-position value against the league's hardest projected schedule.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Arizona as a possible market-value offense because it is being declared hopeless, while Gretch sees meaningful skill talent but acknowledges a difficult environment.
profile_notes.evidence: They cite McBride, Love, Harrison, Wilson, and backfield depth; Gretch says the projected schedule is the NFL's hardest and the club is a large underdog early.
profile_notes.counterweight: The schedule and quarterback uncertainty can make running-back and passing-game efficiency difficult.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Consider discounted Cardinals talent individually, rather than treating the offense as automatically unproductive.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Metcalf returns for Year 2 in Pittsburgh after a solid but unspectacular debut season. The ex-Seahawk missed two games and finished outside the top 20 receivers in targets, catches and yardage (career-low 850), but still did just enough to produce a 21st-place finish in fantasy PPG (his fifth top-25 in his last six seasons). Metcalf soaked up 11 end zone targets and is up to 107 for his career, which leads the NFL since his debut in 2019. The 28-year-old has added target competition this season in the form of Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard, so while he'll certainly remain busy, a slight dip in usage is probable. Metcalf should be valued as a back-end WR3.

profile_notes.subject: DK Metcalf
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Keep near baseline ranks; small reports of more slot usage do not warrant a major upgrade.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers resist changing their Metcalf view merely because he may move around more in the Steelers formation.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon says an increase from a low slot rate may be marginal and expects Pittman/Bernard to fill Z/inside roles; Harris leaves his Steelers ranks unchanged.
profile_notes.counterweight: Fewer multiple-tight-end sets could create some additional slot snaps, but that is not evidence of a transformed player or role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Metcalf at existing value and avoid paying extra for generalized alignment buzz.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: Pittsburgh Steelers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a stable, projectable offense; do not manufacture large camp-based projections.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see a reasonably high/projectable Steelers floor if Aaron Rodgers remains healthy, without an exciting ceiling case.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Mike McCarthy's high-floor play calling, a settled enough offensive line, and known top receivers; Harris calls the roster full of good professionals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both retain concern that Rodgers may have declined further and will avoid contact, limiting offensive aggression.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep established Steelers values near their baseline projections instead of reacting sharply to routine camp headlines.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Tyson was selected by the Saints with the No. 8 overall pick of April's draft. He is a versatile receiver with decent size who led this rookie class with a 35% target share during the nine weeks he was active in 2025. Injuries cost him time during all four collegiate seasons, but he still managed a 158-2,282-22 receiving line in 33 games, posting a strong 2.73 YPRR along the way (third best in this class). Tyson suffered a hamstring injury in August and will miss a month or two of the regular season prior to taking over as the Saints' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave. Once healthy, Tyson has a path to a substantial role in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough and could find himself on the WR3 radar. Of course, with the injury, he's only worth a late flier.

profile_notes.subject: Jordyn Tyson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Let ADP fall after the hamstring issue; avoid assuming an early starter role.
profile_notes.summary: Tyson's talent is clear, but both speakers view current injury and process risk as a redraft landmine.
profile_notes.evidence: He is seeking hamstring specialists; Waldman says his aggressive, dynamic movement has produced injuries and can make route/catch execution unpredictable.
profile_notes.counterweight: Waldman says some plays look like the best receiver in the class.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft only after a meaningful discount and do not build an early-season lineup around him.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Jordan Tyson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Sixth-round upside receiver swing only if fully healthy; exit on meaningful soft-tissue or repeated side-field news.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Tyson as a talented rookie whose draft cost can be defensible in a flat receiver market, but his health is the only meaningful camp determinant.
profile_notes.evidence: The speakers consider the upside commensurate with other high-end recent rookie receivers and say opportunity is already apparent; Tyson's availability is what could change.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris expects rookie hype to make Tyson pricier than he personally ranks, and even a minor recurring hip/knee/soft-tissue issue would create substantial concern.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft only when health reports remain clean; do not rationalize a recurring injury as ordinary rookie maintenance.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Right when it seemed like Pitts might never live up to the hype, the 2021 No. 4 pick put together the best season of his career. Pitts finished second among tight ends in routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy points, setting career highs in all but the yardage category. He scored five touchdowns and has increased his total in that category (by exactly one) each season in the league. Pitts did a big chunk of his damage with Kirk Cousins under center (some with WR Drake London sidelined), which is notable as Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. are set to battle for the Atlanta QB job. There's some obvious risk here considering Pitts finished 17th or lower in PPG three straight seasons before 2025, but he nonetheless enters his age-25 season as a priority target in the Atlanta offense. Consider him a midrange TE1.

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Kyle Pitts
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not price him as a TE3 breakout based on an isolated Week 15 three-touchdown spike.
profile_notes.summary: Harris and McCormick reject Pitts's headline finish because the film still shows poor hands, rounded routes, little suddenness, and no reliable playmaking after the catch.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says that absent the Week 15 three-touchdown game against Tampa, Pitts would have been TE15 rather than TE3; he also cites zero plays of 20-plus yards after catch. McCormick sees routes rounded rather than sharply cut and no compensating blocker value.
profile_notes.counterweight: Pitts is undeniably fast and tall, and injuries to Drake London and others plus Kirk Cousins's late-season volume may have created a situationally better stretch; sports outcomes can change.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid drafting Pitts as a solved breakout and prefer a tight end whose role and film are less dependent on one touchdown eruption.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Kyle Pitts
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris TE10 is still a full stay-away; ignore every August redemption headline.
profile_notes.summary: Harris says no camp development could persuade him to draft Pitts, because the annual redemption cycle has repeatedly converted a weak profile into an expensive bet.
profile_notes.evidence: Pitts was TE22 through Week 12 last year, and Harris expects beat writers to promote him as transformed/ready/leader despite that history.
profile_notes.counterweight: A different quarterback or offense could create a better outcome, and Harris's TE10 technically recognizes positional upside.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Fade Pitts at any price that depends on an August narrative rather than established role and production.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

profile_notes.subject: Atlanta Falcons passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor Michael Penix recovery versus Tua Tagovailoa starting; it affects Drake London/Kyle Pitts predictability more than Bijan Robinson's elite draft status.
profile_notes.summary: The Falcons' actionable camp fork is whether Penix can take first-team work and be ready Week 1 or whether Tua begins the season, with the quarterback mostly changing receiver/tight-end certainty.
profile_notes.evidence: McCormick prefers Tua's timing and predictability for London/Pitts, while Harris worries Tua should not be playing and might feel better if Penix wins. Both say Bijan's elite selection would not become a no-draft solely from Penix.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither option is a clean projection: Tua may be degraded, Penix's NFL competence is unproven, and the new coaching environment adds uncertainty.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track actual first-team recovery evidence; adjust passing-game players more readily than Bijan.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Fannin is a rising star at the tight end position after overcoming the presence of David Njoku and a quarterback merry-go-round to produce a 72-731-6 receiving line (plus 7-13-1 rushing) as a 21-year-old rookie last season. The third-round pick's 108 targets rank eighth all time by a rookie tight end, and he finished no lower than eighth at the position in catches, yards, touchdowns and fantasy points last season. Fannin figures to see some touchdown regression (seven TDs, 3.8 expected, three end zone targets) and Cleveland still has quarterback question marks, but with Njoku gone, Fannin has a path to improve a bit on what was already a healthy 22% target share. He's a solid TE1 target.

profile_notes.subject: Harold Fannin
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Fade in redraft Rounds 6–7; retain a positive long-term dynasty view.
profile_notes.summary: Josh likes Fannin's long-term talent but considers the current redraft cost too aggressive.
profile_notes.evidence: The immediate concerns are Cleveland's quarterback play, a crowded target picture, and cheaper tight ends available later.
profile_notes.counterweight: A quarterback improvement could unlock the talent, and the dynasty endorsement remains intact.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not confuse the redraft fade with a dynasty sell; wait for a cheaper tight end in seasonal leagues.
profile_notes.episode_title: More Flag Players & Cousin Josh's Frag Players

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Conditionally upgrade pass catchers if quarterback play becomes merely passable.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers argue that Cleveland does not need excellent quarterback play for its pass catchers to beat depressed prices.
profile_notes.evidence: The derived analysis identifies KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, and Harold Fannin as players who could benefit if Shedeur Sanders or Dylan Gabriel is simply adequate.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither host expresses confidence that the quarterback outcome will actually be adequate.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Cleveland receivers and tight ends as conditional value rather than automatic targets, and update after credible quarterback evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat early-season cohesion as uncertain after a nearly complete starting-line overhaul.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker calls Cleveland's nearly wholesale replacement of the starting line an unprecedented continuity experiment with high early variance.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Teven Jenkins had been on the team but was not a starter, and cites Spencer Fano, Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins, and Titus Howard as new additions. Tucker grants that most have played meaningful NFL football.
profile_notes.counterweight: The individual additions have shown positive things and could gel by December; Harris also says he is not qualified to make every technique judgment and is not down on every member.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid assuming immediate line quality for Browns assets; prioritize early-season evidence of the new group functioning together.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Browns quarterback competition
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade Browns pass catchers modestly only if Shedeur Sanders wins; avoid treating Deshaun Watson as equivalent.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers believe the Browns quarterback outcome materially affects pass catchers and prefer Sanders over Watson.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Watson's poor form and back-to-back camp interceptions, while saying Sanders can be a flawed but functional NFL passer; Harris says his modest Browns ranks assume Sanders rather than Watson.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris says Sanders must release the ball faster and cannot recreate Colorado-style extended plays; neither calls him an exciting superflex starter.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Browns receiver projections modest, but treat a Sanders starting outcome as a meaningful improvement over Watson.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: Harold Fannin
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Only draft as a TE1 if postoperative groin reports remain positive; health is the immediate prerequisite.
profile_notes.summary: Fannin is being drafted as a TE1, but the speakers identify his offseason groin surgery and ongoing health reporting as the central near-term question.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon directly says monitoring Judkins and Fannin health reports is probably most important because Fannin is recovering from groin surgery.
profile_notes.counterweight: The episode does not supply a new target-share projection or a negative recovery report; the concern is monitoring rather than a declared fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Require continued healthy practice participation before relying on Fannin at a starting tight-end price.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: LaPorta has settled in as one of the league's top tight ends, but the 2023 second-round pick simply hasn't been able to match the fantasy success he enjoyed as a rookie. Since posting an 86-889-10 receiving line in 17 games that first season, LaPorta has totaled a 100-1,215-10 line in 25 games over the past two seasons. LaPorta's 2025 campaign was cut short by a back injury, otherwise he was well on his way to his third straight top-10 fantasy campaign (he finished seventh in PPG). The 25-year-old joins Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs as the clear "Core Four" targets in a good, pass-friendly Detroit offense, and is thus a solid fantasy TE1.

profile_notes.subject: Sam LaPorta
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Pay extra attention to back health; August otherwise should not change the baseline rank.
profile_notes.summary: LaPorta's back recovery is the meaningful Lions health story because his absence appeared to change the offense and may affect Williams's target outlook.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says LaPorta's ruptured discs were not a trivial injury despite reports he is in better shape; Erickson says the offense looked notably different after he was lost and had little depth behind him.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither speaker expects normal August activity to change their underlying LaPorta view, and Harris allows Williams's usage change may have had a different cause.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Follow LaPorta's participation and recovery more closely than generic Lions camp notes; use a setback as a real input for the entire passing-game distribution.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Burrow will attempt to bounce back after injuries limited him to eight games in 2025. The 29-year-old has now missed at least six games in three of his six pro seasons, including two of his past three. Burrow was still a starting-caliber fantasy quarterback when active last season (top-12 scorer in five of his final six games), but his ceiling was limited by a near complete lack of rushing (41 yards on 14 carries). Burrow was a top-five scoring quarterback in each of his past two full seasons, and coach Zac Taylor cut back a bit on his extreme pass-heavy playcalling last season, so Burrow is best valued as more of a midrange QB1 than an elite option.

profile_notes.subject: Cincinnati Bengals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not change elite-player ranks on camp drills; monitor credible evidence of more under-center and modern-concept usage.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers regard Cincinnati's core as settled and already elite, with offensive evolution as a possible path from top-five to No. 1 production.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon wants to see Joe Burrow under center more and the offense move beyond an almost exclusively shotgun approach; he notes incremental increases in Chase motion and varied alignment.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harmon repeatedly says camp talk will not force rank changes for Burrow, Chase, Higgins, or Brown, and the preference may remain Burrow's existing style.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat schematic reports as upside context, not a reason to chase already-expensive Bengals players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Dart is a strong 2026 breakout candidate following an impressive rookie campaign in which he delivered eight top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for fifth most) despite playing the bulk of the snaps in only 12 games. Dart was solid as a passer but elite as a rusher, finishing in the top five at the position in rushing attempts, yards, TDs and carries inside the 5-yard line. Dart's aggressive playing style raises concerns about his durability, but it also provides the 23-year-old with elite fantasy upside. With a new coaching staff led by John Harbaugh and a new playcaller in Matt Nagy, as well as an improved supporting cast that includes a healthy Malik Nabers and newcomers Isaiah Likely and Darnell Mooney, Dart is best valued as a midrange QB1 with a high ceiling.

profile_notes.subject: Jaxson Dart
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid before approximately Round 7.
profile_notes.summary: Josh believes Dart's rushing appeal and short hot streak have pushed his price beyond what the passing profile supports.
profile_notes.evidence: Accuracy concerns, a significant injury history, a shaky receiving group, and concern about the playcaller are cited.
profile_notes.counterweight: Rushing production could still create fantasy value even if the passing remains uneven.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Wait for cheaper quarterbacks with stronger passing floors rather than drafting Dart at the cited premium.
profile_notes.episode_title: More Flag Players & Cousin Josh's Frag Players

profile_notes.subject: Jaxson Dart
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris is out based on his negative tape evaluation.
profile_notes.summary: Harris explicitly fades Dart despite Funston's broader Giants swing-player framing.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says he did not like Dart's tape at all and calls him much more of a fade.
profile_notes.counterweight: Funston identifies Dart as part of the Giants' high-variance group, but does not make a direct positive fantasy recommendation.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft Dart on the premise that the Giants' volatility alone creates upside; Harris's evaluation is a direct talent-based fade.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: New York Giants offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat Giants outcomes as high-variance rather than projecting certainty into Week 1 roles.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers identify the Giants as a team full of volatile fantasy outcomes centered on Skattebo, Jaxson Dart, and Malik Nabers.
profile_notes.evidence: Funston says all three carry wild ranges of outcomes and calls the team fascinating from a fantasy perspective. Harris agrees on Skattebo and Nabers as swing possibilities.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris sharply differs on Dart, saying he disliked the tape and is out on him; the team label is an uncertainty signal, not a blanket endorsement.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not stack Giants assumptions as settled facts; assess each player separately and demand a price that accommodates role and quarterback uncertainty.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Jackson Dart
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid a QB7-style projection until his throwing accuracy, decisions, and self-protection materially improve.
profile_notes.summary: Harris and McCormick fade Dart's current fantasy hype because they view his reckless rushing style and inconsistent passing as unsustainable.
profile_notes.evidence: McCormick estimates 40% of Dart's fantasy points came from frantic running; Harris cites poor accuracy, vision, across-body throws, avoidable mistakes, and repeated exposure to concussions and contact.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both allow that young quarterbacks can improve, and Harris says he will revise the evaluation if the new tape changes; supporters may accept injury risk for weekly rushing-touchdown upside.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft on the rushing run alone; require evidence of competent, sustainable passing and safer decision-making.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

outlook.text: Evans signed with the 49ers after spending his first 12 NFL seasons with the Buccaneers. The future Hall of Famer famously opened his career with 11 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, but that streak ended when he missed nine games due to injury last season. Even when active, Evans wasn't his usual, productive self, delivering only one weekly fantasy finish better than 23rd and none better than 11th. Now 33 years old, Evans is past his prime, but he's in line for a decent chunk of the targets, especially near the goal line, in Kyle Shanahan's high-scoring offense. Evans is best valued as a touchdown-dependent WR3/flex with more value in non-PPR formats.

profile_notes.subject: Mike Evans
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris moves him to WR29 standard and WR32 PPR after Pearsall's absence, but expects the market to overcorrect.
profile_notes.summary: Harris raises Evans for opportunity but maintains that he is a declining player rather than a restored prime receiver.
profile_notes.evidence: With Pearsall out, Evans can still win contested catches and score touchdowns, creating additional practical opportunity.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris expects the market's rise to exceed his own and says Evans is not the player he was a few years ago.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Accept the modest injury-driven upgrade only if drafters do not price him as a former peak version.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Mike Evans
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Raise for Pearsall's absence, but do not chase if the market already moves him well above Harris's rank.
profile_notes.summary: Harris upgrades Evans as the clearest currently draftable San Francisco receiver after Pearsall's knee setback.
profile_notes.evidence: He expects possession and end-zone work to support Evans even if deep-play ability has declined.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris says Evans looked slow last year and expects his ADP to rise after the Pearsall news; he does not expect to roster much at that rising cost.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Consider Evans for role security, but stop at a market price that already captures the Pearsall benefit.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: A strong finish to the 2025 season has made Washington one of the fascinating breakout candidates of 2026. Though he's primarily worked as a situational/depth player since being drafted in the sixth round in 2023, Washington has flashed when asked to play a bigger role. In 21 games since the start of 2024 in which he had a route participation above 50%, Washington handled a 20% target share and averaged 12.2 fantasy PPG. He surprisingly emerged as Jacksonville's top target late last season, which included a stretch of four straight games with at least nine targets and 19 fantasy points to end the season. The 24-year-old appears to have cemented a big role in Jacksonville, though Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas Jr. and perhaps Travis Hunter will battle him for snaps and targets. Washington should be targeted for your flex spot.
