outlook.text: Watson has had quite the boom/bust NFL career and that was on full display in 2025. After missing the first seven games due to injury, Watson returned and scored 18-plus fantasy points four times, but averaged 7.7 in his other six outings. The oft-injured 2022 second-round pick has still yet to play a full regular season, but has weirdly finished with between 611 and 620 receiving yards in three of his four campaigns. Though Watson has yet to deliver a top-40 fantasy season, he's been extremely efficient in his vertical role, ranking exactly second in average depth of target, YPR and YPT each of the last two seasons. Durability is an obvious concern, but the 27-year-old could very well lead Green Bay in targets following Romeo Doubs' departure. Watson should be valued as a volatile flex option with added value in non-PPR leagues.

Golden is eyeing a Year 2 leap following a disappointing rookie season in which he was limited to 39 touches and failed to find the end zone in 14 regular-season games. Golden was limited to 53% of the snaps and never cleared six targets in a single outing. Some optimism was generated from Golden's 4-84-1 receiving line in the playoff loss to Chicago, but even with Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks gone, it's unclear if he will actually see a big boost in usage in Matt LaFleur's offense considering that no Green Bay receiver has cleared a 21% target share since Davante Adams' departure prior to 2022. The speedy Golden, who also contributes as a rusher, is a recent first-round pick entering his second season. He's worth a speculative middle-round flier.

profile_notes.subject: Matthew Golden
profile_notes.action_qualifier: After pick 100 or in the double-digit-round receiver range.
profile_notes.summary: Eisenberg considers Golden a ceiling swing because Green Bay's targets may finally concentrate; Harris agrees the second-year receiver has an accessible upside path.
profile_notes.evidence: Golden scored no regular-season touchdown last year, but Eisenberg identifies 135 vacated targets and a possible three-receiver structure; Harris adds that Matt LaFleur could give him both downfield and designed horizontal work.
profile_notes.counterweight: Eisenberg worries Golden could remain a sacrificial X receiver running mostly deep routes, and Tucker Kraft's health could alter target distribution.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Golden as a bench receiver with a high payoff, rather than relying on him as a weekly starter.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Matthew Golden
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris WR54 and Erickson WR50; only a Round-14-type flyer is acceptable to Harris.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers reject Golden's predictable first-round-rookie training-camp rise because neither liked his prior tape.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says he will not raise Golden no matter how impressed beat reporters become; Erickson recalls poor film, including a deeply underthrown early-season ball on one of Golden's rare deep separations.
profile_notes.counterweight: Green Bay has a narrower receiver tree after departures and injuries, so opportunity arguments exist, but neither sees that as sufficient.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Let others pay for camp helium; draft only at a near-free cost if accepting a long-shot outcome.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: After averaging 4.3 targets and 7.6 fantasy points per game during his first 38 NFL games, Wilson broke out with Jacoby Brissett under center during the final eight games of 2025, averaging 11.0 targets and 21.2 fantasy PPG. The stretch also coincided with Marvin Harrison Jr. dealing with health issues, and it's worth noting that Wilson's receiving lines in the three games Harrison was active weren't quite as good (3-36-0, 2-52-1, 5-89-1). A healthy Harrison (along with TE Trey McBride) figures to lead to a return to earth for Wilson, but the 26-year-old did enough late last season to warrant WR4/flex consideration in drafts.

profile_notes.subject: Michael Wilson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draft near Marvin Harrison at a discount when the market still materially separates them; quarterback continuity with Brissett improves the case.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers keep Wilson close to Harrison because Wilson was the more productive and better-fitting Cardinals receiver last year.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says there is no world in which Wilson did not produce better than Harrison; Gretch highlights his Brissett connection and unusually large target games.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense, quarterback, and receiver roles can change, and Harrison retains superior pedigree and potential untapped growth.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Wilson as a legitimate late receiver target, especially if Brissett remains the starter.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

profile_notes.subject: Cardinals quarterback situation
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Prefer Jacoby Brissett stability for Cardinals pass-catcher volume; lower expectations if Carson Beck earns substantial early work.
profile_notes.summary: Gretch treats the Brissett-versus-Beck outcome as central to Arizona receiver/tight-end volume, while Harris agrees the rookie quarterback would be less exciting.
profile_notes.evidence: Gretch says Brissett's quick release and willingness to throw generated huge target volume, including Wilson's 18-target game and two 15-target games, whereas young quarterbacks can hold the ball and take sacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: A new offense could change deployment regardless of starter, and the transcript does not declare either quarterback the confirmed season-long choice.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use camp/preseason quarterback evidence to refine Cardinals pass-catcher projections rather than treating last year's targets as automatic.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

profile_notes.subject: Arizona Cardinals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not write off the offense because of rebuilding expectations; balance possible skill-position value against the league's hardest projected schedule.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Arizona as a possible market-value offense because it is being declared hopeless, while Gretch sees meaningful skill talent but acknowledges a difficult environment.
profile_notes.evidence: They cite McBride, Love, Harrison, Wilson, and backfield depth; Gretch says the projected schedule is the NFL's hardest and the club is a large underdog early.
profile_notes.counterweight: The schedule and quarterback uncertainty can make running-back and passing-game efficiency difficult.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Consider discounted Cardinals talent individually, rather than treating the offense as automatically unproductive.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Thomas is one of the biggest wild cards in fantasy after a roller-coaster start to his career. The 2024 first-round pick was fantasy's No. 4-scoring wide receiver as a rookie, but only played at that WR1 level with Mac Jones under center. Thomas averaged 5.8 targets and 14.4 fantasy PPG with Trevor Lawrence under center that season, and was even worse with Lawrence in 2025 (6.2 targets, 9.9 PPG). With Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Travis Hunter in the mix, Thomas was utilized as more of a vertical threat in 2025 (his 14.4 aDOT was fourth highest), which led to a big dip in catch rate and touchdowns, as well as more drops. The Jaguars offense is suddenly very crowded, so Thomas is more likely to be a boom/bust flex than he is the superstar we expected one year ago. The 23-year-old's raw talent makes him worth middle-round consideration.

outlook.text: Lawrence is entering his sixth NFL season after a breakout 2025 in which he ranked no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in pass attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns, as well as top 10 in carries, yards and TDs. He reeled off seven consecutive top-10 fantasy outings to finish the season. Lawrence's efficiency has been fine, at best, but he continues to generate big volume, having finished in the top 10 among QBs in pass and rush attempts in each of his four full seasons. With a strong, deep group of pass catchers and Liam Coen back as playcaller, the 26-year-old is well positioned for mid-to-back-end QB1 production.

Prescott is entering his 11th NFL season following a successful 2025 campaign in which he led the NFL in completions and ranked no lower than fourth in dropbacks, pass attempts, passing yards and passing TDs. Prescott appeared in all 17 games and has now finished no worse than 11th in fantasy points during all seven seasons in which he has played at least 16 games. Last season, his nine top-10 fantasy weeks were tied for third most at the position. Prescott is no longer much of a threat with his legs, but he should continue to put up big passing numbers with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens at his disposal. The 33-year-old is a fringe QB1.

profile_notes.subject: Dallas Cowboys skill players
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ignore Cowboys camp hype absent injury or a genuine George Pickens hold-in.
profile_notes.summary: Dallas offers little camp information likely to change established fantasy evaluations.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris describes annual hype around Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, while Ciely says the relevant fantasy roles have little genuine competition. Pickens signed his tag and attended work despite a possible future contract dispute.
profile_notes.counterweight: A Pickens hold-in could hurt early games, and injuries or unavoidably negative reports would be meaningful.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Filter positive Cowboys clips out of draft decisions; only move players for material availability news.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Nix enters his third NFL season after finishing exactly seventh among quarterbacks in fantasy points during each of his first two campaigns. Nix's passing efficiency has a ways to go (career 6.5 yards per attempt), but his dual-threat ability has kept him in the weekly QB1 mix. Nix has finished both seasons no lower than 11th in pass attempts, completions, passing TDs, carries, rushing yards and rushing TDs. Last season, he provided a solid floor (11 games with 15-plus fantasy points), but his ceiling was low (four top-10 weeks). In 2026, he'll have a new playcaller in Davis Webb and an upgraded group of pass catchers with Jaylen Waddle added to the mix. The 26-year-old is a fringe QB1.

Purdy enters his fifth NFL season looking to rebound after injuries caused him to appear in only nine games in 2025. The good news is Purdy played well, scoring 17-plus fantasy points in seven of the nine games, including 26-plus points in three straight games during Weeks 15-17. A highly effective passer and solid contributor as a rusher, Purdy has quietly finished in the top 10 in fantasy points per game in each of the past three seasons. With a good supporting cast led by Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle (once healthy) and free agent additions Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel, Purdy is an underrated mid-to-back-end QB1 in 2026.

The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

profile_notes.subject: Matthew Stafford
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target around Round 9 when waiting at quarterback.
profile_notes.summary: Harris considers Stafford a major quarterback value even after allowing for touchdown-rate regression.
profile_notes.evidence: He argues that regression would still leave a top-seven fantasy quarterback and sees the veteran's profile as comparable to productive late-career quarterback seasons.
profile_notes.counterweight: Age and touchdown regression remain real risks, and the episode does not guarantee that every platform will leave him until Round 9.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Stafford to wait on quarterback and spend earlier selections at scarcer positions.

profile_notes.counterweight: Touchdown regression, age, and normal quarterback volatility remain risks.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Wait in one-QB leagues or use him as the discounted half of a superflex pairing.

profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draft as a cheap QB1/late starter around QB13-16.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers view Stafford's non-starter ADP as a major mismatch with his recent production and the Rams' offensive context.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris calls him a top-five QB in his ranks after an MVP season. Funston points to a Super Bowl favorite with elite receiver projections and says even regression should leave Stafford top 12 if healthy.
profile_notes.counterweight: The only meaningful concern raised is age/injury; Harris explicitly does not project a repeat of 46 passing touchdowns.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Wait at quarterback and target Stafford as an inexpensive starter rather than paying an early premium.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Rams offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a strong environment, but do not let that alone erase individual age, role, and price concerns.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see Los Angeles as the NFC West offense most widely expected to be elite, while Harris warns that assumed certainty creates contradictory player valuations.
profile_notes.evidence: They discuss a possible 30-point-per-game offense, the resolution of Matthew Stafford's prior back concern, and the Rams' recent history of meaningful August role signals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris opens the episode by showing that consensus team projections frequently fail, and individual Rams can still decline or lose role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Rams environment as a supporting factor, then make player decisions on role, talent, health, and market cost.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Williams enters his third NFL season after a solid rookie campaign in 2024 followed by a big leap forward in 2025. Williams finished last season no lower than 11th among QBs in pass attempts, completions, pass yards, passing TDs, carries, rush yards, rush TDs and fantasy points per game. While Williams' completion percentage was one of the worst in the league (58%), his dual-threat ability and turnover avoidance (seven INTs both seasons) has led to solid fantasy output. The 2024 No. 1 draft pick has a good supporting cast in playcaller Ben Johnson and a trio of young pass catchers in Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland. Williams is a fringe QB1 with upside for another leap.

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

outlook.text: One of the league's most underrated players, Meyers is entering his first full season with Jacksonville after being acquired via trade in November. The 2019 UDFA has produced 800-plus receiving yards in five consecutive seasons while operating primarily as a short-to-intermediate target. More of a solid producer than a high-ceiling contributor, Meyers has finished no lower than 32nd in fantasy points over the last five seasons, but has yet to do better than 19th. The 29-year-old isn't much of a touchdown scorer (23 TDs in 78 games since 2021) and has substantial target competition via Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., Brenton Strange and Travis Hunter. Meyers is a good player, but is likely to cap out as a flex option.

outlook.text: Robinson signed with the Titans after catching 90-plus passes each of the past two seasons. The 2022 second-round pick has progressively improved his production each season in the pros, peaking with a 30% target share (ninth among WRs), 1,014 yards (13th) and 13.6 fantasy PPG (16th) in 2025. An undersized, short-range slot target, Robinson isn't positioned for many big plays and is very rarely used near the goal line (he's yet to clear four TDs in a season and has 13 career end zone targets). In Tennessee, Robinson will battle rookie Carnell Tate and Calvin Ridley for the team lead in targets, but his potential for flex production will depend on whether Cam Ward is able to make a Year 2 leap. Robinson, 25, is a low-ceiling, middle-round target.

profile_notes.subject: Tennessee Titans offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-draft Titans skill players gain volume appeal if the planned up-tempo system is confirmed.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker's key Tennessee nugget is a planned up-tempo attack, which could create more snaps for Cam Ward, Tony Pollard, Carnell Tate, and other Titans assets.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Brian Daboll brought Austin Schlottmann in at center because the coordinator trusts him to align the offense, make calls, and play fast. Tucker explicitly connects tempo and snap volume to fantasy value.
profile_notes.counterweight: Tucker says Schlottmann and right guard Volson are not considered average starters; Harris notes August tempo plans can vanish when a weak team is hit in the mouth.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the up-tempo possibility as a late-round upside input, but wait for preseason confirmation that the line can execute it.

outlook.text: Lemon was selected by the Eagles with the 20th overall pick of April's draft. Lemon is on the small side (5-foot-11, 192 pounds), but he posted a 3.04 YPRR (best in this rookie class) during his collegiate career, dropping only three of 190 career targets (his 1.6% drop rate also paced this class). Lemon, who aligned in the slot on 74% of his collegiate routes, posted a dominant 79-1,156-11 receiving line in 2025, while also contributing as a rusher (two TDs) and returner. With A.J. Brown now in New England, Lemon is likely to open his career as a starter opposite DeVonta Smith. Lemon's skill set provides him with upside, but with plenty of mouths to feed in Philly's low-volume pass offense, he's best valued as a flex option in 2026.

profile_notes.subject: Makai Lemon
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not pay a top-100 price until he practices and role clarity returns.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers reject the assumption that Lemon automatically becomes a fantasy starter after Philadelphia's receiver loss.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Lemon has been absent from practice; Waldman notes remaining veterans and doubts that replacement receivers replicate A.J. Brown.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both say he remains draftable at a reduced price.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Let injury/role risk push Lemon down the board; do not be the aggressive drafter.

profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade offense and Saquon Barkley context if interior health holds in the new scheme.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker believes Philadelphia has a high ceiling and high floor because last year's underperformance was substantially injury-driven and the new system should help blockers.
profile_notes.evidence: Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson fought through multiple injuries, surgeries, and rehabilitation; Lane Johnson missed the second half with plantar fasciitis. Tucker says the new coordinator's increased play action avoids isolating tackles in straight dropbacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: The line did not play as a top-five unit last year, and the recovery of injured interior starters must persist.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat a healthy Eagles line as a positive contextual upgrade for Barkley and the offense rather than anchoring on last year's unit ranking.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Makai Lemon
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris has top-40-ish WR optimism; Richard is WR53 pending stronger Eagles camp reports and role proof.
profile_notes.summary: Both see Lemon as talented, but require camp evidence that he can earn a major Eagles hierarchy role after A.J. Brown.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris wants positive reports across drills, padded work, and scrimmages; Richard calls Lemon his favorite draft-class receiver and compares his inside-out route/YAC/zone work to JSN.
profile_notes.counterweight: Philadelphia may run more, has a new offense, and Jalen Hurts must adapt; early reports were mixed and Lemon's path is not guaranteed.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor camp role rather than drafting the prospect profile alone; elevate only with sustained first-team trust.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Keep outside the small trusted-offense tier until the new Mannion system succeeds in games.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers refuse to restore Philadelphia to an automatic top-offense projection after last year's collapse and coordinator replacement.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites A.J. Brown's trade, questions around the line, and the team's decision to replace the coordinator despite prior Super Bowl success. Ciely believes Mannion's changes can help but says practice and preseason cannot prove a top-five result.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense has Jalen Hurts, a strong history, and a scheme that could improve play action/middle-field work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid building draft projections on an assumed Eagles bounce-back; wait for regular-season evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

profile_notes.subject: Makai Lemon
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ciely WR31 and Harris WR34 PPR/WR40 standard; downgrade if missed time or limited two-WR usage persists.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see Lemon as a reasonable middle-round rookie bet but not a player whom a great August can prove into a higher tier.
profile_notes.evidence: Ciely likes Lemon's fit with Hurts and Sean Mannion but says he is already near his ceiling rank; he will lower him if injury lingers, two-WR usage limits snaps, or the middle-field connection does not appear. Harris says camp cannot establish that Hurts has truly unlocked that area.
profile_notes.counterweight: A seventh/eighth-round rookie selection does not destroy a draft, and Lemon could become a workable No. 3 receiver.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor health and starter formations; do not elevate solely for drills or exhibition highlights.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Downs has settled in as a serviceable slot receiver, which has helped him to finish in the 35-to-45 range among WRs in total fantasy points in each of his three NFL seasons. Downs peaked with a 72-803-5 receiving line in 2024, but took a step back in a crowded offense last season, and failed to deliver a single fantasy week better than 15th at the position. The undersized Downs isn't an option near the goal line, as he hasn't cleared five touchdowns or three end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old has a path to a slightly larger role in 2026 with Michael Pittman Jr. gone, leaving Alec Pierce, Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen as his primary target competition. Downs is a sleeper for flex production in PPR formats.

profile_notes.subject: Josh Downs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target if a Keenan Allen rumor or outside-role uncertainty depresses ADP; monitor Colts deployment and concussion risk.
profile_notes.summary: Zachariason sees Downs as an elite separator with a potentially expandable role on a depleted Indianapolis depth chart, while Harris agrees the deep-slot ability has been underused.
profile_notes.evidence: Downs has twitch, speed, efficient movement, short-area change of direction, and the ability to separate short and deep; Colts reports had him working outside with Pierce unavailable.
profile_notes.counterweight: He is small and primarily a slot player, may have prior concussion concerns, and a possible Keenan Allen arrival could cap the ceiling even if it makes his ADP cheaper.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Downs as a value receiver rather than assuming a guaranteed outside breakout; track role and personnel through camp.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

outlook.text: After impressing with a 70-911-10 receiving line on 108 targets as a rookie in 2023, Addison has seen his target, reception, yardage and touchdown totals decrease each of the last two seasons. A few missed games were partially to blame for the dips, but Minnesota's quarterback woes were the main culprit in 2025, as Addison went from 10 TDs and a 65% catch rate in both 2023 and 2024 to three TDs and a 53% catch rate last season. Addison already has a pair of top-25 fantasy campaigns to his name, but it may be a stretch for him to get there in 2026 with Kyler Murray or J.J. McCarthy leading the Minnesota offense, not to mention Jauan Jennings' addition to the lineup. The 24-year-old is best valued as WR4/flex.

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Jordan Addison
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ninth or tenth round as a bench receiver, accepting quarterback and target-competition risk.
profile_notes.summary: Harris believes Addison's talent makes him worth a discounted bet on an improved Minnesota passing environment, and Eisenberg calls the cost/upside combination targetable.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites Addison's speed, ball skills, and strong Sam Darnold-year film, plus confidence in Kevin O'Connell; Eisenberg values him as a bench receiver in a three-WR league.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both acknowledge uncertain quarterback play and the possibility that Kyler Murray cannot support Addison and Justin Jefferson at high levels; Harris also notes Jauan Jennings and T.J. Hockenson competition.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Take Addison as a discounted bench upside receiver, not as a foundation starter.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not raise Jefferson from near his current ceiling on 'dialed in' Kyler Murray camp reports; downgrade only if doubts become sustained evidence.
profile_notes.summary: Richard sees Minnesota quarterback competence as an offense-wide variable for Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and the run game, but Harris sees mostly downside because Jefferson is already near ceiling.
profile_notes.evidence: Richard wants confirmation the quarterback competition is not real and that Murray outplays Minnesota's prior passers, which could force defenses deeper and improve the ecosystem.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both have heard optimistic Kyler camp narratives before and retain concerns about anticipation and inconsistency; Harris says the plausible adjustment is Jefferson falling toward WR12, not rising substantially.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid acting on generic camp praise; retain elite Jefferson pricing but watch for repeated evidence that Minnesota's passing environment is failing.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Jordan Addison
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Rank above Jauan Jennings barring injury, but do not expect camp to settle their target hierarchy.
profile_notes.summary: Addison remains Minnesota's preferred secondary receiver bet because his speed gives him more box-score-changing outcomes than Jennings.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris calls Addison a speed player and polished route runner who can go deep, while describing Jennings as tough, sure-handed, and short/intermediate oriented. Erickson says negative reports—being off schedule with Murray or doing only cardio—would matter more than positive camp stories.
profile_notes.counterweight: Jennings is a respected pro with a role, Murray may not support both, and either receiver can end up useless in a poor offense.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Prefer Addison for upside at similar cost, but keep exposure modest until Minnesota's passing game demonstrates competency.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat all Vikings except Jefferson as non-starter-level drafts until Kyler Murray and line health prove functional.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers believe Minnesota's broken 2025 offense makes a Kyler Murray rescue uncertain, especially for secondary receivers.
profile_notes.evidence: They say J.J. McCarthy was not fine and the offense deteriorated; Murray is better but not automatically a panacea for Jefferson or Addison. Erickson identifies an injured/inconsistent Christian Darrisaw and center instability after Ryan Kelly's concussion-related retirement as major 2025 line failures.
profile_notes.counterweight: Minnesota changed quarterbacks and added linemen, and a coaching offseason could prioritize Jefferson successfully.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid treating secondary Vikings as automatic starters; demand a discount and monitor quarterback/line health rather than believing generic positive camp stories.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Herbert enters his seventh NFL season following a solid 2025 campaign in which he ranked just inside the top 10 quarterbacks in pass attempts, yards and touchdowns. Herbert added serious value with his legs, ranking fifth at the position in carries and second in rushing yards (career highs in both). He finished 10th among quarterbacks in fantasy points, but that's a bit misleading, as his inconsistent production led to five top-five weeks but no other finishes better than 13th. Herbert has finished between 11th and 15th in fantasy points per game in each of the past four seasons, though it's fair to expect a leap forward in 2026 with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater healthy and a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel. Herbert is safest as a QB2, but there's upside for more.

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not assume a healthy or cohesive unit until tackle and interior questions are answered.
profile_notes.summary: The Chargers could benefit from an offensive-line-friendly McDaniel system, but Tucker sees legitimate uncertainty at every starting position.
profile_notes.evidence: Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt are returning from major injuries; Tucker questions center Tyler Biadasz's recovery, Jake Slaughter's shift from Florida center to left guard, and Cole Strange's fit after New England. Harris notes Alt was not fully participating when camp opened.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Shanahan-McVay tree can aid blockers, and all questions can resolve favorably.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor training-camp participation and interior cohesion before assigning a strong line-driven boost to Chargers skill players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target discounted Chargers pieces only on the conditional thesis of healthy line, protected Herbert, and a real offensive jump.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers can imagine a Chargers offense becoming a fantasy answer if health and protection finally cooperate, but view it as a conditional upside case rather than baseline.
profile_notes.evidence: Behrens says a healthy line and protected Justin Herbert could unlock a 28-30-point offense; Harris gives Herbert a mulligan and ties McConkey's rebound to the same factors.
profile_notes.counterweight: It requires unusually good Chargers injury luck, and the team has frequently failed to meet that sort of optimistic offensive projection.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the upside scenario as a tiebreaker for discounted Chargers, not as permission to erase downside.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Mahomes is a bit of a wild card as he embarks on his 10th season. The two-time NFL MVP followed up a pair of disappointing fantasy seasons (2023-24) with an elite start to 2025 (24.5 points per game during Weeks 1-8) and a disappointing finish that included 15.0 points per game during his final six games and a torn ACL in Week 15. Mahomes' efficiency has dipped the past three seasons, and while he made up ground as a rusher in 2025 (fifth among QBs in rushing yards and TDs despite three missed games), he might not be able to run as often this season as he recovers fully from the knee injury. Mahomes might be ready to play in Week 1, but even if he does, he hasn't been a consistent fantasy QB1 since 2022. He's a risky mid-to-late-round flier in drafts.

profile_notes.subject: Patrick Mahomes
profile_notes.action_qualifier: QB12-13 value only if recovery signals include normal preseason routine and sustained mobility; retain a lower ceiling than the 5,000-yard era.
profile_notes.summary: Mahomes's post-injury readiness is the Chiefs' central football story, and both speakers see QB12-13 as a cautious price that can miss a mostly healthy recovery.
profile_notes.evidence: They seek context clues such as normal preseason participation and routine, recognizing that running is a component of his value.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Chiefs have not recently produced the 5,000-yard version of Mahomes and the receiving group may not support it; optimistic 'ahead of schedule' reports are not enough alone.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor recovery rather than automatically fading; take the discount only when signs indicate normal functional preparation.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Warren reached career-high marks in touches (251), yardage (1,291) and touchdowns (eight) last season, his fourth in the league. The former undrafted free agent put up 13.6 fantasy points per game (19th among backs) and PFF tracked him with 56 forced missed tackles (seventh). Pittsburgh swapped out Kenneth Gainwell for Rico Dowdle as Warren's running mate, and the two are expected to split work in a Mike McCarthy offense that rarely deploys its backs in the passing game. Warren is capable and effective as a rusher and receiver, but his ceiling figures to be limited in this committee. He's likely to cap out as a flex.

profile_notes.subject: Jaylen Warren
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Flex-range target around RB27 PPR/RB29 standard, rather than paying an RB2 cost.
profile_notes.summary: Zachariason considers Warren a fringe top-10 real-life back whose contact balance, patience, receiving skill, and pass protection deserve more Pittsburgh volume; Harris strongly agrees with the player evaluation.
profile_notes.evidence: Zachariason says Warren bounces off defenders like a pinball, plays bigger than his size, and is excellent in space and pass protection. He also says Warren was beginning to earn more work before Kenneth Gainwell entered the picture.
profile_notes.counterweight: Warren invites contact despite not being large, and repeated Steelers staffs have limited his workload; Gainwell and market preference for Warren over Rico Dowdle can reduce the price edge.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Warren for efficiency and pass-game upside at a midrange price, while refusing to assume the coaching staff finally grants a true feature workload.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

profile_notes.subject: Jalen Warren and Rico Dowdle
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Use either as a format-dependent RB2 option, but do not infer workload split from first-team camp reps.
profile_notes.summary: Harris and Harmon find both Steelers backs usable but do not believe training camp will reliably identify a decisive winner.
profile_notes.evidence: They note the backs split first-team work and have different profiles; Harris expects Warren to catch checkdowns but says Dowdle can catch them too.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Steelers historically will not publicize deployment, and past late-summer usage surprises show that camp reporting can miss the actual regular-season plan.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft by format and price, not because a routine first-team-rep report implies a true workload edge.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: Pittsburgh Steelers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a stable, projectable offense; do not manufacture large camp-based projections.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see a reasonably high/projectable Steelers floor if Aaron Rodgers remains healthy, without an exciting ceiling case.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Mike McCarthy's high-floor play calling, a settled enough offensive line, and known top receivers; Harris calls the roster full of good professionals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both retain concern that Rodgers may have declined further and will avoid contact, limiting offensive aggression.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep established Steelers values near their baseline projections instead of reacting sharply to routine camp headlines.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Stevenson will battle with second-year back TreVeyon Henderson for touches in the New England backfield. The duo shared the backfield at times last season, but it was the veteran Stevenson who usually operated as the lead back. He earned the role, ranking fifth among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF, second in yards after contact (2.82) and first in yards per target (9.1). Stevenson, who is entering his sixth season, did miss three games (he has missed time three seasons in a row), and his overall volume was limited (9.3 carries and 2.7 targets per game), which led to a 25th-place finish in fantasy points. Now 28 years old and with Henderson likely to play a larger role, Stevenson, who has one top-20 fantasy campaign to his name, is a low-upside bench option.

Dowdle signed with the Steelers after nearly identical campaigns with the Cowboys in 2024 (1,328 yards and five TDs on 274 touches) and Panthers in 2025 (1,373 yards and seven TDs on 275 touches). He was effective as a rusher (4.57 yards per carry) and fairly busy as a receiver (50 targets both years) en route to finishing just inside the top 25 in fantasy points per game both seasons. Now in Pittsburgh, the 28-year-old is expected to share work with Jaylen Warren and perhaps second-year back Kaleb Johnson. Earning lead-rusher duties could get Dowdle into the weekly flex discussion, but the ceiling will be low and he'll likely need an injury in order to find his way to consistent fantasy output. Consider him for your bench.

profile_notes.subject: Jalen Warren and Rico Dowdle
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Use either as a format-dependent RB2 option, but do not infer workload split from first-team camp reps.
profile_notes.summary: Harris and Harmon find both Steelers backs usable but do not believe training camp will reliably identify a decisive winner.
profile_notes.evidence: They note the backs split first-team work and have different profiles; Harris expects Warren to catch checkdowns but says Dowdle can catch them too.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Steelers historically will not publicize deployment, and past late-summer usage surprises show that camp reporting can miss the actual regular-season plan.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft by format and price, not because a routine first-team-rep report implies a true workload edge.

profile_notes.subject: Pittsburgh Steelers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a stable, projectable offense; do not manufacture large camp-based projections.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see a reasonably high/projectable Steelers floor if Aaron Rodgers remains healthy, without an exciting ceiling case.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Mike McCarthy's high-floor play calling, a settled enough offensive line, and known top receivers; Harris calls the roster full of good professionals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both retain concern that Rodgers may have declined further and will avoid contact, limiting offensive aggression.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep established Steelers values near their baseline projections instead of reacting sharply to routine camp headlines.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Gainwell signed with the Buccaneers following a second-half breakout with Pittsburgh last season. After playing sparingly during the first four-and-a-half years of his career, Gainwell averaged 13.3 touches, 85.0 yards and 17.8 fantasy points from Week 8 on last season (eight games). Only five backs scored more points than Gainwell after Week 10. He did most of his damage as a receiver (top six among RBs in targets, catches and receiving yards) and will now look to earn a similar role alongside Bucky Irving in Tampa Bay. Gainwell's strong season suggests he'll have a role, but the 23-year-old Irving is likely to operate as the lead back. Gainwell is best valued as a bench/insurance stash with some flex appeal in deep PPR leagues.

Hubbard is coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he battled injury and lost lead-back duties to Rico Dowdle. The veteran was limited to 734 yards on 164 touches (he cleared 275 touches and 1,100 yards in 2023 and 2024), and he ranked 64th among 65 qualified backs in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Still in his prime at age 27, a bounce-back season is possible, especially with Dowdle gone and unproven Jonathon Brooks and Trevor Etienne as his competition for touches. Hubbard should be considered a flex option.

profile_notes.subject: Carolina Panthers offensive line and backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Be cautious with Chuba Hubbard and Jonathan Brooks while tackle availability and a multi-back split remain unresolved.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker expects Carolina's interior to be sound but sees tackle injuries and a protective run-first plan as constraints on a clean Hubbard/Brooks fantasy projection.
profile_notes.evidence: Taylor Moten's blood-clot timeline is unclear, Ikem Ekwonu is returning from a ruptured patellar tendon, Rashid Walker is new, and rookie Monroe Freeling may need to start. Tucker says the Panthers want to run to protect tackles and Bryce Young, while spreading touches among Hubbard, Brooks, and Etienne.
profile_notes.counterweight: Hubbard remains the apparent leader, and a good interior line can help the run game protect weaker tackles.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid aggressive volume projections for Carolina backs until tackles return and the touch distribution becomes clearer.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Carolina Panthers backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Chuba Hubbard is baseline lead back; raise Jonathan Brooks from RB54 only for credible knee-recovery and meaningful practice-integration evidence.
profile_notes.summary: Both regard Brooks's medical integration as the Panthers camp story most capable of altering Hubbard's workload and Brooks's very-low draft value.
profile_notes.evidence: Carolina let Rico Dowdle leave and added only A.J. Dillon/Trevor Etienne, which Harris reads as possible Brooks optimism. McCormick expects a methodical return after repeated major injuries.
profile_notes.counterweight: Brooks can remain merely a backup or re-injure the knee; Carolina paid Hubbard and routine split reps do not prove a meaningful regular-season role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track true practice participation and recovery language, not generic comeback praise; otherwise draft Hubbard as the more stable option.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Jones is back for a third season in Minnesota after an injury-plagued 2025 campaign limited him to 747 yards (his fewest since his rookie season in 2017) and three touchdowns in 12 games. Jones remained fairly busy (11.0 carries and 3.4 targets per game) but didn't perform well, ranking dead last among 65 backs with 50-plus carries in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Jones failed to record a single top-10 fantasy outing. Now 31 years old, Jones remains a starter and will get some run, but he's well past his prime and unlikely to return to consistent fantasy output. Jones is best valued as a bench player with occasional flex appeal.

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings running backs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris ranks Aaron Jones RB38 and Jordan Mason RB41; Mason is the preferred late side bet if the offense rebounds.
profile_notes.summary: Jones still looks good but is not health-trustworthy, while Mason is the more plausible early-down/goal-line beneficiary if Minnesota's environment improves.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Jones took a substantial pay cut to remain and has recurring health risk. Mason stayed more efficient than Jones in the broken offense but does not catch passes, protect on third downs, or play that role; Harris calls him the goal-line, workload, and late-game grinder.
profile_notes.counterweight: Mason is slow, needs a good environment, and PPR scoring hurts him; Jones remains the nominal leader. Neither expects ordinary August news to alter their baseline.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid assuming either is a weekly starter, but select Mason over cheap alternatives when betting on a Minnesota turnaround and a Jones absence.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Kittle is undoubtedly among the best tight ends in the NFL and fantasy, but he simply can't dodge the injury bug. The 2017 fifth-round pick has played one full season (2018) and tore an Achilles in the team's wild-card victory after missing six regular-season games last season. Kittle could miss a few games to open the season and, now at 32 years old, might not be his usual, dominant self even when he returns. Kittle has finished sixth or better in fantasy PPG in each of the past eight seasons (including first in 2024), so he's worth a late-round flier, especially if you have an available IR slot.

profile_notes.subject: George Kittle
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not rely on optimistic Achilles rehabilitation updates; draft only at a late tight-end price that tolerates early-season uncertainty.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers are skeptical that optimistic camp reports can establish Kittle will retain his pre-injury explosiveness after a late-season Achilles tear.
profile_notes.evidence: Gretch says the relevant question is in-season efficiency, not whether the team says rehab looks good; Harris notes Kittle will play within a year of the January injury.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris still ranks him TE12 and says he is not costly enough to ruin a season, because replacement tight ends can be found.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Discount Kittle for recovery uncertainty and be ready with an alternative if early games show reduced effectiveness.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Kraft's steady career progression had him on the cusp of a full-on breakout last season, but all was derailed by a torn ACL in Week 9. Prior to the injury, Kraft had seen 10 targets in consecutive games, one of which included a career-high 33.3 fantasy points. Through Week 8, only Jake Ferguson had more fantasy points. Granted, Kraft was way over his head in the TD department (six TDs with an expected total of 1.8 and only two end zone targets), but his boost in usage and terrific RAC skills (he has led the position in the category each of his three seasons) were enough to get him into the weekly TE1 mix. Kraft's recovery will need to be monitored, but even if he's ready for Week 1, a dip in production is possible in his first year back from the major injury. He's a risky middle-round target.

profile_notes.subject: Tucker Kraft
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Move out of the premium tight-end tier and closer to the Strange/Johnson/Pitts range.
profile_notes.summary: Harris lowers Kraft because reports suggest he may not retain a full-time role by midseason.
profile_notes.evidence: The ranking change is based on potential playing-time erosion rather than a new talent criticism.
profile_notes.counterweight: The concern is report-driven and could reverse if Kraft secures the expected role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not pay premium-TE cost until the role is clearer; treat him as part of the lower-cost uncertain tier.
profile_notes.episode_title: More Flag Players & Cousin Josh's Frag Players

profile_notes.subject: Tucker Kraft
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris TE3, but lower if he remains inactive; Erickson would take Loveland and Warren ahead while health is unresolved.
profile_notes.summary: Kraft's prior pre-injury production supports a lofty ranking, but his PUP status makes availability the key Green Bay camp question.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Kraft produced at a high level before injury and is TE3; both Packers tight ends are on PUP, and Kraft has said since March he expects Week 1 readiness. Erickson expects a compromised early half and ranks Loveland/Warren ahead.
profile_notes.counterweight: A player's Week 1 optimism is not proof, and Luke Musgrave's OTA-injury PUP placement adds uncertainty to the room.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track actual practice return and avoid paying a premium based solely on an anticipated Week 1 clearance.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Goedert enters the 2026 season as the poster boy for inevitable touchdown regression to the mean. After scoring 24 touchdowns in his first seven seasons (3.4 per year), Goedert inexplicably leaped to 11 scores in 15 games in 2025. Goedert's expected TD total was 5.1, and he saw only five end zone targets (12 tight ends saw more). Goedert is a solid fantasy tight end -- he has finished 12th or better in PPG each of the past seven seasons -- but he often misses games (at least two in each of the past six years) and has never finished in the top eight at the position in targets or catches. The 31-year-old is likely to deliver fringe-TE1 numbers in 2026.

profile_notes.subject: Dallas Goedert
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not rely on him as a TE1 solely because of a TE2 finish driven by touchdowns.
profile_notes.summary: McCormick and Harris both believe Goedert's tape shows pronounced lost speed and separation, making last year's touchdown-led finish a poor baseline.
profile_notes.evidence: McCormick points to schemed red-zone button hooks and the disappearance of seam explosives; Harris says the Eagles were prepared to move on and agrees the speed is gone.
profile_notes.counterweight: Goedert can still stiff-arm defenders and Philadelphia kept him, partly because rookie Eli Stowers had not made camp inroads.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Discount the touchdown spike and draft a different tight end if Goedert's finish is elevating his cost.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade offense and Saquon Barkley context if interior health holds in the new scheme.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker believes Philadelphia has a high ceiling and high floor because last year's underperformance was substantially injury-driven and the new system should help blockers.
profile_notes.evidence: Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson fought through multiple injuries, surgeries, and rehabilitation; Lane Johnson missed the second half with plantar fasciitis. Tucker says the new coordinator's increased play action avoids isolating tackles in straight dropbacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: The line did not play as a top-five unit last year, and the recovery of injured interior starters must persist.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat a healthy Eagles line as a positive contextual upgrade for Barkley and the offense rather than anchoring on last year's unit ranking.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Keep outside the small trusted-offense tier until the new Mannion system succeeds in games.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers refuse to restore Philadelphia to an automatic top-offense projection after last year's collapse and coordinator replacement.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites A.J. Brown's trade, questions around the line, and the team's decision to replace the coordinator despite prior Super Bowl success. Ciely believes Mannion's changes can help but says practice and preseason cannot prove a top-five result.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense has Jalen Hurts, a strong history, and a scheme that could improve play action/middle-field work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid building draft projections on an assumed Eagles bounce-back; wait for regular-season evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Kelce re-signed with the Chiefs and is returning for what might be his final NFL season. The veteran tight end's days as an elite producer are behind him, and he saw a notable dip in usage last season (19.6% target share was his lowest since 2014). Kelce did hold up for 17 games and still finished in the top 10 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and fantasy PPG. Kelce has reeled off 10 consecutive top-five fantasy campaigns despite not offering much in the scoring department (he hasn't cleared five TDs in a season since 2022). The 36-year-old's role could dip even further this season, so he's best valued as a fringe TE1.

profile_notes.subject: Travis Kelce
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris ranks him TE11 as a usable floor play, not a high-ceiling bet.
profile_notes.summary: Harris expected to bury Kelce but instead found enough craft and residual speed to maintain a viable fantasy floor.
profile_notes.evidence: He keeps Kelce's speed at C rather than dropping it to D, says he remains faster than several veteran lumbering tight ends, and credits settling into space, craft, and drawing separation with pushes.
profile_notes.counterweight: Kelce turns 37 in October, is not running past anyone, has a quarterback returning from an ACL tear, and Harris sees little ceiling.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Kelce as a lower-ceiling, usable tight-end option rather than paying for a vintage elite outcome.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

outlook.text: White signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons with the Buccaneers. The 2022 third-round pick operated as a feature back in 2023 (he finished in the top five among backs in touches, yards and fantasy points), but he played a situational role during his other three seasons. White is fine as a rusher, but he's a standout as a receiver. He's the only back in the NFL with 40-plus catches in each of the past four seasons, and his 89.1% career catch rate is easily best in NFL history among players with 100-plus targets. The 27-year-old is the favorite to lead the Washington backfield, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt and perhaps others will be involved. White will find himself on the weekly flex radar as long as he remains atop the depth chart.

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line fallout after starting LT Laremy Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps tear; Harris makes no automatic player-rank change.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps injury as a meaningful downgrade to Washington's offensive environment, though not one that can be precisely assigned to individual ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: He describes the line as thin without its starting left tackle and explicitly says losing good players hurts an offense.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris cannot draw a straight line from the injury to exactly how far Terry McLaurin or Jayden Daniels should fall, so he declines a mechanical rank adjustment.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Washington's pass-game options under review as replacement-line and protection information emerges instead of overreacting with a fixed downgrade.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: No back is top 30 for Harris; Richard prefers Rachaad White as a late PPR target if JCM fails to reclaim lead work.
profile_notes.summary: Harris wants camp to clarify whether Jacory Croskey-Merritt improved enough to lead Washington, while Richard expects White's passing-game role to make him the useful late option.
profile_notes.evidence: Croskey-Merritt was benched late the prior season as Chris Rodriguez emerged; Rodriguez is gone, but White and Katron Allen add competing paths. Richard says White was acquired for high-value touches.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris admits his instinct to fade rookies can create blinders and will listen if reports say JCM owns the job; White can also post very low weeks.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Wait for role clarity and select only at a discount, with White preferred for PPR floor if JCM evidence remains weak.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders running backs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid RB2 prices; a camp winner belongs nearer the RB20-28/fringe-RB2 range.
profile_notes.summary: Washington's White/Krosky-Merritt/Allen competition is camp-actionable, but no speaker wants to treat a named winner as a certain premium asset.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris lists Rachaad White, Jacory Krosky-Merritt, and rookie Katron Allen and says none appears great. Ciely says reports can change the hierarchy, but White's past inefficiency and Krosky-Merritt's limited recent résumé warn against overcommitment.
profile_notes.counterweight: A coordinator can choose a lead back and a good Commanders offense could create usable volume.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Watch for real separation, then prefer the cheaper other back if hype drives one player into Rounds 4-5.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Brooks is hoping to get his career on track in 2026 after appearing in only one game since being drafted in the second round of the 2024 draft. Brooks spent most of his rookie season recovering from a torn ACL suffered while at the University of Texas. He returned in Week 12 and handled 12 touches in three games prior to retearing the same ACL and missing the entire 2025 season. Only 23 years old and skilled as a rusher and receiver, Brooks figures to eventually get his shot at a lead-back role in the pros. He's expected to battle for touches behind starter Chuba Hubbard this season, so it's possible he earns his way into a fantasy-relevant role at some point. Consider him a lottery ticket in the late rounds.

profile_notes.subject: Carolina Panthers offensive line and backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Be cautious with Chuba Hubbard and Jonathan Brooks while tackle availability and a multi-back split remain unresolved.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker expects Carolina's interior to be sound but sees tackle injuries and a protective run-first plan as constraints on a clean Hubbard/Brooks fantasy projection.
profile_notes.evidence: Taylor Moten's blood-clot timeline is unclear, Ikem Ekwonu is returning from a ruptured patellar tendon, Rashid Walker is new, and rookie Monroe Freeling may need to start. Tucker says the Panthers want to run to protect tackles and Bryce Young, while spreading touches among Hubbard, Brooks, and Etienne.
profile_notes.counterweight: Hubbard remains the apparent leader, and a good interior line can help the run game protect weaker tackles.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid aggressive volume projections for Carolina backs until tackles return and the touch distribution becomes clearer.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Carolina Panthers backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Chuba Hubbard is baseline lead back; raise Jonathan Brooks from RB54 only for credible knee-recovery and meaningful practice-integration evidence.
profile_notes.summary: Both regard Brooks's medical integration as the Panthers camp story most capable of altering Hubbard's workload and Brooks's very-low draft value.
profile_notes.evidence: Carolina let Rico Dowdle leave and added only A.J. Dillon/Trevor Etienne, which Harris reads as possible Brooks optimism. McCormick expects a methodical return after repeated major injuries.
profile_notes.counterweight: Brooks can remain merely a backup or re-injure the knee; Carolina paid Hubbard and routine split reps do not prove a meaningful regular-season role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track true practice participation and recovery language, not generic comeback praise; otherwise draft Hubbard as the more stable option.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Dobbins re-signed with Denver and will attempt to fend off sophomore RJ Harvey for the team's lead-back job. With both active during Weeks 1-10 last season (10 games), Dobbins handled 153 carries (60% team share) and 15 targets (4%), compared to 50 carries (20%) and 29 targets (9%) for Harvey. Dobbins ran well (5.05 yards per carry) when healthy, but he was limited to four touchdowns and was a nonfactor as a receiver (37 yards on 15 targets) en route to averaging 11.6 fantasy points (27th). Dobbins enters his age-27 campaign having yet to play a full season in his career (seven-plus missed games in four of the past five years) and without much value even when active (he has never produced a top-20 fantasy campaign). Dobbins is an underwhelming flex option with added value in non-PPR formats.

profile_notes.subject: Denver Broncos running backs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Reassess usage as the Dobbins injury and preseason rotation develop.
profile_notes.summary: Denver's backfield has a preferred healthy player in Dobbins but remains likely to use all three backs.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Dobbins's early-down role was more repeatable and valuable, while Harvey had red-zone receiving work; Denver also drafted Jonah Coleman and re-signed Dobbins.
profile_notes.counterweight: Dobbins cannot be assumed healthy, Harris says Harvey can improve as a second-year player, and he admits he has not evaluated Coleman yet.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft any Denver back as a no-competition bell cow; use incoming health and rotation reports to separate their values.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: J.K. Dobbins
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor the reported soft-tissue injury and Denver's backfield rotation before making a rank change.
profile_notes.summary: Harris still regards Dobbins as Denver's best healthy back among near equals, but his new limp and extensive injury record require close monitoring.
profile_notes.evidence: Sean Payton called the latest issue soft tissue and said Dobbins would be fine; Harris says Dobbins had been RB15 in Week 10, led RBs in 10-plus-yard carries, and looked more repeatably valuable than R.J. Harvey before foot surgery ended his season.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris does not change ranks from one report, but lists meniscus, ACL, Achilles, foot-ligament, and knee injuries; the Broncos also have Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat him as an injury-sensitive committee lead, not a secure workload bet, and wait for camp updates before reacting.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Denver Broncos backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ignore ambiguous camp usage between R.J. Harvey, J.K. Dobbins, and Jonah Coleman unless injury or a durable regular-season role change occurs.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers regard Broncos backfield camp stories as a Rorschach test: optimists and skeptics will interpret small drills to support their existing Harvey/Dobbins takes.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Dobbins was good last year and likely begins as primary runner; reports about Coleman goal-line drills or Harvey opportunities do not settle a role. Behrens notes Harvey is being drafted far earlier than Dobbins in best ball.
profile_notes.counterweight: Dobbins has injury history, Sean Payton could allocate red-zone work unusually, and a real injury would materially change the hierarchy.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not spend attention or draft capital on speculative camp usage; reassess only for meaningful health or deployment evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Harvey will go into his sophomore campaign looking to overtake J.K. Dobbins as Denver's lead back. In the 10 games in which both backs were active last season, Harvey handled 50 carries (20% team share) and 29 targets (9%), compared to Dobbins' 153 carries (60%) and 15 targets (4%). With Dobbins sidelined for the team's remaining nine games (including the playoff run), Harvey handled 115 carries (55%) and 41 targets (13%). He averaged 10.0 fantasy points with Dobbins and 14.2 without, though his 3.3 yards per carry during the final nine games was very poor. The entire Denver backfield is set to return in 2026, so similar deployment (which would include receiving specialist Tyler Badie) could be in the cards, though fourth-round rookie Jonah Coleman could factor in eventually as well. Harvey, 25, has a slight bit of breakout potential, but the committee setup suggests he's safest viewed as no more than a flex.

profile_notes.subject: Denver Broncos running backs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Reassess usage as the Dobbins injury and preseason rotation develop.
profile_notes.summary: Denver's backfield has a preferred healthy player in Dobbins but remains likely to use all three backs.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Dobbins's early-down role was more repeatable and valuable, while Harvey had red-zone receiving work; Denver also drafted Jonah Coleman and re-signed Dobbins.
profile_notes.counterweight: Dobbins cannot be assumed healthy, Harris says Harvey can improve as a second-year player, and he admits he has not evaluated Coleman yet.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft any Denver back as a no-competition bell cow; use incoming health and rotation reports to separate their values.

profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Ferguson has emerged as a reliable target for Dak Prescott in the high-scoring Dallas offense, which has led to solid fantasy production. Ferguson, who has handled a 17% target share each of the past three seasons, is fresh off a career year in which he ranked third among tight ends in receptions, touchdowns and end zone targets (10). His nine top-12 fantasy weeks tied for second, though it's worth noting that his production dropped off substantially with a healthy CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on the field during the second half of the season (under 12.0 fantasy points in each of his final eight healthy games, 7.3 PPG during the span). The 27-year-old's role as a short-range target (4.7 aDOT last season) limits his yardage upside, but he sees just enough work, including near the goal line, to allow fringe-TE1 production. Don't call him "Joke Farterson" ("Fantasy Football Now" viewers get it); Ferguson is vying for his third top-10 fantasy campaign in his past four seasons.

profile_notes.subject: Dallas Cowboys skill players
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ignore Cowboys camp hype absent injury or a genuine George Pickens hold-in.
profile_notes.summary: Dallas offers little camp information likely to change established fantasy evaluations.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris describes annual hype around Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, while Ciely says the relevant fantasy roles have little genuine competition. Pickens signed his tag and attended work despite a possible future contract dispute.
profile_notes.counterweight: A Pickens hold-in could hurt early games, and injuries or unavoidably negative reports would be meaningful.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Filter positive Cowboys clips out of draft decisions; only move players for material availability news.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: One of fantasy's biggest mysteries, Andrews' usage has dipped substantially over the past two seasons. After finishing in the top five in fantasy PPG five seasons in a row from 2019 to 2023, Andrews slipped to eighth in 2024 (it would've been much worse if not for 11 touchdowns on 68 targets) and fell even further to 24th last season. Andrews appeared in all 17 of Baltimore's games but ranked 18th among tight ends in targets and outside the top 20 in catches and yards. The combination of a new coaching staff, a healthy Lamar Jackson and the departure of Isaiah Likely could lead to a rebound season for Andrews, but we now have two straight seasons of underperformance. The 31-year-old remains a force near the goal line (top 10 in end zone targets seven years in a row), but he's now more of a fringe TE1 than a fantasy star.

profile_notes.subject: Baltimore Ravens offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor the three new interior pieces and tackle performance before assuming a strong rushing environment.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker sees Baltimore's changed interior and new under-center offense as a significant continuity risk despite potential upside.
profile_notes.evidence: He names injured-center returnee Ethan Pocic, returning Simpson, and first-round Penn State guard Vega Ioane as a substantially remade interior, while noting the rookie may switch sides. He also says neither Ronnie Stanley nor Roger Rosengarten met expectations last year.
profile_notes.counterweight: If the interior questions resolve positively, Tucker says the line could be good; Derrick Henry remains a rare durability/production outlier.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the interior transition in the downside range for Ravens runners and passing-game projections rather than presuming past line quality.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Mark Andrews
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not use as a starting fantasy tight end; both speakers prefer Isaiah Likely in their respective contexts.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers are reluctant to treat Andrews as a fantasy starter despite Baltimore retaining him.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says he looked slow on 2025 film and had previously survived on touchdowns; Harmon says the offense has lacked an obvious alternative yet Andrews still has struggled to get open or synchronize.
profile_notes.counterweight: Baltimore's personnel decision and lack of a clear in-house tight-end replacement preserve some role stability.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Wait for a different tight-end solution rather than drafting Andrews as the planned weekly starter.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: It's been a rough go for Hockenson since he peaked with a 95-960-5 receiving line in 2023. He tore an ACL in Week 16 that season and was limited to a 41-455-0 receiving line upon his return in 10 games in 2024. A bounce-back was expected in 2025, but Hockenson handled a weak 16% target share (his lowest since he was a rookie in 2019) and couldn't overcome the team's QB woes en route to a 51-438-3 showing. Hockenson has now followed four straight top-seven fantasy PPG seasons with finishes of 17th and 26th. The 29-year-old could very well get back on track in 2026, but he'll need solid play from either Kyler Murray or J.J. McCarthy. Hockenson is a fringe TE1.

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: T.J. Hockenson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid treating the name brand as a dependable TE1 after Harris's TE24 ranking.
profile_notes.summary: McCormick sees a plotting player with a diminished ability to earn targets, and Harris independently agrees that Hockenson did not look like the same athlete after his major knee injury.
profile_notes.evidence: McCormick says Hockenson mostly sits in zones; Harris's film profile repeatedly found no separation and his speed grade has fallen to C. Their statistical reference was a TE29 finish in 15 games.
profile_notes.counterweight: He is another year removed from the knee injury, and the prior season's disastrous surroundings could improve.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Pass on Hockenson as a presumed TE1 and choose a cheaper upside path if the market still prices in his old reputation.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not raise Jefferson from near his current ceiling on 'dialed in' Kyler Murray camp reports; downgrade only if doubts become sustained evidence.
profile_notes.summary: Richard sees Minnesota quarterback competence as an offense-wide variable for Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and the run game, but Harris sees mostly downside because Jefferson is already near ceiling.
profile_notes.evidence: Richard wants confirmation the quarterback competition is not real and that Murray outplays Minnesota's prior passers, which could force defenses deeper and improve the ecosystem.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both have heard optimistic Kyler camp narratives before and retain concerns about anticipation and inconsistency; Harris says the plausible adjustment is Jefferson falling toward WR12, not rising substantially.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid acting on generic camp praise; retain elite Jefferson pricing but watch for repeated evidence that Minnesota's passing environment is failing.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat all Vikings except Jefferson as non-starter-level drafts until Kyler Murray and line health prove functional.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers believe Minnesota's broken 2025 offense makes a Kyler Murray rescue uncertain, especially for secondary receivers.
profile_notes.evidence: They say J.J. McCarthy was not fine and the offense deteriorated; Murray is better but not automatically a panacea for Jefferson or Addison. Erickson identifies an injured/inconsistent Christian Darrisaw and center instability after Ryan Kelly's concussion-related retirement as major 2025 line failures.
profile_notes.counterweight: Minnesota changed quarterbacks and added linemen, and a coaching offseason could prioritize Jefferson successfully.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid treating secondary Vikings as automatic starters; demand a discount and monitor quarterback/line health rather than believing generic positive camp stories.
