profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Shakir has settled in as a reliable, short-range target for Josh Allen, though the role hasn't led to much fantasy success. The 2022 fifth-round pick has cleared a 20% target share and 70 catches in consecutive seasons, ranking top five among receivers in catch rate and RAC both years. A nonfactor near the goal line, however, Shakir totaled eight TDs and five end zone targets during the span. Shakir finished the two seasons just outside of the top 35 fantasy receivers and will now have to compete with DJ Moore for the team lead in targets. Shakir was already barely worth flex consideration, so the potential for a slight decrease in target volume suggests the 26-year-old is no more than a low-ceiling bench option.

profile_notes.subject: Khalil Shakir
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Value target if his prior very short-average-depth role suppresses price; expect a better football player than a guaranteed high-volume stat line.
profile_notes.summary: Zachariason calls Shakir an underrated, intelligent, reliable slot player who can do more than his low-aDOT role, while Harris calls him a 'baller' and a better football player than statistical asset.
profile_notes.evidence: Zachariason highlights YAC elusiveness, zone awareness, and timely playmaking; Harris recalls a Week 15 fourth-and-three contested catch against Marcus Jones and sees a player Buffalo can trust in big moments.
profile_notes.counterweight: Shakir is not as explosive as Downs and may remain a role-dependent player; added receiving talent could alter targets even if it opens better efficiency opportunities.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Target Shakir only when his limited archetype keeps the cost low, and do not require an elite raw-volume projection to value his weekly utility.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

outlook.text: Reed began his NFL career with a pair of top-30 fantasy campaigns, but the Green Bay slot receiver was limited to only seven appearances last season due to injury. Even when active, Reed wasn't as effective as in years past, averaging 6.9 fantasy PPG and finding the end zone once (Week 1). This comes after the 2023 second-round pick produced 75 touches, 900-plus yards and seven-plus touchdowns in each of his first two seasons. The 26-year-old signed a contract extension in April and will battle the likes of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Savion Williams for targets this season. While he'll likely hit for the occasional solid game, his limited usage (career-high 18% target share) will put a cap on his fantasy upside. He's barely in the flex conversation in PPR leagues.

After impressing as a rookie with 101 touches and 12 touchdowns in 20 games (including the playoffs), Worthy had the look of an emerging star. Things didn't go as planned in Year 2, though, as the 2024 first-round pick was injured on his third snap of the season and wasn't productive or utilized as much as expected upon his return. Worthy was limited to one touchdown (Week 6) and reached 12 fantasy points once in 14 games (Week 4). The speedy Worthy is still only 23 years old, so a Year 3 breakout is certainly possible, especially with Rashee Rice and 36-year-old Travis Kelce as his only legit target competition. He's worth a late flier.

Monangai heads into his second NFL season following an impressive rookie campaign in which he quickly forced his way into a committee with D'Andre Swift. The 2025 seventh-round flier played 41% of Chicago's offensive snaps and averaged a healthy 4.6 yards per carry on 169 attempts. Monangai was limited to 7.7 fantasy PPG during the 16 weeks Swift also played, but he showed his insurance value with a 29-touch, 198-yard effort in the one game Swift was sidelined (Week 9). The 24-year-old could see a slight boost in usage this season, but that usage and production will be limited as long as Swift is also healthy.

profile_notes.subject: Chicago Bears running backs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris has Swift RB23 and Kyle Monangai RB37; do not infer a takeover from camp without injury.
profile_notes.summary: Both expect Swift and Monangai to play, but neither believes training camp can prove that the rookie has surpassed the veteran.
profile_notes.evidence: Erickson says both should get significant run. Harris calls Monangai tough and physical but not especially agile, explosive, or likely to catch extensively, leaving a substantial ranking gap behind Swift.
profile_notes.counterweight: An injury changes the entire conversation, and a shared workload can still make either player usable at the right price.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft Monangai as a presumed Swift replacement from camp reports; price both as a committee until a material event occurs.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Sadiq was selected by the Jets with the No. 16 pick of April's draft. After playing a limited role his first two collegiate seasons, he broke out with a 51-560-8 receiving line in 2025. He handled a respectable 17% of Oregon's targets and aligned in the slot 62% of the time. Sadiq is a bit on the small side, but he totaled 106 targets in three collegiate seasons. He needs to cut down on drops (six on 70 targets in 2025), but he's one of the youngest players in this rookie class and crushed it at the combine, posting a ridiculous 4.39 40-yard dash at 241 pounds (130 speed score) and a 43.5-inch vertical, 133-inch broad jump and 26 bench reps. Sadiq's career might start slow, especially with Mason Taylor also on the Jets' TE depth chart, but the rookie has the upside to eventually emerge as a fantasy TE1. Consider him with a mid-to-late pick.

profile_notes.subject: Kenyon Sadiq
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not draft as a fantasy starter after hernia-surgery setback removes most of camp.
profile_notes.summary: Harris calls Sadiq's setback a clear downgrade because a rookie tight end will lose crucial practice time.
profile_notes.evidence: Sadiq had spring hernia surgery, then suffered a camp setback and was expected to miss a couple weeks; Harris notes camp ends near August 29.
profile_notes.counterweight: No long-term talent criticism is made, and the exact recovery could be shorter than feared.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Remove Sadiq from starter plans and only revisit as a late bench gamble after he returns to football activity.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

outlook.text: Likely signed with the Giants after four years of backing up Mark Andrews in Baltimore. Likely is reuniting with coach John Harbaugh and is finally expected to play a consistent offensive role. During his time in Baltimore, Likely was limited to 50% of the team's offensive snaps and never finished a season better than 20th among tight ends in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards or fantasy PPG. His only extensive stretch with Andrews sidelined came back in 2023. During the seven-game span, Likely posted a 23-356-6 receiving line on a 16% target share and averaged a solid 13.5 fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old is obviously unproven, but his receiving skills in New York's ascending offense are enough to put him on the TE2 radar.

profile_notes.subject: Isaiah Likely
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round tight end after passing on the premium tier.
profile_notes.summary: Eisenberg calls Likely one of the best current draft values because a new role could finally unlock target volume; Harris prefers that late gamble to paying a fourth-round tight-end price.
profile_notes.evidence: Eisenberg says Likely has been a Jackson Dart go-to guy, invokes Dart's prior tight-end usage, and notes Likely's strong historical results when receiving six or more targets.
profile_notes.counterweight: Malik Nabers's status, Theo Johnson, two-tight-end usage, and schematic adjustment could cap targets; the transcript's machine text also makes one statistical threshold unclear.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Wait at tight end and select Likely as a cheap upside option; replace him if the target role does not appear.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: New York Giants offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat Giants outcomes as high-variance rather than projecting certainty into Week 1 roles.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers identify the Giants as a team full of volatile fantasy outcomes centered on Skattebo, Jaxson Dart, and Malik Nabers.
profile_notes.evidence: Funston says all three carry wild ranges of outcomes and calls the team fascinating from a fantasy perspective. Harris agrees on Skattebo and Nabers as swing possibilities.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris sharply differs on Dart, saying he disliked the tape and is out on him; the team label is an uncertainty signal, not a blanket endorsement.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not stack Giants assumptions as settled facts; assess each player separately and demand a price that accommodates role and quarterback uncertainty.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Isaiah Likely
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ciely has him inside TE12; Harris TE14, with role evidence against Theo Johnson determining downside.
profile_notes.summary: Likely has a plausible top-two Giants target outcome, but his rank is capped until camp confirms he is more than a predictable passing-down player.
profile_notes.evidence: Ciely invokes Nagy's history of leaning on a lead TE and sees a role near Kyle Pitts/Kelce/Ferguson. Harris says Likely is more slot receiver while Theo Johnson is the better blocker, making two-TE usage and deception relevant.
profile_notes.counterweight: Likely was not fully used in Baltimore, Johnson is an athletic blocker with splash-play ability, and a passing tell would reduce Likely's target ceiling.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor two-TE sets and target role; downgrade if Likely looks like a transparent pass-only specialist.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Kincaid is perhaps fantasy's biggest wild card among tight ends. The 2023 first-round pick has occasionally flashed a high ceiling (he actually led qualified tight ends in YPT and YPRR last season), but he also has missed substantial action (nine games the past two years) and has disappeared way too often (he failed to clear 13.1 fantasy points in any game in 2024, and never cleared six targets in a game in 2025). Kincaid was limited to a 37% snap share when active last season, and he has yet to finish a season better than 14th in fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old has TE1 upside, but he's tough to trust and has added target competition (WR DJ Moore) in 2026. Consider Kincaid only in the mid-to-late rounds.

Henry has settled in as one of Drake Maye's top targets, having reached 85 targets, 60 catches and 650 yards each of the past two seasons (each ranked in the top 10 among tight ends). A threat downfield and near the goal line, Henry has finished in the top 15 in aDOT each of the past seven seasons and 12th or better in end zone targets in seven of his nine campaigns. Despite the solid usage, Henry hasn't sported much fantasy upside, as he has failed to finish in the top 12 in fantasy PPG since 2020 (he has never finished better than eighth). The 31-year-old has added target competition this season (Romeo Doubs and A.J. Brown), so he's no more than a fringe TE2.

One of the most hyped-up players entering the 2025 fantasy season, Croskey-Merritt didn't quite live up to lofty expectations, but he was certainly very busy for a seventh-round rookie. "Bill" played 39% of Washington's offensive snaps but, while he finished 23rd among backs in rushing yards, he wasn't much of a factor in the passing game (3% target share). Croskey-Merritt will now compete with newcomers Rachaad White and Jerome Ford (among others) in what appears to be setting up as a committee in Washington. The 25-year-old has shown to be an effective rusher (4.60 yards per carry, 2.19 YAC), but he'll need a big boost in receiving work to find his way into the RB2/flex discussion. He's worth only a late-round flier.

profile_notes.subject: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid projecting a clear lead-back role in Washington; reassess only if Year 2 tape and usage improve.
profile_notes.summary: Harris labels Croskey-Merritt a Film Room Zero because his first-year tape resembled a backup-quality runner, while McCormick sees Washington's supporting conditions as another obstacle.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says he is fast but small, does not make defenders miss, ran upright, received little passing-game work, and was clearly passed by Chris Rodriguez late last year. The backfield also includes Rachaad White and Katron Allen.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris grants that a chaotic Commanders season, injury fallout, poor line play, and a surprise promotion were poor developmental circumstances; better vision and lateral elusiveness could change the story.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not pay a starter premium for Croskey-Merritt; wait for evidence that he can earn both early-down and passing-down work.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line fallout after starting LT Laremy Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps tear; Harris makes no automatic player-rank change.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps injury as a meaningful downgrade to Washington's offensive environment, though not one that can be precisely assigned to individual ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: He describes the line as thin without its starting left tackle and explicitly says losing good players hurts an offense.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris cannot draw a straight line from the injury to exactly how far Terry McLaurin or Jayden Daniels should fall, so he declines a mechanical rank adjustment.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Washington's pass-game options under review as replacement-line and protection information emerges instead of overreacting with a fixed downgrade.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: No back is top 30 for Harris; Richard prefers Rachaad White as a late PPR target if JCM fails to reclaim lead work.
profile_notes.summary: Harris wants camp to clarify whether Jacory Croskey-Merritt improved enough to lead Washington, while Richard expects White's passing-game role to make him the useful late option.
profile_notes.evidence: Croskey-Merritt was benched late the prior season as Chris Rodriguez emerged; Rodriguez is gone, but White and Katron Allen add competing paths. Richard says White was acquired for high-value touches.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris admits his instinct to fade rookies can create blinders and will listen if reports say JCM owns the job; White can also post very low weeks.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Wait for role clarity and select only at a discount, with White preferred for PPR floor if JCM evidence remains weak.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders running backs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid RB2 prices; a camp winner belongs nearer the RB20-28/fringe-RB2 range.
profile_notes.summary: Washington's White/Krosky-Merritt/Allen competition is camp-actionable, but no speaker wants to treat a named winner as a certain premium asset.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris lists Rachaad White, Jacory Krosky-Merritt, and rookie Katron Allen and says none appears great. Ciely says reports can change the hierarchy, but White's past inefficiency and Krosky-Merritt's limited recent résumé warn against overcommitment.
profile_notes.counterweight: A coordinator can choose a lead back and a good Commanders offense could create usable volume.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Watch for real separation, then prefer the cheaper other back if hype drives one player into Rounds 4-5.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Corum has spent his first two NFL seasons as Kyren Williams' backup, and that's expected to be the case again in 2026. The 2024 third-round NFL draft pick played well in the role last season, averaging a healthy 5.1 yards per carry (seventh among RBs) and scoring six touchdowns on 145 carries. However, Corum played only 29% of the Rams' snaps and remained a nonfactor as a receiver (36 yards on 14 targets). The 25-year-old has no standalone fantasy value, but he's an elite insurance stash, as he'd launch into the fringe-RB1 mix in the Rams' high-powered offense should Williams miss time.

profile_notes.subject: Blake Corum
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target around Round 8.
profile_notes.summary: Kluge sees Corum as an underpriced back with both standalone use and strong contingent upside if Kyren Williams misses time; Harris agrees with the value.
profile_notes.evidence: The case combines a cheap current role with a path to RB1-level work through an injury ahead of him.
profile_notes.counterweight: Corum still plays behind Williams and is not projected as the primary back while both are healthy.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Corum as a bench stash who can contribute modestly and become much more valuable if the depth chart changes.
profile_notes.episode_title: Five ADP Surprises Plus More Injuries

profile_notes.subject: Blake Corum
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draftable Rams RB, but do not elevate solely on predictable committee praise; require convincing passing-down evidence.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers expect Corum to generate positive committee buzz but do not view it as a reliable reason to displace Williams.
profile_notes.evidence: Gretch says Corum split carries but was a poor receiver on 116 routes, while Williams dominated the passing workload; Harris says Rams camp will almost certainly praise both backs.
profile_notes.counterweight: A genuine drumbeat about increased passing-down work, or unexpected Jack Bech/Hunter-type depth buzz, could change the committee forecast.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Corum as contingent workload upside and keep his price below a projection that assumes receiving parity.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

profile_notes.subject: Rams offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a strong environment, but do not let that alone erase individual age, role, and price concerns.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see Los Angeles as the NFC West offense most widely expected to be elite, while Harris warns that assumed certainty creates contradictory player valuations.
profile_notes.evidence: They discuss a possible 30-point-per-game offense, the resolution of Matthew Stafford's prior back concern, and the Rams' recent history of meaningful August role signals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris opens the episode by showing that consensus team projections frequently fail, and individual Rams can still decline or lose role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Rams environment as a supporting factor, then make player decisions on role, talent, health, and market cost.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Marks, a fourth-round NFL draft pick in 2025, played a substantial role as a rookie, soaking up 220 touches (22nd among RBs), but he struggled with efficiency (his 3.59 yards per carry and 1.61 yards after contact both ranked near the basement) and found the end zone only five times. The result was 9.4 fantasy points per game and one top-10 fantasy outing. Marks appears ticketed for a lesser role in 2026 now that David Montgomery was brought in to serve as the likely leader of a backfield committee. Especially in an offense that doesn't use backs in the passing game very much, Marks is no more than a bench/insurance stash.

profile_notes.subject: Houston Texans offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Downgrade Texans skill players only if repeated padded-practice and controlled-scrimmage failures show the line cannot gel.
profile_notes.summary: Richard calls persistent Houston line instability a medium red flag for the offense, while Harris asks what concrete camp evidence would justify changing player ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: Reports had Houston changing lineups daily and struggling to gel; Richard says his current skill-position ranks are optimistic relative to that risk.
profile_notes.counterweight: Preseason games are less useful than controlled scrimmages, and teams can solve line combinations as Chicago did the prior year.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track repeated protection failures in meaningful practice settings before discounting Houston's fantasy assets.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Woody Marks
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not chase pass-catching camp blurbs; possible third-down work does not establish a major workload.
profile_notes.summary: Harris leaves room for Marks to play third downs, while Kluge strongly doubts he is good enough to threaten Montgomery's lead role.
profile_notes.evidence: They cite a circulated report saying Marks could be involved as a pass catcher and agree Houston has no incentive to reveal final deployment.
profile_notes.counterweight: Kluge calls Montgomery far superior; Harris says neither speaker can prove the role before Week 1.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Marks as a low-cost contingent player only; do not upgrade him for a single pass-catching report.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing AFC South & Almanac Stuff

outlook.text: Charbonnet would've been entering his fourth NFL season as the clear lead back in Seattle, but a torn ACL during the team's playoff game against the 49ers has put his 2026 campaign in jeopardy. It's a tough break for the 2020 second-round NFL draft pick, who set career-high marks in touches (204) while ranking fifth among backs in rushing touchdowns (12) and carries inside the 5-yard line (16) last season. Charbonnet's minimal receiving role (career-low 24 targets) limited him to 11.3 fantasy points per game, however, and he has yet to deliver a top-20 fantasy campaign. Kenneth Walker III is gone, but first-round rookie Jadarian Price could very well cement himself a big offensive role by the time Charbonnet is healthy. The 25-year-old is worth only a late-round lottery ticket.

Four weeks into the 2025 season, it appeared Johnston was on the verge of a breakout campaign. The 2023 first-round pick found the end zone four times and scored 14-plus fantasy points in each game during the span. The return to earth was abrupt, as Johnston went on to average 9.2 PPG in his final 10 games. The 25-year-old has posted consistent receiving lines in each of the last two seasons (55-724-8 and 51-735-8), but neither resulted in a top-30 fantasy campaign. The Chargers offense should be better in 2026 with a healthy line and Mike McDaniel calling plays, but Johnston is unlikely to see a big boost in usage with the likes of Ladd McConkey and sophomores Tre Harris, Oronde Gadsden II and Omarion Hampton also in the fold. Johnston is no more than a boom/bust flex in deeper leagues.

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not assume a healthy or cohesive unit until tackle and interior questions are answered.
profile_notes.summary: The Chargers could benefit from an offensive-line-friendly McDaniel system, but Tucker sees legitimate uncertainty at every starting position.
profile_notes.evidence: Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt are returning from major injuries; Tucker questions center Tyler Biadasz's recovery, Jake Slaughter's shift from Florida center to left guard, and Cole Strange's fit after New England. Harris notes Alt was not fully participating when camp opened.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Shanahan-McVay tree can aid blockers, and all questions can resolve favorably.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor training-camp participation and interior cohesion before assigning a strong line-driven boost to Chargers skill players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target discounted Chargers pieces only on the conditional thesis of healthy line, protected Herbert, and a real offensive jump.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers can imagine a Chargers offense becoming a fantasy answer if health and protection finally cooperate, but view it as a conditional upside case rather than baseline.
profile_notes.evidence: Behrens says a healthy line and protected Justin Herbert could unlock a 28-30-point offense; Harris gives Herbert a mulligan and ties McConkey's rebound to the same factors.
profile_notes.counterweight: It requires unusually good Chargers injury luck, and the team has frequently failed to meet that sort of optimistic offensive projection.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the upside scenario as a tiebreaker for discounted Chargers, not as permission to erase downside.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Concepcion was selected by the Browns in the first round of April's draft. He is a quick and explosive short-to-intermediate receiver whose career 27.2% target share topped this entire rookie class. Primarily a slot receiver during his first two seasons at NC State, Concepcion played more on the outside in 2025 at Texas A&M, but he figures to primarily work inside in the pros (career 72% slot rate), while also helping as a rusher and returner. Concepcion will need to fend off the likes of Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie Denzel Boston for targets in an offense with quarterback issues, so while he has upside, he's best valued as a flex.

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Conditionally upgrade pass catchers if quarterback play becomes merely passable.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers argue that Cleveland does not need excellent quarterback play for its pass catchers to beat depressed prices.
profile_notes.evidence: The derived analysis identifies KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, and Harold Fannin as players who could benefit if Shedeur Sanders or Dylan Gabriel is simply adequate.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither host expresses confidence that the quarterback outcome will actually be adequate.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Cleveland receivers and tight ends as conditional value rather than automatic targets, and update after credible quarterback evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: KC Concepcion
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Double-digit rounds in PPR; prefer him if his price is near Denzel Boston's.
profile_notes.summary: Harris finds Concepcion draftable as Cleveland's apparent slot receiver, and Waldman prefers him over Boston as the safer role/price bet.
profile_notes.evidence: Waldman links the projected role to Todd Monken offenses that featured Zay Flowers and Ladd McConkey; Harris cites Concepcion's slot claim.
profile_notes.counterweight: Cleveland quarterback play could suppress both rookie receivers, and Boston's camp momentum may change prices.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Take Concepcion as a low-cost PPR upside receiver, especially when camp buzz pushes Boston ahead.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat early-season cohesion as uncertain after a nearly complete starting-line overhaul.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker calls Cleveland's nearly wholesale replacement of the starting line an unprecedented continuity experiment with high early variance.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Teven Jenkins had been on the team but was not a starter, and cites Spencer Fano, Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins, and Titus Howard as new additions. Tucker grants that most have played meaningful NFL football.
profile_notes.counterweight: The individual additions have shown positive things and could gel by December; Harris also says he is not qualified to make every technique judgment and is not down on every member.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid assuming immediate line quality for Browns assets; prioritize early-season evidence of the new group functioning together.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: KC Concepcion
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round pick inside Harmon's top 160; potential rise toward WR40s only if Jerry Jeudy is released.
profile_notes.summary: Harmon is a strong Concepcion believer and sees designer touches and separation ability creating cheap PPR utility despite Cleveland's quarterback concerns.
profile_notes.evidence: He praises Concepcion's explosion, man-coverage wins, and separation, expects a Zay Flowers-like usage plan, and says he can make plays after easy catches; Harris sees him and Boston as a late tandem worth ranking.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harmon flags catch-point issues/drops and says the fantasy use may initially be only bye-week flex level; Watson would worsen the environment.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use a late pick for PPR/developmental upside and monitor rep distribution and any Jeudy transaction.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: Browns quarterback competition
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade Browns pass catchers modestly only if Shedeur Sanders wins; avoid treating Deshaun Watson as equivalent.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers believe the Browns quarterback outcome materially affects pass catchers and prefer Sanders over Watson.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Watson's poor form and back-to-back camp interceptions, while saying Sanders can be a flawed but functional NFL passer; Harris says his modest Browns ranks assume Sanders rather than Watson.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris says Sanders must release the ball faster and cannot recreate Colorado-style extended plays; neither calls him an exciting superflex starter.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Browns receiver projections modest, but treat a Sanders starting outcome as a meaningful improvement over Watson.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Samuel reunited with the 49ers in July after solid yet unspectacular lone season in Washington. The former second-round pick cleared 85 touches and 800 scrimmage yards for the fifth consecutive season and finished 25th among receivers in fantasy points -- his third-career top-30 fantasy campaign. Samuel's role as a short-area target and occasional rusher gets the ball in his hands plenty (he's ranked in the top 15 among WRs in touches and RAC five years in a row), but it doesn't allow him much scoring upside (10 TDs over the last two years, and he's never cleared five end zone targets in one season). Now 30 years old, Samuel figures to resume his role as a short-area playmaker in Kyle Shanahan's highly-efficient offense. He's a fine late-round flier with WR3/flex upside.

profile_notes.subject: Deebo Samuel
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Outside Harris's top 50 WRs; accept the risk of missing an unlikely heavy-backfield-usage revival.
profile_notes.summary: Harris considers Samuel's recent film and shrinking usage evidence sufficient to fade him aggressively despite a familiar scheme and residual gadget upside.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Samuel looked finished in Washington, had rough hands, became a part-time player late in the year, and was displaced in some usage by Christian McCaffrey; McCormick likewise did not find him threatening even in a schemed role.
profile_notes.counterweight: A coach could manufacture an unusually large backfield workload, and Samuel did open last season with a 10-target, screen-heavy game.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Fade the reputation and do not draft on the assumption that designed touches will recreate prior elite fantasy output.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Deebo Samuel
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor recurring camp role reports before moving him materially above his reduced Pearsall-area rank.
profile_notes.summary: Harris is skeptical that Samuel's one-year San Francisco return restores draft value.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Samuel looked washed in Washington last year and initially cannot rank him much higher than the reduced Pearsall ranking.
profile_notes.counterweight: Samuel could force a rise if daily camp reporting consistently calls him crucial to the offense.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Samuel on a watch list rather than assuming a reunion creates an automatic bounceback.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Diggs signed with the Commanders in August after he was released by the Patriots earlier this offseason. Successful in his return from an ACL tear suffered midway through 2024, the veteran receiver's lone season in New England resulted in 85 catches (ninth among wide receivers) and his seventh career 1,000-yard campaign. Diggs paced the position with an incredible 83% catch rate (second highest all time for a receiver with 100-plus targets) and ranked fourth in yards per route run (2.8). Not used much near the goal line, however, Diggs was limited to four touchdowns and finished 23rd in fantasy PPG. He obviously still has something left in the tank, but is now 32 years old and his usage is trending downward. He has a path to a substantial offense role in Washington and can be viewed as a low-ceiling flex.

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Stefon Diggs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target around Round 10 as a capped-upside bench receiver.
profile_notes.summary: Harris treats Diggs as a fourth-time Flag selection in an 'emeritus' role: useful at a large discount even if the ceiling is no longer elite.
profile_notes.evidence: The cited prior line reached 1,000 yards but only WR24 with four touchdowns, showing both the usable floor and limited ceiling.
profile_notes.counterweight: Washington's offense must function, and the episode does not project a return to peak-career dominance.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Diggs as veteran depth with contingent scoring upside, not as a roster's primary receiver.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line fallout after starting LT Laremy Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps tear; Harris makes no automatic player-rank change.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps injury as a meaningful downgrade to Washington's offensive environment, though not one that can be precisely assigned to individual ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: He describes the line as thin without its starting left tackle and explicitly says losing good players hurts an offense.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris cannot draw a straight line from the injury to exactly how far Terry McLaurin or Jayden Daniels should fall, so he declines a mechanical rank adjustment.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Washington's pass-game options under review as replacement-line and protection information emerges instead of overreacting with a fixed downgrade.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Modest environmental upgrade following Diggs's signing; no Harris downgrade for Terry McLaurin.
profile_notes.summary: Harris believes Diggs gives Washington a needed credible receiver and can improve the environment for Jayden Daniels, McLaurin, and the offense without taking McLaurin out of his prime role.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris notes that all Commanders pass catchers other than McLaurin had unstable week-to-week roles, while Diggs has a distinctly stronger portfolio. More sustained offense would create additional yards, touchdowns, and possession time.
profile_notes.counterweight: Diggs's personal ceiling is tied to the offense returning to its better two-years-ago form; Washington was not good last year, and Harris says some of that may have been Marcus Mariota-related.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not downgrade McLaurin just for a normal complementary receiver addition; modestly improve the outlook for a functional Commanders passing ecosystem.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

profile_notes.subject: Stefon Diggs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draftable as a WR43-45-range receiver whose ceiling depends on Washington becoming a strong offense.
profile_notes.summary: Harris considers Diggs a useful, draftable Washington addition, but as a passenger whose fantasy ceiling requires a better overall offense rather than its primary driver.
profile_notes.evidence: Diggs was strong against zone, reliable, productive from the slot and outside, and retained excellent hands with New England; Harris had already mentally placed him with Washington and therefore did not change his rank.
profile_notes.counterweight: In the playoffs, quality defenses pressed and doubled him because New England had no other man-beating threat; Harris says Diggs no longer has the quicks to punish that coverage and should not be a team's best receiver.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Diggs as a discounted secondary receiver, not as a return to former alpha volume or a standalone bet on target dominance.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

outlook.text: Godwin is on the comeback trail after injuries have limited him to 16 games during the past two seasons. In 2025, he appeared in nine games and reached 11 fantasy points only twice. It seems like a long time ago, Godwin was second among receivers in fantasy points in 2024 when he suffered a severe ankle injury. He wasn't nearly as effective when he was on the field last season, but he's now more than a full year recovered from the injury and has less target competition with Mike Evans no longer on the roster. Entering his age-30 season, Godwin's days as a fantasy WR1 may be over, but with Emeka Egbuka as his only competition to lead the team in targets, he certainly has a path to flex numbers.

profile_notes.subject: Chris Godwin
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Consider as a potentially cheaper path into Tampa Bay if the offense rebounds.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Godwin as a possible lower-cost way to access a Tampa Bay passing offense that could rebound.
profile_notes.evidence: Jets beat reporters reportedly saw wow-factor plays from Godwin and Emeka Egbuka during the teams' joint practice.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris does not name a draft range or project a specific target role, and the positive report is a single practice observation.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Compare Godwin's draft cost with Tampa teammates and use him as a value access point rather than chasing the practice report at any price.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Tampa Bay Buccaneers receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Prefer Egbuka at a reasonable price, but avoid letting camp helium force a WR13 price; Godwin/McMillan remain health and role-dependent.
profile_notes.summary: Harris expects Egbuka to earn the strongest camp drumbeat but warns that any receiver price can become untenable; Tampa's frequent three-WR usage limits the value of two-WR-set chatter.
profile_notes.evidence: Egbuka has helium and is Harris's preferred player; Godwin is a good player recovering from serious injury, while McMillan returned late after a frightening broken-neck injury.
profile_notes.counterweight: Egbuka had hands issues in the prior season, Godwin has burned managers through injury, and camp cannot definitively establish the target order among three regular receivers.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft upside at a rational price and ignore shallow formation/depth-chart claims in a three-WR offense.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of Kayshon Boutte, DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

profile_notes.subject: Romeo Doubs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late WR4/WR5 target if camp confirms expanded slot and easy-button role with Maye; PPR-friendly ceiling is roughly WR34-36.
profile_notes.summary: Daugherty identifies Doubs as the Patriots player most worth tracking because a shift into the short-area Stefon Diggs role could make him a usable WR3 at a depressed cost.
profile_notes.evidence: Reports had Doubs taking the Diggs-like role, with more underneath/easier targets than he received in Green Bay; Harris agrees that a tangible slot alignment change is believable and valuable with Maye.
profile_notes.counterweight: Doubs has been a downfield player, the role has a ceiling, and one early camp talking point is not proof of regular-season usage.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor alignment reports and target cheaply in PPR if the underneath role becomes sustained.
profile_notes.episode_title: Drake Maye & Josh Allen & Previewing AFC East

outlook.text: Higgins is out for the 2026 season after tearing his ACL in mid August. As a rookie, the 2025 second-round pick played 58% of Houston's offensive snaps and handled a 12% target share en route to clearing 500 yards and scoring six touchdowns. Higgins averaged a lowly 7.6 fantasy PPG, but the 6-foot-4 perimeter receiver is a good bet for a larger role opposite Nico Collins once healthy in 2027. Keep him stashed in dynasty.

profile_notes.subject: Jaden Higgins
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Remove from 2026 redraft boards after the reported ACL tear.
profile_notes.summary: Harris removes Higgins from his board because the episode reports a season-ending ACL tear.
profile_notes.evidence: The injury eliminates his 2026 redraft role and creates contingent opportunity for Xavier Hutchinson and late-round option Jalen Noel.
profile_notes.counterweight: This report comes through transcript-derived coverage and should not substitute for current official medical reporting.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Remove Higgins from seasonal draft queues and redirect only inexpensive late interest toward the stated beneficiaries.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Jaden Higgins
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Double-digit-round receiver swing; be patient if early production is uneven.
profile_notes.summary: Harris takes Higgins as a film-driven upside receiver despite a crowded Houston path, and Eisenberg agrees that his eventual ceiling is meaningful.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites repeated quality tape, sideline work, contested catches, hands, speed, and a standout Week 11 Titans catch; Eisenberg calls him a possible eventual 1A opposite Nico Collins.
profile_notes.counterweight: Tank Dell, Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson, Nico Collins's health, and C.J. Stroud's difficulty supporting multiple fantasy receivers all constrain the immediate case.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Higgins for a league-winning range of outcomes and allow several weeks for a role to materialize before abandoning him.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Houston Texans offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Downgrade Texans skill players only if repeated padded-practice and controlled-scrimmage failures show the line cannot gel.
profile_notes.summary: Richard calls persistent Houston line instability a medium red flag for the offense, while Harris asks what concrete camp evidence would justify changing player ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: Reports had Houston changing lineups daily and struggling to gel; Richard says his current skill-position ranks are optimistic relative to that risk.
profile_notes.counterweight: Preseason games are less useful than controlled scrimmages, and teams can solve line combinations as Chicago did the prior year.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track repeated protection failures in meaningful practice settings before discounting Houston's fantasy assets.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Jaden Higgins
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Maintain normal draft value; do not downgrade merely because Dell receives positive recovery coverage.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers expect Higgins to remain Houston's relevant complementary receiver behind Nico Collins and resist letting speculative Dell news change that view.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris came out of film review positive on Higgins; Kluge says Higgins looked good in limited prior-year work and Houston plays substantial 11 personnel.
profile_notes.counterweight: C.J. Stroud and the offensive line were rough, limiting confidence that Houston supports many elite receivers, and a fully recovered Dell adds target competition.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Higgins as a value target at baseline cost and react only to real role/health evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing AFC South & Almanac Stuff

outlook.text: After missing nearly the entire first half of 2025, Coker passed Xavier Legette and took on a larger offensive role opposite Tetairoa McMillan. From Week 8 onward (11 games, including the playoffs), Coker played 73% of the snaps and handled a 17.8% target share. The fantasy output was inconsistent (below 11.5 points in seven games), but he peaked down the stretch (more than 14 points in four of his final six, including a 9-134-1 showing against the Rams in the playoffs). Coker's strong finish is encouraging, though his rookie season went similarly (14-plus points three times, but under 11 in the other nine games). A healthy 2026 could get Coker to the next level, but flex production is his likely ceiling as long as McMillan is commanding one-quarter (if not more) of the targets in Carolina's Bryce Young-led offense.

profile_notes.subject: Jalen Coker
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round pick, particularly in three-receiver leagues.
profile_notes.summary: Eisenberg expects Coker to be Carolina's No. 2 receiver and views the gap between his ADP and Tetairoa McMillan's as too large; Harris agrees with the player evaluation.
profile_notes.evidence: Eisenberg says Coker matched McMillan's targets per game and outproduced him over his final five games including playoffs; Harris highlights Coker's hands, ball skills, and usable alignment versatility.
profile_notes.counterweight: Darren Waller could affect the passing game, Bryce Young still limits certainty, and Eisenberg does not guarantee a top-20 finish.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Coker for affordable WR3-type upside rather than paying for a premium rookie receiver outcome.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Carolina Panthers receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Jalen Coker is a late WR5/6 only; do not let ordinary camp praise create enthusiasm for receivers behind Tetairoa McMillan.
profile_notes.summary: Harris has a soft spot for Coker but neither speaker expects Carolina camp to create strong value beyond McMillan.
profile_notes.evidence: Coker had a standout playoff game and previously flashed as an undrafted player; Harris has him inside his top 60. Chris Brazell joins as a third-round rookie but does not obviously displace him.
profile_notes.counterweight: McCormick calls Coker a theoretical/deep option and sees no serious competition signal; McMillan's expected second-year improvement is not informative.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Coker only as a cheap late dart and do not chase positive camp blurbs.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Jeudy's up-and-down career continues, as he has now finished outside the top 50 receivers in fantasy PPG four times in six seasons and inside the top 25 twice in the last four years. Jeudy has handled a target share in the 19-23% range all six seasons, but he hasn't found the end zone very often (17 TDs in 91 games) and has struggled with drops (32). Horrific efficiency (48% catch rate, 5.7 YPT) was a big issue last season and led to a career-low 7.1 fantasy PPG. Life might not be much better in 2026 with Cleveland's quarterback situation still unsolved and a lot more target competition (rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston join Harold Fannin Jr.). On the other hand, Jeudy, 27, is still in his prime and it has only been one season since he ranked sixth in the league with 1,229 receiving yards. He has some bounce-back potential, but Jeudy is safest as a bench player.

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Conditionally upgrade pass catchers if quarterback play becomes merely passable.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers argue that Cleveland does not need excellent quarterback play for its pass catchers to beat depressed prices.
profile_notes.evidence: The derived analysis identifies KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, and Harold Fannin as players who could benefit if Shedeur Sanders or Dylan Gabriel is simply adequate.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither host expresses confidence that the quarterback outcome will actually be adequate.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Cleveland receivers and tight ends as conditional value rather than automatic targets, and update after credible quarterback evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat early-season cohesion as uncertain after a nearly complete starting-line overhaul.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker calls Cleveland's nearly wholesale replacement of the starting line an unprecedented continuity experiment with high early variance.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Teven Jenkins had been on the team but was not a starter, and cites Spencer Fano, Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins, and Titus Howard as new additions. Tucker grants that most have played meaningful NFL football.
profile_notes.counterweight: The individual additions have shown positive things and could gel by December; Harris also says he is not qualified to make every technique judgment and is not down on every member.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid assuming immediate line quality for Browns assets; prioritize early-season evidence of the new group functioning together.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Browns quarterback competition
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade Browns pass catchers modestly only if Shedeur Sanders wins; avoid treating Deshaun Watson as equivalent.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers believe the Browns quarterback outcome materially affects pass catchers and prefer Sanders over Watson.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Watson's poor form and back-to-back camp interceptions, while saying Sanders can be a flawed but functional NFL passer; Harris says his modest Browns ranks assume Sanders rather than Watson.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris says Sanders must release the ball faster and cannot recreate Colorado-style extended plays; neither calls him an exciting superflex starter.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Browns receiver projections modest, but treat a Sanders starting outcome as a meaningful improvement over Watson.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Murray signed with the Vikings after spending his first seven seasons with the Cardinals. The change comes after a disappointing and injury-shortened 2025 season in which he failed to clear 18.3 fantasy points in any of his five appearances. Murray has settled in as an accurate but conservative passer and continues to add value with his legs (78-572-5 in 17 games in 2024). Prior to the 2025 dud, Murray had finished each of his first six NFL seasons as a top-12 fantasy QB (points per game). Now that he beat out J.J. McCarthy for Minnesota's starting job, he'll have the luxury of working with Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson. Add that to his rushing ability, and the 29-year-old certainly could find his way into the weekly QB1 mix. Consider Murray in the middle to late rounds.

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not raise Jefferson from near his current ceiling on 'dialed in' Kyler Murray camp reports; downgrade only if doubts become sustained evidence.
profile_notes.summary: Richard sees Minnesota quarterback competence as an offense-wide variable for Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and the run game, but Harris sees mostly downside because Jefferson is already near ceiling.
profile_notes.evidence: Richard wants confirmation the quarterback competition is not real and that Murray outplays Minnesota's prior passers, which could force defenses deeper and improve the ecosystem.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both have heard optimistic Kyler camp narratives before and retain concerns about anticipation and inconsistency; Harris says the plausible adjustment is Jefferson falling toward WR12, not rising substantially.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid acting on generic camp praise; retain elite Jefferson pricing but watch for repeated evidence that Minnesota's passing environment is failing.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat all Vikings except Jefferson as non-starter-level drafts until Kyler Murray and line health prove functional.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers believe Minnesota's broken 2025 offense makes a Kyler Murray rescue uncertain, especially for secondary receivers.
profile_notes.evidence: They say J.J. McCarthy was not fine and the offense deteriorated; Murray is better but not automatically a panacea for Jefferson or Addison. Erickson identifies an injured/inconsistent Christian Darrisaw and center instability after Ryan Kelly's concussion-related retirement as major 2025 line failures.
profile_notes.counterweight: Minnesota changed quarterbacks and added linemen, and a coaching offseason could prioritize Jefferson successfully.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid treating secondary Vikings as automatic starters; demand a discount and monitor quarterback/line health rather than believing generic positive camp stories.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: One of the surprise second-half breakout players of 2025, Shough scored 17-plus fantasy points in seven of his nine full games, including six straight to end the season. The 2025 second-round pick was a solid producer with his arm (250.1 passing yards per game) and his legs (19.3 rushing yards per game and three TDs). Shough didn't show a high ceiling (he never reached 22 fantasy points in a game), though that can be traced to a shaky supporting cast. That's an area that should be better in 2026 with Travis Etienne Jr. and No. 8 overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy) joining the team. He's still unproven, but Shough enters Year 2 (same as coach Kellen Moore) as an intriguing fantasy breakout candidate. He's worth a look in the later rounds.

profile_notes.subject: Tyler Shough
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Superflex consideration only; track whether his mobility and accuracy sustain a starting job.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Shough as a mobile, capable young starter with superflex appeal, but not as a certain long-term franchise quarterback.
profile_notes.evidence: He highlights a scramble, off-platform throw, efficient pocket movement, accurate clean-pocket throws, and strong spot fades that boosted Chris Olave late.
profile_notes.counterweight: Shough's wins came against weak opponents, he can become an unnecessary checkdown player, and he must do full quarterbacking work to keep the job.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor early starting-job stability and mobility; avoid treating a promising half-season as proof of a locked franchise role.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Goff is entering his 10th NFL season, including his sixth with the Lions. The 2016 No. 1 draft pick has been extremely successful through the air over the past three seasons (4,500-plus yards and 30-plus touchdowns in all three), which has helped him to fantasy finishes of seventh, sixth and ninth. Of course, there's some survivorship bias here, as Goff's per-game finishes during the span are 15th, seventh and 12th. The reason for the limited fantasy output is a lack of rushing, as Goff has never cleared 108 rushing yards in a season and was held to 45 yards in 2025. Playing at his absolute ceiling as a passer and still no more than a fringe QB1, the 31-year-old is just a solid backup/occasional streaming option in fantasy.

Jones re-signed with the Colts during the offseason and will return as the team's starter. The 2019 No. 6 draft pick made a big leap in 2025 -- his first season with Indianapolis -- finishing no lower than seventh in completion percentage and yards per attempt. Despite the strong play, Jones was inconsistent as a fantasy option, averaging 18.8 fantasy points during 12 full games and posting three top-five weeks but no additional finishes better than ninth. Jones was effective through the air and scored five rushing TDs, but he didn't run the ball as much as in years past and might do even less of that in 2026 after tearing an Achilles in Week 14. He's likely to be ready for Week 1, but effectiveness is a concern, so he's best viewed as a midrange QB2.

profile_notes.subject: Daniel Jones
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Raise into late-QB redraft consideration now that Week 1 readiness appears likely.
profile_notes.summary: Harris raises Jones because the uncertainty around his availability has receded.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Jones now appears ready and moves him up from a prior placement behind Malik Willis.
profile_notes.counterweight: He says Jones would be ranked higher had his 2025 production not been interrupted by a torn Achilles.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Jones as a viable late quarterback rather than avoiding him solely for a presumed Week 1 absence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Daniel Jones
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Raise from QB26 only if strong post-Achilles camp reports continue through joint practices.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees meaningful upward rank mobility for Jones after encouraging camp reports eight months after an Achilles rupture.
profile_notes.evidence: Observers reportedly said Jones looked able to do everything in camp; Harris recalls that at Week 13 he was QB7 with five rushing touchdowns, fifth in passing yards, and top-eight accuracy metrics.
profile_notes.counterweight: Camp does not include hits, Jones's Giants history remains a concern, and Harris will not move him on one week of reports.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor the Patriots joint practice and subsequent health reports; use Jones as a contingent late QB/superflex value rather than a locked Week 1 starter.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

profile_notes.subject: Daniel Jones
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor Week 1 readiness; any training-camp setback triggers broad Colts downgrades, while full early practice restores baseline confidence.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers view Jones's health as the binary/slider variable governing Indianapolis's fantasy environment.
profile_notes.evidence: Kluge says the Colts were one of the league's best offenses with Jones and one of the worst without him; at OTAs he was doing seven-on-sevens and the team expected him at camp.
profile_notes.counterweight: Early verbal assurances are weaker than full practice participation, and a Riley Leonard/Anthony Richardson alternative would materially lower the offense.
profile_notes.practical_implication: If drafting before Jones practices fully, lower Colts players; restore baseline ranks after verified healthy participation, but react sharply to a setback.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing AFC South & Almanac Stuff

outlook.text: Mason is back for his second season in Minnesota and will battle 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr. for backfield opportunities. Mason's role was almost exactly as expected last season, as he was utilized often as a rusher (9.9 carries per game), but a nonfactor as a receiver (1.0 targets per game). Mason reached 13 fantasy points just once in his 16 games and it was a 23.6-point effort in Week 3, one of five games Jones missed. Mason, 27, is an effective rusher -- his 5.10 YPC ranks third and his 2.42 YAC second among 54 RBs with 350-plus carries since he entered the league -- but adding so little as a receiver (34 career targets) severely limits his fantasy output. Even if Jones were to miss time, Mason would max out as a flex.

profile_notes.subject: Jordan Mason
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Around pick 100 or as a later RB3 after securing starting lineup needs.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers target Mason as Minnesota's low-cost rushing-role bet and one of their shared post-hype sleepers.
profile_notes.evidence: Eisenberg says Minnesota's move toward zone concepts fits Mason's San Francisco success and points to his 5.0 career YPC; Harris praises his vision, power, and possible goal-line work.
profile_notes.counterweight: Mason has only 28 career catches, Aaron Jones could remain ahead, and a Jones absence could still introduce committee competition.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Mason as an RB3/bench ceiling bet, especially outside full PPR, instead of treating him as a locked lead back.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings running backs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris ranks Aaron Jones RB38 and Jordan Mason RB41; Mason is the preferred late side bet if the offense rebounds.
profile_notes.summary: Jones still looks good but is not health-trustworthy, while Mason is the more plausible early-down/goal-line beneficiary if Minnesota's environment improves.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Jones took a substantial pay cut to remain and has recurring health risk. Mason stayed more efficient than Jones in the broken offense but does not catch passes, protect on third downs, or play that role; Harris calls him the goal-line, workload, and late-game grinder.
profile_notes.counterweight: Mason is slow, needs a good environment, and PPR scoring hurts him; Jones remains the nominal leader. Neither expects ordinary August news to alter their baseline.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid assuming either is a weekly starter, but select Mason over cheap alternatives when betting on a Minnesota turnaround and a Jones absence.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Kamara is entering his age-31 season with major uncertainty. It's possible that he'll retire, but even if he plays, he's unlikely to be a fantasy option. Over the past seven seasons, only two backs age 31 or older have posted a top-30 fantasy campaign, and both required 16-plus touchdowns. (Kamara hasn't cleared nine TDs since 2020 and scored once in 2025). Injuries limited Kamara to career-low marks across the board last season (including a 10% target share, considerably worse than his previous career low of 18%), and he hasn't played a full season since his rookie year (2017). Kamara may land a change-of-pace role (perhaps even behind Travis Etienne Jr. in New Orleans), but that's the most we should expect. A longtime fantasy star, Kamara is worth no more than a late flier.

profile_notes.subject: New Orleans Saints backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Etienne is RB16 pending Kamara's contract/roster outcome; no-Kamara clarity can accelerate his ADP toward RB11-12.
profile_notes.summary: Kamara's contractual status is the Saints' decisive backfield variable: Etienne has an RB16 baseline after a strong year, but Kamara's receiving trust can materially cap him.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says the Saints may not intend to pay Kamara's $11 million, while McCormick sees Etienne's payment as a path to a clean lead role. Harris names Kendre Miller and Devin Neal as less established alternatives.
profile_notes.counterweight: Kamara staying may be an institutional nuisance but gives a known role; he remains a capable receiver, and any no-Kamara outcome could be followed by another acquisition.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor actual contract/transaction news, not camp touches; draft Etienne more aggressively only once Kamara risk is truly resolved.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Pacheco signed with Detroit in the offseason after a four-year stint with the Chiefs. The 2022 seventh-round NFL draft pick opened his pro career with a bang, totaling 2,139 yards and 14 touchdowns on 432 touches during his first two seasons (31 games). Injuries and a big drop in efficiency have limited him to 952 yards and three TDs on 232 touches over the past two seasons (20 games) and ultimately led to his exit from Kansas City. The 27-year-old will now get a shot to replace David Montgomery as Detroit's change-of-pace back to Jahmyr Gibbs. Pacheco might hit for the occasional touchdown, but he won't have standalone fantasy value unless Gibbs misses time. Consider Pacheco a late-round insurance flier.

Rodriguez, a 2023 sixth-round NFL draft pick, spent his first three seasons with Washington and has primarily played a depth role, but he did hit career-high marks in touches (115), yardage (530) and touchdowns (six) in 2025. Rodriguez has handled more than 10 touches in nine career games and averaged 13.1 touches, 65.9 yards and 11.7 fantasy points with a total of seven touchdowns in those outings. Though he's an effective rusher, Rodriguez is not an option in the passing game (seven career targets). The 26-year-old's contract included a healthy $6.2 million in guarantees, so he's likely to have a legitimate offensive role as a counterpart to second-year backs Bhayshul Tuten and LeQuint Allen Jr. Rodriguez might score the occasional touchdown, but his role won't allow consistent fantasy output. He's best stashed on benches.

profile_notes.subject: Chris Rodriguez
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draft after Round 11 as an inexpensive bench stash.
profile_notes.summary: Harris views Rodriguez as more than a pure handcuff and expects a plausible power and short-yardage role.
profile_notes.evidence: LeQuint Allen's injury and a coaching connection are cited as reasons Rodriguez could receive real work even without owning the backfield.
profile_notes.counterweight: The backfield remains a committee and the derived analysis does not provide a projected touch count.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use a late bench spot on Rodriguez in deeper redraft leagues, but do not draft him as an immediate weekly starter.
profile_notes.episode_title: More Flag Players & Cousin Josh's Frag Players

profile_notes.subject: Chris Rodriguez
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late, lower-cost Jaguars RB target unless an exceptional Bashaud Tuten drumbeat shows Tuten owns the first-team role.
profile_notes.summary: Kluge prefers Rodriguez as Jacksonville's most talented back at a far cheaper cost, while Harris agrees the price gap is larger than the meaningful talent gap.
profile_notes.evidence: Kluge cites tackle-breaking, contact acceleration, success rate, college ties to Liam Coen, and strong film; Harris notes the prior staff shifted toward Rodriguez late last year.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris sees Rodriguez as limited and without long speed; Coen may deploy a hot-hand committee, and Tuten could eventually earn the lead role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Take Rodriguez as a late committee-value bet and change course only if Tuten receives overwhelming, repeated first-team evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing AFC South & Almanac Stuff

outlook.text: After a one-year stint as Christian McCaffrey's backup in San Francisco, Robinson signed with Atlanta where he'll now operate as a change-of-pace back behind Bijan Robinson. The 2022 third-round pick soaked up 200-plus touches in each of his first three NFL seasons (all with Washington) prior to dipping to 100 touches in 2025. Robinson is a big back who can handle early-down and short-yardage work, but he's not much of a factor as a receiver (92 career targets). He's yet to post a top-20 fantasy campaign and he won't come close to that in 2026 unless Bijan Robinson suffers a major injury. The 27-year-old back is no more than a solid insurance stash.

Bigsby was acquired by the Eagles early in the 2025 season and progressively worked his way up to primary backup duties, a role he's expected to play again in 2026. Granted, it's a small sample, but Bigsby has been extremely efficient over the last two seasons. Among 48 backs with 200-plus carries during the span, Bigsby ranks first in yards after contact per attempt (2.75) and eighth in yards per carry (4.86). In fact, Bigsby has led qualified RBs in YAC each of the last two seasons. On the other hand, he hasn't been used much as a receiver (20 career targets). With overworked Saquon Barkley entering his age-29 season, Bigsby certainly has some insurance appeal, even if he defers passing-down work to Will Shipley. Bigsby, 25, is worth consideration in the later rounds.

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade offense and Saquon Barkley context if interior health holds in the new scheme.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker believes Philadelphia has a high ceiling and high floor because last year's underperformance was substantially injury-driven and the new system should help blockers.
profile_notes.evidence: Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson fought through multiple injuries, surgeries, and rehabilitation; Lane Johnson missed the second half with plantar fasciitis. Tucker says the new coordinator's increased play action avoids isolating tackles in straight dropbacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: The line did not play as a top-five unit last year, and the recovery of injured interior starters must persist.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat a healthy Eagles line as a positive contextual upgrade for Barkley and the offense rather than anchoring on last year's unit ranking.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Keep outside the small trusted-offense tier until the new Mannion system succeeds in games.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers refuse to restore Philadelphia to an automatic top-offense projection after last year's collapse and coordinator replacement.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites A.J. Brown's trade, questions around the line, and the team's decision to replace the coordinator despite prior Super Bowl success. Ciely believes Mannion's changes can help but says practice and preseason cannot prove a top-five result.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense has Jalen Hurts, a strong history, and a scheme that could improve play action/middle-field work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid building draft projections on an assumed Eagles bounce-back; wait for regular-season evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Shaheed re-signed with Seattle after the team acquired him at last year's trade deadline. Known primarily for his elite return ability, Shaheed made an impact at times as a receiver with New Orleans, but wasn't used much on offense after the trade. In 12 games with the Seahawks (including the playoffs), Shaheed cleared three touches in only two games and averaged 5.9 fantasy PPG. The team's financial investment in Shaheed suggests his role will expand in 2026, but he still has to fend off Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and second-year WR Tory Horton for snaps and targets. Shaheed enters his age-28 season yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign, and he's unlikely to get there this season while also focusing on special teams and working in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

McMillan is a fascinating late-round sleeper after he impressed as a rookie before missing all but four games due to injury last season. The 2024 third-round pick was featured during the final five games of his rookie season and exploded for a league-high seven TD catches (at least one in all five outings) and 19.8 fantasy PPG (more than 16.7 points in all five) in that span. He was limited in his return to action late in 2025, but did flash with a 7-114-0 performance on nine targets in Week 17. The 24-year-old has a path to a near-every-down role in 2026 with only Emeka Egbuka and 30-year-old Chris Godwin ahead of him on the depth chart. McMillan is worth the inexpensive flier on draft day.

profile_notes.subject: Tampa Bay Buccaneers receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Prefer Egbuka at a reasonable price, but avoid letting camp helium force a WR13 price; Godwin/McMillan remain health and role-dependent.
profile_notes.summary: Harris expects Egbuka to earn the strongest camp drumbeat but warns that any receiver price can become untenable; Tampa's frequent three-WR usage limits the value of two-WR-set chatter.
profile_notes.evidence: Egbuka has helium and is Harris's preferred player; Godwin is a good player recovering from serious injury, while McMillan returned late after a frightening broken-neck injury.
profile_notes.counterweight: Egbuka had hands issues in the prior season, Godwin has burned managers through injury, and camp cannot definitively establish the target order among three regular receivers.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft upside at a rational price and ignore shallow formation/depth-chart claims in a three-WR offense.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Ridley's second season in Tennessee did not go as planned, as the veteran receiver missed 10 full games and was limited to a career-low 17 receptions. He remained a featured target when healthy (seven-plus targets in his four full games), but that led to only one double-digit fantasy performance. The lost season comes after Ridley delivered consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, finishing both as a top-30 fantasy receiver. Ridley is now 31 years old and has added target competition with Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson in the mix. A Year 2 leap from Cam Ward could get Ridley back into the flex discussion, but it's more likely that he's headed for a reduced role. Ridley is worth no more than a middle-round flier.

profile_notes.subject: Tennessee Titans offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-draft Titans skill players gain volume appeal if the planned up-tempo system is confirmed.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker's key Tennessee nugget is a planned up-tempo attack, which could create more snaps for Cam Ward, Tony Pollard, Carnell Tate, and other Titans assets.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Brian Daboll brought Austin Schlottmann in at center because the coordinator trusts him to align the offense, make calls, and play fast. Tucker explicitly connects tempo and snap volume to fantasy value.
profile_notes.counterweight: Tucker says Schlottmann and right guard Volson are not considered average starters; Harris notes August tempo plans can vanish when a weak team is hit in the mouth.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the up-tempo possibility as a late-round upside input, but wait for preseason confirmation that the line can execute it.
