profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

outlook.text: Boston was selected by the Browns in the second round of April's draft. He is a big receiver with terrific ball skills and touchdown-scoring upside. He's not the fastest, but that didn't stop him from producing 62-plus receptions, 830-plus yards and nine-plus TDs during both of his seasons as a starter at Washington. He handled 45% of his team's air yards in 2025 (highest in this rookie class). Boston dropped only four of 209 career targets (1.9% drop rate is fourth best in this WR class) and has the look of a reliable possession receiver. He'll begin his career battling Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie KC Concepcion for targets in a Cleveland offense yet to sort out its quarterback situation. Boston is a fine late-round-upside flier.

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Conditionally upgrade pass catchers if quarterback play becomes merely passable.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers argue that Cleveland does not need excellent quarterback play for its pass catchers to beat depressed prices.
profile_notes.evidence: The derived analysis identifies KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, and Harold Fannin as players who could benefit if Shedeur Sanders or Dylan Gabriel is simply adequate.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither host expresses confidence that the quarterback outcome will actually be adequate.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Cleveland receivers and tight ends as conditional value rather than automatic targets, and update after credible quarterback evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Denzel Boston
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draft in double-digit rounds only if the camp premium remains modest.
profile_notes.summary: Boston is draftable talent with a strong camp, but Waldman sees his boundary role as less safe than Concepcion's slot archetype.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris notes Boston's outside opportunity; Waldman warns that boundary reads are harder for both Boston and Cleveland's quarterback once defenses disguise coverage.
profile_notes.counterweight: Boston may make exciting boundary plays and could be cheaper if market attention has not caught up.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Boston as a late upside pick, but choose Concepcion when their costs converge.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat early-season cohesion as uncertain after a nearly complete starting-line overhaul.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker calls Cleveland's nearly wholesale replacement of the starting line an unprecedented continuity experiment with high early variance.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Teven Jenkins had been on the team but was not a starter, and cites Spencer Fano, Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins, and Titus Howard as new additions. Tucker grants that most have played meaningful NFL football.
profile_notes.counterweight: The individual additions have shown positive things and could gel by December; Harris also says he is not qualified to make every technique judgment and is not down on every member.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid assuming immediate line quality for Browns assets; prioritize early-season evidence of the new group functioning together.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Denzel Boston
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round/dynasty pick inside top 160; monitor whether he earns X snaps over veterans.
profile_notes.summary: Harmon likes Boston's long-term profile and his complement with Concepcion, even though the X role makes immediate fantasy usefulness less likely.
profile_notes.evidence: He compares Boston to bigger X receivers such as Michael Pittman/Courtland Sutton rather than a pure boundary-only player and wants the two rookies to become starters by year end.
profile_notes.counterweight: Downfield X routes are harder with Cleveland's quarterback limitations, and Boston may have less year-one value than Concepcion.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Boston as a late upside/dynasty bet and use practice reps against veteran receivers to decide whether to elevate him.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: Browns quarterback competition
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade Browns pass catchers modestly only if Shedeur Sanders wins; avoid treating Deshaun Watson as equivalent.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers believe the Browns quarterback outcome materially affects pass catchers and prefer Sanders over Watson.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Watson's poor form and back-to-back camp interceptions, while saying Sanders can be a flawed but functional NFL passer; Harris says his modest Browns ranks assume Sanders rather than Watson.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris says Sanders must release the ball faster and cannot recreate Colorado-style extended plays; neither calls him an exciting superflex starter.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Browns receiver projections modest, but treat a Sanders starting outcome as a meaningful improvement over Watson.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Mitchell is entering his first full campaign with the Jets, having been acquired in the Sauce Gardner trade during the 2025 season. After playing sparingly during his first 25 NFL games (all with the Colts), the 2024 second-round pick handled a hefty 24.4% target share in eight games with New York last season. The usage led to two fantasy outings with 17-plus points, but he was otherwise a nonfactor (4.0 PPG). Efficiency remains an issue, as Mitchell's 44% catch rate ranks last, and his 6.0 yards per target is fourth worst among 77 receivers with 100-plus targets since he entered the league. The vertical threat will compete with rookie Omar Cooper Jr. for No. 2 duties opposite a now-healthy Garrett Wilson in the Jets' Geno Smith-led offense. Mitchell, 23, is not worth much more than late-round consideration.

profile_notes.subject: Breece Hall and Adonai Mitchell
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target Hall if nearby RB2 turmoil discounts him; Mitchell is a free deep-league final-bench flyer only.
profile_notes.summary: Harris and Daugherty see Hall as unusually settled as the Jets' lead back despite poor team expectations, while preferring Mitchell only as a no-cost way to test for early-season opportunity.
profile_notes.evidence: Hall is not holding out, being traded, or facing the prior uncertainty; Harris says camp Braylon Allen headlines are least important, while Daugherty agrees the two-back concern failed to manifest. Both call Mitchell a free flyer.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Jets offense may still be poor, Hall's RB2 neighborhood can shift as other camp news arrives, and Mitchell's likely hype would not distinguish him from many free receivers.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid camp overreaction, buy Hall at a discount, and churn Mitchell after one or two weeks if usage does not appear.
profile_notes.episode_title: Drake Maye & Josh Allen & Previewing AFC East

outlook.text: Mayfield is back for Year 4 as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback. He has put together three consecutive top-12 fantasy campaigns, though his 2025 season (12th in total points, but 19th in points per game) was a big step back from 2024 (fourth overall and per game). Mayfield tossed 26 touchdowns (way down from 41 in 2024) and severely lacked upside, managing only four top-10 fantasy weeks. Granted, the 31-year-old was not fully healthy throughout the season and did still finish in the top 10 at the position in key categories, including passing yards, passing TDs and rushing yards. With a solid supporting cast and Zac Robinson as playcaller, Mayfield has some rebound potential and does just enough with his legs to make him an appealing QB2 target.

Willis signed with Miami during the offseason and is set to start after two successful seasons backing up Jordan Love in Green Bay. Willis, a 2022 third-round pick, has very little experience (155 career pass attempts), but he was outstanding in limited work the past two seasons, completing 70 of 89 passes for 972 yards, six TDs and zero INTs (12.1 yards per attempt, 86% completion rate), while also adding major value with his legs (42-261-3) during the span. Willis played at least 80% of the snaps in three games with Green Bay and averaged 23.3 fantasy points in those outings. Willis' inexperience makes him risky and the Miami supporting cast is perhaps the worst in the NFL, but his dual-threat ability makes him a very fascinating late-round flier.

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade associated players only if the offense proves at least competent.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers identify the possibility that Miami is merely mediocre rather than historically bad as a major assumption that could overturn rankings.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon points to under-the-radar line additions, Malik Willis's small-sample improvement, and the fact that Achane could lose roughly four points per game and still approach the cited price.
profile_notes.counterweight: Practice performance remains poor and neither speaker declares the offense fixed.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor quarterback and line competence; buy individual Dolphins only when their price assumes an unrealistically disastrous offense.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line and overall-environment reports before making broad Dolphins downgrades.
profile_notes.summary: Harris treats Washington's dominant joint-practice performance against Miami as a meaningful warning about the Dolphins' environment, but not a final verdict.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Washington reporters described Miami's offensive line as overrun throughout the drills and its defense as repeatedly beaten by Jayden Daniels.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris explicitly wants to see the issue again and look for improvement through the month; De'Von Achane also reportedly broke a third-down touchdown play.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the offensive-line concern in Dolphins player evaluations and seek confirming reports rather than automatically abandoning every Miami asset.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

outlook.text: Stribling was selected by the 49ers with the 33rd overall pick in April's draft. Stribling had a productive collegiate run, catching 44-plus passes in four of his five seasons, three of which came with different schools. That production included 52-882-6 and 55-811-6 receiving lines at Oklahoma State and Ole Miss over the past two seasons. Stribling primarily worked as a perimeter receiver and peaked with a 22% target share with OSU in 2024. His overall efficiency is pedestrian, but he has good size and speed (4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) and is a plus blocker. Stribling has plenty competition for Year 1 playing time (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Christian Kirk), so a slow start is possible, but it's likely he'll eventually find his way to a bigger role and fantasy relevance. He's a fine late-round flier.

profile_notes.subject: De'Zhaun Stribling
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Round-14 lottery ticket in redraft.
profile_notes.summary: Waldman sees Stribling as the best opportunity bet among the discussed camp risers and is open to being wrong on his initial grade; Harris drafts him cheaply.
profile_notes.evidence: Stribling is big, fast, strong, can win contested plays, and has earned Brock Purdy's reported route-running trust amid extensive 49ers injuries.
profile_notes.counterweight: Waldman says his field-reading/route development is incomplete and that a rookie WR1 role would be bad for San Francisco.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Take the late lottery ticket, but do not translate camp highlights into a reliable weekly projection.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: De'Zhaun Stribling
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-draft total dart throw only.
profile_notes.summary: Harris uses Stribling as a low-cost late-round receiver dart after positive joint-practice reporting.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Stribling repeatedly looked like a pro in the 49ers-Titans joint practice and that he has been selecting him late in the show's mock drafts.
profile_notes.counterweight: The observation came without Christian McCaffrey or Mike Evans in the practice and is only a camp-report signal, not an established regular-season role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use a final-round-type pick only where roster construction allows speculative receiver exposure.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: De'Zhaun Stribling
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round draftable receiver; do not pay a ninth-round price.
profile_notes.summary: Harris raises Stribling into late-draft consideration because Pearsall's injury creates a second-round-sized opening.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Stribling was unpopular with draft experts but now has a clearer opportunity behind the injured starter.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris calls him an absolute cipher and notes that nobody knows whether he can play; Deebo Samuel's return further complicates the room.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Stribling as a cheap opportunity bet and avoid converting depth-chart vacancy into a starter projection.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: De'Zhaun Stribling
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Very-late receiver target if reports place him fully in the Jauan Jennings-type role.
profile_notes.summary: Gretch sees Stribling as a limited but interesting player with cheap opportunity if the 49ers intend him to inherit Jauan Jennings's full role.
profile_notes.evidence: Gretch cites Stribling's high draft slot, blocking, and ball-in-hand ability; Harris agrees he is not in his top 80 but recognizes the second-round investment and low current cost.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both note that the role is not proven and San Francisco's sunny receiver messaging is unreliable.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use a late pick if role-specific reports are strong, rather than drafting on draft capital alone.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Bernard was selected by the Steelers in the second round of April's draft. Bernard is a solid, reliable receiver with good size who can align all over the formation (55% slot in 53 collegiate games). Despite playing at three schools in four years, Bernard's production increased each season, including a strong 64-862-7 receiving line (plus 18-101-2 rushing) in 2025. He dropped only four of 240 career targets. Bernard is likely to open his career third in line at receiver behind Michael Pittman Jr. and DK Metcalf. That will create a tough path to consistent rookie-season usage and production, so he's only worth draft consideration in the later rounds.

profile_notes.subject: Jeremy Bernard
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Dynasty and in-season waiver speed-dial watch; seek camp evidence that he has earned an immediate role.
profile_notes.summary: Harmon likes Bernard as a high-floor glue prospect and both speakers see him as the relevant Steelers receiver to monitor for long-term or injury-contingent value.
profile_notes.evidence: They compare his deployment to Pittman's and identify a possible opening if Pittman or Metcalf misses time.
profile_notes.counterweight: Bernard must first earn a role, and neither speaker treats positive practice reports as a reason to draft him into an ordinary redraft lineup.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track his camp reps and add only if a credible depth-chart or injury-related opening appears.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: Pittsburgh Steelers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a stable, projectable offense; do not manufacture large camp-based projections.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see a reasonably high/projectable Steelers floor if Aaron Rodgers remains healthy, without an exciting ceiling case.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Mike McCarthy's high-floor play calling, a settled enough offensive line, and known top receivers; Harris calls the roster full of good professionals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both retain concern that Rodgers may have declined further and will avoid contact, limiting offensive aggression.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep established Steelers values near their baseline projections instead of reacting sharply to routine camp headlines.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: A team's No. 1 wide receiver is often a household name, but that's certainly not the case for the underrated Tucker, Las Vegas' top wideout for most of the 2025 season. Tucker has finished in the top 10 among wide receivers in both snaps and routes each of the last two seasons and ranked just outside of the top 30 in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns in 2025. Tucker, who also contributes as rusher, has yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign while working in the Raiders' struggling offenses and would need a terrific rookie season from Fernando Mendoza to get there in 2026. That's a long shot for the undersized receiver, so he's only worth a late flier.

profile_notes.subject: Las Vegas Raiders wide receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round/double-digit-round receiver dart only if one player becomes the clear alpha behind Brock Bowers.
profile_notes.summary: Harris seeks a late sleeper from a market-dismissed Raiders offense if camp identifies a clear No. 1 wide receiver; Richard expects Tucker or Naylor to emerge as the practical candidates.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris argues presumed bad offenses are often wrongly written off, while Richard notes Clint Kubiak's history of hyper-targeting one receiver but expects Brock Bowers to be the obvious centerpiece.
profile_notes.counterweight: No candidate is expected to crack the top 36, the receiver room is unsettled, and Bowers may soak up the target concentration.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track which player survives camp hierarchy—especially Trey Tucker or Jalen Naylor—and stash only after credible separation emerges.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Las Vegas Raiders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round receiver watch only if a receiver hierarchy emerges and Fernando Mendoza threatens Kirk Cousins for the starting job.
profile_notes.summary: Both see Las Vegas as a useful camp watch because an inexpensive receiver could become relevant if the passing game is better than assumed and a quarterback competition changes the outlook.
profile_notes.evidence: The Raiders publicly prefer Cousins to start the season, but a strong camp/preseason from first-overall-pick Mendoza could force a conversation. Harris says nobody is entitled to a role and wants to identify a clear winner such as Trey Tucker or Jalen Naylor.
profile_notes.counterweight: Brock Bowers is the primary target, the offense is widely expected to be poor, and Harris doubts Naylor's speed/film despite repeated organizational praise.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Follow the receiver and QB hierarchy for a cheap final-round target, but do not rely on a Raiders passer in standard one-QB leagues.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Davis is back as the primary insurance option behind Bills' feature back James Cook III. The 2024 fourth-round pick is one of the most valuable backups in fantasy, but flies a bit under the radar due to a very small game-day role when Cook and passing-down specialist Ty Johnson are both healthy. That's been the scenario most of the last two seasons, but we've seen Davis play more than half of Buffalo's snaps in three games. During those outings, Davis averaged 21.0 touches, 130.3 yards and 19.4 fantasy points per game. The 26-year-old has no standalone value, but he'll leap into the RB2 mix should Cook miss time, which makes him worth stashing on the end of your bench.

profile_notes.subject: James Cook and Ray Davis
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draft Cook at first-round cost for talent, but do not assume Davis becomes a clean handcuff.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers like Cook but see no credible path to a clean Ray Davis inheritance because Allen and multiple complementary backs would likely create a committee.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris calls Cook durable and a transformed runner worthy of a first-round price, but notes his small build and Allen's ability to take goal-line scores. Daugherty expects Davis, Ty Johnson, and Allen usage to frustrate any handcuff.
profile_notes.counterweight: Davis's rookie film appealed to Harris, and a strong team declaration could change the view, but neither expects it.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Cook for his own production, not as a stack with presumed Davis insurance.
profile_notes.episode_title: Drake Maye & Josh Allen & Previewing AFC East

outlook.text: Tracy is set to compete with Devin Singletary for opportunities in a Giants backfield led by second-year back Cam Skattebo. Tracy has produced 200-plus touches and 1,000-plus yards in each of his first two NFL seasons, but that doesn't tell the full story. Tracy got there as a fifth-round rookie in 2024 by impressing and taking New York's starting gig by Week 5. Last season, he quickly lost lead-back duties to Skattebo, but played a much larger role once Skattebo went down for the season with an injury (9.0 touches per game during Weeks 1-9, but 18.6 per game from Weeks 10-18). Tracy has no standalone fantasy value, but he's effective as a rusher and receiver. That makes the 26-year-old a solid backup who would be worth adding if Skattebo misses additional time.

profile_notes.subject: New York Giants offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat Giants outcomes as high-variance rather than projecting certainty into Week 1 roles.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers identify the Giants as a team full of volatile fantasy outcomes centered on Skattebo, Jaxson Dart, and Malik Nabers.
profile_notes.evidence: Funston says all three carry wild ranges of outcomes and calls the team fascinating from a fantasy perspective. Harris agrees on Skattebo and Nabers as swing possibilities.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris sharply differs on Dart, saying he disliked the tape and is out on him; the team label is an uncertainty signal, not a blanket endorsement.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not stack Giants assumptions as settled facts; assess each player separately and demand a price that accommodates role and quarterback uncertainty.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Tyrone Tracy
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late bench value independent of Skattebo camp performance.
profile_notes.summary: Tracy is a cheap contingent bet because Skattebo's high-contact style and injury create a realistic opening, even though the Giants offense is not an elite handcuff environment.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris references Dave Kluge's view that enthusiasm for Skattebo can ignore a near-50/50 possibility. Ciely says Tracy would likely get about 60% if Skattebo were unavailable, rather than a Kyren-Corum-style automatic top-12 workload.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Giants are not a top-five or top-10 offense, other backups exist, and Tracy's ceiling is lower than elite handcuffs.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Stash Tracy as affordable injury/committee exposure rather than drafting him because of ordinary camp depth-chart rotations.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Washington was selected by the Raiders in the fourth round of April's draft. He's a big back with terrific speed who lit up the combine with a 4.33 40-yard dash at 6-foot-1, 223 pounds (127 speed score), while also checking in with the longest arms in this rookie RB class. His collegiate efficiency wasn't very good during stops in Buffalo and New Mexico State, but it was better in 2025 -- his lone season at Arkansas -- as he averaged 6.41 yards per carry and 3.62 yards after contact, both of which rank seventh or better in this RB class. He might not be much of an option in the passing game, as his career 4.2 yards per target is the worst in this RB class, but his traits make him an intriguing prospect. Washington will open his career as a clear No. 2 option behind Ashton Jeanty, which makes him an intriguing end-of-bench insurance stash.

Allgeier signed with the Cardinals during free agency. The 2022 fifth-round NFL draft pick impressed as a rookie in Atlanta, totaling 1,174 yards on 226 touches, but he hasn't come close to those marks while playing second fiddle to Bijan Robinson over the past three seasons, and he has yet to produce a top-25 fantasy campaign. Allgeier did score eight touchdowns last season, but he remains a nonfactor as a receiver, never clearing 18 catches in a season. The 26-year-old will step into a similar role in Arizona, as the primary backup and change-of-pace option behind No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love. Same as in Atlanta, Allgeier has no standalone value, but he's a very good insurance stash.

profile_notes.subject: Arizona Cardinals backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat Jeremiah Love as RB16 upside only if roster and usage clarity arrives; do not assume top-five draft capital mandates a massive workload.
profile_notes.summary: Harris makes Arizona's unresolved four-back camp hierarchy a key story because Love's ADP can be distorted both by rookie draft capital and pessimistic team projections; Richard sees a constrained environment.
profile_notes.evidence: The camp may end with only Love and Tyler Allgeier clearly relevant, or retain four bodies. Richard cites a hard schedule, weak line, first-year offense, and low team outlook; Harris cites historical splits involving Bijan Robinson/Allgeier and Gibbs/Montgomery.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris argues fantasy analysts routinely overstate certainty about bad teams, and a Conner or Benson trade could create immediate upside; Love is talented enough for hot-hand games.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor cuts, trades, joint practices, and ADP; draft Love only where a committee outcome is already discounted.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Arizona Cardinals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not write off the offense because of rebuilding expectations; balance possible skill-position value against the league's hardest projected schedule.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Arizona as a possible market-value offense because it is being declared hopeless, while Gretch sees meaningful skill talent but acknowledges a difficult environment.
profile_notes.evidence: They cite McBride, Love, Harrison, Wilson, and backfield depth; Gretch says the projected schedule is the NFL's hardest and the club is a large underdog early.
profile_notes.counterweight: The schedule and quarterback uncertainty can make running-back and passing-game efficiency difficult.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Consider discounted Cardinals talent individually, rather than treating the offense as automatically unproductive.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Sampson is back for Year 2 in Cleveland after an underwhelming rookie campaign in which he struggled on a small sample of work as a rusher (his 2.69 yards per carry was dead last among 65 qualified backs), but was a contributor in the passing game (23rd among RBs with 33 receptions). Sampson was a young rookie (he doesn't turn 22 until September), so there's still some room for growth, and he's positioned for a larger role behind Quinshon Judkins with Jerome Ford no longer on the roster. Expect Sampson to see some change-of-pace carries and a moderate pass-catching role in 2026. He'll land on the flex radar only if Judkins misses time.

profile_notes.counterweight: Neither host expresses confidence that the quarterback outcome will actually be adequate.

profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat early-season cohesion as uncertain after a nearly complete starting-line overhaul.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker calls Cleveland's nearly wholesale replacement of the starting line an unprecedented continuity experiment with high early variance.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Teven Jenkins had been on the team but was not a starter, and cites Spencer Fano, Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins, and Titus Howard as new additions. Tucker grants that most have played meaningful NFL football.
profile_notes.counterweight: The individual additions have shown positive things and could gel by December; Harris also says he is not qualified to make every technique judgment and is not down on every member.

profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

outlook.text: Ferguson is a potential breakout candidate in his second NFL season. As expected, the 2025 second-rounder played a situational role behind the likes of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen as a rookie. He didn't get much run, but when he did, he was used as a vertical threat to the extreme. His 17.5 aDOT is highest by any tight end (minimum 10 targets) in at least a decade. The Rams are returning the same tight end room plus second-round pick Max Klare, so while consistent production could prove elusive, Ferguson very well could emerge as the No. 3 pass catcher behind Puka Nacua and 33-year-old Davante Adams in the Rams' elite offense. The 23-year-old, who also saw five end zone targets as a rookie, is worth a late-round lottery ticket.

profile_notes.subject: Terrance Ferguson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Super-deep late tight-end sleeper; pounce only if September role evidence shows he is more slot receiver than third tight end.
profile_notes.summary: Harris calls Ferguson a super-deep sleeper because his small-sample film is exceptional, and Gretch identifies him as the Rams youngster most worth absorbing positive August buzz.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris describes explosive slot-route wins and says half of Ferguson's catches traveled 20-plus air yards; Gretch notes strong rookie efficiency and a possible matchup-piece role in heavy personnel.
profile_notes.counterweight: Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, and rookie Max Clare compete in a 13-personnel offense, making a consistent target role uncertain.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Ferguson on a watch list and add/draft only if role reports indicate a real flexed-out receiving job.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

profile_notes.subject: Rams offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a strong environment, but do not let that alone erase individual age, role, and price concerns.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see Los Angeles as the NFC West offense most widely expected to be elite, while Harris warns that assumed certainty creates contradictory player valuations.
profile_notes.evidence: They discuss a possible 30-point-per-game offense, the resolution of Matthew Stafford's prior back concern, and the Rams' recent history of meaningful August role signals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris opens the episode by showing that consensus team projections frequently fail, and individual Rams can still decline or lose role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Rams environment as a supporting factor, then make player decisions on role, talent, health, and market cost.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Johnson's impressive progression continued in 2025, as the converted wide receiver posted career-high marks in targets, catches, yardage and fantasy points (all four were eighth or better among tight ends). Johnson produced nine top-12 fantasy weeks, which tied for second at the position. He has finished in the top 12 in aDOT each of the past four seasons but hasn't been much of an option near the goal line (no more than four TDs or end zone targets in each of the past three seasons). The 29-year-old has added target competition, including eighth-overall pick Jordyn Tyson (once healthy), but he very well could settle in as high as third in target priority in the Saints' Tyler Shough-led offense. Johnson is a fine TE2.

Nailor signed with the Raiders and will battle the likes of Tre Tucker and second-year receivers Jack Bech and Dont'e Thornton Jr. for a starting gig in Las Vegas' new-look offense. Nailor was a rarely used commodity during his first four NFL seasons, all with the Vikings. The 2022 sixth-round pick totaled a 69-1,066-11 receiving line and never reached 30 catches or 450 yards in a single season. In fact, he's yet to clear six targets in a game. The 27-year-old very well could lock down a starting job in Las Vegas, but he's a long shot to make the big leap to consistent fantasy output in his fifth professional season. He's no more than a late-round wild card in deep leagues.

profile_notes.subject: Las Vegas Raiders wide receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round/double-digit-round receiver dart only if one player becomes the clear alpha behind Brock Bowers.
profile_notes.summary: Harris seeks a late sleeper from a market-dismissed Raiders offense if camp identifies a clear No. 1 wide receiver; Richard expects Tucker or Naylor to emerge as the practical candidates.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris argues presumed bad offenses are often wrongly written off, while Richard notes Clint Kubiak's history of hyper-targeting one receiver but expects Brock Bowers to be the obvious centerpiece.
profile_notes.counterweight: No candidate is expected to crack the top 36, the receiver room is unsettled, and Bowers may soak up the target concentration.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track which player survives camp hierarchy—especially Trey Tucker or Jalen Naylor—and stash only after credible separation emerges.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Las Vegas Raiders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round receiver watch only if a receiver hierarchy emerges and Fernando Mendoza threatens Kirk Cousins for the starting job.
profile_notes.summary: Both see Las Vegas as a useful camp watch because an inexpensive receiver could become relevant if the passing game is better than assumed and a quarterback competition changes the outlook.
profile_notes.evidence: The Raiders publicly prefer Cousins to start the season, but a strong camp/preseason from first-overall-pick Mendoza could force a conversation. Harris says nobody is entitled to a role and wants to identify a clear winner such as Trey Tucker or Jalen Naylor.
profile_notes.counterweight: Brock Bowers is the primary target, the offense is widely expected to be poor, and Harris doubts Naylor's speed/film despite repeated organizational praise.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Follow the receiver and QB hierarchy for a cheap final-round target, but do not rely on a Raiders passer in standard one-QB leagues.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Cooper was selected by the Jets in the first round of April's draft. The Indiana product is fresh off a breakout 2025 season in which he posted a 69-937-13 receiving line after totaling 46 catches during his first three seasons with the Hoosiers. Primarily a perimeter target in limited action from 2022 to 2024, Cooper aligned in the slot on 80% of his routes last season. He is a short-area target (9.0 aDOT last season), but still posted strong efficiency numbers, including a 2.61 YPRR. He'll begin his career opposite Garrett Wilson in New York's Geno Smith-led offense and is unlikely to produce consistent flex value as a rookie.

profile_notes.subject: Omar Cooper
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Wait for him to earn a starting role before using a redraft pick.
profile_notes.summary: Harris is discouraged that Cooper apparently will not start, while Waldman says the correct response is to make Cooper prove the concern wrong.
profile_notes.evidence: The discussion contrasts Cooper's first-round/Indiana story with immediate depth-chart evidence and possible A.D. Mitchell competition.
profile_notes.counterweight: Waldman acknowledges some players need multiple years to develop.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Leave Cooper on redraft benches/waivers until role evidence changes; retain patience in longer formats.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

outlook.text: Bateman is entering his sixth season in Baltimore following an injury-plagued 2025 campaign in which he was limited to a career-low 224 receiving yards in 13 games. After scoring nine touchdowns on only 45 receptions in 2024, Bateman had "regression" written all over him entering last season, but it was worse than expected. The 2021 first-round pick saw his target share fall from 15.4% to a career-low 11.4% and his only double-digit fantasy effort came in Week 3. The 26-year-old remains second on Baltimore's depth chart behind Zay Flowers, but even in a new scheme and with a healthy Lamar Jackson under center, he's unlikely to produce his first top-35 fantasy campaign. Bateman isn't the most appealing late-round draft pick.

profile_notes.subject: Baltimore Ravens offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor the three new interior pieces and tackle performance before assuming a strong rushing environment.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker sees Baltimore's changed interior and new under-center offense as a significant continuity risk despite potential upside.
profile_notes.evidence: He names injured-center returnee Ethan Pocic, returning Simpson, and first-round Penn State guard Vega Ioane as a substantially remade interior, while noting the rookie may switch sides. He also says neither Ronnie Stanley nor Roger Rosengarten met expectations last year.
profile_notes.counterweight: If the interior questions resolve positively, Tucker says the line could be good; Derrick Henry remains a rare durability/production outlier.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the interior transition in the downside range for Ravens runners and passing-game projections rather than presuming past line quality.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

outlook.text: Jennings signed with the Vikings in May. The 2020 seventh-round pick was a situational player during his first three pro campaigns in San Francisco prior to breaking out with a 77-975-6 receiving line and 27th-place finish in fantasy PPG in 2024. He dipped quite a bit statistically in 2025 and failed to produce a single top-10 fantasy week, but did score nine touchdowns (sixth among WRs) in a good Niners offense. The 29-year-old will now file in third on the Minnesota depth chart behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. He's headed for a big dip in targets and, especially with Kyler Murray or J.J. McCarthy under center, won't be a consistent fantasy option. He's barely worth late-round consideration.

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not raise Jefferson from near his current ceiling on 'dialed in' Kyler Murray camp reports; downgrade only if doubts become sustained evidence.
profile_notes.summary: Richard sees Minnesota quarterback competence as an offense-wide variable for Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and the run game, but Harris sees mostly downside because Jefferson is already near ceiling.
profile_notes.evidence: Richard wants confirmation the quarterback competition is not real and that Murray outplays Minnesota's prior passers, which could force defenses deeper and improve the ecosystem.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both have heard optimistic Kyler camp narratives before and retain concerns about anticipation and inconsistency; Harris says the plausible adjustment is Jefferson falling toward WR12, not rising substantially.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid acting on generic camp praise; retain elite Jefferson pricing but watch for repeated evidence that Minnesota's passing environment is failing.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat all Vikings except Jefferson as non-starter-level drafts until Kyler Murray and line health prove functional.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers believe Minnesota's broken 2025 offense makes a Kyler Murray rescue uncertain, especially for secondary receivers.
profile_notes.evidence: They say J.J. McCarthy was not fine and the offense deteriorated; Murray is better but not automatically a panacea for Jefferson or Addison. Erickson identifies an injured/inconsistent Christian Darrisaw and center instability after Ryan Kelly's concussion-related retirement as major 2025 line failures.
profile_notes.counterweight: Minnesota changed quarterbacks and added linemen, and a coaching offseason could prioritize Jefferson successfully.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid treating secondary Vikings as automatic starters; demand a discount and monitor quarterback/line health rather than believing generic positive camp stories.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Dell is on the comeback trail after suffering a devastating knee injury late in 2024 that cost him the entire 2025 season. It was a tough break for the 2023 third-round pick, who finished 18th among receivers in fantasy PPG as a rookie. While he wasn't quite as productive the next season, he was on pace for career highs in catches and yardage. The undersized Dell is certainly a question mark off the major injury, but, with Jayden Higgins out for the 2026 season, he has a path back to No. 2 duties behind Nico Collins. The 26-year-old could work his way into the WR3/flex mix and is a fine late-round flier.

profile_notes.subject: Houston Texans offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Downgrade Texans skill players only if repeated padded-practice and controlled-scrimmage failures show the line cannot gel.
profile_notes.summary: Richard calls persistent Houston line instability a medium red flag for the offense, while Harris asks what concrete camp evidence would justify changing player ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: Reports had Houston changing lineups daily and struggling to gel; Richard says his current skill-position ranks are optimistic relative to that risk.
profile_notes.counterweight: Preseason games are less useful than controlled scrimmages, and teams can solve line combinations as Chicago did the prior year.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track repeated protection failures in meaningful practice settings before discounting Houston's fantasy assets.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Tank Dell
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not factor into draft projections until practice/preseason film shows pre-injury movement; current positive team sentiment is insufficient.
profile_notes.summary: Kluge excludes Dell from the present Texans receiver forecast because of the severity of his knee injury and incomplete OTA participation.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Dell was still working on the sideline rather than fully practicing at OTAs; Harris warns that the room considers Dell an alpha and may create overly favorable reports.
profile_notes.counterweight: Kluge would change the expectation if visual preseason evidence shows Dell moving like his pre-injury version.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Leave Dell out of ordinary redraft plans until actual athletic recovery is visible, rather than responding to team optimism.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing AFC South & Almanac Stuff

outlook.text: Spears is set for his fourth NFL season, including his third as a change-of-pace backup to Tony Pollard. The role hasn't been particularly fruitful from a fantasy standpoint, as Spears has yet to clear five touchdowns in a season, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. Spears, who has also struggled with durability (nine games missed over the past two years), isn't used much as a rusher (100 or fewer carries all three seasons), but he is an effective receiver (top 10 among RBs in catches in both 2023 and 2025). The 25-year-old will resume his role as a receiving specialist in 2026 and, even if the Titans' offense makes a big leap in QB Cam Ward's second season, Spears is unlikely to find his way to consistent fantasy value.

profile_notes.subject: Tennessee Titans offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-draft Titans skill players gain volume appeal if the planned up-tempo system is confirmed.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker's key Tennessee nugget is a planned up-tempo attack, which could create more snaps for Cam Ward, Tony Pollard, Carnell Tate, and other Titans assets.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Brian Daboll brought Austin Schlottmann in at center because the coordinator trusts him to align the offense, make calls, and play fast. Tucker explicitly connects tempo and snap volume to fantasy value.
profile_notes.counterweight: Tucker says Schlottmann and right guard Volson are not considered average starters; Harris notes August tempo plans can vanish when a weak team is hit in the mouth.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the up-tempo possibility as a late-round upside input, but wait for preseason confirmation that the line can execute it.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Tyjae Spears
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Be receptive to a genuine new-staff workload shift, but retain durability risk in any upgrade.
profile_notes.summary: Kluge believes Spears has the talent for more than a satellite role and that a new Titans staff could choose him over Pollard, while Harris says he would be persuaded by a sustained role-vibes shift.
profile_notes.evidence: Kluge praises his quickness and notes the old staff restricted him after multiple collegiate ACL injuries and repeated year-two injuries; he cites first-team reps and explicit trust as meaningful evidence.
profile_notes.counterweight: Spears's extensive knee history is the reason prior workloads stayed low, and a healthy Singleton could further split work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor actual reps and staff trust, but do not assume a smaller back's change-of-pace history disappears without durability proof.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing AFC South & Almanac Stuff

outlook.text: Hopes were high for Allen entering 2025, but a slow start was followed by a season-ending knee injury in Week 4. During Weeks 1-3, Allen played 28% of the Jets' snaps and totaled 67 yards and one touchdown on 16 touches. The 2024 fourth-round pick has shown he can contribute as both a rusher (110 career carries) and receiver (32 targets), but he's simply not going to see the field much as long as feature back Breece Hall is healthy. Allen, 22, has some late-round insurance stash appeal, as he'd likely start over Isaiah Davis in the event of a Hall injury and would thus find himself on the flex radar.

Mitchell signed with the Chargers after spending his first three NFL seasons with Baltimore. The 2023 UDFA will compete with Kimani Vidal for change-of-pace touches behind starter Omarion Hampton. Mitchell has been limited to 140 touches over his first three NFL seasons, but he has been extremely productive when called upon. His career 6.34 yards per carry ranks second and his 2.50 YAC fourth among 89 backs with 100-plus carries since 2023. He has also put up 184 yards on 23 targets (8.0 YPT). Mitchell is on the small side, so his ceiling is likely capped (he has never cleared 11 touches in a game), but the 24-year-old would be worth adding should Hampton miss time.

profile_notes.subject: Keaton Mitchell
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draft late according to platform-specific ADP rather than a universal round.
profile_notes.summary: Harris wants exposure to Mitchell's speed and change-of-pace ability in a potentially explosive Chargers offense.
profile_notes.evidence: The appeal comes from an inexpensive path to splash plays rather than a projection that Mitchell will lead the backfield.
profile_notes.counterweight: He is explicitly the secondary portion of a timeshare, and platform ADPs vary widely.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Identify the local platform price before drafting and use Mitchell as a bench upside bet rather than a starting RB.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Keaton Mitchell
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round lottery ticket only; avoid an eighth-round-type escalation.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Mitchell's speed as a cheap path to explosive plays in a strong offense, while Eisenberg views him as a contingent split-back upside play.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris contrasts Mitchell's film speed with Omarion Hampton's; Eisenberg expects a creative Chargers offense and estimates a small regular role with a larger opening if Hampton misses time.
profile_notes.counterweight: Eisenberg does not expect Mitchell to inherit a full Hampton workload, projecting Kimani Vidal to remain involved; Harris also says growing hype could make the price unacceptable.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Stash Mitchell for explosive-play and injury-contingent upside, but do not draft him as a standalone volume back.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not assume a healthy or cohesive unit until tackle and interior questions are answered.
profile_notes.summary: The Chargers could benefit from an offensive-line-friendly McDaniel system, but Tucker sees legitimate uncertainty at every starting position.
profile_notes.evidence: Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt are returning from major injuries; Tucker questions center Tyler Biadasz's recovery, Jake Slaughter's shift from Florida center to left guard, and Cole Strange's fit after New England. Harris notes Alt was not fully participating when camp opened.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Shanahan-McVay tree can aid blockers, and all questions can resolve favorably.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor training-camp participation and interior cohesion before assigning a strong line-driven boost to Chargers skill players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Keaton Mitchell
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Free/late bench upside if a high-scoring Chargers offense creates a meaningful secondary role.
profile_notes.summary: Harris and Behrens see a plausible cheap path for Mitchell if the Chargers become a high-functioning offense, even while they do not project him as Hampton's equal.
profile_notes.evidence: They compare the possible offense to peak Mike McDaniel systems and say a Week-8 flex role is believable if the team scores heavily and uses a split backfield.
profile_notes.counterweight: This requires a specific offensive breakout; Hampton remains clearly the most valuable Charger runner and Vidal also competes for remaining work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Mitchell as a late contingent stash, not as a reason to project Hampton out of the lead role.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target discounted Chargers pieces only on the conditional thesis of healthy line, protected Herbert, and a real offensive jump.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers can imagine a Chargers offense becoming a fantasy answer if health and protection finally cooperate, but view it as a conditional upside case rather than baseline.
profile_notes.evidence: Behrens says a healthy line and protected Justin Herbert could unlock a 28-30-point offense; Harris gives Herbert a mulligan and ties McConkey's rebound to the same factors.
profile_notes.counterweight: It requires unusually good Chargers injury luck, and the team has frequently failed to meet that sort of optimistic offensive projection.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the upside scenario as a tiebreaker for discounted Chargers, not as permission to erase downside.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: James is an intriguing insurance stash as a candidate to work as 30-year-old Christian McCaffrey's primary backup in San Francisco. The 2025 fifth-round pick didn't record a single touch on three snaps during a rookie campaign spent buried behind McCaffrey and a host of veterans. James wasn't utilized much as a receiver at the collegiate level and underwhelmed at last year's combine, so it's unclear what his upside will be in the pros. However, if the 22-year-old wins the No. 2 gig over rookie Kaelon Black and McCaffrey misses action, he'll be a priority add. Consider him in the final few rounds in deep leagues.

profile_notes.subject: 49ers running-back handcuff
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not spend material draft capital attempting to identify Christian McCaffrey's backup from opaque August reports.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers have extremely low confidence that camp will identify a usable McCaffrey handcuff.
profile_notes.evidence: Jordan James logged only three regular-season offensive snaps; Kaelon Black was viewed as a reach, neither prospect has a McCaffrey-like receiving profile, and San Francisco does not disclose roles clearly.
profile_notes.counterweight: If a reserve is repeatedly reported to run the receiving playbook, that would matter, and managers with deep benches can cheaply stash both options.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Accept McCaffrey's unique injury risk rather than overpaying for a false certainty; use waivers or very late stashes if needed.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Strange played well in his first season as Jacksonville's clear No. 1 tight end, but it simply didn't lead to much fantasy success. The 2023 second-round pick handled a solid 16% target share during the 12 games he was healthy, but that was only enough to lead to 9.8 fantasy PPG (18th among tight ends). Strange simply hasn't been utilized much near the goal line, as he's yet to clear three touchdowns or four end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old is a reliable target for QB Trevor Lawrence, but with the team so well-stocked at wide receiver, consistent fantasy production is a long shot. Consider Strange a low-ceiling TE2.

profile_notes.subject: Brenton Strange
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Select very late as a low-cost tight-end swing.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Strange as a discounted version of a versatile receiving tight end with untapped upside.
profile_notes.evidence: The derived summary uses a 'souped-down Trey McBride' comparison to express the talent/role possibility.
profile_notes.counterweight: Jacksonville has a crowded pass-catching group, so target volume is not secure.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Wait at tight end if desired and use Strange as a low-obligation upside or streaming selection.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Jacksonville Jaguars pass catchers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Require a discount on Brian Thomas Jr. and Parker Washington; Harris would consider Washington in Round 6.
profile_notes.summary: Kluge calls Jacksonville's receiver pricing a trap because the market is paying for multiple pass catchers as though each can command a concentrated role.
profile_notes.evidence: Brian Thomas Jr. and Parker Washington must share opportunities with Jakobi Meyers, Brenton Strange, and Travis Hunter; Harris agrees the market cannot be right about all of them.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense could improve and one receiver could separate, so the conclusion is a price fade rather than a claim that every player fails.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid paying the crowded room's optimistic prices and select the cheapest exposure if pursuing Jacksonville.
profile_notes.episode_title: Five ADP Surprises Plus More Injuries

profile_notes.subject: Brenton Strange
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late tight-end target, often around the 14th round, after passing on premium options.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Strange as a potential breakout whose hands, athletic body control, slot usage, and speed create a loose pre-breakout Trey McBride resemblance; Zachariason agrees he is underrated.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris was impressed enough to move Strange from TE29 to TE8 after a TE23, injury-shortened season. Zachariason calls him a balanced natural catcher and important Jacksonville piece.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris explicitly says the McBride comparison should be tempered: Strange's downfield usage is far smaller, Jacksonville has many capable bodies, and he is not a power/explosiveness outlier.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Wait at tight end and choose Strange as an inexpensive breakout bet instead of paying for the established tier.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

outlook.text: Conner is entering his 10th NFL season without a clear path to touches. For starters, we haven't seen him in a while after he suffered a season-ending foot injury in Week 3 last season. Even prior to the injury, Conner was splitting work with Trey Benson, totaling 28 touches in two full games. Conner restructured his contract during the offseason, but his days as Arizona's lead back are over after Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier were added to the roster during the offseason. Conner, who delivered four straight top-15 fantasy (points per game) campaigns prior to 2025, will need to find a new home in order to have any shot at 2026 fantasy relevance.

profile_notes.subject: Arizona Cardinals backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat Jeremiah Love as RB16 upside only if roster and usage clarity arrives; do not assume top-five draft capital mandates a massive workload.
profile_notes.summary: Harris makes Arizona's unresolved four-back camp hierarchy a key story because Love's ADP can be distorted both by rookie draft capital and pessimistic team projections; Richard sees a constrained environment.
profile_notes.evidence: The camp may end with only Love and Tyler Allgeier clearly relevant, or retain four bodies. Richard cites a hard schedule, weak line, first-year offense, and low team outlook; Harris cites historical splits involving Bijan Robinson/Allgeier and Gibbs/Montgomery.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris argues fantasy analysts routinely overstate certainty about bad teams, and a Conner or Benson trade could create immediate upside; Love is talented enough for hot-hand games.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor cuts, trades, joint practices, and ADP; draft Love only where a committee outcome is already discounted.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Arizona Cardinals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not write off the offense because of rebuilding expectations; balance possible skill-position value against the league's hardest projected schedule.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Arizona as a possible market-value offense because it is being declared hopeless, while Gretch sees meaningful skill talent but acknowledges a difficult environment.
profile_notes.evidence: They cite McBride, Love, Harrison, Wilson, and backfield depth; Gretch says the projected schedule is the NFL's hardest and the club is a large underdog early.
profile_notes.counterweight: The schedule and quarterback uncertainty can make running-back and passing-game efficiency difficult.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Consider discounted Cardinals talent individually, rather than treating the offense as automatically unproductive.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Hill heads into his seventh NFL season positioned for a larger role following the offseason departure of Keaton Mitchell. Derrick Henry remains the team's lead rusher, but he plays only about half of the snaps, leaving plenty of opportunity for Hill, particularly in passing situations. We've seen Hill in that role recently, including a 2024 campaign in which he posted a 42-383-3 receiving line on 55 targets (11th most among backs). Of course, Hill isn't trusted with much rushing work (his career high in carries is 84), which is why he has never had a top-35 fantasy campaign in his career. The 28-year-old has a limited ceiling and would be on the flex radar in PPR formats only if Henry were to miss time.

profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor the three new interior pieces and tackle performance before assuming a strong rushing environment.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker sees Baltimore's changed interior and new under-center offense as a significant continuity risk despite potential upside.

profile_notes.counterweight: If the interior questions resolve positively, Tucker says the line could be good; Derrick Henry remains a rare durability/production outlier.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the interior transition in the downside range for Ravens runners and passing-game projections rather than presuming past line quality.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

outlook.text: Branch was selected by the Falcons in the third round of April's draft. Branch is a tiny slot receiver who posted an extremely low 5.2 aDOT during 37 collegiate games. That limited his efficiency numbers a bit, though he caught 71% of his targets and was terrific after the catch (7.9 RAC). Branch has the look of a versatile (perhaps gadget) player who will help as a rusher, slot receiver and returner. That role makes him a longshot for consistent fantasy output, but he does have a path to No. 2 receiver duties behind Drake London with the likes of Olamide Zaccheaus and Jahan Dotson his primary competition. Branch should only be drafted in dynasty.

profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
