profile_notes.subject: Atlanta Falcons passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor Michael Penix recovery versus Tua Tagovailoa starting; it affects Drake London/Kyle Pitts predictability more than Bijan Robinson's elite draft status.
profile_notes.summary: The Falcons' actionable camp fork is whether Penix can take first-team work and be ready Week 1 or whether Tua begins the season, with the quarterback mostly changing receiver/tight-end certainty.
profile_notes.evidence: McCormick prefers Tua's timing and predictability for London/Pitts, while Harris worries Tua should not be playing and might feel better if Penix wins. Both say Bijan's elite selection would not become a no-draft solely from Penix.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither option is a clean projection: Tua may be degraded, Penix's NFL competence is unproven, and the new coaching environment adds uncertainty.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track actual first-team recovery evidence; adjust passing-game players more readily than Bijan.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Love is back for his fourth season as the Packers' starting quarterback. The 2020 first-round pick has emerged as one of the league's best passers (he has finished ninth, fifth and third in QBR during his three seasons as a starter), but that hasn't converted to much fantasy production as of late. After finishing sixth in fantasy points per game in 2023, Love has finished 17th and 21st the past two seasons. A dramatic dip in both passing (19th in pass attempts both years) and rushing (282 yards and one TD total during the two seasons) has been the culprit. Love, who produced just five weekly finishes better than 16th last season, has a limited ceiling in Matt LaFleur's scheme. He's best valued as a back-end QB2.

Ward is eyeing a Year 2 leap following an underwhelming rookie campaign, albeit under tough circumstances. The 2025 No. 1 draft pick was plenty busy as a rookie (eighth in the league in dropbacks and pass attempts), but he struggled to 5.9 yards per attempt and took a league-high 55 sacks. Ward was rarely a factor with his legs (more than 12 yards three times) and produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 12th. The good news is that a tough rookie year isn't overly damning for a quarterback's career trajectory, and he'll be in a better spot in 2026 with new playcaller Brian Daboll and an improved supporting cast (Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson join a now-healthy Calvin Ridley). Ward will need to run more to become an elite fantasy option, but Year 2 is the breakout season for many quarterbacks, so he's well worth a late flier.

profile_notes.subject: Tennessee Titans offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-draft Titans skill players gain volume appeal if the planned up-tempo system is confirmed.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker's key Tennessee nugget is a planned up-tempo attack, which could create more snaps for Cam Ward, Tony Pollard, Carnell Tate, and other Titans assets.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Brian Daboll brought Austin Schlottmann in at center because the coordinator trusts him to align the offense, make calls, and play fast. Tucker explicitly connects tempo and snap volume to fantasy value.
profile_notes.counterweight: Tucker says Schlottmann and right guard Volson are not considered average starters; Harris notes August tempo plans can vanish when a weak team is hit in the mouth.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the up-tempo possibility as a late-round upside input, but wait for preseason confirmation that the line can execute it.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

outlook.text: Stroud enters his fourth NFL season yet to emerge as a quality fantasy option and having seen his passing production dip during each season of his career. Stroud impressed as a rookie with 24 passing TDs, three rushing TDs and a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game (18.4). During the past two seasons, he failed to clear 20 passing touchdowns, has a total of one rushing TD and averaged 13.8 points, ranking outside the top 20 both years. Stroud's efficiency has been solid at best and thanks in part to Houston's elite defense, he hasn't needed to throw the ball (or scramble) very often. There's little reason to expect much change in 2026, so even with a good, deep group of pass catchers, the 24-year-old is best viewed as a low-upside, fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

profile_notes.subject: Houston Texans offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Downgrade Texans skill players only if repeated padded-practice and controlled-scrimmage failures show the line cannot gel.
profile_notes.summary: Richard calls persistent Houston line instability a medium red flag for the offense, while Harris asks what concrete camp evidence would justify changing player ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: Reports had Houston changing lineups daily and struggling to gel; Richard says his current skill-position ranks are optimistic relative to that risk.
profile_notes.counterweight: Preseason games are less useful than controlled scrimmages, and teams can solve line combinations as Chicago did the prior year.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track repeated protection failures in meaningful practice settings before discounting Houston's fantasy assets.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

outlook.text: Mooney signed with the Giants and is the top bet to replace Wan'Dale Robinson as the team's No. 2 receiver behind Malik Nabers. Mooney's production has been all over the map throughout his career, having posted strong 81-1,055-4 and 64-992-5 receiving lines over the past five seasons, while also finishing in the 400-to-500-yard range the other three campaigns during the span. The 28-year-old has proven to be a serviceable starting receiver and could easily settle in second or third in line for targets in the Giants' ascending, Jaxson Dart-led offense. Mooney's ceiling isn't very high, but he's not the worst late-round pick in deeper leagues, especially if it's looking like Nabers won't be healthy in time for the season opener.

profile_notes.subject: New York Giants offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat Giants outcomes as high-variance rather than projecting certainty into Week 1 roles.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers identify the Giants as a team full of volatile fantasy outcomes centered on Skattebo, Jaxson Dart, and Malik Nabers.
profile_notes.evidence: Funston says all three carry wild ranges of outcomes and calls the team fascinating from a fantasy perspective. Harris agrees on Skattebo and Nabers as swing possibilities.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris sharply differs on Dart, saying he disliked the tape and is out on him; the team label is an uncertainty signal, not a blanket endorsement.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not stack Giants assumptions as settled facts; assess each player separately and demand a price that accommodates role and quarterback uncertainty.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

outlook.text: Harris is a Year 2 breakout candidate after flashing in a limited role as a rookie. The 2025 second-round pick quietly played 49% of the Chargers' offensive snaps, but he spent a lot of that blocking and was limited to an 8% target share. Harris is likely to open the 2026 season behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, but with Keenan Allen gone, his competition for No. 3 duties is 2025 fifth-round pick KeAndre Lambert-Smith and rookie Brenen Thompson. A potential starter in new playcaller Mike McDaniel's offense, the 24-year-old Harris is an intriguing late-round sleeper.

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not assume a healthy or cohesive unit until tackle and interior questions are answered.
profile_notes.summary: The Chargers could benefit from an offensive-line-friendly McDaniel system, but Tucker sees legitimate uncertainty at every starting position.
profile_notes.evidence: Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt are returning from major injuries; Tucker questions center Tyler Biadasz's recovery, Jake Slaughter's shift from Florida center to left guard, and Cole Strange's fit after New England. Harris notes Alt was not fully participating when camp opened.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Shanahan-McVay tree can aid blockers, and all questions can resolve favorably.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor training-camp participation and interior cohesion before assigning a strong line-driven boost to Chargers skill players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target discounted Chargers pieces only on the conditional thesis of healthy line, protected Herbert, and a real offensive jump.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers can imagine a Chargers offense becoming a fantasy answer if health and protection finally cooperate, but view it as a conditional upside case rather than baseline.
profile_notes.evidence: Behrens says a healthy line and protected Justin Herbert could unlock a 28-30-point offense; Harris gives Herbert a mulligan and ties McConkey's rebound to the same factors.
profile_notes.counterweight: It requires unusually good Chargers injury luck, and the team has frequently failed to meet that sort of optimistic offensive projection.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the upside scenario as a tiebreaker for discounted Chargers, not as permission to erase downside.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Flournoy is an intriguing deep sleeper as the favorite for No. 3 wide receiver duties behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in Dallas. Flournoy flashed in 2025, putting up 14.2 fantasy PPG during the only five games in which his route participation was at least 60%. Flournoy did disappear quite a bit behind the heavily targeted Lamb and Pickens (three or fewer targets in seven of his final 10 games), so he's a long shot for standalone fantasy value even if he locks down the No. 3 gig. The 26-year-old should be added to rosters only if Lamb or Pickens are sidelined.

profile_notes.subject: Dallas Cowboys skill players
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ignore Cowboys camp hype absent injury or a genuine George Pickens hold-in.
profile_notes.summary: Dallas offers little camp information likely to change established fantasy evaluations.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris describes annual hype around Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, while Ciely says the relevant fantasy roles have little genuine competition. Pickens signed his tag and attended work despite a possible future contract dispute.
profile_notes.counterweight: A Pickens hold-in could hurt early games, and injuries or unavoidably negative reports would be meaningful.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Filter positive Cowboys clips out of draft decisions; only move players for material availability news.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Williams was selected by the Commanders in the third round of April's draft. He is an undersized slot receiver (75% slot in his collegiate career) who soaked up 208 catches (fourth most in this rookie class) during his four seasons (43 games) at Clemson. He was primarily a short-range option (8.0 aDOT), but he caught a healthy 75% of his targets and added value as a rusher (career 25-187-2 rushing), punt returner and even as a passer (143 yards and two TDs on four attempts). Williams is in an all-out battle with the likes of Van Jefferson, Dyami Brown, Jaylin Lane and Treylon Burks for the No. 3 WR gig behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs. He's worth no more than a late pick in deep leagues.

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line fallout after starting LT Laremy Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps tear; Harris makes no automatic player-rank change.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps injury as a meaningful downgrade to Washington's offensive environment, though not one that can be precisely assigned to individual ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: He describes the line as thin without its starting left tackle and explicitly says losing good players hurts an offense.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris cannot draw a straight line from the injury to exactly how far Terry McLaurin or Jayden Daniels should fall, so he declines a mechanical rank adjustment.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Washington's pass-game options under review as replacement-line and protection information emerges instead of overreacting with a fixed downgrade.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Modest environmental upgrade following Diggs's signing; no Harris downgrade for Terry McLaurin.
profile_notes.summary: Harris believes Diggs gives Washington a needed credible receiver and can improve the environment for Jayden Daniels, McLaurin, and the offense without taking McLaurin out of his prime role.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris notes that all Commanders pass catchers other than McLaurin had unstable week-to-week roles, while Diggs has a distinctly stronger portfolio. More sustained offense would create additional yards, touchdowns, and possession time.
profile_notes.counterweight: Diggs's personal ceiling is tied to the offense returning to its better two-years-ago form; Washington was not good last year, and Harris says some of that may have been Marcus Mariota-related.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not downgrade McLaurin just for a normal complementary receiver addition; modestly improve the outlook for a functional Commanders passing ecosystem.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

profile_notes.subject: Jaylin Noel
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Remove from top-80 receiver consideration while the finger injury costs him early camp time.
profile_notes.summary: Harris lowers Noel after a finger injury that is expected to sideline him for a couple of weeks.
profile_notes.evidence: The episode directly states that Noel is out for a couple of weeks and that Harris removed him from his top 80 receivers.
profile_notes.counterweight: The transcript does not establish a long-term diagnosis or remove all future fantasy utility.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft Noel at the former tier; reassess when he returns and his role is visible.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Freiermuth's career trajectory has been quite the head-scratcher, but the bottom line is he is yet to emerge as a consistent fantasy starter. The 2021 second-round pick flirted with TE1 status in both 2022 (11th in fantasy PPG) and 2024 (14th) but saw a dramatic dip in usage in Pittsburgh's crowded tight end room in 2025. Freiermuth posted a career-low 10% target share and finished outside the top 20 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and end zone targets, and 30 tight ends bested his 6.7 fantasy PPG. The 27-year-old figures to play more in 2026 with Jonnu Smith gone and Mike McCarthy running the offense, but Pittsburgh is also better at wide receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard in the fold. Freiermuth has some sleeper appeal, but he's best valued as a back-end TE2.

profile_notes.subject: Pittsburgh Steelers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a stable, projectable offense; do not manufacture large camp-based projections.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see a reasonably high/projectable Steelers floor if Aaron Rodgers remains healthy, without an exciting ceiling case.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Mike McCarthy's high-floor play calling, a settled enough offensive line, and known top receivers; Harris calls the roster full of good professionals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both retain concern that Rodgers may have declined further and will avoid contact, limiting offensive aggression.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep established Steelers values near their baseline projections instead of reacting sharply to routine camp headlines.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Schultz has been one of the league's most consistent tight ends over the past six years, but with the exception of one season, he hasn't been overly useful in fantasy. Schultz was fantasy's No. 3 tight end in scoring while he was in Dallas in 2021, but he has finished 10th or worse in his other eight campaigns (that includes exactly 10th in three of the past four seasons). In 2025, Schultz ranked sixth or better at the position in targets, catches and yards, but he found the end zone only three times and has now cleared five touchdowns once in his career (eight in 2021). Schultz is a reliable target for QB C.J. Stroud, but with Houston's depth at wide receiver, he simply doesn't offer much upside. Consider him a low-ceiling TE2.

outlook.text: Legette is eyeing a Year 3 leap after a boom/bust start to his NFL career. The 2024 first-round pick flashed with 521 yards and four touchdowns on 55 touches as a rookie, but fell to 363 yards and three scores on 36 touches in 2025. Legette did post a pair of big games (24.2 points in Week 7 and 18.3 points in Week 11), but was otherwise held in check (3.6 PPG in the other 13 games). Legette has struggled with the ball in his hands (woeful 2.1 RAC in his career) and is behind Tetairoa McMillan and likely Jalen Coker on the Carolina WR depth chart. The 25-year-old will see some situational targets and carries, but he'll need a big Year 3 leap to find his way to fantasy relevance. He's no more than a late-round lottery ticket.

profile_notes.subject: Carolina Panthers receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Jalen Coker is a late WR5/6 only; do not let ordinary camp praise create enthusiasm for receivers behind Tetairoa McMillan.
profile_notes.summary: Harris has a soft spot for Coker but neither speaker expects Carolina camp to create strong value beyond McMillan.
profile_notes.evidence: Coker had a standout playoff game and previously flashed as an undrafted player; Harris has him inside his top 60. Chris Brazell joins as a third-round rookie but does not obviously displace him.
profile_notes.counterweight: McCormick calls Coker a theoretical/deep option and sees no serious competition signal; McMillan's expected second-year improvement is not informative.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Coker only as a cheap late dart and do not chase positive camp blurbs.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Bech is a candidate for a Year 2 leap after an underwhelming rookie campaign. The 2025 second-round pick was limited to 36% of Las Vegas' offensive snaps and cleared three targets in a game only twice. He failed to find the end zone while predominantly working as a short-range target. Bech will now compete with the likes of Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Dont'e Thornton Jr. for a starting gig in a new-look offense led by coach Klint Kubiak and, at some point, No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza. The 23-year-old is likely headed for a larger role in his second season and is worth a late-round flier.

profile_notes.subject: Las Vegas Raiders wide receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round/double-digit-round receiver dart only if one player becomes the clear alpha behind Brock Bowers.
profile_notes.summary: Harris seeks a late sleeper from a market-dismissed Raiders offense if camp identifies a clear No. 1 wide receiver; Richard expects Tucker or Naylor to emerge as the practical candidates.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris argues presumed bad offenses are often wrongly written off, while Richard notes Clint Kubiak's history of hyper-targeting one receiver but expects Brock Bowers to be the obvious centerpiece.
profile_notes.counterweight: No candidate is expected to crack the top 36, the receiver room is unsettled, and Bowers may soak up the target concentration.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track which player survives camp hierarchy—especially Trey Tucker or Jalen Naylor—and stash only after credible separation emerges.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Las Vegas Raiders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round receiver watch only if a receiver hierarchy emerges and Fernando Mendoza threatens Kirk Cousins for the starting job.
profile_notes.summary: Both see Las Vegas as a useful camp watch because an inexpensive receiver could become relevant if the passing game is better than assumed and a quarterback competition changes the outlook.
profile_notes.evidence: The Raiders publicly prefer Cousins to start the season, but a strong camp/preseason from first-overall-pick Mendoza could force a conversation. Harris says nobody is entitled to a role and wants to identify a clear winner such as Trey Tucker or Jalen Naylor.
profile_notes.counterweight: Brock Bowers is the primary target, the offense is widely expected to be poor, and Harris doubts Naylor's speed/film despite repeated organizational praise.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Follow the receiver and QB hierarchy for a cheap final-round target, but do not rely on a Raiders passer in standard one-QB leagues.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: TeSlaa is a candidate for a Year 2 leap as the favorite for No. 3 WR duties in Detroit behind Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. TeSlaa barely played as a rookie (27 total targets), but he had a very specific role and, believe it or not, tied for 11th in the entire NFL with 11 end zone targets. That helped lead to six touchdowns, four of which came when his snaps increased during Detroit's final six games. The 2025 third-round pick has a big size edge on both St. Brown and Williams, so while consistent targets are a long shot, he's still likely to remain busy near the goal line. TeSlaa won't be more than a boom/bust situational target most weeks, but if one of the starters misses time, he'll be on the flex radar. Consider him with a late pick.

Bell was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. The heaviest receiver in this rookie class at 222 pounds, Bell is a perimeter, possession target who increased his production in each of his four seasons at Louisville. That includes a 72-917-6 receiving line in 11 games last season, though he did tear his ACL in December. The injury could lead to a slow start to his NFL career, but considering he's joining a Miami offense devoid of playmakers, he also has a path to pacing the team in targets as a rookie. Bell could find his way to fantasy relevance if healthy and if Malik Willis plays well, but there are enough concerns that he's only worth a late flier.

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade associated players only if the offense proves at least competent.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers identify the possibility that Miami is merely mediocre rather than historically bad as a major assumption that could overturn rankings.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon points to under-the-radar line additions, Malik Willis's small-sample improvement, and the fact that Achane could lose roughly four points per game and still approach the cited price.
profile_notes.counterweight: Practice performance remains poor and neither speaker declares the offense fixed.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor quarterback and line competence; buy individual Dolphins only when their price assumes an unrealistically disastrous offense.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line and overall-environment reports before making broad Dolphins downgrades.
profile_notes.summary: Harris treats Washington's dominant joint-practice performance against Miami as a meaningful warning about the Dolphins' environment, but not a final verdict.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Washington reporters described Miami's offensive line as overrun throughout the drills and its defense as repeatedly beaten by Jayden Daniels.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris explicitly wants to see the issue again and look for improvement through the month; De'Von Achane also reportedly broke a third-down touchdown play.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the offensive-line concern in Dolphins player evaluations and seek confirming reports rather than automatically abandoning every Miami asset.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Chris Bell
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Remove from standard redraft ranks while ACL rehabilitation keeps him out of camp.
profile_notes.summary: Harris removes Bell from his redraft ranks because ongoing knee rehabilitation leaves no current draft case.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Bell is newly coming off knee reconstruction, has not participated in camp, and that the team is proceeding cautiously with his rehab.
profile_notes.counterweight: The transcript does not dispute Bell's longer-term talent; the conclusion is explicitly limited to present redraft availability.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Leave Bell undrafted in ordinary redraft leagues and reevaluate only when he returns to practice and a role emerges.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins receiver room
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Grind camp rotations for a free late receiver, especially Malik Washington; do not assume any player has guaranteed targets.
profile_notes.summary: Both say Miami offers a rare chance to find late value because the market views the team as hopeless and no receiver is penciled into targets behind the headline names.
profile_notes.evidence: Daugherty will watch Malik Washington; Harris lists Kevin Coleman, Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas, Jalen Tolbert, Tutu Atwell, and Terrace Marshall and says reporters should expose two- and three-WR rotations.
profile_notes.counterweight: Miami may struggle to push the ball, Bell's knee clouds availability, and open competition can yield no dependable player rather than a hidden breakout.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track repeated first-team usage and stash only the receiver who earns a real role; be willing to churn quickly.
profile_notes.episode_title: Drake Maye & Josh Allen & Previewing AFC East

outlook.text: Coleman was selected by the Broncos in the fourth round of April's draft. He is a 220-pound back who was highly efficient during four collegiate seasons at Arizona and Washington. Coleman didn't get much pre-contact help (1.80 YBC), but he made up for it after contact (3.73 YAC ranks second in this rookie RB class) and his career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is best in this class. Also solid as a receiver and blocker, Coleman has three-down ability, but may not get that opportunity until 2027. The rookie will begin his career behind J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey and perhaps even receiving specialist Tyler Badie. Coleman should be added only if Dobbins or Harvey goes down with an injury.

profile_notes.subject: Jonah Coleman
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid paying for Broncos camp/archetype hype.
profile_notes.summary: Waldman is skeptical that Coleman becomes a high-value rookie despite a plausible short-yardage role.
profile_notes.evidence: He sees adequate crease recognition, protection, and hands but insufficient burst, long speed, and contact balance; he expects Sean Payton's committee and J.K. Dobbins to retain primary/red-zone work.
profile_notes.counterweight: Coleman can receive early short-yardage or goal-line opportunities.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft him as the presumed Broncos lead; prefer Dobbins at his cited RB4/flex-type cost.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Denver Broncos running backs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Reassess usage as the Dobbins injury and preseason rotation develop.
profile_notes.summary: Denver's backfield has a preferred healthy player in Dobbins but remains likely to use all three backs.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Dobbins's early-down role was more repeatable and valuable, while Harvey had red-zone receiving work; Denver also drafted Jonah Coleman and re-signed Dobbins.
profile_notes.counterweight: Dobbins cannot be assumed healthy, Harris says Harvey can improve as a second-year player, and he admits he has not evaluated Coleman yet.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft any Denver back as a no-competition bell cow; use incoming health and rotation reports to separate their values.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Denver Broncos backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ignore ambiguous camp usage between R.J. Harvey, J.K. Dobbins, and Jonah Coleman unless injury or a durable regular-season role change occurs.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers regard Broncos backfield camp stories as a Rorschach test: optimists and skeptics will interpret small drills to support their existing Harvey/Dobbins takes.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Dobbins was good last year and likely begins as primary runner; reports about Coleman goal-line drills or Harvey opportunities do not settle a role. Behrens notes Harvey is being drafted far earlier than Dobbins in best ball.
profile_notes.counterweight: Dobbins has injury history, Sean Payton could allocate red-zone work unusually, and a real injury would materially change the hierarchy.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not spend attention or draft capital on speculative camp usage; reassess only for meaningful health or deployment evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Black was selected by the 49ers in the third round of April's draft. It was a bit of a surprise selection after Black failed to clear 190 touches in four collegiate seasons prior to not landing an invite to the scouting combine. He did clear 1,000 rushing yards at Indiana in 2025, but remained a nonfactor as a receiver, totaling exactly four receptions in each of his two seasons with the Hoosiers. Black will open his career in a battle with Jordan James for No. 2 duties behind Christian McCaffrey. He'll be worth an add if the 30-year-old McCaffrey misses time, but a lack of third-down ability may severely limit his fantasy output. Stash Black in dynasty formats.

profile_notes.subject: Kaelon Black
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Deep roster or dynasty stash; monitor 49ers health and the RB2 committee.
profile_notes.summary: Waldman views Black as a smart, versatile runner who could matter if he distinguishes himself in San Francisco, but not as a current certainty.
profile_notes.evidence: He credits Black's screens/receiving work, tough-yard finish, and versatility; Black has an abductor strain while the 49ers' backfield is depleted.
profile_notes.counterweight: Waldman expects an RB2-by-committee setup and notes Black lacks top-end speed.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Stash only where bench depth permits and react to a defined role rather than camp attrition alone.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Kalen Black
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round contingent handcuff in all formats, particularly after drafting Christian McCaffrey.
profile_notes.summary: Harris elevates Black as San Francisco's current best late handcuff candidate behind McCaffrey.
profile_notes.evidence: Isaac Guerendo is recovering from shoulder surgery, Jordan James has a fractured rib expected to cost two weeks to a month, and the remaining competition is thin; Harris calls Black the obvious third-round-shaped answer to the depth-chart hole.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris stresses that Kyle Shanahan will not reliably reveal the backup and that San Francisco may not give any reserve meaningful work unless McCaffrey is injured.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Black as a cheap contingency stash, not as an independent weekly flex.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: 49ers running-back handcuff
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not spend material draft capital attempting to identify Christian McCaffrey's backup from opaque August reports.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers have extremely low confidence that camp will identify a usable McCaffrey handcuff.
profile_notes.evidence: Jordan James logged only three regular-season offensive snaps; Kaelon Black was viewed as a reach, neither prospect has a McCaffrey-like receiving profile, and San Francisco does not disclose roles clearly.
profile_notes.counterweight: If a reserve is repeatedly reported to run the receiving playbook, that would matter, and managers with deep benches can cheaply stash both options.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Accept McCaffrey's unique injury risk rather than overpaying for a false certainty; use waivers or very late stashes if needed.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Allen was selected by the Commanders in the sixth round of April's draft. Allen has a good size and a solid efficiency profile, having ranked seventh in this rookie class in YAC (3.35) and 10th in forced missed tackle rate (4.5) during his four seasons at Penn State. Though he out-carried fellow draft prospect Nicholas Singleton in all four seasons at PSU, Allen was less involved as a receiver (career 70-490-4 line, including a weak 5.1 YPT) and doesn't figure to get much run as a receiver in the pros. Allen is a long shot as a sixth-rounder, but he's a name to monitor considering the state of the Washington backfield (Rachaad White, Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Jerome Ford). If Allen impresses during the offseason, he could sneak onto the fantasy radar.

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line fallout after starting LT Laremy Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps tear; Harris makes no automatic player-rank change.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps injury as a meaningful downgrade to Washington's offensive environment, though not one that can be precisely assigned to individual ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: He describes the line as thin without its starting left tackle and explicitly says losing good players hurts an offense.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris cannot draw a straight line from the injury to exactly how far Terry McLaurin or Jayden Daniels should fall, so he declines a mechanical rank adjustment.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Washington's pass-game options under review as replacement-line and protection information emerges instead of overreacting with a fixed downgrade.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: No back is top 30 for Harris; Richard prefers Rachaad White as a late PPR target if JCM fails to reclaim lead work.
profile_notes.summary: Harris wants camp to clarify whether Jacory Croskey-Merritt improved enough to lead Washington, while Richard expects White's passing-game role to make him the useful late option.
profile_notes.evidence: Croskey-Merritt was benched late the prior season as Chris Rodriguez emerged; Rodriguez is gone, but White and Katron Allen add competing paths. Richard says White was acquired for high-value touches.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris admits his instinct to fade rookies can create blinders and will listen if reports say JCM owns the job; White can also post very low weeks.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Wait for role clarity and select only at a discount, with White preferred for PPR floor if JCM evidence remains weak.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders running backs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid RB2 prices; a camp winner belongs nearer the RB20-28/fringe-RB2 range.
profile_notes.summary: Washington's White/Krosky-Merritt/Allen competition is camp-actionable, but no speaker wants to treat a named winner as a certain premium asset.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris lists Rachaad White, Jacory Krosky-Merritt, and rookie Katron Allen and says none appears great. Ciely says reports can change the hierarchy, but White's past inefficiency and Krosky-Merritt's limited recent résumé warn against overcommitment.
profile_notes.counterweight: A coordinator can choose a lead back and a good Commanders offense could create usable volume.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Watch for real separation, then prefer the cheaper other back if hype drives one player into Rounds 4-5.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Helm quietly caught 44 passes during his rookie season, which -- believe it or not -- ranks 11th among rookie tight ends over the past decade. Impressively, the 2025 fourth-round pick hit that mark despite playing second fiddle to starter Chig Okonkwo. Helm, who caught a healthy 79% of his 56 targets, wasn't much of a fantasy option as a rookie (5.7 PPG), but with Okonkwo out of the picture, he's positioned for a much larger role in his second season. Helm will need a leap from QB Cam Ward, but if that happens, a breakout season is possible. The 24-year-old is worth a late flier in deeper leagues.

profile_notes.subject: Tennessee Titans offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-draft Titans skill players gain volume appeal if the planned up-tempo system is confirmed.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker's key Tennessee nugget is a planned up-tempo attack, which could create more snaps for Cam Ward, Tony Pollard, Carnell Tate, and other Titans assets.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Brian Daboll brought Austin Schlottmann in at center because the coordinator trusts him to align the offense, make calls, and play fast. Tucker explicitly connects tempo and snap volume to fantasy value.
profile_notes.counterweight: Tucker says Schlottmann and right guard Volson are not considered average starters; Harris notes August tempo plans can vanish when a weak team is hit in the mouth.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the up-tempo possibility as a late-round upside input, but wait for preseason confirmation that the line can execute it.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

outlook.text: Okonkwo signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons in Tennessee. The 2022 fourth-round pick is one of only four tight ends who have appeared in all 68 games since he entered the league, and he's also one of only six tight ends who have registered 50-plus receptions each of the past three seasons. On the other hand, Okonkwo has yet to clear a 16% target share in a single season, and he has been a nonfactor near the goal line (eight TDs and 11 end zone targets in his career). As a result, he has finished exactly 21st in fantasy points each of the past three seasons. Perhaps he'll make a leap as one of Jayden Daniels' top targets, but the 27-year-old is no more than a back-end TE2 lottery ticket.

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Modest environmental upgrade following Diggs's signing; no Harris downgrade for Terry McLaurin.
profile_notes.summary: Harris believes Diggs gives Washington a needed credible receiver and can improve the environment for Jayden Daniels, McLaurin, and the offense without taking McLaurin out of his prime role.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris notes that all Commanders pass catchers other than McLaurin had unstable week-to-week roles, while Diggs has a distinctly stronger portfolio. More sustained offense would create additional yards, touchdowns, and possession time.
profile_notes.counterweight: Diggs's personal ceiling is tied to the offense returning to its better two-years-ago form; Washington was not good last year, and Harris says some of that may have been Marcus Mariota-related.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not downgrade McLaurin just for a normal complementary receiver addition; modestly improve the outlook for a functional Commanders passing ecosystem.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

outlook.text: Barner was a solid contributor for the Seattle offense last season. The 2024 fourth-round pick worked his way to the top of the depth chart, and although his overall volume was limited (20th among TEs in targets and yards), he found the end zone seven times and finished 14th in fantasy points (21st in PPG). The 24-year-old is a serviceable, short-range target for Sam Darnold, but even with some rushing worked in, his role in Seattle's low-volume passing offense won't allow much upside. In fact, it's possible he loses some targets to second-year TE Elijah Arroyo this season. Barner is a fringe TE2, at best.

Darnold's first season with the Super Bowl champion Seahawks couldn't have gone much better from a real-life standpoint, but it simply didn't translate to much fantasy success. Despite finishing fifth in the NFL in passing yards for the second season in a row, Darnold finished 27th in fantasy points per game. He was very boom or bust, delivering seven top-10 weeks but also nine finishes outside the top 20. Turnovers (15 INTs were second most in the NFL) and a lack of rushing were the culprits. The 29-year-old will have a new playcaller in Brian Fleury, but otherwise it's roughly the status quo offensively. Darnold is no more than a fringe QB2 with a limited ceiling.

Young has yet to find his way to any sort of fantasy relevance during his first three NFL seasons. The 2023 No. 1 draft pick has yet to finish a season better than 20th in passing yards, 10th in rushing yards or 24th in fantasy points per game. Efficiency has been a problem, as last season's career-high 6.3 yards per attempt was barely up from 2024 and still among the worst in the NFL. Young's 47.6 QBR last season ranked 22nd among 28 qualified quarterbacks. Perhaps the 25-year-old will make a leap in top target Tetairoa McMillan's second season and Brad Idzik's debut as the offensive playcaller, but it will be asking a lot to expect QB1 production. Young is best viewed as a fringe QB2 in 12-team leagues.

Mendoza was selected by the Raiders with the No. 1 overall pick in April's draft. The reigning Heisman Trophy winner and national champion, Mendoza is a big, pocket quarterback with elite accuracy (his career 7.1% off-target rate is easily the best in this rookie class) and a solid arm. Mendoza's 2025 campaign at Indiana included class-best marks in passing TDs (41) and QBR (90.3). He posted a 65-440-7 rushing line in 16 games last season and figures to add some value with his legs in the pros. Mendoza will get some run as a rookie, but his supporting cast isn't overly impressive and he may not start in Week 1 (Kirk Cousins is in the mix), so there's not much sense in drafting him in most formats. He'll be worth a speculative add only when he's named Las Vegas' starter.

profile_notes.subject: Las Vegas Raiders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round receiver watch only if a receiver hierarchy emerges and Fernando Mendoza threatens Kirk Cousins for the starting job.
profile_notes.summary: Both see Las Vegas as a useful camp watch because an inexpensive receiver could become relevant if the passing game is better than assumed and a quarterback competition changes the outlook.
profile_notes.evidence: The Raiders publicly prefer Cousins to start the season, but a strong camp/preseason from first-overall-pick Mendoza could force a conversation. Harris says nobody is entitled to a role and wants to identify a clear winner such as Trey Tucker or Jalen Naylor.
profile_notes.counterweight: Brock Bowers is the primary target, the offense is widely expected to be poor, and Harris doubts Naylor's speed/film despite repeated organizational praise.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Follow the receiver and QB hierarchy for a cheap final-round target, but do not rely on a Raiders passer in standard one-QB leagues.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Singleton was selected by the Titans in the fifth round of April's draft. He is a big, versatile back with terrific speed who can contribute as a rusher, receiver, blocker and returner. While working in a committee with fellow rookie Kaytron Allen at Penn State the past four years, Singleton was effective after contact (3.46 YAC is sixth best in this RB rookie class) but struggled with elusiveness (8.0 forced missed tackle rate is worst). He was solid as receiver (102-987-9) and returner (class-high 1,138 kick return yards) during his 53-game tenure. Singleton will open his career behind Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears, but would make for an interesting waiver add in the event of a Pollard injury.

profile_notes.subject: Nick Singleton
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Dynasty hold or in-season injury-related waiver dart.
profile_notes.summary: Waldman believes Singleton is better than his public portrayal, but not likely to receive much first-year work.
profile_notes.evidence: He attributes some Penn State limitations to static roles, coaching execution, and quarterback play rather than solely to Singleton.
profile_notes.counterweight: Waldman explicitly expects limited immediate playing time.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep or acquire Singleton patiently in dynasty and avoid forcing him into ordinary redraft lineups.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Nick Singleton
profile_notes.action_qualifier: If healthy and heavily involved from the start of camp, lower both Pollard and Spears; if he misses camp, do not factor him into redraft roles.
profile_notes.summary: Kluge calls Singleton's broken-foot recovery the key Titans backfield variable because a healthy rookie creates a difficult three-way committee.
profile_notes.evidence: He says rookies who miss camp struggle to join a moving regular-season offense; he also cites Singleton's five-star athletic ceiling and the new staff's ability to assess him with Pollard/Spears on expiring deals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Kluge preferred Kaytron Allen at Penn State and says Singleton's fall reflected concerns that he checked out after quarterback injury; Harris does not assume an immediate takeover.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid projecting Singleton if unavailable, but treat healthy, repeated first-team involvement as a reason to lower the whole Titans RB group.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing AFC South & Almanac Stuff

outlook.text: Claiborne was selected by the Vikings in the sixth round of April's draft. Claiborne is an undersized back who struggled badly with efficiency during his four seasons at Wake Forest. On 558 career carries, Claiborne averaged 4.66 yards per attempt (second worst in this RB rookie class), 2.68 yards after contact and produced 5-plus yards on a class-low 32% of his carries. Also not much of a factor in the passing game, Claiborne may be limited to change-of-pace/return work in the pros. He'll open his career as a depth player behind Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason.

profile_notes.subject: Demond Claiborne
profile_notes.action_qualifier: 20-round dart throw and dynasty target; expect a possible wait until next year.
profile_notes.summary: Waldman calls Claiborne the class's most exciting pound-for-pound back and endorses deep/dynasty exposure.
profile_notes.evidence: He compares the rookie's size profile to rookie James Cook and Aaron Jones and sees occasional promising work behind Minnesota's lead back.
profile_notes.counterweight: His size and uncertain offensive environment make him unlikely to be an immediate dependable fantasy starter.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Claiborne as cheap upside, not as a planned weekly contributor.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Damond Claiborne
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not chase an August riser; Harris ranks him RB75.
profile_notes.summary: Harris rejects Claiborne as the fashionable small receiving back who will supposedly replace Jones or Mason.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Claiborne is tiny, compares him to Brashard Smith and a list of hyped undersized players, and argues Achane succeeded only because Miami made him a feature back rather than a gadget receiver. Erickson does not believe Claiborne can handle 15 carries.
profile_notes.counterweight: Claiborne could flash with a five-catch game and camp pass-pro reports can create hype, but neither speaker sees that as proof of a stable role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid Claiborne at a meaningful pick; do not turn one splashy camp or receiving outing into a feature-back projection.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings running backs
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Harris ranks Aaron Jones RB38 and Jordan Mason RB41; Mason is the preferred late side bet if the offense rebounds.
profile_notes.summary: Jones still looks good but is not health-trustworthy, while Mason is the more plausible early-down/goal-line beneficiary if Minnesota's environment improves.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Jones took a substantial pay cut to remain and has recurring health risk. Mason stayed more efficient than Jones in the broken offense but does not catch passes, protect on third downs, or play that role; Harris calls him the goal-line, workload, and late-game grinder.
profile_notes.counterweight: Mason is slow, needs a good environment, and PPR scoring hurts him; Jones remains the nominal leader. Neither expects ordinary August news to alter their baseline.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid assuming either is a weekly starter, but select Mason over cheap alternatives when betting on a Minnesota turnaround and a Jones absence.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Returning for his third year with the Chargers, Vidal is set to compete with newcomer Keaton Mitchell for change-of-pace touches behind Omarion Hampton. Vidal had some big moments in 2025, clearing 17 fantasy points in four games, but the notable disclaimer here is that Hampton was sidelined for all of those outings. In fact, Vidal scored only 4.1 fantasy PPG in his other nine games. The 2024 sixth-round pick is a fine depth player who showed he can handle big workloads when needed, but he'll be worth rostering only should Hampton miss time and, even then, Mitchell figures to play a role.

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not assume a healthy or cohesive unit until tackle and interior questions are answered.
profile_notes.summary: The Chargers could benefit from an offensive-line-friendly McDaniel system, but Tucker sees legitimate uncertainty at every starting position.
profile_notes.evidence: Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt are returning from major injuries; Tucker questions center Tyler Biadasz's recovery, Jake Slaughter's shift from Florida center to left guard, and Cole Strange's fit after New England. Harris notes Alt was not fully participating when camp opened.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Shanahan-McVay tree can aid blockers, and all questions can resolve favorably.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor training-camp participation and interior cohesion before assigning a strong line-driven boost to Chargers skill players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target discounted Chargers pieces only on the conditional thesis of healthy line, protected Herbert, and a real offensive jump.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers can imagine a Chargers offense becoming a fantasy answer if health and protection finally cooperate, but view it as a conditional upside case rather than baseline.
profile_notes.evidence: Behrens says a healthy line and protected Justin Herbert could unlock a 28-30-point offense; Harris gives Herbert a mulligan and ties McConkey's rebound to the same factors.
profile_notes.counterweight: It requires unusually good Chargers injury luck, and the team has frequently failed to meet that sort of optimistic offensive projection.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the upside scenario as a tiebreaker for discounted Chargers, not as permission to erase downside.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Washington was a sixth-round flier back in 2024, but that didn't stop him from working his way into a substantial offensive role last season. Washington finished third on the Dolphins in targets, trailing only Jaylen Waddle and De'Von Achane. Of course, Miami's shaky group of offensive personnel was an obvious factor and Washington's efficiency wasn't very good (5.0 yards per target, 7.0 yards per reception, 0.9 yards per route run). The 25-year-old is fine as a short-range target and occasional rusher, but that's likely his ceiling with newcomers Jalen Tolbert, Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman Jr. expected to factor in at wide receiver.

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade associated players only if the offense proves at least competent.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers identify the possibility that Miami is merely mediocre rather than historically bad as a major assumption that could overturn rankings.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon points to under-the-radar line additions, Malik Willis's small-sample improvement, and the fact that Achane could lose roughly four points per game and still approach the cited price.
profile_notes.counterweight: Practice performance remains poor and neither speaker declares the offense fixed.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor quarterback and line competence; buy individual Dolphins only when their price assumes an unrealistically disastrous offense.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line and overall-environment reports before making broad Dolphins downgrades.
profile_notes.summary: Harris treats Washington's dominant joint-practice performance against Miami as a meaningful warning about the Dolphins' environment, but not a final verdict.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Washington reporters described Miami's offensive line as overrun throughout the drills and its defense as repeatedly beaten by Jayden Daniels.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris explicitly wants to see the issue again and look for improvement through the month; De'Von Achane also reportedly broke a third-down touchdown play.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the offensive-line concern in Dolphins player evaluations and seek confirming reports rather than automatically abandoning every Miami asset.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins receiver room
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Grind camp rotations for a free late receiver, especially Malik Washington; do not assume any player has guaranteed targets.
profile_notes.summary: Both say Miami offers a rare chance to find late value because the market views the team as hopeless and no receiver is penciled into targets behind the headline names.
profile_notes.evidence: Daugherty will watch Malik Washington; Harris lists Kevin Coleman, Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas, Jalen Tolbert, Tutu Atwell, and Terrace Marshall and says reporters should expose two- and three-WR rotations.
profile_notes.counterweight: Miami may struggle to push the ball, Bell's knee clouds availability, and open competition can yield no dependable player rather than a hidden breakout.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track repeated first-team usage and stash only the receiver who earns a real role; be willing to churn quickly.
profile_notes.episode_title: Drake Maye & Josh Allen & Previewing AFC East

outlook.text: Wright will once again compete with second-year Ollie Gordon II for backup reps behind feature back De'Von Achane. Wright has barely cleared 70 touches during each of his first two NFL seasons, but he has shined at times, including a 24-107-1 rushing line in Week 14 last season. The 2024 fourth-round pick has been effective as a rusher, but hasn't been involved in the passing game (15 targets in 25 games). The 23-year-old would be worth adding only in the event of an Achane injury and even then, it's possible he would split (or be on the short end of a committee) with Gordon in a rebuilding offense that may not score very often.

Gordon is still very young (22 years old), and his size (6-foot-1, 226 pounds) adds to his long-term intrigue. He'll have some insurance appeal if he beats out Wright for primary backup duties.

outlook.text: Tolbert signed with Miami after spending his first four NFL seasons in Dallas. The 2022 third-round pick has a path to a substantial offensive role, with Malik Washington, Tutu Atwell and rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas as his top competition for snaps and targets. We have seen Tolbert as a near-full-time player in a much better offense and he wasn't much of a fantasy option. That came in 2024 when he played 76% of the Cowboys' offensive snaps. He found the end zone seven times, but was held to 610 yards and finished 54th among receivers in fantasy PPG. Tolbert played a reduced role last season and his 203 yards were the fewest since his rookie season. The 27-year-old has very limited upside and isn't worth much late-round consideration.

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade associated players only if the offense proves at least competent.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers identify the possibility that Miami is merely mediocre rather than historically bad as a major assumption that could overturn rankings.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon points to under-the-radar line additions, Malik Willis's small-sample improvement, and the fact that Achane could lose roughly four points per game and still approach the cited price.
profile_notes.counterweight: Practice performance remains poor and neither speaker declares the offense fixed.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor quarterback and line competence; buy individual Dolphins only when their price assumes an unrealistically disastrous offense.

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line and overall-environment reports before making broad Dolphins downgrades.
profile_notes.summary: Harris treats Washington's dominant joint-practice performance against Miami as a meaningful warning about the Dolphins' environment, but not a final verdict.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Washington reporters described Miami's offensive line as overrun throughout the drills and its defense as repeatedly beaten by Jayden Daniels.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris explicitly wants to see the issue again and look for improvement through the month; De'Von Achane also reportedly broke a third-down touchdown play.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the offensive-line concern in Dolphins player evaluations and seek confirming reports rather than automatically abandoning every Miami asset.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins receiver room
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Grind camp rotations for a free late receiver, especially Malik Washington; do not assume any player has guaranteed targets.
profile_notes.summary: Both say Miami offers a rare chance to find late value because the market views the team as hopeless and no receiver is penciled into targets behind the headline names.
profile_notes.evidence: Daugherty will watch Malik Washington; Harris lists Kevin Coleman, Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas, Jalen Tolbert, Tutu Atwell, and Terrace Marshall and says reporters should expose two- and three-WR rotations.
profile_notes.counterweight: Miami may struggle to push the ball, Bell's knee clouds availability, and open competition can yield no dependable player rather than a hidden breakout.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track repeated first-team usage and stash only the receiver who earns a real role; be willing to churn quickly.
profile_notes.episode_title: Drake Maye & Josh Allen & Previewing AFC East

outlook.text: Kupp heads into his age-33 season positioned for situational targets in Seattle's run-first offense. The longtime Rams slot man appeared in 16 games for Seattle in 2025 -- his first season with the team -- and was limited to a career-low 16% target share. Kupp was a nonfactor in fantasy, clearing 12.0 fantasy points only once (16.0 in Week 2). The veteran remains a reliable short-range target, but his ceiling is very low with Jaxon Smith-Njigba soaking up a huge share of the targets and the likes of Rashid Shaheed and Tory Horton also in the mix. Kupp is an unexciting late-round pick.

Douglas was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. Douglas is a tall, perimeter receiver with big hands and long arms who, after not seeing much work during two seasons at Florida, exploded for 60-877-6 and 54-846-7 receiving lines at Texas Tech over the last two seasons. His overall efficiency was underwhelming, including six drops and a shaky 1.81 YPRR in 2025. He impressed with a 4.39 40-yard dash at 206 pounds (111 speed score) at the combine. Douglas has a path to a large offensive role as a rookie (Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert and fellow rookie Chris Bell are his primary competition), but life may be tough in a rebuilding Miami offense led by unproven Malik Willis. He's only worth a late flier.

profile_notes.subject: Caleb Douglas
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late/deep-league churn candidate, not a standard-league priority.
profile_notes.summary: Douglas may start for Miami and is viable as a cheap momentum bet, but Waldman ties the role to a constrained offense and simplified usage.
profile_notes.evidence: Waldman saw preseason usage in soft zone windows and size-based routes rather than high-proficiency route work, and questions Malik Willis's ability to reach later reads.
profile_notes.counterweight: A shallow role can still produce if Douglas catches the ball and uses his speed.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Douglas as a late churn option only; do not elevate him because of camp-start reports.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Caleb Douglas
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Very-late redraft or deep-league receiver dart; keep monitoring the camp drumbeat.
profile_notes.summary: Harris elevates Douglas as Miami's currently most appealing late receiver after repeated positive camp and joint-practice reports.
profile_notes.evidence: Washington reporters reportedly singled out the 6-foot-4, fast Douglas; Harris says he has received Dolphins camp raves and moved him from WR91 into his top-80 receivers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris notes Douglas had mixed pre-draft reviews, including drops and questions about whether his speed translated, and calls the pick borderline in ordinary leagues.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Douglas as a late upside pick only if the positive role evidence continues; do not assume camp praise alone proves a fantasy starter.

outlook.text: Reportedly a cut/trade candidate throughout most of the 2025 offseason, Boutte went on to lead the AFC champion Patriots' wide receiver room in routes and touchdowns while playing 67% of the offensive snaps when active. Despite the generous usage in a good offense, Boutte wasn't a reliable fantasy option, averaging 8.9 fantasy PPG. After seeing a career-high nine targets in Week 1, Boutte didn't clear five in a game the rest of the regular season. The 2023 sixth-round pick has finished in the range of 500-600 yards each of the last two seasons and has yet to produce a top-50 fantasy campaign. His 2026 role figures to decrease, with Romeo Doubs and likely A.J. Brown taking over atop the depth chart, and second-year wideout Kyle Williams likely to get more run. Boutte, 24, will only be worth late-round consideration if he is traded.

Aiyuk is expected to be released or traded by San Francisco this offseason. The veteran receiver was out all of last season while recovering from a torn ACL and MCL suffered in October 2024. In his two full seasons prior to the injury, Aiyuk delivered back-to-back top-15 fantasy seasons, including a 2023 campaign in which he produced a career-high 1,342 yards (seventh among wide receivers) and ranked in the top five at the position in yards per reception, yards per target and yards per route run. Even prior to the 2024 injury, however, Aiyuk was underperforming, scoring zero TDs and reaching double-digit fantasy points only once in seven games. Aiyuk is still in his prime at 28 years old, but his role and effectiveness are currently unclear. He is barely worth late-round consideration in deep leagues.

Lane was selected by the Ravens in the third round of April's draft. Lane is a tall, perimeter receiver with the biggest hands in this rookie class. He produced solid 43-525-12 and 49-745-4 receiving lines during his final two seasons at USC. Lane was rarely used in the intermediate area and struggled to produce after the catch (career 3.7 RAC is second worst in this class), but he has the frame and skill set to allow him plenty of pro potential. He'll battle the likes of Devontez Walker and fellow rookie Elijah Surratt for work behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman in Baltimore's low-volume pass offense. Lane's primary value is as dynasty stash.

profile_notes.subject: Ja'Kobi Lane
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not chase camp buzz; wait one to two years.
profile_notes.summary: Waldman treats Lane as a talented acrobatic athlete rather than a ready route/coverage technician.
profile_notes.evidence: He praises one-handed catches and body control but flags zone-route breaks that can create interceptions or expose teammates.
profile_notes.counterweight: Lane is ahead of Elijah Surratt in camp and could eventually develop.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid paying for a preseason depth-chart story in redraft and use dynasty patience.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Jacoby Lane
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Deep-league or late-draft watchlist; reassess after Ravens intra-squad work over the next one to two weeks.
profile_notes.summary: Harris identifies Lane, rather than Elijah Sarratt, as Baltimore's less-heralded rookie receiver generating meaningful camp buzz.
profile_notes.evidence: Baltimore beat reporters have repeatedly praised Lane; one reportedly called it the best rookie-receiver training camp he has seen.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris has not moved Lane into draftable territory, and camp praise needs confirmation in the coming intra-squad scrimmages.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track Lane rather than drafting on the headline alone; add him to late-round or waiver radar if the role evidence persists.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Baltimore Ravens offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor the three new interior pieces and tackle performance before assuming a strong rushing environment.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker sees Baltimore's changed interior and new under-center offense as a significant continuity risk despite potential upside.
profile_notes.evidence: He names injured-center returnee Ethan Pocic, returning Simpson, and first-round Penn State guard Vega Ioane as a substantially remade interior, while noting the rookie may switch sides. He also says neither Ronnie Stanley nor Roger Rosengarten met expectations last year.
profile_notes.counterweight: If the interior questions resolve positively, Tucker says the line could be good; Derrick Henry remains a rare durability/production outlier.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the interior transition in the downside range for Ravens runners and passing-game projections rather than presuming past line quality.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Jacoby Lane
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Deep-league/dynasty role watch, not a current volume-receiver target.
profile_notes.summary: Harmon sees Lane as a possible role-playing sacrificial X receiver rather than a likely high-volume fantasy option.
profile_notes.evidence: He praises Lane's spectacular contested catches and hands but says Lane does not separate; he imagines a Marquez Valdes-Scantling-like deployment with better hands.
profile_notes.counterweight: A Lane emergence could let Rashod Bateman move off ball, but Flowers would remain the clear top option and Lane's lack of separation caps volume.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor whether Lane earns an X role; do not draft him for a presumed target share.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Hurst was selected by the Buccaneers in the third round of April's draft. Granted he played at a small school, but Hurst ranked third in this rookie class target share (26%) and first in air yard share (45%) during his FBS career. A tall, vertical receiver, Hurst posted solid collegiate efficiency despite inconsistent QB play (only 68% of his 235 FBS targets were catchable, which is easily lowest among qualified WRs in this class). His 135-inch broad jump was best among wide receivers at the combine. Hurst will get some run at 'X' receiver as a rookie, but he's a longshot for consistent rookie-season fantasy production with Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan in the fold.

profile_notes.subject: Ted Hurst
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not project an immediate 800-900-yard season.
profile_notes.summary: Hurst has a chance at a limited Tampa Bay role, but Waldman does not see an advanced enough prospect for immediate volume.
profile_notes.evidence: Waldman calls him a go-up-and-win-it receiver and outlines a very high development ceiling, but says he is unlikely to become a timing-route technician.
profile_notes.counterweight: Jalen McMillan's knee issue could create some near-term opportunity.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Hurst as a developmental/deep-league watch, not a standard redraft target.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Tampa Bay Buccaneers receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Prefer Egbuka at a reasonable price, but avoid letting camp helium force a WR13 price; Godwin/McMillan remain health and role-dependent.
profile_notes.summary: Harris expects Egbuka to earn the strongest camp drumbeat but warns that any receiver price can become untenable; Tampa's frequent three-WR usage limits the value of two-WR-set chatter.
profile_notes.evidence: Egbuka has helium and is Harris's preferred player; Godwin is a good player recovering from serious injury, while McMillan returned late after a frightening broken-neck injury.
profile_notes.counterweight: Egbuka had hands issues in the prior season, Godwin has burned managers through injury, and camp cannot definitively establish the target order among three regular receivers.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft upside at a rational price and ignore shallow formation/depth-chart claims in a three-WR offense.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: So far, so bust for Coleman, who has struggled to make an impact after being selected 33rd overall in the 2024 draft. After flashing in a situational deep-threat role as a rookie (15.0 aDOT), Coleman saw more high percentage looks in 2025 (11.2 aDOT). That led to a much better catch rate (from 51% to 66%), but a big dip in yardage (19.2 YPR to 10.9). Coleman has yet to emerge as a reliable, full-time starter and was even a healthy scratch at times last season. Perhaps the 23-year-old will make a Year 3 leap with Joe Brady now running the show, but he'll have his hands full overtaking DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir atop the depth chart. Coleman is only worth a late flier in deeper leagues.

Randall was selected by the Ravens in the fifth round of April's draft. More specifically, he was handpicked by owner Steve Bisciotti. Randall is the biggest back in this rookie class and he possesses terrific speed (4.50 40-yard dash, 113 speed score), a combination that makes him an interesting developmental flier. A converted wide receiver, Randall had a grand total of four carries during his first three seasons at Clemson prior to posting a 168-814-10 rushing line in 2025. His experience as a receiver suggests he has big upside in that area, as well (he totaled an 84-787-5 receiving line with the Tigers). He has some 2026 insurance appeal, but he'll primarily learn the ropes behind Derrick Henry and Justice Hill in 2026, with eyes on lead-back duties upon Henry's departure.
