profile_notes.subject: Adam Randall
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Waiver-wire speed-dial option if camp reports are surprisingly strong or Derrick Henry misses time.
profile_notes.summary: Neither speaker has a strong current fantasy take on Randall, but both identify him as the relevant Ravens contingency back to track.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris notes the thin depth behind 32-year-old Derrick Henry and passing-down specialist Justice Hill; Harmon says Randall could matter if Henry slows or misses time.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris is skeptical of the owner-pick narrative, while Harmon says Hill would not simply become the starter and that Randall still needs encouraging practice evidence.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track Randall for role confirmation and be ready to add after an actual Henry-related opening.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Perine is expected to resume his role as Chase Brown's primary backup in Cincinnati. The veteran back played 31% of the Bengals' snaps last season, totaling 84 carries and 21 targets. He cleared 400 total yards for the fifth consecutive season, though he has yet to reach 200 touches in a single season in his career, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. The 30-year-old has reached double-digit fantasy points three times over the last two seasons and would require a Brown injury in order to flirt with flex appeal. He can be left on waivers.

profile_notes.subject: Cincinnati Bengals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not change elite-player ranks on camp drills; monitor credible evidence of more under-center and modern-concept usage.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers regard Cincinnati's core as settled and already elite, with offensive evolution as a possible path from top-five to No. 1 production.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon wants to see Joe Burrow under center more and the offense move beyond an almost exclusively shotgun approach; he notes incremental increases in Chase motion and varied alignment.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harmon repeatedly says camp talk will not force rank changes for Burrow, Chase, Higgins, or Brown, and the preference may remain Burrow's existing style.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat schematic reports as upside context, not a reason to chase already-expensive Bengals players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: A 2025 seventh-round pick, Allen is set to compete with fellow second-year back Bhayshul Tuten and newcomer Chris Rodriguez Jr. for work in the Jacksonville backfield. As a rookie, Allen played 22% of the Jaguars' offensive snaps (82% of which were pass plays), but was limited to just 33 touches and failed to find the end zone or reach 4.0 fantasy points in a single game. It's likely that Tuten will operate as the Jaguars' primary back, with Rodriguez busy on early downs and short-yardage situations, and Allen used as a passing-down specialist, same as in 2025. That said, none of the three are established as lead backs, so there's an opportunity for Allen to force his way into a larger role. The 22-year-old is worth no more than a late-round flier.

profile_notes.subject: MarShawn Lloyd
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target in Rounds 10-12; increase priority only if Josh Jacobs suspension news becomes concrete.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see Lloyd as a late upside back whose opportunity could grow through Jacobs's health, workload management, or unresolved legal situation.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says camp reporters have liked Lloyd and notes Jacobs's groin issue and potential discipline; Eisenberg notes the Packers used Emmanuel Wilson meaningfully as a No. 2 last year and believes Lloyd is more talented.
profile_notes.counterweight: Lloyd's repeated injuries leave his ability unproven, and neither speaker treats a suspension as confirmed; Jacobs could still keep the lead role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Lloyd as a contingent bench bet and do not draft as if Jacobs is definitely unavailable.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: MarShawn Lloyd
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late contingent option only; do not treat rehab optimism as established professional production.
profile_notes.summary: Lloyd is worth watching because Jacobs uncertainty could open opportunity, but both speakers see a player valued more for an idea than an NFL résumé.
profile_notes.evidence: Erickson mentions work at a hamstring institute and compares the hope to Jonathan Brooks; Harris says there are several alternative backs, including Pierre Strong and Chris Brooks, and seeks genuine separation day by day.
profile_notes.counterweight: Lloyd has not stayed healthy or shown enough professionally, and Brooks—not Lloyd—is presently on the non-football injury list.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Lloyd only as discounted insurance while awaiting actual depth-chart separation or Jacobs news.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

profile_notes.subject: Dallas Cowboys skill players
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ignore Cowboys camp hype absent injury or a genuine George Pickens hold-in.
profile_notes.summary: Dallas offers little camp information likely to change established fantasy evaluations.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris describes annual hype around Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, while Ciely says the relevant fantasy roles have little genuine competition. Pickens signed his tag and attended work despite a possible future contract dispute.
profile_notes.counterweight: A Pickens hold-in could hurt early games, and injuries or unavoidably negative reports would be meaningful.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Filter positive Cowboys clips out of draft decisions; only move players for material availability news.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Holani is on the 2026 fantasy radar with Kenneth Walker III no longer on the Seattle roster and Zach Charbonnet (ACL) in doubt for the early portion of the season. Holani will compete with rookie Jadrian Price, Emanuel Wilson and Kenny McIntosh for touches while Charbonnet is sidelined. The 2024 UDFA has 25 carries and three targets to his name through two NFL seasons. Price figures to get the first shot at lead back duties and, even if forced into a few starts in Seattle's run-friendly offense, Holani would be working in a committee and no more than a deep league flex.

profile_notes.subject: George Holani
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Deep roster/waiver speed-dial only; use his disappearance from reports as indirect evidence favoring Price, not as a draft trigger.
profile_notes.summary: Gretch finds Holani's offseason positive buzz worth tracking but not enough to make him a current selection.
profile_notes.evidence: Holani has been mentioned positively despite limited offensive NFL work and a special-teams/depth history; Gretch says a drop in that chatter while Price dominates the news could matter more than generic Price praise.
profile_notes.counterweight: The buzz may be offseason fluff, and Harris does not expect Holani to be drafted in most leagues.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not chase the praise; watch whether he actually earns a persistent offensive role.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Johnson has settled in as a productive change-of-pace and receiving option in the Buffalo backfield behind James Cook. Johnson enters his eighth NFL season having yet to clear 63 carries or 34 catches in a season, but his role allows for him to hit for the occasional big game (15-plus fantasy points four times over the last two seasons). Of course, those games have come at random, making Johnson an unusable fantasy commodity. Even if Cook misses time this season, it's likely that Johnson would remain in his role, with Ray Davis instead stepping into lead back duties. Johnson plays a valuable role for Buffalo, but he's not a fantasy option.

Johnson was selected by the Chiefs in the fifth round of April's draft. His career 3.4 forced missed tackle rate is fourth best in this RB rookie class and his elusiveness helped him to 1,451 rushing yards (fourth in the nation and first in this class) last season. His lack of speed -- last among 10 RBs who ran the 40-yard dash (4.56) and speed score (93) at the combine -- and size limits him after initial contact (career 2.86 YAC), but he can help out in the passing game (92 collegiate receptions). Johnson will battle in what should be a wide-open competition for No. 2 duties behind Kenneth Walker III. He'll be worth rostering only if Walker misses action.

profile_notes.subject: Emmett Johnson
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Draft/hold as a Chiefs contingency back, especially in dynasty or deep leagues.
profile_notes.summary: Waldman sees Johnson as a quick-learning, creative back with the ability to materially change the Chiefs' fortunes if injuries create a real opening.
profile_notes.evidence: He praises Johnson's footwork, quickness, contact balance, intelligence, creativity, and Nebraska tape, while Harris notes Kenneth Walker's durability risk.
profile_notes.counterweight: Johnson is behind established options and needs injuries that are substantial rather than brief.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Johnson as a bench/dynasty stash rather than projecting starter volume now.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

outlook.text: Wicks was traded to the Eagles after spending his first three NFL seasons in Green Bay. The 2023 fifth-round pick was limited to situational work during his Packers tenure, never finishing a season among the top 50 receivers in snaps, routes, targets, catches or yards. Wicks flashed at times (exactly one game of 24-plus points in each season), but otherwise scored 5.3 PPG. Even after the Eagles traded A.J. Brown, Wicks' path to targets may not be any easier in Philly. DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and Saquon Barkley are all assured substantial roles, with first-round rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown also very much in the mix. Wicks, 25, will need to win the team's No. 2 receiver gig in order to have any shot at weekly flex consideration. He's barely worth late-round consideration in deep leagues.

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade offense and Saquon Barkley context if interior health holds in the new scheme.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker believes Philadelphia has a high ceiling and high floor because last year's underperformance was substantially injury-driven and the new system should help blockers.
profile_notes.evidence: Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson fought through multiple injuries, surgeries, and rehabilitation; Lane Johnson missed the second half with plantar fasciitis. Tucker says the new coordinator's increased play action avoids isolating tackles in straight dropbacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: The line did not play as a top-five unit last year, and the recovery of injured interior starters must persist.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat a healthy Eagles line as a positive contextual upgrade for Barkley and the offense rather than anchoring on last year's unit ranking.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Keep outside the small trusted-offense tier until the new Mannion system succeeds in games.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers refuse to restore Philadelphia to an automatic top-offense projection after last year's collapse and coordinator replacement.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites A.J. Brown's trade, questions around the line, and the team's decision to replace the coordinator despite prior Super Bowl success. Ciely believes Mannion's changes can help but says practice and preseason cannot prove a top-five result.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense has Jalen Hurts, a strong history, and a scheme that could improve play action/middle-field work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid building draft projections on an assumed Eagles bounce-back; wait for regular-season evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Williams is primed for a larger role in his second NFL season. The 2025 third-round pick had a unique rookie campaign, handling more carries (11) than he did targets (10). Williams' gadget role allowed him only 90 snaps (12%) and he was utilized only near the line of scrimmage (1.4 aDOT). The Green Bay WR rotation no longer includes Romeo Doubs or Dontayvion Wicks, but Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and fellow second-year wideout Matthew Golden remain in the mix. Williams will need to beat out one (or perhaps two) of them and start to see more downfield targets in order to land on the fantasy radar. The 24-year-old is only worth late-round consideration in deeper formats.

Gadsden's rookie season was quite the roller coaster. The 2025 fifth-round pick didn't get much early run prior to exploding for 29.4 fantasy points in Week 7 and 18.7 points in Week 8. He went on to score one touchdown and average 6.2 fantasy PPG the rest of the season, never clearing 12.2 points in a single outing. Gadsden finished the season eighth or better at the position in end zone targets, aDOT, YPR, YPT and YPRR. The 23-year-old's second-half fall is concerning, and he now enters Year 2 set to compete for work with newcomer David Njoku. It's still possible Gadsden emerges as a featured target in new playcaller Mike McDaniel's offense, but consistent fantasy output may be tough in an offense that figures to spread the ball around. Gadsden is only worth a late pick in deeper leagues.

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not assume a healthy or cohesive unit until tackle and interior questions are answered.
profile_notes.summary: The Chargers could benefit from an offensive-line-friendly McDaniel system, but Tucker sees legitimate uncertainty at every starting position.
profile_notes.evidence: Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt are returning from major injuries; Tucker questions center Tyler Biadasz's recovery, Jake Slaughter's shift from Florida center to left guard, and Cole Strange's fit after New England. Harris notes Alt was not fully participating when camp opened.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Shanahan-McVay tree can aid blockers, and all questions can resolve favorably.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor training-camp participation and interior cohesion before assigning a strong line-driven boost to Chargers skill players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Rondale Gadsden
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late TE2/streaming consideration at Harris TE13; David Njoku remains a role-risk, not a draft priority.
profile_notes.summary: Harris retains moderate upside interest in Gadsden but says generic Herbert-Gadsden camp chemistry is likely fluff and Njoku can still interfere with the target path.
profile_notes.evidence: Gadsden is Harris's TE13, whereas Njoku is TE31; both agree Njoku is unlikely to become a top-eight or top-10 fantasy option but can still muck up another player's result.
profile_notes.counterweight: A steady, credible connection report would be mildly reassuring, but it does not prove a usable regular-season role; Njoku's presence is the direct countercase.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Gadsden in late-TE range and monitor deployment rather than reacting to standard camp praise.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target discounted Chargers pieces only on the conditional thesis of healthy line, protected Herbert, and a real offensive jump.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers can imagine a Chargers offense becoming a fantasy answer if health and protection finally cooperate, but view it as a conditional upside case rather than baseline.
profile_notes.evidence: Behrens says a healthy line and protected Justin Herbert could unlock a 28-30-point offense; Harris gives Herbert a mulligan and ties McConkey's rebound to the same factors.
profile_notes.counterweight: It requires unusually good Chargers injury luck, and the team has frequently failed to meet that sort of optimistic offensive projection.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the upside scenario as a tiebreaker for discounted Chargers, not as permission to erase downside.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Dulcich is back on the fantasy radar as the top tight end on the Miami depth chart. The 2022 third-round pick for the Denver Broncos made some noise as a rookie with a 33-411-2 receiving line in 10 games, but he went on to total 16 targets during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before landing in Miami last season. Dulcich didn't see his first target until Week 9 but went on to post a 26-335-1 receiving line the rest of the way. He wasn't a regular fantasy option (one top-15 week among TEs), but he certainly has a path to a substantial target share in 2026 with minimal competition at tight end and with Miami so short-handed at wide receiver. The 26-year-old is a long shot for consistent fantasy value in an offense expected to struggle, but there's some deep-league sleeper appeal.

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade associated players only if the offense proves at least competent.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers identify the possibility that Miami is merely mediocre rather than historically bad as a major assumption that could overturn rankings.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon points to under-the-radar line additions, Malik Willis's small-sample improvement, and the fact that Achane could lose roughly four points per game and still approach the cited price.
profile_notes.counterweight: Practice performance remains poor and neither speaker declares the offense fixed.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor quarterback and line competence; buy individual Dolphins only when their price assumes an unrealistically disastrous offense.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line and overall-environment reports before making broad Dolphins downgrades.
profile_notes.summary: Harris treats Washington's dominant joint-practice performance against Miami as a meaningful warning about the Dolphins' environment, but not a final verdict.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Washington reporters described Miami's offensive line as overrun throughout the drills and its defense as repeatedly beaten by Jayden Daniels.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris explicitly wants to see the issue again and look for improvement through the month; De'Von Achane also reportedly broke a third-down touchdown play.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the offensive-line concern in Dolphins player evaluations and seek confirming reports rather than automatically abandoning every Miami asset.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

outlook.text: Otton re-signed with Tampa Bay after spending his first four NFL seasons with the team. Since entering the league in 2022, Otton ranks first among all tight ends in snaps (3,530) and second in routes (1,838). That simply hasn't translated to much target volume (he is yet to clear 86 in a season) or goal-line work (11 TDs and 19 end zone targets in 63 games). In fact, Otton was the only player with 75-plus targets who didn't score multiple touchdowns last season. The 27-year-old has finished 25th or lower in fantasy PPG in three of four seasons and is a poor bet for his first top-10 finish in 2026. He's well off the fantasy radar.

A 2025 third-round pick, Bryant played a situational role throughout his rookie season and is likely to do the same in 2026 after Denver added Jaylen Waddle as a running mate for Courtland Sutton. Bryant will battle the likes of Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims Jr. and Lil'Jordan Humphrey for No. 3 duties. During his rookie campaign, Bryant barely saw the field early on, but eventually passed Franklin on the depth chart and earned more work down the stretch. That led to more snaps but not much fantasy production, as he failed to clear 13.2 fantasy points in a single game and found the end zone once. The 23-year-old isn't on the fantasy radar right now, but he makes for a fine dynasty stash.

profile_notes.subject: Pat Bryant
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Tentative camp-based lean over Troy Franklin; confirm through the rest of August.
profile_notes.summary: Harris is leaning toward raising Bryant above Troy Franklin in Denver's receiver competition.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Bryant had drawn more positive camp reports by August 7 and may need an Almanac profile and rank swap.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris explicitly has not changed the ranks yet, so the signal is preliminary camp reporting rather than an established role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track the Denver competition and give Bryant a small edge only after the positive practice pattern persists.
profile_notes.episode_title: Acid-Reflux All-Stars & Cousin Josh Returns

profile_notes.subject: Denver Broncos wide receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not elevate Troy Franklin or Pat Bryant on four-wide camp headlines without actual sustainable usage.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers reject a reported Broncos move toward more four-wide formations as a reason to project multiple new fantasy receivers.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Denver threw from four-wide only 15 times last year, while Behrens categorizes the report with familiar but unfulfilled preseason role claims.
profile_notes.counterweight: An injury could alter the depth chart, and Courtland Sutton/Waddle opinions differ, but they do not believe the offense and quarterback can support three or four viable fantasy receivers.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Franklin and Bryant off priority lists unless game-relevant volume emerges.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Horton had the look of a Day 3 find by Seattle early on in 2025 prior to a season-ending shin injury suffered in Week 9. The 2025 fifth-round pick opened his career buried on the depth chart behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp, but still found a way to make an impact while being limited to 46% of the offensive snaps. Though his production was volatile and he never cleared five targets in a game, he found the end zone five times on 23 targets. Despite the impressive showing, Horton's short-term outlook is dicey with JSN, Kupp and Rashid Shaheed presumably ahead of him on the depth chart. The 23-year-old's primary value is as a dynasty stash.

profile_notes.subject: Tory Horton
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late receiver target if health reports stay positive and he earns a role behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
profile_notes.summary: Harris likes Horton enough to rank him ahead of Rashid Shaheed, and Gretch is open to positive camp news after Horton's promising but injury-shortened rookie season.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites a standout route/touchdown before Horton was hurt; Gretch notes five touchdowns on 13 catches and says his rookie role appeared to be growing.
profile_notes.counterweight: The tiny sample and health uncertainty make the efficiency unsustainable proof rather than a forecast, and the Seahawks' receiver hierarchy may remain unclear.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft Horton only as bench upside once camp confirms health and a usable role.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Sarratt was selected by the Ravens in the fourth round of April's draft. Surratt is a big, perimeter receiver who hauled in 31 touchdown receptions (most in this rookie WR class) in 40 collegiate games, which includes a FBS-high 15 in 2025. His efficiency was terrific across the board, including 10.7 yards per target, 2.69 YPRR and a 72% catch rate. Surratt is an intriguing prospect, but he may not see the field a ton as a rookie with Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and fellow rookie Ja'Kobi Lane also in the mix in Baltimore's low-volume pass attack. He's best as a dynasty stash.

profile_notes.subject: Baltimore Ravens offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor the three new interior pieces and tackle performance before assuming a strong rushing environment.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker sees Baltimore's changed interior and new under-center offense as a significant continuity risk despite potential upside.
profile_notes.evidence: He names injured-center returnee Ethan Pocic, returning Simpson, and first-round Penn State guard Vega Ioane as a substantially remade interior, while noting the rookie may switch sides. He also says neither Ronnie Stanley nor Roger Rosengarten met expectations last year.
profile_notes.counterweight: If the interior questions resolve positively, Tucker says the line could be good; Derrick Henry remains a rare durability/production outlier.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the interior transition in the downside range for Ravens runners and passing-game projections rather than presuming past line quality.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Elijah Surratt
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Dynasty/deep-roster developmental bet if camp shows a transition toward power-slot work.
profile_notes.summary: Harmon finds Surratt interesting as a potential power-slot conversion rather than a ready perimeter separator.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Surratt beat zone coverage in college but did not separate outside, and compares the possible slot profile to a less-developed Amon-Ra St. Brown archetype.
profile_notes.counterweight: Moving from outside contested-catch work to a power slot is a major positional transition, though Harmon says Surratt's high-character football makeup supports the attempt.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Stash only in formats that can wait for role development, then react if slot deployment becomes real.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line fallout after starting LT Laremy Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps tear; Harris makes no automatic player-rank change.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps injury as a meaningful downgrade to Washington's offensive environment, though not one that can be precisely assigned to individual ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: He describes the line as thin without its starting left tackle and explicitly says losing good players hurts an offense.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris cannot draw a straight line from the injury to exactly how far Terry McLaurin or Jayden Daniels should fall, so he declines a mechanical rank adjustment.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Washington's pass-game options under review as replacement-line and protection information emerges instead of overreacting with a fixed downgrade.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Modest environmental upgrade following Diggs's signing; no Harris downgrade for Terry McLaurin.
profile_notes.summary: Harris believes Diggs gives Washington a needed credible receiver and can improve the environment for Jayden Daniels, McLaurin, and the offense without taking McLaurin out of his prime role.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris notes that all Commanders pass catchers other than McLaurin had unstable week-to-week roles, while Diggs has a distinctly stronger portfolio. More sustained offense would create additional yards, touchdowns, and possession time.
profile_notes.counterweight: Diggs's personal ceiling is tied to the offense returning to its better two-years-ago form; Washington was not good last year, and Harris says some of that may have been Marcus Mariota-related.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not downgrade McLaurin just for a normal complementary receiver addition; modestly improve the outlook for a functional Commanders passing ecosystem.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

profile_notes.subject: Dallas Cowboys skill players
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ignore Cowboys camp hype absent injury or a genuine George Pickens hold-in.
profile_notes.summary: Dallas offers little camp information likely to change established fantasy evaluations.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris describes annual hype around Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, while Ciely says the relevant fantasy roles have little genuine competition. Pickens signed his tag and attended work despite a possible future contract dispute.
profile_notes.counterweight: A Pickens hold-in could hurt early games, and injuries or unavoidably negative reports would be meaningful.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Filter positive Cowboys clips out of draft decisions; only move players for material availability news.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Smith was traded to the Jets following an unsuccessful one-year stint in Las Vegas. Smith, who began his career as a second-round pick with the Jets in 2013, is in line to start, though he's a long shot for consistent fantasy production. Smith peaked with a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game with Seattle in 2022, but he has finished no better than 16th over the past three seasons. He paced the NFL in both interceptions and sacks in 2025 after finishing third in both categories in 2024 and is no longer much of a factor with his legs. The 35-year-old might bring some stability to the fantasy outlook of the team's pass catchers, but we shouldn't expect much more than that. Consider Smith only in superflex formats.

Rodgers re-signed with the Steelers and will return for his second season with the team. The 42-year-old is reuniting with his longtime head coach from Green Bay, Mike McCarthy. The duo will look to improve on a 2025 campaign in which Rodgers finished just outside the top 12 in passing yards and touchdowns while ranking 23rd among 28 qualified QBs in QBR. Even if Rodgers' efficiency improves, he remains a nonfactor as a rusher (he last cleared 107 yards in 2020) and hasn't been fantasy relevant since 2021 (25th, 18th and 25th in points per game in his past three full seasons). Even with a more pass-friendly playcaller and with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard added to the wide receiver room, Rodgers is no more than a low-ceiling QB2.

profile_notes.subject: Pittsburgh Steelers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a stable, projectable offense; do not manufacture large camp-based projections.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see a reasonably high/projectable Steelers floor if Aaron Rodgers remains healthy, without an exciting ceiling case.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Mike McCarthy's high-floor play calling, a settled enough offensive line, and known top receivers; Harris calls the roster full of good professionals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both retain concern that Rodgers may have declined further and will avoid contact, limiting offensive aggression.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep established Steelers values near their baseline projections instead of reacting sharply to routine camp headlines.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Brissett is back for his second season in Arizona and is currently positioned as the team's probable Week 1 starter. One of the biggest fantasy surprises of 2025, Brissett reeled off nine consecutive top-12 fantasy outings spanning Weeks 6 to 15. He averaged 18.9 fantasy points across 12 starts, which was a big surprise considering his prior career high was 12.9, and that was way back in 2017. Brissett played solid ball, but he's not a major contributor with his legs (260 yards is his career high for a season). He certainly benefited from the league's pass-heaviest offense, a luxury he's unlikely to have with Mike LaFleur now calling plays. Expect the 33-year-old to regress to fringe QB2 production, and keep in mind that it's possible Arizona will turn to rookie Carson Beck at some point this season.

profile_notes.subject: Cardinals quarterback situation
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Prefer Jacoby Brissett stability for Cardinals pass-catcher volume; lower expectations if Carson Beck earns substantial early work.
profile_notes.summary: Gretch treats the Brissett-versus-Beck outcome as central to Arizona receiver/tight-end volume, while Harris agrees the rookie quarterback would be less exciting.
profile_notes.evidence: Gretch says Brissett's quick release and willingness to throw generated huge target volume, including Wilson's 18-target game and two 15-target games, whereas young quarterbacks can hold the ball and take sacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: A new offense could change deployment regardless of starter, and the transcript does not declare either quarterback the confirmed season-long choice.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use camp/preseason quarterback evidence to refine Cardinals pass-catcher projections rather than treating last year's targets as automatic.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

profile_notes.subject: Arizona Cardinals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not write off the offense because of rebuilding expectations; balance possible skill-position value against the league's hardest projected schedule.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Arizona as a possible market-value offense because it is being declared hopeless, while Gretch sees meaningful skill talent but acknowledges a difficult environment.
profile_notes.evidence: They cite McBride, Love, Harrison, Wilson, and backfield depth; Gretch says the projected schedule is the NFL's hardest and the club is a large underdog early.
profile_notes.counterweight: The schedule and quarterback uncertainty can make running-back and passing-game efficiency difficult.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Consider discounted Cardinals talent individually, rather than treating the offense as automatically unproductive.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Watson is expected to return to the field this season after a disastrous four years in Cleveland. A top-six fantasy QB (points per game) during each of his first four NFL seasons, Watson has appeared in a total of 19 games since joining the Browns, averaging a poor 13.1 fantasy points during the span. A torn Achilles suffered in Week 7 of 2024 (followed by tearing it again less than three months later) cost Watson all of 2025, and he'll now compete with Shedeur Sanders for Cleveland's starting job. Now 30 years old, with a young, unproven supporting cast and having not been a factor since 2020, Watson is a long shot to return to fantasy relevance. He should be considered only in superflex formats.

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Conditionally upgrade pass catchers if quarterback play becomes merely passable.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers argue that Cleveland does not need excellent quarterback play for its pass catchers to beat depressed prices.
profile_notes.evidence: The derived analysis identifies KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, and Harold Fannin as players who could benefit if Shedeur Sanders or Dylan Gabriel is simply adequate.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither host expresses confidence that the quarterback outcome will actually be adequate.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Cleveland receivers and tight ends as conditional value rather than automatic targets, and update after credible quarterback evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat early-season cohesion as uncertain after a nearly complete starting-line overhaul.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker calls Cleveland's nearly wholesale replacement of the starting line an unprecedented continuity experiment with high early variance.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Teven Jenkins had been on the team but was not a starter, and cites Spencer Fano, Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins, and Titus Howard as new additions. Tucker grants that most have played meaningful NFL football.
profile_notes.counterweight: The individual additions have shown positive things and could gel by December; Harris also says he is not qualified to make every technique judgment and is not down on every member.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid assuming immediate line quality for Browns assets; prioritize early-season evidence of the new group functioning together.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Browns quarterback competition
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade Browns pass catchers modestly only if Shedeur Sanders wins; avoid treating Deshaun Watson as equivalent.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers believe the Browns quarterback outcome materially affects pass catchers and prefer Sanders over Watson.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Watson's poor form and back-to-back camp interceptions, while saying Sanders can be a flawed but functional NFL passer; Harris says his modest Browns ranks assume Sanders rather than Watson.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris says Sanders must release the ball faster and cannot recreate Colorado-style extended plays; neither calls him an exciting superflex starter.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Browns receiver projections modest, but treat a Sanders starting outcome as a meaningful improvement over Watson.

profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor Michael Penix recovery versus Tua Tagovailoa starting; it affects Drake London/Kyle Pitts predictability more than Bijan Robinson's elite draft status.
profile_notes.summary: The Falcons' actionable camp fork is whether Penix can take first-team work and be ready Week 1 or whether Tua begins the season, with the quarterback mostly changing receiver/tight-end certainty.

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade offense and Saquon Barkley context if interior health holds in the new scheme.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker believes Philadelphia has a high ceiling and high floor because last year's underperformance was substantially injury-driven and the new system should help blockers.
profile_notes.evidence: Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson fought through multiple injuries, surgeries, and rehabilitation; Lane Johnson missed the second half with plantar fasciitis. Tucker says the new coordinator's increased play action avoids isolating tackles in straight dropbacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: The line did not play as a top-five unit last year, and the recovery of injured interior starters must persist.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat a healthy Eagles line as a positive contextual upgrade for Barkley and the offense rather than anchoring on last year's unit ranking.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.action_qualifier: Keep outside the small trusted-offense tier until the new Mannion system succeeds in games.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers refuse to restore Philadelphia to an automatic top-offense projection after last year's collapse and coordinator replacement.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites A.J. Brown's trade, questions around the line, and the team's decision to replace the coordinator despite prior Super Bowl success. Ciely believes Mannion's changes can help but says practice and preseason cannot prove a top-five result.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense has Jalen Hurts, a strong history, and a scheme that could improve play action/middle-field work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid building draft projections on an assumed Eagles bounce-back; wait for regular-season evidence.

profile_notes.summary: Denver's backfield has a preferred healthy player in Dobbins but remains likely to use all three backs.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Dobbins's early-down role was more repeatable and valuable, while Harvey had red-zone receiving work; Denver also drafted Jonah Coleman and re-signed Dobbins.
profile_notes.counterweight: Dobbins cannot be assumed healthy, Harris says Harvey can improve as a second-year player, and he admits he has not evaluated Coleman yet.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft any Denver back as a no-competition bell cow; use incoming health and rotation reports to separate their values.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Denver Broncos backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ignore ambiguous camp usage between R.J. Harvey, J.K. Dobbins, and Jonah Coleman unless injury or a durable regular-season role change occurs.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers regard Broncos backfield camp stories as a Rorschach test: optimists and skeptics will interpret small drills to support their existing Harvey/Dobbins takes.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Dobbins was good last year and likely begins as primary runner; reports about Coleman goal-line drills or Harvey opportunities do not settle a role. Behrens notes Harvey is being drafted far earlier than Dobbins in best ball.
profile_notes.counterweight: Dobbins has injury history, Sean Payton could allocate red-zone work unusually, and a real injury would materially change the hierarchy.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not spend attention or draft capital on speculative camp usage; reassess only for meaningful health or deployment evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

profile_notes.subject: Taj Brooks
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Camp-only depth-chart watch; do not draft as Chase Brown's handcuff without compelling role evidence.
profile_notes.summary: Brooks is an unknown contingent-back possibility, not a present fantasy recommendation.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Brooks did not force anyone's hand last year but could become relevant if reports show he has displaced Samaje Perine as Cincinnati's second back; Harmon calls him worth monitoring.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both suspect Cincinnati may seek help outside the roster and say even positive reports would not automatically make Brooks the draftable Brown handcuff.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Leave Brooks undrafted in standard leagues and add him to a waiver speed dial only if his role becomes concrete.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: Cincinnati Bengals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not change elite-player ranks on camp drills; monitor credible evidence of more under-center and modern-concept usage.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers regard Cincinnati's core as settled and already elite, with offensive evolution as a possible path from top-five to No. 1 production.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon wants to see Joe Burrow under center more and the offense move beyond an almost exclusively shotgun approach; he notes incremental increases in Chase motion and varied alignment.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harmon repeatedly says camp talk will not force rank changes for Burrow, Chase, Higgins, or Brown, and the preference may remain Burrow's existing style.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat schematic reports as upside context, not a reason to chase already-expensive Bengals players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: Carolina Panthers offensive line and backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Be cautious with Chuba Hubbard and Jonathan Brooks while tackle availability and a multi-back split remain unresolved.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker expects Carolina's interior to be sound but sees tackle injuries and a protective run-first plan as constraints on a clean Hubbard/Brooks fantasy projection.
profile_notes.evidence: Taylor Moten's blood-clot timeline is unclear, Ikem Ekwonu is returning from a ruptured patellar tendon, Rashid Walker is new, and rookie Monroe Freeling may need to start. Tucker says the Panthers want to run to protect tackles and Bryce Young, while spreading touches among Hubbard, Brooks, and Etienne.
profile_notes.counterweight: Hubbard remains the apparent leader, and a good interior line can help the run game protect weaker tackles.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid aggressive volume projections for Carolina backs until tackles return and the touch distribution becomes clearer.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Carolina Panthers backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Chuba Hubbard is baseline lead back; raise Jonathan Brooks from RB54 only for credible knee-recovery and meaningful practice-integration evidence.
profile_notes.summary: Both regard Brooks's medical integration as the Panthers camp story most capable of altering Hubbard's workload and Brooks's very-low draft value.
profile_notes.evidence: Carolina let Rico Dowdle leave and added only A.J. Dillon/Trevor Etienne, which Harris reads as possible Brooks optimism. McCormick expects a methodical return after repeated major injuries.
profile_notes.counterweight: Brooks can remain merely a backup or re-injure the knee; Carolina paid Hubbard and routine split reps do not prove a meaningful regular-season role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track true practice participation and recovery language, not generic comeback praise; otherwise draft Hubbard as the more stable option.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: McGowan was selected by the Colts in the seventh round of April's draft. McGowan is an older prospect (25), having bounced around five schools due to an off-field issue in 2021 that led to jail time and a dismissal from Oklahoma. He slowly rebuilt his career and peaked with 1,100 yards and six TDs at New Mexico State in 2024 prior to delivering 851 yards and 12 TDs at Kentucky last season. His efficiency is hit or miss, as his career 2.65 YAC is very poor, but his 4.2 forced missed tackle rate is strong. He's been effective in the passing game, as well, so there's some hope for a pro level impact. McGowan impressed at the combine, posting the top vertical and broad jump in this RB rookie class and running a solid 4.49 40-yard dash at 223 pounds. McGowan will battle DJ Giddens for primary backup duties behind Jonathan Taylor, so it's possible he finds his way to some value as an insurance hold.

profile_notes.subject: Seth McGowan
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor as Jonathan Taylor's contingency; consider only if the opening is long term.
profile_notes.summary: Waldman thinks McGowan can overtake D.J. Giddens and would be the Colts' two-down component if Taylor suffered a lengthy injury.
profile_notes.evidence: He calls McGowan a hard, fast gap-scheme runner and says Giddens repeatedly leaves correctable flaws on tape.
profile_notes.counterweight: Waldman projects a McGowan/Ulysses Bentley split rather than a full every-down takeover.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not chase a preseason report in shallow leagues; add him promptly if depth-chart opportunity becomes durable.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: New Orleans Saints backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Etienne is RB16 pending Kamara's contract/roster outcome; no-Kamara clarity can accelerate his ADP toward RB11-12.
profile_notes.summary: Kamara's contractual status is the Saints' decisive backfield variable: Etienne has an RB16 baseline after a strong year, but Kamara's receiving trust can materially cap him.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says the Saints may not intend to pay Kamara's $11 million, while McCormick sees Etienne's payment as a path to a clean lead role. Harris names Kendre Miller and Devin Neal as less established alternatives.
profile_notes.counterweight: Kamara staying may be an institutional nuisance but gives a known role; he remains a capable receiver, and any no-Kamara outcome could be followed by another acquisition.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor actual contract/transaction news, not camp touches; draft Etienne more aggressively only once Kamara risk is truly resolved.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

profile_notes.subject: Houston Texans offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Downgrade Texans skill players only if repeated padded-practice and controlled-scrimmage failures show the line cannot gel.
profile_notes.summary: Richard calls persistent Houston line instability a medium red flag for the offense, while Harris asks what concrete camp evidence would justify changing player ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: Reports had Houston changing lineups daily and struggling to gel; Richard says his current skill-position ranks are optimistic relative to that risk.
profile_notes.counterweight: Preseason games are less useful than controlled scrimmages, and teams can solve line combinations as Chicago did the prior year.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track repeated protection failures in meaningful practice settings before discounting Houston's fantasy assets.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Denver Broncos wide receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not elevate Troy Franklin or Pat Bryant on four-wide camp headlines without actual sustainable usage.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers reject a reported Broncos move toward more four-wide formations as a reason to project multiple new fantasy receivers.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Denver threw from four-wide only 15 times last year, while Behrens categorizes the report with familiar but unfulfilled preseason role claims.
profile_notes.counterweight: An injury could alter the depth chart, and Courtland Sutton/Waddle opinions differ, but they do not believe the offense and quarterback can support three or four viable fantasy receivers.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Franklin and Bryant off priority lists unless game-relevant volume emerges.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: There was an era when Gesicki was a viable starting option in fantasy, but that time has come and gone. Since posting back-to-back top-eight fantasy campaigns in 2020 and 2021, Gesicki has finished 23rd, 37th, 13th and 41st the past four seasons. The latter came during a 2025 campaign in which he was limited to 41 targets in 13 games. Gesicki is no more than a situational seam stretcher and not much of an option near the goal line (he has exactly two TDs and five end zone targets each of the past three seasons). The 30-year-old will be a risky streaming option even if Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins misses time.

outlook.text: Engram returns for his second season in Denver after an underwhelming debut campaign with the team. The veteran tight end was limited to a career-low 13% target share and finished 15th or lower among tight ends in routes, targets, catches and yardage, despite appearing in 16 games. Engram worked as a short-area target but still struggled to a poor 68% catch rate and was, as usual, a nonfactor near the goal line (one TD, two end zone targets). Engram hasn't cleared four touchdowns in a season since he scored six as a rookie in 2017. He finished 32nd among tight ends in fantasy PPG and isn't a good bet for a larger role this season, especially with Jaylen Waddle added to the offense. The 32-year-old Engram is a fantasy TE3, at best.

Njoku signed with the Chargers after spending his first nine NFL seasons in Cleveland. The 2017 first-round pick was a late bloomer and has struggled with durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2018), but he has been a productive fantasy starter in recent years. Prior to a lost 2025 campaign, Njoku finished in the top eight among tight ends in fantasy PPG three seasons in a row. A force near the goal line, Njoku paced the position in end zone targets in both 2023 and 2024. At 30 years old, Njoku likely still has something left in the tank, but he has a tough path to fantasy relevance in a Los Angeles tight end room that also includes ascending Oronde Gadsden II. Njoku will only be worth a late flier if he quickly takes control as the team's clear starter at the position.

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not assume a healthy or cohesive unit until tackle and interior questions are answered.
profile_notes.summary: The Chargers could benefit from an offensive-line-friendly McDaniel system, but Tucker sees legitimate uncertainty at every starting position.
profile_notes.evidence: Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt are returning from major injuries; Tucker questions center Tyler Biadasz's recovery, Jake Slaughter's shift from Florida center to left guard, and Cole Strange's fit after New England. Harris notes Alt was not fully participating when camp opened.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Shanahan-McVay tree can aid blockers, and all questions can resolve favorably.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor training-camp participation and interior cohesion before assigning a strong line-driven boost to Chargers skill players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target discounted Chargers pieces only on the conditional thesis of healthy line, protected Herbert, and a real offensive jump.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers can imagine a Chargers offense becoming a fantasy answer if health and protection finally cooperate, but view it as a conditional upside case rather than baseline.
profile_notes.evidence: Behrens says a healthy line and protected Justin Herbert could unlock a 28-30-point offense; Harris gives Herbert a mulligan and ties McConkey's rebound to the same factors.
profile_notes.counterweight: It requires unusually good Chargers injury luck, and the team has frequently failed to meet that sort of optimistic offensive projection.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the upside scenario as a tiebreaker for discounted Chargers, not as permission to erase downside.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Mayer enters his first contract year expected to resume his role as Las Vegas' oft-utilized No. 2 TE behind Brock Bowers. The 2023 second-round pick has yet to come close to playing a full season, nor has he emerged as a reliable fantasy option. Last season, he averaged 2.9 targets and 3.4 fantasy points in nine games with Bowers, compared to 6.0 targets and 10.9 PPG in the four games in which Bowers was sidelined. A short-range target (career 5.5 aDOT) with minimal goal line work (one career end zone target), Mayer is way off the fantasy radar. He should be added to rosters only if Bowers misses time.

profile_notes.subject: Las Vegas Raiders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round receiver watch only if a receiver hierarchy emerges and Fernando Mendoza threatens Kirk Cousins for the starting job.
profile_notes.summary: Both see Las Vegas as a useful camp watch because an inexpensive receiver could become relevant if the passing game is better than assumed and a quarterback competition changes the outlook.
profile_notes.evidence: The Raiders publicly prefer Cousins to start the season, but a strong camp/preseason from first-overall-pick Mendoza could force a conversation. Harris says nobody is entitled to a role and wants to identify a clear winner such as Trey Tucker or Jalen Naylor.
profile_notes.counterweight: Brock Bowers is the primary target, the offense is widely expected to be poor, and Harris doubts Naylor's speed/film despite repeated organizational praise.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Follow the receiver and QB hierarchy for a cheap final-round target, but do not rely on a Raiders passer in standard one-QB leagues.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

outlook.text: Tonges enters his fourth NFL season very much on the fantasy radar due to a torn Achilles suffered by George Kittle during last season's playoffs. Kittle is expected to return at some point this season, but while he's out, Tonges is set to replace him as the 49ers' top pass catcher at the position. Kittle missed seven full games last season, including the playoffs (Weeks 2-6, 17, 20). During those games, Tonges handled a 17.9% target share (6.6 per game) and posted a 34-328-3 receiving line. That works out to 11.8 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth among all tight ends last season, ahead of the likes of Harold Fannin Jr., Travis Kelce, Tyler Warren and Jake Ferguson. Tonges will be a fringe TE1 as long as Kittle is sidelined and is thus worth late-round consideration.

profile_notes.subject: Dallas Cowboys skill players
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ignore Cowboys camp hype absent injury or a genuine George Pickens hold-in.
profile_notes.summary: Dallas offers little camp information likely to change established fantasy evaluations.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris describes annual hype around Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, while Ciely says the relevant fantasy roles have little genuine competition. Pickens signed his tag and attended work despite a possible future contract dispute.
profile_notes.counterweight: A Pickens hold-in could hurt early games, and injuries or unavoidably negative reports would be meaningful.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Filter positive Cowboys clips out of draft decisions; only move players for material availability news.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line fallout after starting LT Laremy Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps tear; Harris makes no automatic player-rank change.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps injury as a meaningful downgrade to Washington's offensive environment, though not one that can be precisely assigned to individual ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: He describes the line as thin without its starting left tackle and explicitly says losing good players hurts an offense.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris cannot draw a straight line from the injury to exactly how far Terry McLaurin or Jayden Daniels should fall, so he declines a mechanical rank adjustment.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Washington's pass-game options under review as replacement-line and protection information emerges instead of overreacting with a fixed downgrade.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Modest environmental upgrade following Diggs's signing; no Harris downgrade for Terry McLaurin.
profile_notes.summary: Harris believes Diggs gives Washington a needed credible receiver and can improve the environment for Jayden Daniels, McLaurin, and the offense without taking McLaurin out of his prime role.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris notes that all Commanders pass catchers other than McLaurin had unstable week-to-week roles, while Diggs has a distinctly stronger portfolio. More sustained offense would create additional yards, touchdowns, and possession time.
profile_notes.counterweight: Diggs's personal ceiling is tied to the offense returning to its better two-years-ago form; Washington was not good last year, and Harris says some of that may have been Marcus Mariota-related.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not downgrade McLaurin just for a normal complementary receiver addition; modestly improve the outlook for a functional Commanders passing ecosystem.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

outlook.text: Tagovailoa signed with Atlanta during the offseason after spending his first six seasons in Miami. The 2020 first-round pick showed signs of life a few years ago, which included a 4,624-yard, 29-TD season in 2023, but his production and efficiency have declined since. The final straw was a rough 2025 in which he threw 15 INTs (second most in the league) in just 14 games and was benched. Tagovailoa is a nonfactor with his legs (fewer than 75 yards in four straight seasons, with zero TDs during the span) and has, in turn, never finished better than 10th in fantasy points per game (he was 33rd in 2025). Even if Tagovailoa starts in Week 1, he's unlikely to be anything more than a fringe QB2 in fantasy and figures to eventually lose work to Michael Penix Jr. (recovering from a torn ACL). Tagovailoa is way off the fantasy radar.

profile_notes.subject: Atlanta Falcons passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor Michael Penix recovery versus Tua Tagovailoa starting; it affects Drake London/Kyle Pitts predictability more than Bijan Robinson's elite draft status.
profile_notes.summary: The Falcons' actionable camp fork is whether Penix can take first-team work and be ready Week 1 or whether Tua begins the season, with the quarterback mostly changing receiver/tight-end certainty.
profile_notes.evidence: McCormick prefers Tua's timing and predictability for London/Pitts, while Harris worries Tua should not be playing and might feel better if Penix wins. Both say Bijan's elite selection would not become a no-draft solely from Penix.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither option is a clean projection: Tua may be degraded, Penix's NFL competence is unproven, and the new coaching environment adds uncertainty.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track actual first-team recovery evidence; adjust passing-game players more readily than Bijan.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Sanders enters his second NFL season set to compete with Deshaun Watson for the Browns' starting quarterback gig. Sanders made eight appearances during his rookie season and wasn't overly productive, scoring eight all-purpose touchdowns, throwing 10 interceptions and completing 57% of his passes. The fifth-round pick produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 18th, though it was an impressive 364-yard passing game with four total touchdowns (33.5 points). Sanders added some value with his legs, including 20-plus yards in five straight games to end the season. The 24-year-old remains a wild card, and that's enough to make him worthy of late-round consideration in superflex leagues.

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Conditionally upgrade pass catchers if quarterback play becomes merely passable.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers argue that Cleveland does not need excellent quarterback play for its pass catchers to beat depressed prices.
profile_notes.evidence: The derived analysis identifies KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, and Harold Fannin as players who could benefit if Shedeur Sanders or Dylan Gabriel is simply adequate.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither host expresses confidence that the quarterback outcome will actually be adequate.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Cleveland receivers and tight ends as conditional value rather than automatic targets, and update after credible quarterback evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat early-season cohesion as uncertain after a nearly complete starting-line overhaul.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker calls Cleveland's nearly wholesale replacement of the starting line an unprecedented continuity experiment with high early variance.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Teven Jenkins had been on the team but was not a starter, and cites Spencer Fano, Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins, and Titus Howard as new additions. Tucker grants that most have played meaningful NFL football.
profile_notes.counterweight: The individual additions have shown positive things and could gel by December; Harris also says he is not qualified to make every technique judgment and is not down on every member.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid assuming immediate line quality for Browns assets; prioritize early-season evidence of the new group functioning together.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Browns quarterback competition
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade Browns pass catchers modestly only if Shedeur Sanders wins; avoid treating Deshaun Watson as equivalent.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers believe the Browns quarterback outcome materially affects pass catchers and prefer Sanders over Watson.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Watson's poor form and back-to-back camp interceptions, while saying Sanders can be a flawed but functional NFL passer; Harris says his modest Browns ranks assume Sanders rather than Watson.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris says Sanders must release the ball faster and cannot recreate Colorado-style extended plays; neither calls him an exciting superflex starter.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Browns receiver projections modest, but treat a Sanders starting outcome as a meaningful improvement over Watson.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Cousins signed with the Raiders and will battle projected No. 1 overall draft selection Fernando Mendoza for the team's Week 1 starting job. Cousins made eight starts for Atlanta last season and was not much of a fantasy option, averaging 12.5 fantasy points per game while reaching 18 points only once. The 38-year-old will be a bridge starter at best until Mendoza is ready and is no longer a threat with his legs (7 yards on 14 carries last season). He won't be a fantasy option, even when on the field. He should only be drafted late in superflex leagues.

profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round receiver watch only if a receiver hierarchy emerges and Fernando Mendoza threatens Kirk Cousins for the starting job.
