outlook.text: Johnson's rookie season didn't go as planned. Drafted in the third round as a potential Najee Harris replacement, Johnson quickly found himself buried behind Jaylen Warren and Kenneth Gainwell and never recovered, even losing his kick returner role after a costly Week 2 blunder. He ended his first campaign with 78 yards on 29 touches. The 23-year-old will enter his second season with a fresh start under new coach Mike McCarthy, but he still has a steep hill to climb with Warren and newcomer Rico Dowdle ahead of him on depth chart. He's only worth rostering in dynasty.

profile_notes.subject: Jalen Warren and Rico Dowdle
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Use either as a format-dependent RB2 option, but do not infer workload split from first-team camp reps.
profile_notes.summary: Harris and Harmon find both Steelers backs usable but do not believe training camp will reliably identify a decisive winner.
profile_notes.evidence: They note the backs split first-team work and have different profiles; Harris expects Warren to catch checkdowns but says Dowdle can catch them too.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Steelers historically will not publicize deployment, and past late-summer usage surprises show that camp reporting can miss the actual regular-season plan.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Draft by format and price, not because a routine first-team-rep report implies a true workload edge.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: Pittsburgh Steelers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a stable, projectable offense; do not manufacture large camp-based projections.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see a reasonably high/projectable Steelers floor if Aaron Rodgers remains healthy, without an exciting ceiling case.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Mike McCarthy's high-floor play calling, a settled enough offensive line, and known top receivers; Harris calls the roster full of good professionals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both retain concern that Rodgers may have declined further and will avoid contact, limiting offensive aggression.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep established Steelers values near their baseline projections instead of reacting sharply to routine camp headlines.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: 49ers running-back handcuff
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not spend material draft capital attempting to identify Christian McCaffrey's backup from opaque August reports.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers have extremely low confidence that camp will identify a usable McCaffrey handcuff.
profile_notes.evidence: Jordan James logged only three regular-season offensive snaps; Kaelon Black was viewed as a reach, neither prospect has a McCaffrey-like receiving profile, and San Francisco does not disclose roles clearly.
profile_notes.counterweight: If a reserve is repeatedly reported to run the receiving playbook, that would matter, and managers with deep benches can cheaply stash both options.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Accept McCaffrey's unique injury risk rather than overpaying for a false certainty; use waivers or very late stashes if needed.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Smith heads into his second NFL season set to compete with Emmett Johnson and Emari Demercado for No. 2 duties behind new Chiefs' lead back Kenneth Walker III. Smith played just 17% of the Chiefs' offensive snaps as a rookie and had nearly as many targets (35) as he did carries (44). The seventh-round pick wasn't overly effective (3.43 yards per carry, 4.9 yards per target) and was able to reach double-digit fantasy points only once (13.1 in a Week 7 blowout win). The undersized 23-year-old would likely share the backfield even if Walker were to miss time, and he has minimal fantasy appeal.

profile_notes.subject: Arizona Cardinals backfield
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat Jeremiah Love as RB16 upside only if roster and usage clarity arrives; do not assume top-five draft capital mandates a massive workload.
profile_notes.summary: Harris makes Arizona's unresolved four-back camp hierarchy a key story because Love's ADP can be distorted both by rookie draft capital and pessimistic team projections; Richard sees a constrained environment.
profile_notes.evidence: The camp may end with only Love and Tyler Allgeier clearly relevant, or retain four bodies. Richard cites a hard schedule, weak line, first-year offense, and low team outlook; Harris cites historical splits involving Bijan Robinson/Allgeier and Gibbs/Montgomery.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris argues fantasy analysts routinely overstate certainty about bad teams, and a Conner or Benson trade could create immediate upside; Love is talented enough for hot-hand games.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor cuts, trades, joint practices, and ADP; draft Love only where a committee outcome is already discounted.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Arizona Cardinals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not write off the offense because of rebuilding expectations; balance possible skill-position value against the league's hardest projected schedule.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Arizona as a possible market-value offense because it is being declared hopeless, while Gretch sees meaningful skill talent but acknowledges a difficult environment.
profile_notes.evidence: They cite McBride, Love, Harrison, Wilson, and backfield depth; Gretch says the projected schedule is the NFL's hardest and the club is a large underdog early.
profile_notes.counterweight: The schedule and quarterback uncertainty can make running-back and passing-game efficiency difficult.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Consider discounted Cardinals talent individually, rather than treating the offense as automatically unproductive.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

profile_notes.subject: Baltimore Ravens offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor the three new interior pieces and tackle performance before assuming a strong rushing environment.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker sees Baltimore's changed interior and new under-center offense as a significant continuity risk despite potential upside.
profile_notes.evidence: He names injured-center returnee Ethan Pocic, returning Simpson, and first-round Penn State guard Vega Ioane as a substantially remade interior, while noting the rookie may switch sides. He also says neither Ronnie Stanley nor Roger Rosengarten met expectations last year.
profile_notes.counterweight: If the interior questions resolve positively, Tucker says the line could be good; Derrick Henry remains a rare durability/production outlier.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the interior transition in the downside range for Ravens runners and passing-game projections rather than presuming past line quality.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

outlook.text: Penix is no longer guaranteed a starting job entering his third season. The 2024 first-round pick has appeared in 14 games and has 14 total touchdowns, a 21% off-target rate and a 60% completion percentage to show for it. Penix has done well to avoid turnovers (six career INTs), but he's a nonfactor with his legs (career 28-81-2 rushing) and failed to post a single fantasy outing better than 10th last season. Penix tore an ACL in Week 11, which further complicates his path to beating out newcomer Tua Tagovailoa for the team's Week 1 starting gig. The 26-year-old might eventually emerge into a fine NFL starter, but even if he does, his lack of rushing will limit his fantasy output. He's well off the fantasy radar.

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Atlanta Falcons passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor Michael Penix recovery versus Tua Tagovailoa starting; it affects Drake London/Kyle Pitts predictability more than Bijan Robinson's elite draft status.
profile_notes.summary: The Falcons' actionable camp fork is whether Penix can take first-team work and be ready Week 1 or whether Tua begins the season, with the quarterback mostly changing receiver/tight-end certainty.
profile_notes.evidence: McCormick prefers Tua's timing and predictability for London/Pitts, while Harris worries Tua should not be playing and might feel better if Penix wins. Both say Bijan's elite selection would not become a no-draft solely from Penix.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither option is a clean projection: Tua may be degraded, Penix's NFL competence is unproven, and the new coaching environment adds uncertainty.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track actual first-team recovery evidence; adjust passing-game players more readily than Bijan.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: Sanders is back as a pass-catching tight end in Carolina, though he's unlikely to see a larger share of the target pie with veteran Darren Waller now in the mix. Sanders - a 2024 fourth-round pick - flashed as a rookie with a 33-342-1 receiving line while playing 55% of Carolina's offensive snaps and handling 9.1% of the targets across 16 games. He simply didn't progress in Year 2, posting a 29-190-1 line while playing 52% of the snaps and handling a 10% target share in 12 healthy games. Sanders has been an inefficient short-range target with little goal line activity thus far (four career end zone targets), placing the 23-year-old well off the fantasy radar.

Parkinson is set to resume his role in the Rams' TE committee. The 2020 fourth-round pick was a part-time player early last season, but graduated to a much larger role in the second half. In fact, from Week 10 on (12 games, including the playoffs), Parkinson averaged 5.0 targets and 12.1 fantasy points per game, scoring nine touchdowns along the way. He finished the regular season with career-high marks across the board, which included his first top-35 fantasy campaign (17th). If Parkinson carries his increased role into 2026, he'll be a sneaky fantasy option, but the problem is that he needs to fend off Tyler Higbee and recent second-round picks Terrance Ferguson and Max Klare for work in an offense that also includes Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Parkinson, 27, is a deep sleeper worth a look in leagues that start two tight ends.

profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a strong environment, but do not let that alone erase individual age, role, and price concerns.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see Los Angeles as the NFC West offense most widely expected to be elite, while Harris warns that assumed certainty creates contradictory player valuations.
profile_notes.evidence: They discuss a possible 30-point-per-game offense, the resolution of Matthew Stafford's prior back concern, and the Rams' recent history of meaningful August role signals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris opens the episode by showing that consensus team projections frequently fail, and individual Rams can still decline or lose role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Rams environment as a supporting factor, then make player decisions on role, talent, health, and market cost.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Though he never quite made it onto the fantasy radar, Washington was one of the most fun, surprising "breakout" players of 2025. Essentially an extension of the offensive line at 6-foot-6, 264 pounds, Washington is known mainly for his blocking. Still, the 2023 third-round pick played well enough that he was stealing snaps and targets from both Jonnu Smith and Pat Freiermuth. Washington never cleared six targets or 10.7 fantasy points in any game, but he was effective with the ball in his hands and averaged 8.5 yards per target. Though Smith has been released, Pittsburgh's offense is no longer being led by TE superfan Arthur Smith, which is likely to lead to a lesser role for Washington. Expect him to operate as a rarely targeted blocking complement to Freiermuth.

profile_notes.subject: Pittsburgh Steelers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a stable, projectable offense; do not manufacture large camp-based projections.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see a reasonably high/projectable Steelers floor if Aaron Rodgers remains healthy, without an exciting ceiling case.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Mike McCarthy's high-floor play calling, a settled enough offensive line, and known top receivers; Harris calls the roster full of good professionals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both retain concern that Rodgers may have declined further and will avoid contact, limiting offensive aggression.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep established Steelers values near their baseline projections instead of reacting sharply to routine camp headlines.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Knox enters his eighth season as a solid role player for the Buffalo offense. He is on the field quite a bit (20th among tight ends in snaps last season), but defers to Dalton Kincaid when it comes to the team's top target priority at the TE position. Even when Kincaid was sidelined last season, Knox was limited to only 3.6 targets and 6.1 fantasy points per game. Knox has never posted a top-10 fantasy campaign and has finished outside the top 30 in PPG each of the last three seasons. Even if Kincaid misses additional time, Knox will max out as a fantasy TE2.

McCarthy's career is off to a slow start after the 2024 first-round pick missed his entire rookie season because of an injury then struggled through 2025. McCarthy appeared in 10 games and totaled 11 passing TDs and 12 interceptions while completing an ugly 58% of his passes. McCarthy added some value with his legs (including four TDs), but his production was extremely inconsistent (18-plus fantasy points in four games, but 6.7 per game in his other six outings). The 23-year-old still has plenty of time to develop, but that will come as a backup to Kyler Murray this season. McCarthy is worth considering only in dynasty leagues.

profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not raise Jefferson from near his current ceiling on 'dialed in' Kyler Murray camp reports; downgrade only if doubts become sustained evidence.
profile_notes.summary: Richard sees Minnesota quarterback competence as an offense-wide variable for Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and the run game, but Harris sees mostly downside because Jefferson is already near ceiling.
profile_notes.evidence: Richard wants confirmation the quarterback competition is not real and that Murray outplays Minnesota's prior passers, which could force defenses deeper and improve the ecosystem.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both have heard optimistic Kyler camp narratives before and retain concerns about anticipation and inconsistency; Harris says the plausible adjustment is Jefferson falling toward WR12, not rising substantially.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid acting on generic camp praise; retain elite Jefferson pricing but watch for repeated evidence that Minnesota's passing environment is failing.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat all Vikings except Jefferson as non-starter-level drafts until Kyler Murray and line health prove functional.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers believe Minnesota's broken 2025 offense makes a Kyler Murray rescue uncertain, especially for secondary receivers.
profile_notes.evidence: They say J.J. McCarthy was not fine and the offense deteriorated; Murray is better but not automatically a panacea for Jefferson or Addison. Erickson identifies an injured/inconsistent Christian Darrisaw and center instability after Ryan Kelly's concussion-related retirement as major 2025 line failures.
profile_notes.counterweight: Minnesota changed quarterbacks and added linemen, and a coaching offseason could prioritize Jefferson successfully.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid treating secondary Vikings as automatic starters; demand a discount and monitor quarterback/line health rather than believing generic positive camp stories.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Beck was selected by the Cardinals in the third round of April's draft. Beck is a big, experienced quarterback who started for two seasons at Georgia prior to leading Miami to the national championship game last season. Beck paced this rookie QB class in completion percentage last season (72.4%) and for his career (69.5%), while also leading this group with an 80.9 QBR and 8.4 YPA during his 55-game collegiate career. He's unlikely to offer much with his legs in the pros, however, and will begin his career behind Jacoby Brissett and likely Gardner Minshew. Beck has no short-term fantasy value, though he could very well make some starts during his rookie season. Monitor him in superflex.

profile_notes.subject: Cardinals quarterback situation
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Prefer Jacoby Brissett stability for Cardinals pass-catcher volume; lower expectations if Carson Beck earns substantial early work.
profile_notes.summary: Gretch treats the Brissett-versus-Beck outcome as central to Arizona receiver/tight-end volume, while Harris agrees the rookie quarterback would be less exciting.
profile_notes.evidence: Gretch says Brissett's quick release and willingness to throw generated huge target volume, including Wilson's 18-target game and two 15-target games, whereas young quarterbacks can hold the ball and take sacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: A new offense could change deployment regardless of starter, and the transcript does not declare either quarterback the confirmed season-long choice.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use camp/preseason quarterback evidence to refine Cardinals pass-catcher projections rather than treating last year's targets as automatic.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: After failing to lock down a starting gig with the Bears, Steelers and Jets, Fields was traded to the Chiefs and will move forward as Patrick Mahomes' backup. That's obviously unlikely to lead to much playing time, but with Mahomes recovering from a torn ACL, there's a small chance Fields could get some early-season run in 2026. Should Fields start, he'll find his way into the QB1 discussion because of his elite rushing ability (45.1 rush rushing yards per game last season and four-plus rushing TDs in four straight seasons). In seven full games last season, Fields averaged 19.2 fantasy points, including 25 points in three of those games. He averaged 18.9 points with Pittsburgh in 2024 and 19.3 during his final two seasons in Chicago. Roster Fields in only deep superflex leagues.

Flacco re-signed with the Bengals and will back up Joe Burrow this season. The veteran quarterback made six starts for Cincinnati last season and showed well, totaling 14 touchdowns and four interceptions while averaging 19.9 fantasy PPG. The 41-year-old can still sling it, but he's a nonfactor with his legs and hasn't finished a season better than 20th in fantasy points since 2014. If Burrow is sidelined, Flacco will do enough through the air to land in the QB2 discussion, but that's his ceiling.

profile_notes.subject: Cincinnati Bengals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not change elite-player ranks on camp drills; monitor credible evidence of more under-center and modern-concept usage.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers regard Cincinnati's core as settled and already elite, with offensive evolution as a possible path from top-five to No. 1 production.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon wants to see Joe Burrow under center more and the offense move beyond an almost exclusively shotgun approach; he notes incremental increases in Chase motion and varied alignment.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harmon repeatedly says camp talk will not force rank changes for Burrow, Chase, Higgins, or Brown, and the preference may remain Burrow's existing style.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat schematic reports as upside context, not a reason to chase already-expensive Bengals players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Jones returns for his second go as Brock Purdy's backup in San Francisco after showing well in relief duties in eight starts last season. In those eight appearances, Jones completed 70% of his passes and threw 13 touchdowns to six interceptions. The 2021 first-round pick was a nonfactor with his legs (28-64-0), however, which limited him to an underwhelming 16.3 fantasy PPG. Should Purdy miss time in 2026, Jones will be no more than a fringe QB2. The 28-year-old shouldn't be considered on draft day.

Arroyo is eyeing a Year 2 breakout after an underwhelming rookie campaign in which he played a clear second fiddle to A.J. Barner. The 2025 second-round pick was limited to 39% of the offensive snaps during the 13 games he was active. He cleared three targets in a game only once (five in Week 7) and his lone touchdown came on one of just two targets in Week 9. Arroyo was effective as a vertical target at the collegiate level, so he remains an intriguing dynasty hold, but the 23-year-old has a tough path to short-term fantasy relevance while stuck behind Barner in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

Stowers was selected by the Eagles in the second round of April's draft. Stowers is a converted quarterback who improved his production each of the last three seasons, peaking with a 62-769-4 receiving line in 2025. He aligned in the slot on 72% of his collegiate routes (highest among this rookie tight end class) and his career 2.38 YPRR is easily tops in this TE class. He's not much of a blocker, but he sports good speed and athleticism (he posted the best vertical and broad jumps among TEs at the combine). Stowers will have minimal fantasy value while working behind Dallas Goedert as a rookie, but he has long-term TE1 upside and will be a popular breakout candidate in 2027.

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade offense and Saquon Barkley context if interior health holds in the new scheme.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker believes Philadelphia has a high ceiling and high floor because last year's underperformance was substantially injury-driven and the new system should help blockers.
profile_notes.evidence: Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson fought through multiple injuries, surgeries, and rehabilitation; Lane Johnson missed the second half with plantar fasciitis. Tucker says the new coordinator's increased play action avoids isolating tackles in straight dropbacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: The line did not play as a top-five unit last year, and the recovery of injured interior starters must persist.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat a healthy Eagles line as a positive contextual upgrade for Barkley and the offense rather than anchoring on last year's unit ranking.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Keep outside the small trusted-offense tier until the new Mannion system succeeds in games.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers refuse to restore Philadelphia to an automatic top-offense projection after last year's collapse and coordinator replacement.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites A.J. Brown's trade, questions around the line, and the team's decision to replace the coordinator despite prior Super Bowl success. Ciely believes Mannion's changes can help but says practice and preseason cannot prove a top-five result.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense has Jalen Hurts, a strong history, and a scheme that could improve play action/middle-field work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid building draft projections on an assumed Eagles bounce-back; wait for regular-season evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Taylor was a busy man during his rookie season, playing 81% of the Jets' offensive snaps and handling a healthy 19% of the targets in 13 games. The 2025 second-round pick struggled badly with efficiency while dealing with the team's quarterback woes, ranking near the basement in catch rate (65%) and yards per target (5.4). Taylor also dropped five passes (fourth most), scored only one touchdown and finished 30th in fantasy PPG. Taylor would've been a potential 2026 breakout candidate, but that was quickly derailed when the Jets selected Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of April's draft. Taylor will play a role in the New York offense, but he won't see nearly enough targets to allow any sort of fantasy relevance.

Johnson was a solid find by the Giants in the fourth round of the 2024 draft, but he's headed for a reduced role this season following New York's signing of Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers' return to health. The change comes after Johnson ranked top 12 among tight ends in both snaps and routes, but 23rd in catches and 19th in yards last season. Johnson was busy near the goal line (seven end zone targets), but struggled with drops (tight end-high nine), which led to a poor 63% catch rate. Johnson finished 23rd in fantasy PPG and now may be lucky to see a target or two per game. He's well off the fantasy radar.

profile_notes.subject: New York Giants offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat Giants outcomes as high-variance rather than projecting certainty into Week 1 roles.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers identify the Giants as a team full of volatile fantasy outcomes centered on Skattebo, Jaxson Dart, and Malik Nabers.
profile_notes.evidence: Funston says all three carry wild ranges of outcomes and calls the team fascinating from a fantasy perspective. Harris agrees on Skattebo and Nabers as swing possibilities.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris sharply differs on Dart, saying he disliked the tape and is out on him; the team label is an uncertainty signal, not a blanket endorsement.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not stack Giants assumptions as settled facts; assess each player separately and demand a price that accommodates role and quarterback uncertainty.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

outlook.text: Higbee re-signed with the Rams and will battle for work with the likes of Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson and rookie Max Klare. The 2016 fourth-round pick has a pair of top-10 fantasy campaigns in his career, but the last one came in 2022 and he's finished 24th or worse in three consecutive seasons. Injuries have been part of the issue (21 missed games over the last two seasons), but so has a lesser role and minimal goal-line work (seven touchdowns and four end zone targets over the last three years). Now 33 years old, Higbee is likely third in line for targets at his position on his own team and, thus, nowhere close to fantasy relevance.

outlook.text: Klare was selected by the Rams in the second round of April's draft. Klare is a receiving tight end who has experience playing in line and in the slot. He might not offer much as a blocker in the pros, but he showed his receiving ability at two different schools, posting a 51-685-4 line with Purdue in 2024 and a 43-448-2 line with Ohio State in 2025. Klare has the speed and athleticism to eventually emerge as a fantasy option, but hell begin his career in a crowded tight end room that also includes Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and 2025 second-round pick Terrance Ferguson. Klare is nowhere close to fantasy relevance at the moment.

outlook.text: Winston is back with the Giants and with Russell Wilson out of the picture, he is expected to serve as the primary backup to Jaxson Dart in 2026. Winston hasn't been a full-time starter since 2019 and was limited to two starts last season. In typical Winston style, results varied, with 11.0 fantasy points against Green Bay in Week 11, followed by a 32.2-point showing against Detroit the very next week. The 32-year-old doesn't do much with his legs, but his boom/bust passing style makes him an occasional streaming option when the matchup is right. That's what he'll be, if called on for a spot start in place of Dart this season.

profile_notes.subject: New York Giants offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat Giants outcomes as high-variance rather than projecting certainty into Week 1 roles.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers identify the Giants as a team full of volatile fantasy outcomes centered on Skattebo, Jaxson Dart, and Malik Nabers.
profile_notes.evidence: Funston says all three carry wild ranges of outcomes and calls the team fascinating from a fantasy perspective. Harris agrees on Skattebo and Nabers as swing possibilities.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris sharply differs on Dart, saying he disliked the tape and is out on him; the team label is an uncertainty signal, not a blanket endorsement.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not stack Giants assumptions as settled facts; assess each player separately and demand a price that accommodates role and quarterback uncertainty.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

outlook.text: Simpson was selected by the Rams in the first round of April's draft. Simpson was a one-year starter at Alabama and wasn't overly impressive statistically, completing 64% of his passes and posting a pedestrian 76.6 QBR. He's fairly accurate with an average arm, but he's a bit undersized and doesn't figure to move the needle a ton with his legs (62-309-2 rushing in 2025). Simpson won't see the field consistently until Matthew Stafford retires, so he's well off the 2026 fantasy radar. Keep him stashed in dynasty, especially superflex formats.

profile_notes.subject: Rams offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a strong environment, but do not let that alone erase individual age, role, and price concerns.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see Los Angeles as the NFC West offense most widely expected to be elite, while Harris warns that assumed certainty creates contradictory player valuations.
profile_notes.evidence: They discuss a possible 30-point-per-game offense, the resolution of Matthew Stafford's prior back concern, and the Rams' recent history of meaningful August role signals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris opens the episode by showing that consensus team projections frequently fail, and individual Rams can still decline or lose role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Rams environment as a supporting factor, then make player decisions on role, talent, health, and market cost.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Richardson enters his fourth NFL season currently as a backup to Daniel Jones, but still a candidate to be traded. Last season, Richardson played just 14 snaps off the bench and missed most of the season with an eye injury. If ever called on to start, Richardson will be an interesting fantasy wild card. On one hand, the 2023 fourth-overall pick has a ton of upside; he ranked no lower than sixth among QBs in carries, rushing yards and rush TDs in 2024 despite only playing 10 full games, while also pacing the position in average depth of throw and yards per completion. That led to four 20-plus fantasy point games. On the other hand, Richardson's poor passing may lead to many duds. He had fewer than 15 fantasy points in his other six outings, threw 12 INTs on the season (fourth most) and his 48% completion percentage ranked last. In total, he averaged 15.8 fantasy PPG in the 10 games, which would've ranked 15th over the full season. Richardson's elite rushing ability and aggressive passi…

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line fallout after starting LT Laremy Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps tear; Harris makes no automatic player-rank change.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Tunsil's likely season-ending triceps injury as a meaningful downgrade to Washington's offensive environment, though not one that can be precisely assigned to individual ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: He describes the line as thin without its starting left tackle and explicitly says losing good players hurts an offense.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris cannot draw a straight line from the injury to exactly how far Terry McLaurin or Jayden Daniels should fall, so he declines a mechanical rank adjustment.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Washington's pass-game options under review as replacement-line and protection information emerges instead of overreacting with a fixed downgrade.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Zeroes For 2026 & Luther Burden Injury

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Modest environmental upgrade following Diggs's signing; no Harris downgrade for Terry McLaurin.
profile_notes.summary: Harris believes Diggs gives Washington a needed credible receiver and can improve the environment for Jayden Daniels, McLaurin, and the offense without taking McLaurin out of his prime role.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris notes that all Commanders pass catchers other than McLaurin had unstable week-to-week roles, while Diggs has a distinctly stronger portfolio. More sustained offense would create additional yards, touchdowns, and possession time.
profile_notes.counterweight: Diggs's personal ceiling is tied to the offense returning to its better two-years-ago form; Washington was not good last year, and Harris says some of that may have been Marcus Mariota-related.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not downgrade McLaurin just for a normal complementary receiver addition; modestly improve the outlook for a functional Commanders passing ecosystem.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

profile_notes.subject: Dallas Cowboys skill players
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ignore Cowboys camp hype absent injury or a genuine George Pickens hold-in.
profile_notes.summary: Dallas offers little camp information likely to change established fantasy evaluations.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris describes annual hype around Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, while Ciely says the relevant fantasy roles have little genuine competition. Pickens signed his tag and attended work despite a possible future contract dispute.
profile_notes.counterweight: A Pickens hold-in could hurt early games, and injuries or unavoidably negative reports would be meaningful.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Filter positive Cowboys clips out of draft decisions; only move players for material availability news.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Vele is expected to open the season as New Orleans' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave until Jordyn Tyson returns from injury near midseason. Vele's first season with the Saints was marred with injuries. The 2024 seventh-round pick, who posted a 41-475-3 receiving line with Denver as a rookie, barely played throughout most of 2025 prior to taking on an every-down role during Weeks 10-15. In those five games (one of which he left hurt), he averaged 5.6 targets per game, but reached 12.0 fantasy points once (an 8-93-1 effort in Week 13 against Miami). The 28-year-old has yet to show he can be relied on for consistent targets and fantasy production, but he'll play an every-down role early on, which makes him a sleeper for flex value in deep leagues. He'll be worth a roster spot until Tyson returns.

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade associated players only if the offense proves at least competent.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers identify the possibility that Miami is merely mediocre rather than historically bad as a major assumption that could overturn rankings.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon points to under-the-radar line additions, Malik Willis's small-sample improvement, and the fact that Achane could lose roughly four points per game and still approach the cited price.
profile_notes.counterweight: Practice performance remains poor and neither speaker declares the offense fixed.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor quarterback and line competence; buy individual Dolphins only when their price assumes an unrealistically disastrous offense.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor offensive-line and overall-environment reports before making broad Dolphins downgrades.
profile_notes.summary: Harris treats Washington's dominant joint-practice performance against Miami as a meaningful warning about the Dolphins' environment, but not a final verdict.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Washington reporters described Miami's offensive line as overrun throughout the drills and its defense as repeatedly beaten by Jayden Daniels.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris explicitly wants to see the issue again and look for improvement through the month; De'Von Achane also reportedly broke a third-down touchdown play.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the offensive-line concern in Dolphins player evaluations and seek confirming reports rather than automatically abandoning every Miami asset.
profile_notes.episode_title: Post-Hype Sleepers For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Miami Dolphins receiver room
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Grind camp rotations for a free late receiver, especially Malik Washington; do not assume any player has guaranteed targets.
profile_notes.summary: Both say Miami offers a rare chance to find late value because the market views the team as hopeless and no receiver is penciled into targets behind the headline names.
profile_notes.evidence: Daugherty will watch Malik Washington; Harris lists Kevin Coleman, Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas, Jalen Tolbert, Tutu Atwell, and Terrace Marshall and says reporters should expose two- and three-WR rotations.
profile_notes.counterweight: Miami may struggle to push the ball, Bell's knee clouds availability, and open competition can yield no dependable player rather than a hidden breakout.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track repeated first-team usage and stash only the receiver who earns a real role; be willing to churn quickly.
profile_notes.episode_title: Drake Maye & Josh Allen & Previewing AFC East

outlook.text: Coleman Jr. was selected by the Dolphins in the fifth round of April's draft. Coleman is a small, slot receiver and punt returner who aligned inside on 83% of his 943 collegiate pass routes. Despite playing at three different FBS schools over the last three seasons, Coleman handled a solid 21% target share during the span and played well, catching 72% of his targets and dropping only four of 229 targets (1.7%). He posted a weak, 88 speed score at the combine, running a 4.49 40-yard dash at 179 pounds. Coleman will battle fellow rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, as well as a host of veterans for a role in a Miami offense likely to struggle to score points. He should only be drafted in dynasty.

outlook.text: Brown signed with the Eagles and he's likely to slot in either third or fourth on the team's depth chart behind DeVonta Smith, first-round rookie Makai Lemon and perhaps Dontayvion Wicks. Once a featured target in Baltimore and Arizona, Brown was more of a situational player during his two seasons in Kansas City. He barely saw the field in 2024 due to injury before handling a career-low 14.2% target share in 16 games in 2025. Brown cleared 10 fantasy points three times, but all came prior to Week 7. With Dallas Goedert and Saquon Barkley also heavily in the mix for targets in Philly, Brown will have to beat out Lemon and Wicks for a starting gig in order to have any chance at flex value.

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade offense and Saquon Barkley context if interior health holds in the new scheme.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker believes Philadelphia has a high ceiling and high floor because last year's underperformance was substantially injury-driven and the new system should help blockers.
profile_notes.evidence: Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson fought through multiple injuries, surgeries, and rehabilitation; Lane Johnson missed the second half with plantar fasciitis. Tucker says the new coordinator's increased play action avoids isolating tackles in straight dropbacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: The line did not play as a top-five unit last year, and the recovery of injured interior starters must persist.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat a healthy Eagles line as a positive contextual upgrade for Barkley and the offense rather than anchoring on last year's unit ranking.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Philadelphia Eagles offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Keep outside the small trusted-offense tier until the new Mannion system succeeds in games.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers refuse to restore Philadelphia to an automatic top-offense projection after last year's collapse and coordinator replacement.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris cites A.J. Brown's trade, questions around the line, and the team's decision to replace the coordinator despite prior Super Bowl success. Ciely believes Mannion's changes can help but says practice and preseason cannot prove a top-five result.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense has Jalen Hurts, a strong history, and a scheme that could improve play action/middle-field work.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid building draft projections on an assumed Eagles bounce-back; wait for regular-season evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Midway through the 2025 season, Franklin appeared well on his way to a Year 2 breakout. The 2024 fourth-round pick entered Denver's Week 12 bye with five touchdowns and a team-high 81 targets (22% share). He was demoted during the week off, however, and ended up with just 24 total targets (a 9% share) over his final seven games, including the playoffs. In total, Franklin finished a respectable 41st among receivers in fantasy PPG, but the 23-year-old's demotion, coupled with Denver's offseason acquisition of Jaylen Waddle, means he's nowhere close to the fantasy radar. Franklin will battle Pat Bryant, Marvin Mims Jr. and Lil'Jordan Humphrey for No. 3 duties. Ignore him on draft day.

profile_notes.subject: Denver Broncos wide receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not elevate Troy Franklin or Pat Bryant on four-wide camp headlines without actual sustainable usage.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers reject a reported Broncos move toward more four-wide formations as a reason to project multiple new fantasy receivers.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Denver threw from four-wide only 15 times last year, while Behrens categorizes the report with familiar but unfulfilled preseason role claims.
profile_notes.counterweight: An injury could alter the depth chart, and Courtland Sutton/Waddle opinions differ, but they do not believe the offense and quarterback can support three or four viable fantasy receivers.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Franklin and Bryant off priority lists unless game-relevant volume emerges.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

profile_notes.subject: Cardinals quarterback situation
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Prefer Jacoby Brissett stability for Cardinals pass-catcher volume; lower expectations if Carson Beck earns substantial early work.
profile_notes.summary: Gretch treats the Brissett-versus-Beck outcome as central to Arizona receiver/tight-end volume, while Harris agrees the rookie quarterback would be less exciting.
profile_notes.evidence: Gretch says Brissett's quick release and willingness to throw generated huge target volume, including Wilson's 18-target game and two 15-target games, whereas young quarterbacks can hold the ball and take sacks.
profile_notes.counterweight: A new offense could change deployment regardless of starter, and the transcript does not declare either quarterback the confirmed season-long choice.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use camp/preseason quarterback evidence to refine Cardinals pass-catcher projections rather than treating last year's targets as automatic.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

profile_notes.subject: Arizona Cardinals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not write off the offense because of rebuilding expectations; balance possible skill-position value against the league's hardest projected schedule.
profile_notes.summary: Harris sees Arizona as a possible market-value offense because it is being declared hopeless, while Gretch sees meaningful skill talent but acknowledges a difficult environment.
profile_notes.evidence: They cite McBride, Love, Harrison, Wilson, and backfield depth; Gretch says the projected schedule is the NFL's hardest and the club is a large underdog early.
profile_notes.counterweight: The schedule and quarterback uncertainty can make running-back and passing-game efficiency difficult.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Consider discounted Cardinals talent individually, rather than treating the offense as automatically unproductive.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

profile_notes.subject: Chicago Bears pass catchers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not assign Lions roles to Bears players solely because Ben Johnson is the coach.
profile_notes.summary: Ben Johnson's arrival does not make any Bears receiver a copy of Amon-Ra St. Brown or guarantee a WR6 outcome.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Amon-Ra is better than the available Bears options and rejects the temptation to call a Luther Burden highlight proof that he is the new Amon-Ra. Erickson adds that 12/13 personnel, a third-round TE, and Johnson's strong run design can limit assumed target windfalls.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense could still improve and Chicago's traded DJ Moore leaves targets available, but that allocation cannot be known from camp clips.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft Chicago receivers on role-mapping narratives; wait for actual season usage and make only evidence-based adjustments.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Kirk signed with the 49ers after spending his first eight seasons with Arizona, Jacksonville and Houston. The 2018 second-round pick peaked with a 12th-place finish in fantasy points in 2022, but that marks his only career top-25 finish and he's been way off the fantasy radar the last two seasons, partially due to injury woes (13 missed games). Kirk doesn't have a clear path to consistent targets in San Francisco, with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling also in the mix (not to mention Christian McCaffrey and eventually George Kittle). The 29-year-old is barely worth a late flier in deep leagues.

profile_notes.subject: 49ers running-back handcuff
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not spend material draft capital attempting to identify Christian McCaffrey's backup from opaque August reports.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers have extremely low confidence that camp will identify a usable McCaffrey handcuff.
profile_notes.evidence: Jordan James logged only three regular-season offensive snaps; Kaelon Black was viewed as a reach, neither prospect has a McCaffrey-like receiving profile, and San Francisco does not disclose roles clearly.
profile_notes.counterweight: If a reserve is repeatedly reported to run the receiving playbook, that would matter, and managers with deep benches can cheaply stash both options.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Accept McCaffrey's unique injury risk rather than overpaying for a false certainty; use waivers or very late stashes if needed.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

outlook.text: Bell was selected by the Bills in the fourth round of April's draft. Bell is an undersized, but versatile, receiver who finished 2025 second in the nation (first in this WR rookie class) in receiving yards (1,278) and, while he had a class-high 25 drops across 52 collegiate games, he was better in this area last season (five drops on 146 targets). Bell showed well at the combine, running a solid 4.40 40-yard dash and posting terrific marks in the vertical and broad jump. With DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir locked in atop Buffalo's WR depth chart, Bell will compete with Keon Coleman and Josh Palmer for work. He's only worth drafting in dynasty formats.

Lance was selected by the Saints in the fourth round of April's draft. Trey's little brother is the lone wide receiver in this rookie class who didn't play a single snap at the FBS level. However, he was productive as a perimeter receiver at North Dakota State, posting receiving lines of 75-1,053-17 and 51-1,079-8 over the last two seasons. He's a year or so older than most of his classmates, but he dominated at the combine with terrific showings in the 40-yard dash (4.34), vertical (41.5) and broad jump (133). He has the size and skillset to battle Devaughn Vele for New Orleans' No. 3 gig behind Chris Olave and first-round rookie Jordyn Tyson. Lance's primary value is in dynasty leagues.

profile_notes.subject: Cincinnati Bengals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not change elite-player ranks on camp drills; monitor credible evidence of more under-center and modern-concept usage.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers regard Cincinnati's core as settled and already elite, with offensive evolution as a possible path from top-five to No. 1 production.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon wants to see Joe Burrow under center more and the offense move beyond an almost exclusively shotgun approach; he notes incremental increases in Chase motion and varied alignment.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harmon repeatedly says camp talk will not force rank changes for Burrow, Chase, Higgins, or Brown, and the preference may remain Burrow's existing style.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat schematic reports as upside context, not a reason to chase already-expensive Bengals players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

outlook.text: Kacmarek was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. Kacmarek is a massive, strong blocking tight end who won't see much receiving work in the pros. He's likely to play a lot of snap as a rookie considering Miami's shaky roster, but Greg Dulcich is expected to operate as the team's top pass-catcher at the tight end position. Kacmarek is no more than the deepest of deep sleepers.

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not raise Jefferson from near his current ceiling on 'dialed in' Kyler Murray camp reports; downgrade only if doubts become sustained evidence.
profile_notes.summary: Richard sees Minnesota quarterback competence as an offense-wide variable for Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and the run game, but Harris sees mostly downside because Jefferson is already near ceiling.
profile_notes.evidence: Richard wants confirmation the quarterback competition is not real and that Murray outplays Minnesota's prior passers, which could force defenses deeper and improve the ecosystem.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both have heard optimistic Kyler camp narratives before and retain concerns about anticipation and inconsistency; Harris says the plausible adjustment is Jefferson falling toward WR12, not rising substantially.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid acting on generic camp praise; retain elite Jefferson pricing but watch for repeated evidence that Minnesota's passing environment is failing.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.subject: Minnesota Vikings passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat all Vikings except Jefferson as non-starter-level drafts until Kyler Murray and line health prove functional.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers believe Minnesota's broken 2025 offense makes a Kyler Murray rescue uncertain, especially for secondary receivers.
profile_notes.evidence: They say J.J. McCarthy was not fine and the offense deteriorated; Murray is better but not automatically a panacea for Jefferson or Addison. Erickson identifies an injured/inconsistent Christian Darrisaw and center instability after Ryan Kelly's concussion-related retirement as major 2025 line failures.
profile_notes.counterweight: Minnesota changed quarterbacks and added linemen, and a coaching offseason could prioritize Jefferson successfully.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid treating secondary Vikings as automatic starters; demand a discount and monitor quarterback/line health rather than believing generic positive camp stories.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

outlook.text: Raridon was selected by the Patriots in the third round of April's draft. Raridon is a tall, blocking tight end who was barely targeted (5% share) and totaled a 48-623-3 receiving line during four seasons at Notre Dame. Most of the receiving work came in 2025, so perhaps there's some hope in that area, but he's a long shot for fantasy value any time soon, especially with Hunter Henry and likely Julian Hill ahead of him on the depth chart this season.

Thomas was selected by the Bears in the third round of April's draft. The LSU product is small (5'10/190), but extremely fast (4.28 40-yard dash) and figures to make his hay as a situational rusher, receiver and returner in the pros. He was limited to a 13% target share across his final three collegiate seasons (one at Mississippi State and two at LSU), having failed to clear 41 catches, 536 receiving yards or five touchdowns in any of the three campaigns. He'll battle Kalif Raymond and Jahdae Walker for work behind Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Thomas is unlikely to emerge into a reliable fantasy option.

profile_notes.subject: Falcons, Vikings, Bears, and Commanders passing environments
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Avoid premium prices until quarterback or offensive-line uncertainty improves.
profile_notes.summary: The hosts warn that elite individual talent does not remove uncertainty created by questionable quarterback development, playcalling, or offensive-line injuries.
profile_notes.evidence: Atlanta's quarterback quality, Minnesota's distributor, Caleb Williams's mechanics, and Washington's Laremy Tunsil injury are each presented as environment risks affecting multiple pass catchers.
profile_notes.counterweight: Each offense can outperform these assumptions, so the discussion is a monitoring framework rather than a blanket fade.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Separate player talent from environment certainty and require an appropriate discount until the team-level risk resolves.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Chicago Bears pass catchers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not assign Lions roles to Bears players solely because Ben Johnson is the coach.
profile_notes.summary: Ben Johnson's arrival does not make any Bears receiver a copy of Amon-Ra St. Brown or guarantee a WR6 outcome.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris says Amon-Ra is better than the available Bears options and rejects the temptation to call a Luther Burden highlight proof that he is the new Amon-Ra. Erickson adds that 12/13 personnel, a third-round TE, and Johnson's strong run design can limit assumed target windfalls.
profile_notes.counterweight: The offense could still improve and Chicago's traded DJ Moore leaves targets available, but that allocation cannot be known from camp clips.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not draft Chicago receivers on role-mapping narratives; wait for actual season usage and make only evidence-based adjustments.
profile_notes.episode_title: The Beastly NFC North & Jahmyr Gibbs Preview

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not assume a healthy or cohesive unit until tackle and interior questions are answered.
profile_notes.summary: The Chargers could benefit from an offensive-line-friendly McDaniel system, but Tucker sees legitimate uncertainty at every starting position.
profile_notes.evidence: Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt are returning from major injuries; Tucker questions center Tyler Biadasz's recovery, Jake Slaughter's shift from Florida center to left guard, and Cole Strange's fit after New England. Harris notes Alt was not fully participating when camp opened.
profile_notes.counterweight: The Shanahan-McVay tree can aid blockers, and all questions can resolve favorably.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Monitor training-camp participation and interior cohesion before assigning a strong line-driven boost to Chargers skill players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Los Angeles Chargers offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Target discounted Chargers pieces only on the conditional thesis of healthy line, protected Herbert, and a real offensive jump.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers can imagine a Chargers offense becoming a fantasy answer if health and protection finally cooperate, but view it as a conditional upside case rather than baseline.
profile_notes.evidence: Behrens says a healthy line and protected Justin Herbert could unlock a 28-30-point offense; Harris gives Herbert a mulligan and ties McConkey's rebound to the same factors.
profile_notes.counterweight: It requires unusually good Chargers injury luck, and the team has frequently failed to meet that sort of optimistic offensive projection.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the upside scenario as a tiebreaker for discounted Chargers, not as permission to erase downside.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

profile_notes.subject: Houston Texans offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Downgrade Texans skill players only if repeated padded-practice and controlled-scrimmage failures show the line cannot gel.
profile_notes.summary: Richard calls persistent Houston line instability a medium red flag for the offense, while Harris asks what concrete camp evidence would justify changing player ranks.
profile_notes.evidence: Reports had Houston changing lineups daily and struggling to gel; Richard says his current skill-position ranks are optimistic relative to that risk.
profile_notes.counterweight: Preseason games are less useful than controlled scrimmages, and teams can solve line combinations as Chicago did the prior year.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track repeated protection failures in meaningful practice settings before discounting Houston's fantasy assets.
profile_notes.episode_title: ALMANAC DAY & Five Most Important Training Camp Stories

profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Washington's pass-game options under review as replacement-line and protection information emerges instead of overreacting with a fixed downgrade.

profile_notes.subject: Washington Commanders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Modest environmental upgrade following Diggs's signing; no Harris downgrade for Terry McLaurin.
profile_notes.summary: Harris believes Diggs gives Washington a needed credible receiver and can improve the environment for Jayden Daniels, McLaurin, and the offense without taking McLaurin out of his prime role.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris notes that all Commanders pass catchers other than McLaurin had unstable week-to-week roles, while Diggs has a distinctly stronger portfolio. More sustained offense would create additional yards, touchdowns, and possession time.
profile_notes.counterweight: Diggs's personal ceiling is tied to the offense returning to its better two-years-ago form; Washington was not good last year, and Harris says some of that may have been Marcus Mariota-related.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not downgrade McLaurin just for a normal complementary receiver addition; modestly improve the outlook for a functional Commanders passing ecosystem.
profile_notes.episode_title: Film Room Heroes & Diggs To Commanders

outlook.text: Fields was selected by the Giants in the third round of April's draft. One of the biggest and strongest receivers in this rookie class, Fields figures to work as a perimeter, vertical target in the pros (career 13.3 aDOT during 49 collegiate games). Fields, who dropped just seven passes in college, handled a target share of, at least, 20% and air yard share of, at least, 30% during each of his final three collegiate seasons (two at Virginia, one at Notre Dame). Fields will battle Darnell Mooney, Darius Slayton and Calvin Austin III for New York's No. 2 receiver gig behind Malik Nabers. The rookie is no more than a late-round flier.

profile_notes.subject: Malachi Fields
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Move ahead of Ja'Kobi Lane and Ted Hurst; Harris suggests roughly WR72.
profile_notes.summary: Waldman strongly prefers Fields to the other big camp receivers because he combines real route technique with athletic finish ability.
profile_notes.evidence: He cites intermediate timing routes, flat breaks, short-area quickness, acceleration, contested wins, and post-catch tackle breaking.
profile_notes.counterweight: Both speakers distrust Jackson Dart's passing development, making Fields more of an undervalued dynasty/waiver profile than a clean immediate redraft starter.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Rank Fields above Lane/Hurst and draft him at that modest cost, while keeping quarterback risk in the projection.
profile_notes.episode_title: Re-Assessing The Rookies For 2026

profile_notes.subject: New York Giants offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat Giants outcomes as high-variance rather than projecting certainty into Week 1 roles.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers identify the Giants as a team full of volatile fantasy outcomes centered on Skattebo, Jaxson Dart, and Malik Nabers.
profile_notes.evidence: Funston says all three carry wild ranges of outcomes and calls the team fascinating from a fantasy perspective. Harris agrees on Skattebo and Nabers as swing possibilities.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris sharply differs on Dart, saying he disliked the tape and is out on him; the team label is an uncertainty signal, not a blanket endorsement.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Do not stack Giants assumptions as settled facts; assess each player separately and demand a price that accommodates role and quarterback uncertainty.
profile_notes.episode_title: Swing Players For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Las Vegas Raiders wide receivers
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round/double-digit-round receiver dart only if one player becomes the clear alpha behind Brock Bowers.
profile_notes.summary: Harris seeks a late sleeper from a market-dismissed Raiders offense if camp identifies a clear No. 1 wide receiver; Richard expects Tucker or Naylor to emerge as the practical candidates.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris argues presumed bad offenses are often wrongly written off, while Richard notes Clint Kubiak's history of hyper-targeting one receiver but expects Brock Bowers to be the obvious centerpiece.
profile_notes.counterweight: No candidate is expected to crack the top 36, the receiver room is unsettled, and Bowers may soak up the target concentration.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track which player survives camp hierarchy—especially Trey Tucker or Jalen Naylor—and stash only after credible separation emerges.

profile_notes.subject: Las Vegas Raiders passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-round receiver watch only if a receiver hierarchy emerges and Fernando Mendoza threatens Kirk Cousins for the starting job.
profile_notes.summary: Both see Las Vegas as a useful camp watch because an inexpensive receiver could become relevant if the passing game is better than assumed and a quarterback competition changes the outlook.
profile_notes.evidence: The Raiders publicly prefer Cousins to start the season, but a strong camp/preseason from first-overall-pick Mendoza could force a conversation. Harris says nobody is entitled to a role and wants to identify a clear winner such as Trey Tucker or Jalen Naylor.
profile_notes.counterweight: Brock Bowers is the primary target, the offense is widely expected to be poor, and Harris doubts Naylor's speed/film despite repeated organizational praise.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Follow the receiver and QB hierarchy for a cheap final-round target, but do not rely on a Raiders passer in standard one-QB leagues.
profile_notes.episode_title: Ladd McConkey Profile & Previewing AFC West

profile_notes.subject: Atlanta Falcons passing offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Monitor Michael Penix recovery versus Tua Tagovailoa starting; it affects Drake London/Kyle Pitts predictability more than Bijan Robinson's elite draft status.
profile_notes.summary: The Falcons' actionable camp fork is whether Penix can take first-team work and be ready Week 1 or whether Tua begins the season, with the quarterback mostly changing receiver/tight-end certainty.
profile_notes.evidence: McCormick prefers Tua's timing and predictability for London/Pitts, while Harris worries Tua should not be playing and might feel better if Penix wins. Both say Bijan's elite selection would not become a no-draft solely from Penix.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither option is a clean projection: Tua may be degraded, Penix's NFL competence is unproven, and the new coaching environment adds uncertainty.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Track actual first-team recovery evidence; adjust passing-game players more readily than Bijan.
profile_notes.episode_title: Welcome Back - Previewing NFC South

outlook.text: A first-team All-Pro in his first professional season, Dike broke Tim Brown's NFL rookie record for all-purpose yards. Most of that damage came as a returner (398 yards and two TDs on punts, 1,588 yards on kicks), but Dike also produced a bit as a receiver (423 yards and four TDs) and rusher (18 yards). The versatile Dike will remain a major factor in the return game, but he has added competition at wide receiver with Calvin Ridley healthy, Carnell Tate drafted fourth overall and target hog Wan'Dale Robinson signed during free agency. The 23-year-old will handle situational short-area targets and a few carries, but he's not a fantasy option.

profile_notes.subject: Tennessee Titans offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Late-draft Titans skill players gain volume appeal if the planned up-tempo system is confirmed.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker's key Tennessee nugget is a planned up-tempo attack, which could create more snaps for Cam Ward, Tony Pollard, Carnell Tate, and other Titans assets.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Brian Daboll brought Austin Schlottmann in at center because the coordinator trusts him to align the offense, make calls, and play fast. Tucker explicitly connects tempo and snap volume to fantasy value.
profile_notes.counterweight: Tucker says Schlottmann and right guard Volson are not considered average starters; Harris notes August tempo plans can vanish when a weak team is hit in the mouth.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use the up-tempo possibility as a late-round upside input, but wait for preseason confirmation that the line can execute it.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Conditionally upgrade pass catchers if quarterback play becomes merely passable.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers argue that Cleveland does not need excellent quarterback play for its pass catchers to beat depressed prices.
profile_notes.evidence: The derived analysis identifies KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, and Harold Fannin as players who could benefit if Shedeur Sanders or Dylan Gabriel is simply adequate.
profile_notes.counterweight: Neither host expresses confidence that the quarterback outcome will actually be adequate.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat Cleveland receivers and tight ends as conditional value rather than automatic targets, and update after credible quarterback evidence.
profile_notes.episode_title: Flag Players & Offenses We Might Be Wrong About

profile_notes.subject: Cleveland Browns offensive line
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat early-season cohesion as uncertain after a nearly complete starting-line overhaul.
profile_notes.summary: Tucker calls Cleveland's nearly wholesale replacement of the starting line an unprecedented continuity experiment with high early variance.
profile_notes.evidence: He says Teven Jenkins had been on the team but was not a starter, and cites Spencer Fano, Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins, and Titus Howard as new additions. Tucker grants that most have played meaningful NFL football.
profile_notes.counterweight: The individual additions have shown positive things and could gel by December; Harris also says he is not qualified to make every technique judgment and is not down on every member.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Avoid assuming immediate line quality for Browns assets; prioritize early-season evidence of the new group functioning together.
profile_notes.episode_title: Top Almanac Talents & O-Line Stories For 2026

profile_notes.subject: Browns quarterback competition
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Upgrade Browns pass catchers modestly only if Shedeur Sanders wins; avoid treating Deshaun Watson as equivalent.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers believe the Browns quarterback outcome materially affects pass catchers and prefer Sanders over Watson.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon cites Watson's poor form and back-to-back camp interceptions, while saying Sanders can be a flawed but functional NFL passer; Harris says his modest Browns ranks assume Sanders rather than Watson.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris says Sanders must release the ball faster and cannot recreate Colorado-style extended plays; neither calls him an exciting superflex starter.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep Browns receiver projections modest, but treat a Sanders starting outcome as a meaningful improvement over Watson.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: Cincinnati Bengals offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Do not change elite-player ranks on camp drills; monitor credible evidence of more under-center and modern-concept usage.
profile_notes.summary: The speakers regard Cincinnati's core as settled and already elite, with offensive evolution as a possible path from top-five to No. 1 production.
profile_notes.evidence: Harmon wants to see Joe Burrow under center more and the offense move beyond an almost exclusively shotgun approach; he notes incremental increases in Chase motion and varied alignment.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harmon repeatedly says camp talk will not force rank changes for Burrow, Chase, Higgins, or Brown, and the preference may remain Burrow's existing style.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Treat schematic reports as upside context, not a reason to chase already-expensive Bengals players.
profile_notes.episode_title: Bribing The Audience & Previewing The AFC North

profile_notes.subject: Rams offense
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Treat as a strong environment, but do not let that alone erase individual age, role, and price concerns.
profile_notes.summary: Both speakers see Los Angeles as the NFC West offense most widely expected to be elite, while Harris warns that assumed certainty creates contradictory player valuations.
profile_notes.evidence: They discuss a possible 30-point-per-game offense, the resolution of Matthew Stafford's prior back concern, and the Rams' recent history of meaningful August role signals.
profile_notes.counterweight: Harris opens the episode by showing that consensus team projections frequently fail, and individual Rams can still decline or lose role.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Use Rams environment as a supporting factor, then make player decisions on role, talent, health, and market cost.
profile_notes.episode_title: Previewing NFC West & A Super-Deep Sleeper From The Rams

profile_notes.subject: Dallas Cowboys skill players
profile_notes.action_qualifier: Ignore Cowboys camp hype absent injury or a genuine George Pickens hold-in.
profile_notes.summary: Dallas offers little camp information likely to change established fantasy evaluations.
profile_notes.evidence: Harris describes annual hype around Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, while Ciely says the relevant fantasy roles have little genuine competition. Pickens signed his tag and attended work despite a possible future contract dispute.
profile_notes.counterweight: A Pickens hold-in could hurt early games, and injuries or unavoidably negative reports would be meaningful.
profile_notes.practical_implication: Filter positive Cowboys clips out of draft decisions; only move players for material availability news.
profile_notes.episode_title: Jayden Daniels Profile & NFC East Training Camp Preview

outlook.text: Thompson was selected by the Chargers in the fourth round of April's draft. Thompson is an extremely small and very fast (4.26 40-yard dash) receiver who posted a rookie-class-high 18.5 YPR during his career and handled a massive 43% of Mississippi State's air yards last season. He didn't see much work prior to 2025, however, and figures to operate as a situational deep threat in the pros. He'll battle second-years Tre Harris and KeAndre Lamber-Smith for occasional looks behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston this season.

profile_notes.practical_implication: Keep the interior transition in the downside range for Ravens runners and passing-game projections rather than presuming past line quality.
